The federation learning technology family comprises a horizontal federation learning, a vertical federation learning, a federation learning variant, a distributed federation learning, a federation reinforcement learning and a federation learning variant, wherein the horizontal federation learning is suitable for a data horizontal segmentation scene, the vertical federation learning is suitable for a characteristic vertical segmentation scene, the federation migration learning is combined with knowledge migration, the distributed federation learning adopts a complete decentralization architecture, and the federation reinforcement learning is combined with the reinforcement learning. For each federal learning variant, technical examples of different parameter configurations, such as a combination of different aggregation algorithms (FedAvg, fedProx, etc.) and different privacy enhancement mechanisms (differential privacy, security aggregation, etc.), are further subdivided.
The homomorphic encryption technology family comprises partial homomorphic encryption such as Paillier encryption (supporting addition) and ElGamal encryption (supporting multiplication), homomorphic encryption such as BFV scheme (suitable for integer calculation) and CKKS scheme (suitable for approximate real number calculation), algebraic homomorphic encryption supporting operation on a specific algebraic structure, and ring homomorphic encryption based on a homomorphic scheme of a ring structure. Each homomorphic encryption technique is further subdivided into variations of different parameter settings, such as different security levels, different polynomial modulus sizes, and configurations of different optimization strategies.
The secure multiparty computing technology families include circuit-based secure computing such as garbled circuits (Garbled Circuits) and boolean shares, secret-sharing-based secure computing such as Shamir secret sharing and additive secret sharing, protocols based on inadvertent transmission (Oblivious Transfer), zero-Knowledge Proof of technology (Zero-knowledgeproof of technology), secure hardware-assisted multiparty computing such as solutions based on Trusted Execution Environments (TEE). These techniques are also subdivided into a number of technical examples according to different parameter settings and optimization strategies.
Each technology is represented as a technical feature vector, capturing key features of the technology, including dimensions of computational efficiency, communication overhead, memory requirements, security strength, flexibility, implementation maturity, and the like. For example, CKKS-based isomorphic encryption techniques may be expressed as <0.2, 0.3, 0.2, 0.9, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 0.4, 0.6, 0.5, 0.7, 0.8>, which represent the characteristics of low computational efficiency but high security, support complex operations, but high communication overhead.
This step innovatively builds a Task-technology mapping framework (Task-Technology Mapping Framework, TTMF), which is a core structure connecting medical computing tasks and privacy computing technologies. TTMF contains three key components:
and defining a feature space, and unifying the task feature vector space and the technical feature vector space into a multidimensional mapping space so that the task feature vector space and the technical feature vector space can be compared. This involves feature reduction and spatial transformation, ensuring that the two classes of vectors are comparable in space after conversion.
Compatibility functions define a compatibility metric comp (t i ,h j ) between task t i and technology h j , reflecting the applicability of the technology to the task. The compatibility function considers the function matching degree (whether the technology can realize the function required by the task) and the performance matching degree (whether the technical performance meets the task requirement), the output value range is [0,1], and the higher the value is, the more compatible is represented.
A rule set is mapped defining which class of technology the task should select under certain conditions. These rules are based on expert knowledge AND historical experience in forms such as "IF condition THEN recommendation technique", e.g. "IF task involves a high-dimensional AND sensitivity level high AND attack model recommending lateral federal learning + differential privacy for semi-honest THEN.
The TTMF framework provides conceptual foundations and initial elicitations for subsequent optimization modeling by mapping abstract task features and technical characteristics to specific selection suggestions. The framework particularly considers special requirements of medical data processing, such as strict privacy protection requirements, high-dimensional sparse data characteristics and complex calculation modes, and ensures that technical selection can meet special challenges of medical scenes.
Medical computing tasks are abstracted into feature vectors, including dimensions such as data scale (such as data size), computing complexity (such as algorithm complexity), privacy requirements (such as sensitivity level) and the like, available privacy computing technologies (including variants of different parameter configurations) are defined as technology sets, and a task-to-technology mapping relation framework is established.
Step S232, based on the task-technology mapping framework, defining a distance function to represent the cost when the tasks in the medical data computing task set are executed by adopting the technologies in the technology set, defining capacity constraints for each technology in the technology set to represent the maximum task number and radius constraints that can be processed simultaneously by each technology to represent the maximum execution cost acceptable by each technology, and obtaining a constraint condition set.
Based on the task-technology mapping framework constructed in the previous step, quantized distance functions and constraint conditions are further defined, and a foundation is laid for mathematical optimization modeling of privacy computing technology selection problems. This step converts the abstract mapping relationship into a computable mathematical model, enabling the optimization problem to be accurately expressed and solved.
First, a medical task-to-technology distance function (MEDICAL TASK-Technology Distance Function, MTTDF) is designed, which is a multi-dimensional weighted distance metric that represents the cost incurred when a medical computing task is performed using a particular privacy computing technique. MTTDF consider various cost factors and give different weights according to the characteristics of medical scenes to form a comprehensive distance measure:
The calculation time cost reflects the processing time required by task execution, and the consideration factors comprise the original calculation complexity, the complexity of a task algorithm, the additional cost introduced by the technology, such as additional calculation introduced by encryption operation, security protocol and the like, the influence of data scale, the influence coefficient of data quantity on the calculation time, the parallel acceleration potential and the support degree of the technology on parallel calculation.
The communication overhead cost represents the data transmission quantity and communication round in the task execution process, and the consideration factors comprise the number of protocol interaction rounds, the number of communication rounds required for completing calculation, the total quantity of data to be transmitted, the bandwidth utilization rate, the effective utilization degree of the technology on the available bandwidth, the delay sensitivity and the sensitivity of the calculation process to network delay.
The memory and storage requirements in the quantitative calculation process of the memory and storage cost are considered, wherein the considerations comprise the peak memory usage, the maximum memory occupation in the calculation process, the intermediate result storage requirement, the intermediate calculation result size required to be stored, different efficiencies caused by the memory access mode, the sequential access or the random access, the cache efficiency and the utilization efficiency of the technology to the cache of the processor.
The adaptation degree of the security cost reflection technology in meeting the task security requirement comprises a security strength gap, a gap between a security level provided by the technology and the task requirement, a privacy leakage risk, a possible information leakage degree, an attack model coverage, a security proving level and formalized proving strength of the technical security, wherein the attack model is specified by the task, and the security model coverage can be judged whether the technology can deal with the task.
The flexibility and the adaptability cost represent the capability of the technology to adapt to special requirements of tasks, and the considerations include the functional coverage, the matching degree of an operation set of technical support and the requirements of the tasks, the precision guarantee, whether the technology can meet the calculation precision requirements of the tasks, the expandability, the performance when the data scale grows, the fault tolerance capability and the capability of coping with the failure of the participants or the network problems.
Based on the multi-dimensional cost factor described above, MTTDF is defined as a form of weighted cosine distance, and the distance between task feature vector t i and technical feature vector h j is calculated, denoted as d (t i ,h j ). The weighted cosine distance considers the angle difference and the direction consistency between vectors, and is more suitable for capturing the matching degree between tasks and technologies than the Euclidean distance. The weight of each dimension in the distance calculation is determined by analyzing historical task execution data and expert evaluation, for example, in privacy analysis processing genome data, the security dimension is given a higher weight, whereas in real-time medical monitoring analysis, the calculation time dimension weight is higher.
To address special cases in medical scenarios, MTTDF also contains an adaptive adjustment mechanism. This mechanism adjusts the base distance calculation by context factors, taking into account contextual factors such as urgency (emergency analysis vs. routine research), resource fluctuations (peak vs. idle), and regulatory requirement changes. For example, for medical analysis tasks labeled "urgent", the weight of the computation time dimension will automatically increase, while the weight of the security dimension will correspondingly increase in the face of strict new data protection regulations.
Secondly, this step defines two types of key constraints for each privacy computing technique, forming a set of technical constraints (Technology Constraint Set, TCS):
The capacity constraint (Capacity Constraint) represents the maximum number of tasks that a particular technology can handle simultaneously, reflecting the upper limit of the technology's processing capacity. The capacity constraint considers various factors including computing resource limitation, such as available CPU core, GPU unit and memory capacity, concurrent processing capacity, maximum number of parallel tasks supported by technology, license limitation, concurrent use license limitation of certain commercial technical schemes, system stability and maximum load for maintaining stable operation of the system. The capacity constraint is defined as the maximum number of tasks cap (h j ) of technology j, for example, an fully homomorphic encryption system of a particular configuration may be limited to processing a maximum of 5 computationally intensive tasks at the same time to ensure performance and stability.
Radius constraints (Radius Constraint) represent the maximum task-to-technology distance that is technically acceptable, defining the limits of the applicable scope of the technology. Radius constraints reflect a key concept that a task is no longer a viable choice for a task when its "distance" from the technology (i.e., the cost of performing the task using the technology) exceeds a particular threshold. Radius constraint consideration includes a performance degradation threshold, a distance point at which technical performance begins to be remarkably reduced, an upper limit of resource consumption, acceptable maximum resource consumption, a safety guarantee base line, a minimum safety standard which can be guaranteed by a technology, a quality guarantee limit and a maximum distance which can maintain quality of a result. Radius constraints are defined as the maximum acceptable distance rad (h j ) for a technique j, e.g., a particular federal learning scheme may set rad (h j ) =0.7, meaning that when the task-to-technique distance exceeds 0.7, the technique is no longer applicable, possibly because security is not guaranteed or performance is severely degraded.
In addition to technology specific constraints, this step defines a System-level global constraint (System-level Global Constraints, SGC) that captures constraints of the overall medical data processing System:
The overall resource constraints limit the total computing, storage, and network resources available to the system, ensuring that the sum of the resource usage of all technologies does not exceed the system capacity. This includes CPU/GPU total computational power limitations, total memory and storage space limitations, network bandwidth upper limits, energy consumption limitations (especially for ambulatory medical devices).
Compliance constraints ensure that technical choices meet applicable regulatory and standard requirements, including data retention requirements, data must be kept in a specific geographic location, process transparency requirements, process auditability, algorithm interpretability requirements, decision making processes must be understandable and interpretable, disaster recovery requirements, and systems must be able to recover from failures.
Load balancing constraints facilitate balanced use of system resources, preventing overload of certain technology or infrastructure components. This includes distributing requirements across technology loads, balancing requirements across hardware nodes, peak load management policies, quality of service guarantees requirements.
By integrating MTTDF and TCS, this step builds a complete set of constraints, providing the necessary elements for mathematical modeling of the optimization problem. These constraints not only take into account the direct cost and limitations of technical choice, but also incorporate the specific requirements of the medical environment, such as factors like data protection regulations, medical decision timeliness and system reliability, ensuring that the final technical choice scheme not only optimizes performance, but also meets the specific requirements of the medical scenario.
A multi-dimensional distance function is defined, the cost of quantized tasks executed by a specific technology is defined, the weighted combination of factors including calculation time, memory occupation, communication overhead and the like, and two types of constraints are defined for each technology, wherein capacity constraints represent the maximum number of tasks which can be processed simultaneously by the technology, radius constraints represent the maximum task distance (cost) which can be accepted by the technology, and the constraints reflect the processing capacity and application range limitations of the technology.
And S233, constructing an objective function to minimize the maximum task-technology distance in all tasks according to the constraint condition set, setting constraint conditions such that the number of tasks allocated by each technology does not exceed the corresponding capacity constraint and the distance between each task and the corresponding allocation technology does not exceed the radius constraint of the corresponding technology, and obtaining the mathematical optimization model.
Based on the distance function and the constraint condition set defined in the previous step, the privacy calculation technology selection Problem is formally modeled as a Non-uniform k-center Problem (Non-uniform k-center Problem), which is a classical combination optimization Problem variant. The modeling method converts abstract technical choices into structured mathematical optimization problems, so that the mathematical optimization problems can be solved through an optimization algorithm.
First, the correspondence between the non-uniform k-center problem and the privacy computing technique selection problem is elucidated. The conventional k-center problem seeks to assign a set of points to k center points such that the maximum point-center distance is minimized. An extension of the non-uniform k-center problem is that each center point has different capacity and service radius limitations. In the medical privacy computing context, medical data is computed into a set of task corresponding points, each task is a point in a feature space, privacy computing technologies are corresponding to a center point, each technology can serve multiple tasks, task-technology distance corresponds to point-center distance, cost of executing tasks by using a specific technology is represented, technology capacity constraint corresponds to center point capacity limitation, maximum number of tasks which can be simultaneously served by each technology is represented, technology radius constraint corresponds to center point service radius, and maximum service distance acceptable by technologies is represented. The correspondence enables the medical privacy computing technology selection problem to be formally expressed and solved by means of the theoretical framework of the non-uniform k-center problem.
Secondly, the step builds a mathematical optimization model, and accurately expresses objective functions and constraint conditions of the problem:
The objective function is set to minimize the maximum task-to-technology distance among all tasks, i.e., minimax optimize the objective, min max { d (t i ,h j ) | t i is assigned to h j }. This objective function reflects a "bottleneck optimization" strategy, focusing on task-technology pairing in the system that is most costly to perform, trying to reduce this maximum cost, thereby increasing the lower efficiency limit of the overall system.
The constraint condition set comprises four key constraints, namely, distributing integrity constraints, capacity constraints, radius constraints, global resource constraints, total resources used by all technologies, and system feasibility, wherein the integrity constraints require that each task must be distributed to one technology only, all tasks can be processed, the total number of tasks required to be distributed to each technology does not exceed the upper capacity limit cap (h j ) of the technology, technical overload is prevented, the distance between the tasks and the distributed technology does not exceed the upper radius limit rad (h j ) of the technology, the technologies are ensured to be suitable for the distributed tasks, and the total resources used by all the technologies do not exceed the upper available resources of the system.
By introducing a decision variable x ij (indicating whether task i is assigned to a technology j) and an auxiliary variable z (indicating the maximum task-technology distance), the complete mathematical optimization model is expressed formally. This model is a mixed integer programming problem, the complexity of which stems from the binary nature of the decision variables (tasks either assigned to a particular technique or not) and the minimax nature of the objective function.
For processing the calculation complexity of the model, the step provides a problem characteristic analysis and algorithm selection strategy:
complexity analysis shows that the non-uniform k-center problem is NP-hard, meaning that for large-scale instances, finding an exact global optimal solution is not generally computationally feasible. In the medical privacy computing scenario, the number of tasks may reach hundreds to thousands, and the technology is changed into tens of types, so that the problem scale is further enlarged.
The structural analysis of the problems discovers that the medical privacy computing technology has some beneficial characteristics that sparse connectivity can not be processed by all technologies, that a plurality of tasks-technologies automatically exclude due to radius constraint, that technology hierarchy exists, that advanced technologies generally cover functions of low-level technologies, that local independence, and that certain task groups are independent of each other and can be decomposed into sub-problems for parallel solving.
Based on these characteristics, an algorithm selection framework is proposed to select an appropriate solution method according to the problem size and structural characteristics, for small-scale problems (< 50 tasks, <10 techniques), accurate algorithms such as branch-and-bound methods can be used, for medium-scale problems, approximate algorithms such as greedy plus local search are recommended, for large-scale problems meta-heuristic algorithms such as simulated annealing or genetic algorithms are recommended, or problem decomposition methods split large problems into manageable sub-problems.
In addition, the dynamic characteristics of the medical environment are considered, and the model is expanded to adapt to changing requirements:
Dynamic task processing extensions allow the model to adapt to newly added tasks or task priority changes. When a new medical analysis task is submitted, the system may incrementally update the allocation scheme instead of re-solving the entire problem. This dynamic adaptation capability is particularly important in responding to emergency medical analysis needs.
Elastic technology capability extension considers the situation where technology resources may change over time. For example, in a computing resource scalable cloud environment, the capacity constraints of the technology may be elastic, allowing expansion during high demand. The model captures this elasticity by setting the capacity parameter as a function of time rather than a fixed constant.
Robustness considerations extend to enable the model to handle parameter uncertainties. Measurement errors or fluctuations may exist in task characteristics and technical performance in a medical environment. The model ensures that the selected solution remains viable and efficient in all possible scenarios by introducing scene analysis and worst case optimization.
Finally, the applicability of the mathematical model is verified, and evaluation is performed through the real medical data analysis task and the test scenes of various privacy calculation technologies. The verification result shows that the model can effectively capture the core requirements and constraints of the medical privacy calculation scene, and the generated technical allocation scheme improves the overall performance by 25% -40% compared with a manual selection or simple heuristic method on average, and simultaneously ensures that all safety and resource constraints are met.
Through mathematical modeling of the step, the privacy computing technology selection problem is converted from an abstract decision process to a structured optimization problem, and systematic solving can be performed by means of mature optimization theory and algorithm. The transition makes the complex technology selection process more transparent, reproducible and optimizable, and provides a solid theoretical basis for improving the efficiency and safety of medical data privacy calculation.
Based on the defined task-technical distance and constraint conditions, an optimization target is set to minimize the maximum execution cost (maximum task-technical distance) in all tasks, meanwhile, the constraint of technical capacity and application range is met, a complete non-uniform k center mathematical optimization model is constructed, and a privacy computing technology selection problem is formed into a process of solving the model.
In one embodiment of the present invention, step S34 designs and implements a minimum weight base solution algorithm according to the element weight matrix, and selects a protocol element combination with a differential privacy parameter epsilon value smaller than a preset security threshold and minimum total computation cost and communication overhead from protocol elements, so as to obtain a protocol minimum weight base.
Specifically, step S341 extracts all protocol elements in the element weight matrix to create a protocol element selection set based on the calculation cost, communication overhead and security intensity weight of each protocol element defined in the element weight matrix, and sorts all protocol elements according to the order of security intensity from high to low, so as to obtain a candidate element sequence.
First, a protocol element set is extracted from the constructed element weight matrix, and priority ranking is performed based on the security index. The element weight matrix is a multidimensional data structure for describing the attributes of each component element of the privacy computing protocol, and comprises key indexes such as computing cost, communication overhead, security intensity and the like of each protocol element.
First, all available protocol elements are extracted from the element weight matrix to form an initial candidate set. The protocol elements are the basic components that make up the privacy computing protocol, including encryption primitives like state encryption, blind signatures or zero knowledge proof, communication mechanisms such as secure channel or garbled circuit transmissions, computing components such as security aggregation or distributed query processing, privacy enhancement techniques such as differential privacy, k-anonymity or randomized responses, etc. For medical data privacy calculations, a typical set of elements contains 30-50 different protocol elements, each element having specific functional and performance characteristics.
Next, the security intensity index of each element is extracted, mainly based on the differential privacy parameter epsilon value. The differential privacy parameter epsilon is a key indicator quantifying the strength of privacy protection, with smaller epsilon values indicating a higher degree of privacy protection, but also generally implying higher computational costs or lower data availability. For example, epsilon=0.1 indicates a very strong privacy protection, while epsilon=10 indicates a weaker protection. For each protocol element, the system evaluates its native epsilon value or its contribution to the overall protocol epsilon value.
Besides epsilon value, the comprehensive safety strength score is constructed by considering various safety indexes, wherein the comprehensive safety strength score comprises resistance model strength, attacker model types (such as semi-honest, malicious or bypass attack) which can be resisted by elements, calculation safety, strength and safety proof strictness based on cryptography assumption, communication safety, protection degree and eavesdropping resistance of a communication channel, and information leakage quantity, wherein the maximum information leakage possibly caused by the elements. These indices form a composite security intensity score for each element by weighted combination.
The security priority ordering algorithm is realized, and all protocol elements are ordered from high security intensity to low security intensity. The ranking process employs a two-stage strategy, firstly, a primary ranking based on epsilon values, with smaller epsilon values ranking earlier, and secondly, a secondary ranking based on a composite security intensity score for elements with the same or close epsilon values. The ranking algorithm takes into account the trade-off relationship between the security indicators, e.g., some elements may have very low epsilon values but risk bypass attacks, at which point the system adjusts the final ranking according to the importance of the application scenario.
Through the ranking process, a sequence of candidate elements is generated that gradually transitions from the most secure element to a less secure but potentially more computationally efficient element. The front end of the sequence typically contains elements with strong differential privacy guarantees, such as randomized response mechanisms or noise addition techniques using low epsilon values, while the back end of the sequence contains elements that are more computationally efficient but relatively weaker in security guarantees. This ordering ensures that security requirements can be prioritized during subsequent selections.
And sorting the elements from high to low according to a security intensity index (mainly a differential privacy parameter epsilon value), forming a candidate element sequence with priority sorting, and ensuring that the security requirement is prioritized.
And S342, sequentially selecting protocol elements meeting the condition that the epsilon value of the differential privacy parameter is smaller than a preset safety threshold by adopting a greedy strategy according to the candidate element sequence, and calculating the total computation cost and the communication cost of the currently selected element combination to obtain an initial protocol element combination.
And constructing an initial protocol element combination by applying a greedy strategy based on the candidate element sequence generated in the previous step. Greedy strategy is an iterative decision method, making a selection at each step that is currently seen to be optimal, with the expectation that a globally optimal or near optimal solution will ultimately be obtained.
First, a differential privacy security threshold value εmax is set, which is the maximum ε value that a protocol element is allowed to. The security threshold is set based on the privacy requirements of the application scenario and related regulatory requirements, e.g., epsilon max may be set to 0.5 or less when processing highly sensitive medical data (e.g., genetic information or mental health records), and epsilon max may be relaxed to 2 or 3 when processing less sensitive aggregate statistics. Thresholding also takes into account data size and query complexity, simple queries on larger data sets may use lower thresholds, while complex analysis or small data sets may need to be relaxed appropriately.
Next, an empty set of element combinations S is initialized and a set of necessary functional requirements F is defined, including all functions that the protocol must support, such as security aggregation, condition queries, model training, etc. Each functional requirement may be satisfied by a plurality of different protocol elements, but at least one element is required to be implemented.
The greedy selection process is performed in an iterative manner. In each iteration, sequentially considering an element e from a candidate element sequence, checking whether the element e meets three conditions, namely a security condition, a difference privacy parameter epsilon (e) of e is less than or equal to epsilon max, ensuring that the element meets a security threshold requirement, a function condition, wherein e can meet at least one of the function requirements which are not covered currently, and a compatibility condition, wherein e is compatible with all elements in a selected element set S, and no function conflict or security conflict exists.
For an element that satisfies these three conditions, the marginal cost increase after adding the element is calculated, including the calculation cost increment Δcomp and the communication overhead increment Δcomm. The computation takes into account synergistic effects between elements, and some combinations of elements may create additional optimizations or overhead. The marginal Cost is calculated by a weighted combination of Δcost=w1·Δcomp+w2·Δcomm, where w1 and w2 are weights reflecting the relative importance of the computing resources and the network resources.
Elements are selected to be added to S that can cover the unmet functional requirements with minimal marginal cost. If multiple elements have the same marginal cost, then the element with higher security strength is preferentially selected. After each addition of an element, the uncovered set of functional requirements and the current total cost are updated.
The greedy process continues until all functional requirements are met or no new elements can be found that meet the conditions. In the latter case, the security threshold or functionality requirements may be relaxed or the user may be prompted that the protocol cannot be constructed under the current constraints.
After greedy selection is completed, an integrity check is performed on the initial element combination to ensure that all necessary functions are covered. The checking comprises function coverage verification, security compatibility verification and resource demand assessment, wherein the function coverage verification ensures that at least one element is supported for each function demand, the security compatibility verification ensures that no security conflict exists among all selected elements, and the total computation cost and the communication cost of the computing combination are ensured to be within the range of the system resource capacity.
The key innovation in this step is a function driven security preference policy, i.e. first consider the highest security elements, and only if these elements fail to meet certain functional requirements, consider the elements that are less secure but still meet the threshold. This ensures that the protocol uses as safe a combination of elements as possible, while meeting the functional requirements.
Through greedy strategy, an initial protocol element combination is constructed, which meets all functional requirements and safety threshold requirements, and reduces total computation cost and communication overhead as much as possible. This initial combination will serve as a starting point for the subsequent optimization.
And adopting a greedy strategy, sequentially selecting elements with differential privacy parameter epsilon values meeting the safety threshold requirements from the ordered candidate element sequences, evaluating the influence of each element on the total cost after being added to the current combination, and selecting elements capable of meeting the functional requirements and increasing the minimum total cost until a complete initial protocol element combination is formed.
And step S343, performing element replacement and combination optimization in an iterative mode based on the initial protocol element combination, continuously reducing total calculation cost and communication cost on the premise of ensuring that the epsilon value of the differential privacy parameter meets a safety threshold, and stopping iteration when the total calculation cost and the communication cost cannot be reduced by continuous multiple iterations, so as to obtain the local optimal element combination.
Based on the initial protocol element combination constructed in the previous step, an iterative optimization process is implemented to further reduce the cost. Iterative optimization is a method of improving the initial solution, gradually approaching the optimal solution by continuously adjusting the current solution by small amounts.
First, an optimization objective function is defined, and the total Cost of the quantized element combination is Cost (S) =alpha-CompCost (S) +beta-CommCost (S) +gamma-OverheadCost (S), wherein CompCost is the calculation Cost, commCost is the communication Cost, overheadCost is the management Cost, and alpha, beta and gamma are weight factors to reflect the relative importance of different resource dimensions. In a medical data processing scenario, the computation cost is usually measured in terms of processor time and memory usage, the communication overhead is measured in terms of data transmission amount and communication round, and the management overhead comprises additional costs such as key management, synchronization coordination and the like.
The "neighborhood" of the current solution is explored to find a better solution using a local search optimization strategy. A neighborhood is defined as all possible combinations that can be reached through single element substitution, element pair exchange, or finite element set adjustment. Specifically, the system implements three types of local improvement operations:
The element replacement operation considers replacing a certain element in the current combination with other elements in the candidate set, provided that the functional requirements and the safety threshold are still met after the replacement. Enumerating each element e1 in the current combination, attempting to replace with each element e2 within the security threshold in the candidate set, if e2 can cover all functions of e1 and Cost (S- { e1} + { e2 }) < Cost (S), then performing the replacement. For example, the system may replace the accurate but computationally intensive mechanism with a more computationally efficient approximate differential privacy mechanism, provided that the security parameters still meet the threshold.
Element combination optimization considers replacing multiple elements in the current combination as a functionally equivalent but lower overall cost replacement group. Identifying overlapping subsets of elements of a function, exploring whether alternatives exist that can provide the same function at a lower cost. For example, it is possible to replace individual encryption, aggregation, and decryption elements with one comprehensive security aggregation element, reducing coordination overhead and communication costs.
Redundancy elimination analyzes functional redundancy in the current combination, removing unnecessary elements. Checking whether the function of each element is completely covered by other elements, and if so, removing the function without affecting the overall security. This optimization is particularly useful for redundancy that may be introduced by the greedy construction process.
In each iteration, all possible local improvement operations are evaluated, and the operation yielding the greatest cost reduction is selected for execution. If multiple operations produce the same cost reduction, the operation with the greatest security improvement is preferentially selected. After each operation, the system updates the current element combination and the total cost.
A dynamic security constraint checking mechanism is introduced in the optimization process, so that any element change is ensured not to violate security requirements. This mechanism calculates the effective differential privacy parameter εeff before and after the combination change, ensuring εeff is less than εmax. Epsilon eff calculations take into account the combined effects between elements, some of which may produce superimposed security effects or security weaknesses.
To avoid locally optimal traps, variants of simulated annealing strategies were implemented. In some iterations, there is a small probability of accepting an operation with a slight increase in cost but possibly leading to a better solution path. The acceptance probability decreases with the cost increase and the current iteration number, ensuring the final convergence of the algorithm.
The iterative process sets a termination condition that a locally optimal solution is considered to be reached when none of the consecutive k iterations (typically k=5 to 10) can reduce the total cost beyond a predetermined threshold δ (typically set to 0.5%). In addition, the maximum iteration number max iter is set as a standby termination condition to prevent the algorithm from sinking into the loop.
After the iterative optimization is completed, a local optimal element combination is output, the combination meets the requirement of a safety threshold, and the total cost of the initial combination is obviously reduced through multiple rounds of optimization. Experiments have shown that iterative optimization can generally reduce the cost of the initial combination by 15% -30% while maintaining or improving security.
Based on the initial element combination, the solution is continuously improved through an iterative optimization process, wherein the existing elements are tried to be replaced by lower-cost substitutes, the adjustment possibility of the element combination is explored, the influence of the replacement and the adjustment on the total cost is evaluated in each iteration, the change capable of reducing the cost is accepted on the premise that the safety threshold is not violated, and when the cost cannot be further reduced by multiple iterations, the local optimal solution is considered to be reached.
Step 344, according to the locally optimal element combination, verifying the independence constraint and the quasi-array property of the selected protocol element, and ensuring that the element combination meets the protocol integrity and security requirements to obtain the protocol minimum weight base.
Based on the local optimal element combination obtained in the previous step, the method carries out comprehensive verification and confirms that the local optimal element combination meets all requirements of a protocol minimum weight base. The minimum weight base verification is a key step for ensuring that an optimization result meets theoretical guarantee, and relates to independence constraint verification and quasi-array property verification.
First, the independence constraint of the selected combination of elements is verified. An independence constraint refers to the absence of functional redundancy or cyclic dependencies in a collection of elements, each element having its irreplaceable role. The system implements three layers of independence verification:
The functional independence check ensures that each element provides a function that at least one other element cannot completely replace. Building a functional coverage matrix M, where M [ i, j ] = 1 represents that element i supports a function j, and then verifying that removing any element results in at least one of the functions being decovered. Such checking prevents the presence of redundant elements, ensuring the minimality of the combination.
The security independence analysis ensures that each element has a unique contribution to overall security. The effect of removing each element on the combined differential privacy parameter epsilonff is evaluated, and if the removal results in a significant increase in epsilonff (security degradation), the element is security independent. Some elements may not provide differential privacy protection themselves, but synergistically with other elements to enhance overall security.
Resource independence assessment ensures that element combinations are not unnecessarily duplicated in resource utilization. Checking for resource sharing and multiplexing possibilities between elements ensures that there are no duplicate elements that can be consolidated to reduce resource consumption.
Next, the nature of the pseudo-array of combinations of elements is verified, which is the theoretical basis for ensuring that the combinations form a valid minimum weight basis. A pseudo-array is a structure in combinatorial mathematics that has specific properties that make it suitable for describing the independence between elements. In the context of privacy computation protocols, the pseudo-array model treats the protocol as a set of elements and a set of independence constraints. The system verifies three key matrix properties:
Genetic property checks ensure that any subset of the independent element subsets are also independent. Validating any subset S 'in the combination' Whether S also satisfies the independence constraint that no element in a subset can be completely replaced by other elements in the subset. This property ensures that there is no hidden redundancy level in the combination.
The exchange property verification ensures that the combination of elements has optimal exchange properties. For any independent set I and independent set J larger than I, it is always possible to find an element from J to add to I to maintain independence. The system verifies this property by trying various element exchange operations, ensuring that the combination cannot be further optimized by simple exchanges.
The maximization verification ensures that the element combination is a very large set in the sense of containment relationship, i.e. no more elements can be added while maintaining independence and meeting the security threshold. An attempt is made to add each remaining element in the candidate set to the current combination to verify whether it would result in an independence constraint violation or a security threshold exceeding.
And after the verification of the quasi-array property is completed, executing the final confirmation of the minimum weight base. The minimum weight base refers to a base having the smallest total weight (cost) among all the bases satisfying the requirements. The total weight W (S) of the current combination is calculated and compared with the theoretical lower bound. Although the exact computation of the optimal solution is typically computationally too complex, the system uses approximate comparison and lower bound estimation to evaluate the quality of the current solution, confirming that it is close to the globally optimal solution.
And finally, comprehensively verifying the protocol integrity and the security, wherein the comprehensive verification comprises the steps of checking the functional completeness, confirming that all necessary functions are fully supported, verifying whether the final epsilon eff meets epsilon max requirements or not, calculating the resource feasibility, confirming that the total computation cost and the communication cost are in the system resource capacity range, verifying the protocol consistency, and ensuring that selected elements can be seamlessly cooperated to form a complete protocol.
And (3) comprehensively verifying the local optimal element combination, and checking whether the independency constraint defined in the uncertain pseudo-array model is met, namely, functional completeness (whether all necessary functions are covered), safety compatibility (whether safety conflict exists among elements) and resource feasibility (whether total resource requirements are within system capacity) or not, wherein the element combination is confirmed to form an effective pseudo-array base, and a final protocol minimum weight base is formed and is used as a basis of an optimized privacy calculation protocol.
As shown in fig. 3, the present invention further provides a high-efficiency privacy computation fusion engine system for medical data, including:
The state management module 10 is configured to construct a mapping relationship from a state identifier to a prefix tree node through a prefix tree data structure based on the multi-source medical data feature, and implement a read-write lock mechanism and a dynamic memory allocation policy for supporting multi-thread concurrent access, so as to obtain a state management module;
The adaptive technology selection module 20 is configured to analyze performance characteristics of multiple privacy computing technologies under different medical data scenarios according to the state management module, classify and model computing tasks into optimization problems according to data sizes, computing complexity and privacy requirements, and design an approximate algorithm to integrate data types, computing tasks and system resource states, so as to generate an adaptive privacy computing technology combination strategy;
The protocol optimization module 30 is configured to decompose a privacy computing protocol into basic operation elements and construct a mathematical model according to the adaptive privacy computing technology combination policy, define multidimensional weights of computing cost, communication overhead and security intensity of the protocol elements, and design a solution algorithm to select a minimum cost protocol element combination meeting a preset security threshold to obtain an optimized privacy computing protocol framework;
The encryption and decryption module 40 is configured to perform privacy sensitivity analysis and classification on the medical data based on the optimized privacy computing protocol framework, design a hybrid encryption strategy, and implement a distributed key generation, distribution and management system to obtain a medical data encryption and decryption system;
The privacy calculation execution engine 50 is configured to implement standardized encapsulation and define a unified interface for multiple privacy calculation technologies based on the medical data encryption and decryption system, and construct an execution engine to implement multi-technology collaborative scheduling and execution, so as to obtain a medical data privacy calculation fusion system.

1. A method for an efficient privacy-preserving computation fusion engine for medical data, characterized by comprising:
Based on the characteristics of multi-source medical data, a mapping relationship between state identifiers and prefix tree nodes is constructed through a prefix tree data structure to realize a read-write lock mechanism that supports multi-threaded concurrent access and a dynamic memory allocation strategy, thus obtaining the state management module.
Based on the state management module, the performance characteristics of various privacy computing technologies under different medical data scenarios are analyzed. The computing tasks are classified and modeled as optimization problems according to data scale, computing complexity and privacy requirements. An approximate algorithm is designed to integrate data types, computing tasks and system resource states to generate an adaptive privacy computing technology combination strategy.
Based on the adaptive privacy computing technology combination strategy, the privacy computing protocol is decomposed into basic operational elements and a mathematical model is constructed. The multidimensional weights of the computational cost, communication overhead and security strength of the protocol elements are defined. A solution algorithm is designed to select the minimum cost combination of protocol elements that meets the preset security threshold, and the optimized privacy computing protocol framework is obtained.
Based on the optimized privacy computing protocol framework, privacy sensitivity analysis and classification of medical data are performed, a hybrid encryption strategy is designed, and a distributed key generation, distribution and management system is implemented to obtain a medical data encryption and decryption system.
Based on the aforementioned medical data encryption and decryption system, various privacy computing technologies are standardized and encapsulated, and a unified interface is defined. An execution engine is built to achieve collaborative scheduling and execution of multiple technologies, resulting in a medical data privacy computing fusion system.

Based on the concurrent optimization prefix tree state management module, the path compression technology of the prefix tree is implemented to merge paths with a single child node, and the incremental persistence mechanism is implemented to write only the changed prefix tree nodes to the storage medium, thereby reducing storage overhead and supporting breakpoint recovery of large-scale medical models, thus obtaining the state management module.

Based on the computational cost, communication overhead, and security strength weight of each protocol element defined in the element weight matrix, a protocol element selection set is created by extracting all protocol elements in the element weight matrix and sorting all protocol elements in descending order of security strength to obtain a candidate element sequence.
Based on the candidate element sequence, a greedy strategy is used to sequentially select protocol elements that satisfy the differential privacy parameter ε value being less than a preset security threshold. The total computational cost and communication overhead of the currently selected element combination are calculated to obtain the initial protocol element combination.
Based on the initial combination of protocol elements, element replacement and combination optimization are performed iteratively. Under the premise of ensuring that the differential privacy parameter ε meets the security threshold, the total computational cost and communication overhead are continuously reduced. When the total computational cost and communication overhead cannot be reduced in multiple consecutive iterations, the iteration stops, and a local optimal combination of elements is obtained.
Based on the locally optimal combination of elements, the independence constraints and matroid properties of the selected protocol elements are verified to ensure that the combination of elements meets the requirements of protocol integrity and security, and the minimum weight basis of the protocol is obtained.
10. A high-efficiency privacy-preserving computing fusion engine system for medical data, characterized in that it comprises:
The state management module is used to construct a mapping relationship between state identifiers and prefix tree nodes based on the characteristics of multi-source medical data through a prefix tree data structure, and to implement a read-write lock mechanism that supports multi-threaded concurrent access and a dynamic memory allocation strategy, thus obtaining the state management module.
The adaptive technology selection module is used to analyze the performance characteristics of various privacy computing technologies in different medical data scenarios based on the state management module, classify computing tasks according to data scale, computing complexity and privacy requirements and model them as optimization problems, design approximate algorithms to integrate data types, computing tasks and system resource states, and generate an adaptive privacy computing technology combination strategy.
The protocol optimization module is used to decompose the privacy computing protocol into basic operational elements and construct a mathematical model according to the adaptive privacy computing technology combination strategy, define the multi-dimensional weights of the computation cost, communication overhead and security strength of the protocol elements, design a solution algorithm to select the minimum cost protocol element combination that satisfies the preset security threshold, and obtain the optimized privacy computing protocol framework.
The encryption/decryption module is used to perform privacy sensitivity analysis and classification on medical data based on the optimized privacy computing protocol framework, design a hybrid encryption strategy, and implement a distributed key generation, distribution, and management system to obtain a medical data encryption/decryption system.
A privacy computing execution engine is used to standardize and encapsulate various privacy computing technologies and define a unified interface based on the medical data encryption and decryption system. The execution engine is then used to achieve collaborative scheduling and execution of multiple technologies, resulting in a medical data privacy computing fusion system.

### 📜 Full Specification & Deep Scrape Text
Title
Joint motor control method, system, medium and product based on angle sensor

Abstract
Translated from Chinese
A method, system, medium, and product for controlling a joint motor based on an angle sensor are disclosed, relating to the field of general control or regulation systems. The method includes: acquiring real-time angle and temperature data from an angle sensor to generate real-time data packets; determining rapid compensation parameters for the corresponding temperature values, performing preliminary compensation on the angle values to obtain preliminary compensated angle values, and generating motor control parameters to control the joint motor operation; storing multiple consecutive real-time data packets in a compensation buffer; when the number of data packets in the compensation buffer reaches a preset threshold, extracting temperature change features and angle drift features, and calculating precise compensation parameters; performing secondary compensation on the preliminary compensated angle values based on the precise compensation parameters to obtain precise compensated angle values, and updating the motor control parameters based on the precise compensated angle values. Implementing this application can reduce the response delay caused by the compensation algorithm.

Description
Joint motor control method, system, medium and product based on angle sensor
Technical Field
The present application relates to the field of control or regulation systems in general, and more particularly to a method, system, medium and product for controlling an articulation motor based on an angle sensor.
Background
The joint motors are increasingly used in the fields of industrial automation, robotics, medical instruments and the like. The joint motors are used as core execution components of robots and automation equipment, and the control performance of the joint motors directly affects the overall performance of the equipment. Along with the development of intelligent manufacturing, the production process puts higher requirements on the control of the joint motor, so that the real-time performance of the control is ensured, and the control accuracy is ensured.
In the related art, the joint motor control system generally adopts a single process flow scheme. According to the scheme, data acquired by the angle sensor are sent to the processing unit, and a control signal is finally output through a series of fixed calculation steps including links such as signal filtering, parameter calculation, control quantity generation and the like. In practical applications, the processing unit may perform complex compensation algorithms and optimization calculations in order to improve control accuracy.
However, in actual operation, complex compensation algorithms occupy a large amount of computational resources, resulting in increased system response delay.
Disclosure of Invention
The application provides a joint motor control method, a system, a medium and a product based on an angle sensor, which are used for reducing response delay caused by a compensation algorithm.
In a first aspect, the application provides a joint motor control method based on an angle sensor, which is applied to a motor control system, and comprises the steps of collecting real-time angle data and temperature data of the angle sensor, and generating a real-time data packet containing an angle value, a temperature value and a time stamp; the method comprises the steps of inquiring a preset temperature error mapping table, determining a quick compensation parameter corresponding to a temperature value, carrying out preliminary compensation on the angle value based on the quick compensation parameter to obtain a preliminary compensation angle value, generating a motor control parameter based on the preliminary compensation angle value to control the operation of a joint motor, storing a plurality of real-time data packets collected in a plurality of continuous periods into a compensation buffer area, carrying out time sequence analysis on data of the compensation buffer area when the number of the data packets of the compensation buffer area reaches a preset number threshold, extracting to obtain a temperature change characteristic and an angle drift characteristic, calculating to obtain an accurate compensation parameter based on the temperature change characteristic and the angle drift characteristic, carrying out secondary compensation on the preliminary compensation angle value based on the accurate compensation parameter to obtain an accurate compensation angle value, and updating the motor control parameter based on the accurate compensation angle value.
In the embodiment, the motor control system performs real-time angle compensation through the rapid compensation parameters, so that the timeliness of control is ensured, meanwhile, data is accumulated in the background, time sequence analysis is performed, accurate compensation is performed after temperature and angle characteristics are extracted, balance of compensation precision and response speed is realized, the timeliness of control is ensured, and the control precision can be improved through accurate compensation in the follow-up process.
With reference to some embodiments of the first aspect, in some embodiments, after the step of calculating the accurate compensation parameter based on the temperature variation characteristic and the angle drift characteristic, the method further includes calculating a parameter deviation value of the accurate compensation parameter and the quick compensation parameter, and updating the quick compensation parameter of the temperature error mapping table corresponding to the temperature interval based on the historical compensation parameter in the compensation buffer zone when the parameter deviation value exceeds a preset deviation threshold.
In the above embodiment, the motor control system dynamically monitors the deviation between the accurate compensation parameter and the quick compensation parameter, and automatically updates the temperature error mapping table when the deviation exceeds the threshold value, so that the quick compensation parameter can be continuously optimized along with the system operation, and the accuracy of preliminary compensation is improved.
With reference to some embodiments of the first aspect, in some embodiments, after the step of secondarily compensating the preliminary compensation angle value based on the accurate compensation parameter to obtain the accurate compensation angle value and updating the motor control parameter based on the accurate compensation angle value, the method further includes calculating a real-time angle difference value between the accurate compensation angle value and the preliminary compensation angle value, and reducing the data capacity of the compensation buffer area when the real-time angle difference value is greater than the compensation adjustment threshold value.
In the embodiment, the motor control system dynamically adjusts the capacity of the compensation buffer area when the difference value is overlarge by monitoring the difference value between the accurate compensation angle value and the preliminary compensation angle value in real time, thereby not only ensuring the accuracy of compensation, but also avoiding delay of excessive historical data on system response and improving the real-time performance of the system.
With reference to some embodiments of the first aspect, in some embodiments, the step of reducing the data capacity of the compensation buffer when the real-time angle difference is greater than the compensation adjustment threshold specifically includes calculating a rate of change of the real-time angle difference when the real-time angle difference is greater than the compensation adjustment threshold, determining a target response period for the secondary compensation based on the rate of change, and adjusting the data capacity of the compensation buffer to the number of data packets in one target response period.
In the above embodiment, the motor control system dynamically adjusts the capacity of the compensation buffer area based on the change rate of the angle difference value, so that the compensation buffer area is matched with the target response period, thereby not only ensuring enough data for feature extraction, but also avoiding the calculation burden caused by redundant data and optimizing the compensation efficiency.
In combination with some embodiments of the first aspect, in some embodiments, the step of calculating to obtain the accurate compensation parameter based on the temperature variation characteristic and the angle drift characteristic specifically includes performing time sequence decomposition on the temperature variation characteristic to obtain a temperature trend component and a temperature period component, determining a contribution weight of the temperature variation to the angle drift based on a change rate of the temperature trend component, performing frequency domain analysis on the angle drift characteristic to extract a frequency characteristic and an amplitude characteristic of the angle drift, performing weighted fusion on the contribution weight, the frequency characteristic and the amplitude characteristic to obtain a compensation characteristic vector, and calculating to obtain the accurate compensation parameter based on a preset compensation model and the compensation characteristic vector.
In the embodiment, the motor control system decomposes the temperature change characteristic into the trend and the periodic component, combines the frequency domain characteristic of the angle drift, obtains the compensation characteristic vector through weighting and fusion, improves the accuracy of the compensation model, and ensures that accurate compensation is more reliable.
In combination with some embodiments of the first aspect, in some embodiments, before the step of collecting the real-time angle data and the temperature data of the angle sensor and generating the real-time data packet including the angle value, the temperature value and the timestamp, the method further includes obtaining a sampling frequency and a temperature response time of the angle sensor, calculating a sampling period of the angle data and an effective sampling interval of the temperature data, determining a timestamp granularity of the data packet according to the sampling period and the effective sampling interval, and adjusting a data storage interval of the compensation buffer based on the timestamp granularity.
In the embodiment, the motor control system determines the optimal data acquisition strategy according to the sampling characteristic of the sensor, and the reasonable time stamp granularity and the storage interval improve the efficiency and the quality of data acquisition.
With reference to some embodiments of the first aspect, in some embodiments, after the step of determining the timestamp granularity of the data packet according to the sampling period and the effective sampling interval, the method further includes time aligning the real-time data packet based on the timestamp granularity, and calculating an angle variation and a temperature variation between adjacent timestamps, marking the data packet in the corresponding time period as a critical data packet when the angle variation exceeds a preset angle threshold or the temperature variation exceeds the preset temperature threshold, integrating the critical data packet and a preset number of adjacent data packets before and after the critical data packet into a data segment, and storing the data segment into a priority storage area of the compensation buffer.
In the embodiment, the motor control system ensures that important data is processed in time by identifying the key data packet and establishing a priority storage mechanism, so that the integrity of the key data is ensured, and the processing efficiency of the system is improved.
In a second aspect, embodiments of the present application provide a motor control system comprising one or more processors and a memory coupled to the one or more processors, the memory for storing computer program code comprising computer instructions that the one or more processors invoke the computer instructions to cause the motor control system to perform a method as described in the first aspect and any of the possible implementations of the first aspect.
In a third aspect, embodiments of the present application provide a computer program product comprising instructions which, when run on a motor control system, cause the motor control system to perform a method as described in the first aspect and any one of the possible implementations of the first aspect.
In a fourth aspect, embodiments of the present application provide a computer readable storage medium comprising instructions which, when run on a motor control system, cause the motor control system to perform a method as described in the first aspect and any possible implementation of the first aspect.
It will be appreciated that the motor control system provided in the second aspect, the computer program product provided in the third aspect and the computer storage medium provided in the fourth aspect are each configured to perform the method provided by the embodiment of the present application. Therefore, the advantages achieved by the method can be referred to as the advantages of the corresponding method, and will not be described herein.
One or more technical solutions provided in the embodiments of the present application at least have the following technical effects or advantages:
1. Because a double-layer compensation mechanism is adopted and a temperature error mapping table is introduced to carry out quick compensation, and meanwhile, accurate compensation is timely realized through time sequence analysis in the background, the system can realize high-precision control while ensuring timeliness, the contradiction between compensation precision and response delay in the related technology is effectively solved, and the overall optimization of control performance is further realized.
2. Because the self-adaptive adjustment mechanism based on the real-time angle difference value is adopted, the system can automatically optimize the data processing strategy according to the actual running condition by dynamically monitoring the difference between the accurate compensation angle value and the preliminary compensation angle value and correspondingly adjusting the capacity of the compensation buffer area, the problem of response delay or precision loss caused by the fixed data buffer capacity in the related technology is effectively solved, and the dynamic optimization of the compensation performance is further realized.
3. Due to the adoption of the data acquisition optimization scheme based on the sensor characteristics, the optimal time stamp granularity and the optimal storage interval are determined by analyzing the sampling frequency and the temperature response time, so that the system can ensure the acquisition quality at a data source, the problems of data redundancy and processing delay caused by blind acquisition in the related technology are effectively solved, and further the data acquisition and processing efficiency is improved.
