Detailed Description
The terminology used in the following embodiments of the application is for the purpose of describing particular embodiments only and is not intended to be limiting of the application. As used in the specification of the present application, the singular forms "a", "an", "the" and "the" are intended to include the plural forms as well, unless the context clearly indicates to the contrary. It should also be understood that the term "and/or" as used in this disclosure is intended to encompass any or all possible combinations of one or more of the listed items.
The terms "first," "second," and the like, are used below for descriptive purposes only and are not to be construed as implying or implying relative importance or implicitly indicating the number of technical features indicated. Thus, a feature defining "a first" or "a second" may explicitly or implicitly include one or more such feature, and in the description of embodiments of the application, unless otherwise indicated, the meaning of "a plurality" is two or more.
In order to facilitate understanding, an application scenario of the embodiment of the present application is described below.
On some industrial robot production line, the cooperative robot needs to perform a high-precision assembly task. The angle sensor of the robot joint motor is severely affected by the ambient temperature, and especially after 8 hours of continuous operation, the workshop temperature rises from 20 ℃ in the morning to 35 ℃ in the afternoon, resulting in significant drift of the angle measurement. For example, when a glass panel of a mobile phone is assembled, the originally set assembly accuracy of 0.1mm is difficult to maintain, and quality problems such as missing and dislocation occur. The traditional periodic calibration method needs to be stopped and adjusted, and seriously affects the production efficiency.
In the related art, the compensation of the temperature drift of the angle sensor can be achieved by adopting a fixed calibration table method and a simple linear compensation strategy. However, this method requires a lot of off-line calibration work and cannot accommodate the change of sensor characteristics with time, and the compensation effect is poor when the temperature is rapidly changed. A scenario using the related art angle sensor-based joint motor control method will be described.
A factory adopts a table look-up compensation method to process the angle error caused by temperature. And (3) calibrating different temperature points by engineers during installation, establishing a temperature-error corresponding table, and acquiring a compensation value according to a current temperature table during operation. However, in the case of frequent start-up and shut-down of the air conditioning system in summer, the temperature fluctuates rapidly (3 ℃ change in 5 minutes), whereas the temperature interval of the calibration table is 5 ℃, resulting in a compensation discontinuity. Meanwhile, due to aging of the sensor, the original calibration data gradually fail, and the compensation accuracy is obviously reduced after three months. When the temperature change is faster, the actual temperature and the measured temperature have delay due to the thermal inertia of the sensor, so that the compensation parameter is delayed, and the control effect is influenced.
By adopting the joint motor control method based on the angle sensor, the accurate compensation of angle measurement is realized through the real-time data acquisition and the double-layer compensation mechanism, the temperature change can be responded quickly, the compensation effect can be continuously optimized through the historical data analysis, and the problems of low compensation precision and poor adaptability of the traditional method are effectively solved. A scenario using the joint motor control method based on the angle sensor in the present application will be described below.
The self-adaptive compensation method of the scheme is applied by a certain precision instrument manufacturer, and a remarkable effect is achieved on the optical lens assembly robot. The system collects angle and temperature data in real time, ensures basic accuracy through quick compensation, and simultaneously accumulates historical data for deep analysis. When the rapid temperature rise (2 ℃ per minute) is detected, the system predicts the temperature change trend and adjusts the compensation parameters in advance. By analyzing the temperature change characteristics and the angle drift characteristics, the system can accurately model the temperature influence and realize accurate compensation. Even under the condition of severe temperature fluctuation, the assembly precision can still be kept within the range of +/-0.02 mm, and the product yield is improved.
Therefore, by adopting the joint motor control method based on the angle sensor, the problem of angle drift caused by dynamic temperature change can be effectively solved while quick compensation is realized, and further motor control with high precision and high reliability is realized.
For ease of understanding, the method provided in this embodiment is described in the following in conjunction with the above scenario. Fig. 1 is a schematic flow chart of a joint motor control method based on an angle sensor according to an embodiment of the application.
S101, acquiring real-time angle data and temperature data of an angle sensor, and generating a real-time data packet containing an angle value, a temperature value and a time stamp.
The angle sensor is used for detecting the rotation angle of the joint motor and comprises a Hall sensor, an encoder and the like, real-time angle data are angle position information measured by the angle sensor at each sampling time, temperature data are temperature values of the working environment of the sensor and can come from an integrated or external temperature sensor, a time stamp is used for marking the accurate time of data acquisition, and a real-time data packet is a data structure formed by packaging the acquired angle values, the temperature values and corresponding time stamps.
After the motor control system starts to run, the motion state and the working environment information of the joint motor need to be continuously acquired so as to realize accurate control. Specifically, the motor control system first determines the sampling frequency (e.g., 1000 Hz) of the angle sensor and then periodically collects angle data at that frequency, while collecting temperature data at a relatively low frequency (e.g., 100 Hz) because of the relatively slow temperature change. For each group of collected data, the motor control system can generate a time stamp with microsecond precision according to a system clock, and the three data are organized into a unified data packet format, so that the subsequent processing and analysis are convenient.
In some embodiments, the data acquisition and packaging process can be realized in various modes, wherein the motor control system can adopt an interrupt mode to acquire data, set two timing interrupts with different priorities, take charge of angle acquisition for high-priority interrupts and take charge of temperature acquisition for low-priority interrupts, acquire data and transmit the data to a system memory in a DMA mode, and then generate a time stamp by a processor and package the data, and the motor control system can also adopt a polling mode to read the data by checking a data ready mark in a main cycle and package the data after the reading is finished. It will be appreciated that other data acquisition methods, such as data preprocessing using FPGA, may be used, and are not limited herein.
In practical application, a problem of asynchronous acquisition of sensor data, namely deviation of sampling moments of angle data and temperature data, may be encountered. In this regard, the motor control system employs a data alignment algorithm that first determines an effective time window (e.g., + -5 ms) for each temperature data, and then time-weighted averages the angle data within the window to generate an angle value corresponding to the temperature data time. For example, when the temperature sampling time is t, angle data in a [ t-5ms, t+5ms ] time window is selected, the data weight is larger when the temperature sampling time is closer to t, and the corresponding angle value is obtained through weighted average. This approach both ensures the time consistency of the data and avoids errors that may be caused by simple interpolation.
S102, inquiring a preset temperature error mapping table, and determining a quick compensation parameter of a corresponding temperature value.
The temperature error mapping table is used for storing compensation parameters corresponding to different temperature intervals, the fast compensation parameters are correction values for real-time angle compensation, including but not limited to offset, scale factors and the like, the temperature interval is a discretized temperature range and is used for mapping continuous temperature values to a limited compensation parameter set, and the corresponding relation is a mapping function between the temperature interval and the compensation parameters.
After acquiring the real-time temperature data, the motor control system needs to quickly determine corresponding compensation parameters to correct in real time. Specifically, the motor control system maps the measured temperature value to a predefined temperature interval, such as mapping 23.7 ℃ to a [20 ℃ and 25 ℃ interval, searches a compensation parameter set corresponding to the temperature interval, including zero offset, sensitivity correction coefficient and the like, and calculates more accurate compensation parameters through linear interpolation if the measured temperature value is near the boundary of the two temperature intervals so as to avoid control jitter caused by parameter mutation.
In some embodiments, the temperature error mapping can be realized in various ways, alternatively, the motor control system can adopt a lookup table mode to uniformly divide the temperature range into a plurality of intervals (such as one interval at every 5 ℃), each interval stores a set of calibrated compensation parameters, a target interval is quickly positioned through binary search during query and then linear interpolation is carried out to obtain an accurate compensation value, alternatively, the motor control system can also adopt a polynomial fitting mode to fit a functional relation between the temperature and the compensation parameters by utilizing a plurality of groups of temperature-error sample points, and the compensation parameters are directly substituted into the temperature values to calculate the compensation parameters during query. It will be appreciated that other mapping methods, such as neural network models, may also be employed, and are not limited herein.
In practical applications, problems may be encountered in which rapid changes in temperature lead to a compensating parameter tracking lag. In this regard, the motor control system adopts a temperature prediction compensation algorithm, namely, a temperature value at the next moment is predicted by calculating the temperature change rate and the acceleration, and corresponding compensation parameters are queried in advance. In specific implementation, a second-order polynomial fitting is performed by using the latest N temperature sampling points, a temperature change trend function is obtained, the temperature change within 100ms in the forward direction is predicted, and compensation parameters which can be used are prepared in advance. This predictive mechanism can effectively reduce the compensation lag when the temperature changes drastically.
S103, performing preliminary compensation on the angle value based on the quick compensation parameter to obtain a preliminary compensation angle value, and generating a motor control parameter based on the preliminary compensation angle value to control the operation of the joint motor.
The preliminary compensation refers to real-time correction of an original angle value by using a quick compensation parameter, the preliminary compensation angle value represents angle data subjected to temperature compensation, the motor control parameter refers to control quantity used for driving a joint motor, the control quantity comprises but is not limited to current, voltage, PWM duty ratio and the like, and the running state of the joint motor comprises dynamic characteristics such as position, speed and acceleration.
The motor control system needs to complete angle compensation and control parameter generation in each control period. Specifically, the motor control system firstly applies a quick compensation parameter to a real-time angle value, compensation calculation comprises three links of zero point correction, sensitivity correction and nonlinear correction, then compares the compensated angle value with a target angle, calculates a required control quantity through a PID control algorithm, and finally converts the control quantity into a specific motor driving parameter, such as a current instruction value or PWM waveform parameter, and outputs the specific motor driving parameter to a motor driving circuit. The whole process needs to be completed within one control period (usually 1 ms) to ensure the real-time performance of the control.
In some embodiments, the angle compensation and control parameter generation can be realized in various modes, alternatively, the motor control system can adopt a piecewise linear compensation method to divide the angle range into a plurality of intervals, each interval uses different compensation coefficients, compensation calculation is rapidly completed through table lookup and linear interpolation, and then the incremental PID algorithm is used for generating the control quantity, alternatively, the motor control system can also adopt a neural network model, takes temperature, angle and the like as input, directly outputs the compensated angle value and control parameter, and realizes end-to-end control. It will be appreciated that other control strategies may be employed, such as model predictive control, and the like, and are not limited in this regard.
In practical applications, a problem may be encountered in that the load mutation causes mismatch of control parameters. In this regard, the motor control system employs an adaptive control gain adjustment algorithm to dynamically adjust PID parameters by monitoring motor response characteristics (e.g., tracking error, overshoot, oscillation frequency, etc.) in real time. For example, when a large tracking error is detected, the proportional gain is appropriately increased to increase the response speed, and when an oscillation occurs, the differential gain is increased to provide damping. In specific implementation, a mapping relation between error characteristics and control parameters is established, and the control parameters are updated in real time according to a preset regulation rule.
S104, storing a plurality of real-time data packets acquired in a plurality of continuous periods into the compensation buffer area.
The compensation buffer area represents a circulation buffer data structure for temporarily storing historical data packets, a plurality of continuous periods refer to a continuous time window, usually hundreds of milliseconds to seconds, data packet storage comprises data writing, buffer management, data elimination and other operations, and the size of the buffer area represents the number of data packets which can be stored and needs to be reasonably set according to system resources and analysis requirements.
The motor control system, while performing the fast compensation, needs to accumulate enough historical data for subsequent accurate compensation calculations. Specifically, the motor control system writes the data packets acquired in each control period into the compensation buffer area according to time sequence, eliminates earliest data by adopting a first-in first-out strategy when the buffer area is full, maintains the time index of the data packets, facilitates quick access to data in a specific time period, and also needs to periodically check the continuity of the data to ensure that no data is lost or repeated.
In some embodiments, data buffer management can be achieved in various ways, wherein the motor control system can adopt a double-buffer mechanism, two buffer areas with equal size are arranged, one buffer area is used for data writing, the other buffer area is used for data analysis, exchange is performed when the writing buffer area is full, data writing and analysis are guaranteed not to interfere with each other, the motor control system can adopt a multi-level buffer structure, the first-level buffer can store high-frequency sampled original data, and the second-level buffer can store downsampled data for long-time feature analysis. It will be appreciated that other caching strategies may be employed, such as distributed storage, and the like, without limitation.
In practical applications, problems may be encountered in that the amount of data is excessive, resulting in increased storage and processing pressures. In this regard, the motor control system employs an adaptive data compression algorithm that dynamically adjusts the storage strategy based on the characteristics of the data changes. When the data change slowly, the sampling interval is increased or the data compression is carried out, and when the data change rapidly, the high-frequency sampling is kept and the data is stored completely. For example, the storage interval can be automatically adjusted according to the change rate for the temperature data, and the temperature data is stored every 10ms when the change is severe, and can be stored once when the change is slow and is prolonged to 100 ms. The self-adaptive storage strategy not only ensures the integrity of key data, but also optimizes the use efficiency of the storage space.
S105, when the number of the data packets in the compensation buffer area reaches a preset number threshold, performing time sequence analysis on the data in the compensation buffer area, and extracting to obtain a temperature change characteristic and an angle drift characteristic.
The preset quantity threshold value represents the minimum data packet quantity required for triggering data analysis, which is usually hundreds to thousands of samples, the time sequence analysis refers to statistics and feature extraction of data arranged in time sequence, the temperature change features comprise characteristics of change trend, periodic fluctuation, abrupt change points and the like, and the angle drift features refer to systematic deviation of angle measurement values caused by temperature change, including zero drift, gain change and the like.
The motor control system needs to analyze the effect of temperature changes on the angular measurements in depth based on the accumulated historical data. The motor control system firstly checks the number of data packets in a compensation buffer zone, starts analysis processing after the number reaches a threshold value, then carries out trend decomposition on a temperature data sequence to separate long-term trend, periodic fluctuation and random disturbance, simultaneously carries out baseline drift analysis on angle data to identify systematic deviation related to temperature, and finally carries out association analysis on temperature change characteristics and angle drift characteristics to establish a mapping relation between the temperature change characteristics and the angle drift characteristics.
In some embodiments, the time series analysis can be realized in various modes, wherein the motor control system can adopt a wavelet transformation method to carry out multi-scale decomposition on temperature and angle data, respectively extract the change characteristics on different time scales and then obtain a main change mode through reconstruction, and can also adopt an autoregressive moving average model to establish a time series model of data, and the change characteristics of the data are reflected through model parameters. It will be appreciated that other analysis methods, such as deep learning timing models, may also be employed, and are not limited in this regard.
S106, calculating to obtain accurate compensation parameters based on the temperature change characteristics and the angle drift characteristics.
The accurate compensation parameter represents a high-precision compensation value obtained through deep analysis and comprises static compensation and dynamic compensation components, the feature fusion refers to comprehensive consideration of multidimensional features of temperature change and angle drift, the calculation process comprises the steps of feature normalization, weight distribution, parameter optimization and the like, and the compensation precision is generally required to be superior to that of a quick compensation parameter.
The motor control system needs to calculate more accurate compensation parameters based on the extracted features. The motor control system comprises a motor control system, a temperature change feature analysis system, a temperature-angle response model, a multi-feature fusion algorithm, a compensation parameter optimization system and a cross-validation system.
In some embodiments, the calculation of the accurate compensation parameters can be achieved in various ways, alternatively, the motor control system can use a recursive least square method to update parameters of a temperature-angle response model in real time, the model comprises a linear term and a nonlinear term, the parameters are optimized by minimizing a prediction error, alternatively, the motor control system can also use a parameter estimation method based on Kalman filtering, the compensation parameters are used as state variables, and parameter estimation is continuously corrected through observation values of temperature and angle. It will be appreciated that other parameter optimization methods, such as genetic algorithms, may also be employed, and are not limited in this regard.
In practical applications, a problem of slow convergence speed of the compensation parameter calculation may be encountered. In this regard, the motor control system employs an adaptive learning rate strategy to dynamically adjust the optimization step size based on the variation in parameter estimation error. When the error is larger, the parameter is quickly adjusted by using larger learning rate, and when the error is smaller, the learning rate is reduced to improve the stability. In concrete implementation, a learning rate adjusting function based on error gradient is designed, and a dynamic term is introduced to accelerate convergence. The self-adaptive optimization strategy ensures the speed of parameter convergence and avoids parameter oscillation.
And S107, performing secondary compensation on the primary compensation angle value based on the accurate compensation parameter to obtain the accurate compensation angle value, and updating the motor control parameter based on the accurate compensation angle value.
The secondary compensation represents further correction based on the primary compensation, the accurate compensation angle value refers to a final angle value obtained after the secondary compensation, the control parameter updating comprises real-time parameter adjustment and control strategy optimization, and the updating process needs to ensure the control stability and continuity.
The motor control system needs to smoothly apply the accurate compensation parameters to the control process. Specifically, the motor control system firstly compares the accurate compensation parameter with the currently used rapid compensation parameter to calculate the parameter difference, then designs a gradual transition strategy to smoothly transition the compensation parameter from the current value to the target value, then recalculates the angle value based on the new compensation parameter and correspondingly adjusts the motor control parameter, and finally monitors the control effect to ensure that the control instability is not caused by the update of the compensation parameter.
In some embodiments, the smooth updating of the compensation parameters can be achieved in various ways, wherein the motor control system can adopt an exponential sliding average method to gradually replace the old parameters with the new compensation parameters, the smooth coefficient can be dynamically adjusted according to the difference of the parameters, the motor control system can also adopt a predictive control strategy, control quantity changes possibly caused by parameter updating are calculated in advance, and an optimal transition track is designed. It will be appreciated that other update strategies, such as fuzzy control, may also be employed, and are not limited in this regard.
In practical applications, problems may be encountered in that the compensation parameter update causes control jitter. In this regard, the motor control system employs a hierarchical smoothing strategy that employs different update rates for the compensation parameters of the different frequency components. For the low-frequency compensation component, a larger smoothing time constant is used to ensure stable updating, and for the high-frequency compensation component, a smaller smoothing time constant is used to ensure quick response. For example, the compensation parameters are decomposed into two parts, baseline drift compensation, which uses smoothing time on the order of 10 seconds, and dynamic fluctuation compensation, which uses smoothing time on the order of 100 milliseconds. This layering strategy both ensures control stability and maintains responsiveness to rapid changes.
The method provided in this embodiment will be described in more detail. Fig. 2 is a schematic flow chart of a joint motor control method based on an angle sensor according to an embodiment of the application.
S201, acquiring the sampling frequency and the temperature response time of the angle sensor, and calculating the sampling period of the angle data and the effective sampling interval of the temperature data.
The sampling frequency represents the data acquisition times of the angle sensor in unit time, usually in hertz (Hz), the temperature response time is the time required by the temperature sensor from detecting the temperature change to outputting stability and is used for representing the dynamic characteristic of the sensor, the sampling period represents the time interval of two adjacent angle data acquisition and is equal to the reciprocal of the sampling frequency, the effective sampling interval is the temperature data acquisition interval determined by considering the temperature response time and is required to be greater than the temperature response time to ensure the data reliability, and the data acquisition precision represents the quantization resolution of the sensor.
The motor control system needs to determine the basic parameters of data acquisition in the initialization stage. Specifically, the motor control system firstly reads the specification parameters of the angle sensor, acquires the maximum sampling frequency (such as 2000 Hz) and the data bit number (such as12 bits), then tests the step response characteristic of the temperature sensor, records the time from the step change of input to the steady state of output (such as 50 ms), then sets the actually used angle sampling frequency (such as 1000 Hz) according to the control requirement and the hardware capability, calculates the sampling period (1 ms), and finally determines the effective sampling interval (such as 100 ms) of the temperature data based on the temperature response time, wherein the interval needs to ensure that enough time exists between two adjacent temperature samples to enable the sensor to reach the steady state.
In some embodiments, the determination of the sampling parameters may be achieved in a number of ways, alternatively, the motor control system may determine the optimal sampling parameters by an adaptive sampling mechanism, first run the system at a low sampling rate and record the control performance index, then step up the sampling rate until the performance improvement is not apparent, finally set the sampling rate at the inflection point location, determine the temperature sampling interval by analyzing the rise time and the settling time of the temperature response curve, alternatively, the motor control system may also employ a sampling strategy based on the signal bandwidth, determine the minimum required sampling rate according to the nyquist sampling theorem by measuring the spectral characteristics of the angle signal and the temperature signal, and leave sufficient margin, and the temperature sampling interval is determined based on the highest frequency component of the temperature signal. It will be appreciated that other parameter determination means may be employed, such as automatic parameter adjustment based on control performance optimization, etc., and are not limited herein.
In practical applications, a problem may be encountered in that the temperature response time changes dynamically due to severe fluctuations in the ambient temperature. In this regard, the motor control system employs an adaptive response time estimation algorithm that dynamically adjusts the sampling parameters by monitoring the varying characteristics of the temperature signal in real time. In specific implementation, a sliding time window is used to calculate the rising time and the stabilizing time of the temperature signal, and a temperature-response time mapping model is constructed. When a severe temperature change is detected, the sampling interval is appropriately increased to ensure data reliability, and when a gentle temperature change is detected, the sampling interval may be appropriately decreased to increase the data update frequency. For example, a sampling interval of 100ms is used at standard operating temperatures, but is increased to 200ms when the temperature changes rapidly (rate of change exceeds 1 ℃ per second) to ensure that the temperature data for each sample is stable and reliable.
S202, determining the time stamp granularity of the data packet according to the sampling period and the effective sampling interval.
The time stamp granularity represents the minimum resolution unit of a time stamp in a data packet and is used for quantifying the accuracy of time information, the sampling period refers to the time interval of angle data acquisition and determines the minimum requirement of the time stamp, the effective sampling interval represents the acquisition period of temperature data and influences the storage efficiency of the time stamp, the quantization error refers to the approximate error generated when continuous time is converted into discrete time stamp, and the time synchronization accuracy represents the time alignment degree among different data sources.
The motor control system needs to set the appropriate time stamp format after determining the sampling parameters. Specifically, the motor control system firstly analyzes numerical characteristics of an angle sampling period (such as1 ms) and a temperature sampling interval (such as 100 ms) to determine a numerical range of time data, then selects a proper time representation format in consideration of resolution (such as 0.1 mu s) and storage space limitation of a system clock, then designs bit field distribution of a time stamp, including seconds, milliseconds and microseconds, to ensure that all sampling moments can be accurately expressed, and finally verifies whether the representation range of the time stamp meets the longest operation time requirement of the system.
In some embodiments, the determination of the granularity of the time stamp can be achieved in various ways, alternatively, the motor control system can adopt a dynamic time stamp strategy, a high-precision time stamp (microsecond level) is used for diagonal data, complete time information is recorded, a relative time stamp is used for temperature data, only a time difference relative to a reference time is recorded, storage space is reduced through differential encoding, finally a time stamp decoding algorithm is designed, complete time information is restored during data processing, alternatively, the motor control system can also adopt a hierarchical time stamp structure, a basic time layer and an offset time layer structure are designed, the basic layer records a longer time scale (such as a second level), the offset layer records a fine time scale (such as a microsecond level), and the complete time stamp is obtained through combining the two layers of information. It will be appreciated that other timestamp designs may be employed, such as event-triggered adaptive timestamps and the like, and are not limited in this regard.
In practical applications, the problem of time stamp deviation caused by time dyssynchrony of multiple sensors may be encountered. In this regard, the motor control system employs a time synchronization compensation algorithm that establishes a system level time reference to calibrate the time of all data sources. In specific implementation, a uniform time reference is provided through a high-precision timer, and then the time delay characteristics of each sensor are measured to establish a delay compensation model. For example, when the temperature sensor is found to have an inherent delay of 5ms, this delay value is automatically compensated for when the timestamp is generated. In addition, the system periodically performs time synchronization calibration to ensure time consistency during long-term operation by sending synchronization signal measurements and updating delay compensation values.
In some embodiments, the motor control system performs critical data integration to avoid frequent compensation, that is, the motor control system performs time alignment on real-time data packets based on the granularity of time stamps and calculates an angle variation and a temperature variation between adjacent time stamps, marks the data packets in the corresponding time period as critical data packets when the angle variation exceeds a preset angle threshold or the temperature variation exceeds a preset temperature threshold, integrates the critical data packets and a preset number of adjacent data packets before and after the critical data packets into data fragments, and stores the data fragments in a priority storage area of the compensation buffer.
The time alignment represents a processing process of unifying and standardizing different data packets according to time stamps, the angle change quantity refers to the difference of angle values at adjacent time, the temperature change quantity represents the change amplitude of the temperature values at adjacent time, the key data packet refers to a data record containing important state change information, the data fragment represents a section of continuous data sequence taking the key data packet as a center, and the priority storage area refers to a specific space for storing important data in the compensation buffer area.
The motor control system needs to identify and save data that has an important impact on the compensation calculations. The motor control system firstly performs time standardization processing on all data packets according to the granularity of the time stamp to ensure the time sequence consistency of the data, then calculates the angle difference value and the temperature difference value between each pair of adjacent data packets, compares the angle difference value and the temperature difference value with a preset change threshold (such as 0.5 degree of the angle threshold and 1 ℃ of the temperature threshold), marks the data packets exceeding the threshold as key data packets, and extends the data packets with preset numbers (such as 50 data packets before and after) respectively around the data packets as the center to form complete data fragments, and finally writes the data fragments into a priority storage area of a compensation buffer area to ensure that the important data are preferentially reserved when the storage space is insufficient.
In some embodiments, the identification and storage of key data can be realized in various ways, wherein the motor control system can adopt a multi-level change detection strategy, firstly calculate statistical characteristics in a sliding window at a macroscopic level, identify time intervals possibly containing important changes, then accurately position change points at a microscopic level, determine the specific range of key data packets, finally prioritize data fragments according to the importance of the changes, guide storage management, and can also adopt a mode identification method, automatically identify the data fragments containing typical change modes through a pre-trained classifier, and realize intelligent data screening. It will be appreciated that other data identification methods may be employed, such as, but not limited to, importance assessment based on information entropy, and the like.
In practical applications, the problem of important information loss caused by inaccurate identification of key data may be encountered. In this regard, the motor control system employs an adaptive threshold adjustment strategy that adjusts the decision criteria by dynamically evaluating the system state. The method comprises the steps of firstly establishing a normal change baseline distribution based on historical data statistics, then calculating the deviation degree of the current change quantity relative to the baseline, and finally dynamically adjusting a judgment threshold according to the deviation degree. For example, a larger decision threshold (e.g., 3 times the baseline standard deviation) is used to avoid over-marking when the system is operating steadily, and a threshold (e.g., 2 times the baseline standard deviation) is lowered to increase sensitivity when the system enters the dynamic adjustment phase. Meanwhile, the system can also periodically evaluate the distribution characteristics of the key data, and if the density of the key data is abnormal (for example, exceeds 30%) in certain time periods, the threshold optimization flow is automatically triggered, and more reasonable judgment standards are recalculated. This adaptive mechanism ensures the accuracy and integrity of critical data identification.
S203, adjusting the data storage interval of the compensation buffer area based on the granularity of the time stamp.
The compensation buffer area represents a memory space structure for storing historical data and comprises a data storage, management and access mechanism, wherein a data storage interval refers to a time interval of adjacent data packets in the buffer area, a storage density refers to the number of the data packets stored in unit time, a buffer strategy refers to a storage, reading and eliminating rule of the data, and data alignment refers to a matching relation of different types of data in a time dimension.
The motor control system needs to optimize the data storage structure according to the determined timestamp granularity. Specifically, the motor control system firstly calculates the minimum storage interval corresponding to the granularity of the time stamp (such as 1 ms), then designs a multi-level storage structure comprising a high-frequency data area (for storing original angle data), a medium-frequency data area (for storing integrated data after downsampling) and a low-frequency data area (for storing statistical characteristic data) according to the memory capacity and the data analysis requirement, then establishes a data downsampling and aggregation rule, uses different time intervals in different storage areas, and finally realizes an automatic hierarchical storage and management mechanism of the data packet to ensure the complete storage of key data.
In some embodiments, the adjustment of the storage interval can be realized in various ways, alternatively, the motor control system can adopt a self-adaptive storage strategy, firstly analyze the data change characteristics, calculate the information entropy under different time scales, then design a variable sampling rate storage scheme based on the information entropy, improve the storage density when the data change is severe, reduce the storage density when the data change is stable, finally dynamically evaluate the storage effect through a sliding window, and timely adjust the storage parameter. It will be appreciated that other storage optimization approaches may be employed, such as dynamic storage based on importance sampling, etc., and are not limited in this regard.
S204, acquiring real-time angle data and temperature data of the angle sensor, and generating a real-time data packet containing the angle value, the temperature value and the time stamp.
Referring to step S101, the motor control system generates a real-time data packet.
S205, inquiring a preset temperature error mapping table, and determining a quick compensation parameter of a corresponding temperature value.
Referring to step S102, the motor control system determines a fast compensation parameter.
S206, performing preliminary compensation on the angle value based on the quick compensation parameter to obtain a preliminary compensation angle value, and generating a motor control parameter based on the preliminary compensation angle value to control the operation of the joint motor.
Referring to step S103, the motor control system performs preliminary compensation.
S207, storing a plurality of real-time data packets acquired in a plurality of continuous periods into a compensation buffer area.
Referring to step S104, the motor control system collects a plurality of real-time data packets and stores the data packets in the compensation buffer.
And S208, when the number of the data packets in the compensation buffer area reaches a preset number threshold, performing time sequence analysis on the data in the compensation buffer area, and extracting to obtain a temperature change characteristic and an angle drift characteristic.
Referring to step S105, the motor control system extracts a temperature change characteristic and an angle drift characteristic.
S209, calculating to obtain accurate compensation parameters based on the temperature change characteristics and the angle drift characteristics.
Referring to step S106, the motor control system calculates accurate compensation parameters.
In some embodiments, the motor control system may perform quick compensation update in time, that is, the motor control system calculates parameter deviation values of the accurate compensation parameter and the quick compensation parameter, and updates the quick compensation parameter of the corresponding temperature interval in the temperature error mapping table based on the historical compensation parameter in the compensation buffer when the parameter deviation value exceeds a preset deviation threshold.
The parameter deviation value represents the numerical value difference between an accurate compensation parameter and a quick compensation parameter, the preset deviation threshold value refers to a judgment standard for triggering the updating of a mapping table, the history compensation parameter refers to past compensation data stored in a compensation buffer area, the temperature interval represents a discretized temperature range in a temperature error mapping table, the updating strategy refers to a modification rule and an updating mode of the mapping table parameter, and the quick compensation parameter comprises compensation quantities such as a zero point correction value, a sensitivity correction coefficient and the like.
The motor control system needs to dynamically optimize the temperature compensation strategy based on the real-time operating effect. The motor control system firstly calculates vector differences between accurate compensation parameters and quick compensation parameters in each control period to obtain deviation vectors in a multidimensional parameter space, then calculates weighted norms of the deviation vectors, compares the weighted norms with a preset updating threshold (such as 5% of a nominal value), extracts latest N groups (such as N=100) of historical compensation data from a compensation buffer memory area when the deviation continuously exceeds the threshold, performs statistical analysis and feature extraction, then updates the quick compensation parameters of corresponding temperature intervals by adopting a recursive least square method based on the extracted features, and finally ensures the continuity of parameters of adjacent temperature intervals through a smooth transition function.
In some embodiments, dynamic updating of the mapping table can be achieved in various ways, alternatively, the motor control system can adopt an adaptive learning strategy, firstly, a time sequence model of parameter deviation is established, trend characteristics and period characteristics of the deviation are analyzed, then learning rate and updating period of parameter updating are designed based on characteristic analysis results, finally, rapid compensation parameters are optimized through a gradient descent method to gradually approach the precise compensation parameters, alternatively, the motor control system can also adopt a hierarchical optimization method to decompose the compensation parameters into a basic compensation layer and a fine adjustment compensation layer, and when the parameter deviation is detected, the parameters of the fine adjustment layer are updated preferentially, so that the rapidity and stability of system response are ensured. It will be appreciated that other optimization methods may be employed, such as reinforcement learning based parameter tuning, and the like, and are not limited in this regard.
In practical applications, a problem of system oscillation caused by parameter update may be encountered. For this, the motor control system employs a progressive parameter update strategy that ensures the reliability of the update process through multi-stage verification. The protection mechanism for parameter updating is realized by firstly calculating the maximum allowable step length of parameter updating, determining a safety boundary based on system stability analysis, then decomposing the updating quantity into a plurality of small step lengths for progressive adjustment, observing the system response after each adjustment, and immediately backing to the last stable state if control error sudden increase (such as 2 times of a normal value) or output oscillation (such as frequency component mutation) is detected. For example, when the compensation parameter of a certain temperature interval needs to be adjusted by 10%, the system can uniformly divide the adjustment amount into 5 times for execution, adjust 2% each time, monitor the system performance of at least 100 control cycles after each adjustment, and ensure the stability of the adjustment process.
In some embodiments, the motor control system performs accurate compensation based on a preset compensation model, that is, the motor control system performs time sequence decomposition on the temperature change feature to obtain a temperature trend component and a temperature period component, determines a contribution weight of the angular drift based on the change rate of the temperature trend component, performs frequency domain analysis on the angular drift feature to extract the frequency feature and the amplitude feature of the angular drift, performs weighted fusion on the contribution weight, the frequency feature and the amplitude feature to obtain a compensation feature vector, and calculates accurate compensation parameters based on the preset compensation model and the compensation feature vector.
The time sequence decomposition shows a mathematical treatment process of separating a temperature change signal into different characteristic components, the temperature trend component shows a long-term change trend of temperature change, the temperature period component shows a periodic fluctuation characteristic of the temperature change, the contribution weight shows a quantization index of the influence degree of the temperature change on the angle drift, the frequency domain analysis shows a mathematical method of researching the angle drift characteristic in a frequency domain, the compensation characteristic vector shows a multidimensional characteristic quantity used for calculating an accurate compensation parameter, and the compensation model shows a mapping relation of the characteristic vector to the compensation parameter.
The motor control system needs to analyze in depth the correlation characteristics between the temperature change and the angular drift. The motor control system firstly carries out empirical mode decomposition on temperature data, separates the temperature data into a plurality of eigenvalue functions reflecting different time scale characteristics, then obtains a long-term change trend of the temperature through a trend extraction algorithm, calculates a first derivative of the trend as a change rate index, then carries out frequency spectrum analysis on the angle drift data by utilizing fast Fourier transform, extracts amplitude and phase information of main frequency components, then designs a self-adaptive weight function based on the temperature change rate, quantifies the influence degree of the temperature change on each frequency component, finally combines all the characteristics into characteristic vectors, and inputs a pre-trained compensation model to calculate accurate compensation parameters.
The preset compensation model is trained by collecting a large number of temperature-angle sample pairs, multidimensional feature vectors comprising temperature trend components, temperature period components, frequency features of angle drift, amplitude features and the like are input, the multidimensional feature vectors are output as a compensation parameter set, and model parameters are optimized by a least square method, so that the mean square error between a predicted compensation value and an actually required compensation value is minimized. The temperature change prediction model uses a temperature sequence in a sliding time window as training data, constructs an LSTM neural network structure, outputs a temperature prediction value in 100ms in the future, and minimizes a prediction error through a back propagation algorithm. The response time prediction model is trained based on historical compensation process data, the characteristics including angle difference values, change rates and the like are input, the shortest time required for achieving target accuracy is output, and cross verification optimization model generalization performance is adopted. The data importance assessment model is trained by using expert-labeled key data samples, is input into statistical features of data fragments, is output into importance scores, and balances the recognition accuracy of different types of data through a weighted loss function.
The preset compensation model adopts a multi-layer perceptron structure and comprises three functional modules of feature extraction, nonlinear mapping and parameter prediction. The temperature change prediction model uses a gating cycle unit to process the time sequence characteristics and introduces a attention mechanism to highlight the effect of key time points. The response time prediction model combines a convolutional neural network and a cyclic neural network to capture local and global features of angle changes. The data importance assessment model adopts a gradient lifting tree structure, and classification accuracy is improved through feature combination. All models contained a regularization layer to prevent overfitting and batch normalization was used to improve training stability. In real-time operation, a preset compensation model receives the latest feature vector in each control period, compensation parameters are calculated quickly, a temperature change prediction model predicts a temperature change trend based on the latest N temperature sampling points and is used for adjusting a compensation strategy in advance, a response time prediction model dynamically adjusts the capacity of a buffer area according to the change characteristics of angle difference values and optimizes the response speed of a system, a data importance assessment model analyzes data flow in real time, marks key data segments and guides storage management. The prediction results of the models are comprehensively decided in a weighted fusion mode, so that the accuracy and reliability of compensation control are ensured. The system can also evaluate the performance of the model periodically, trigger on-line fine tuning or off-line retraining if necessary, and maintain the prediction accuracy of the model.
In practical application, the problem of insufficient real-time performance caused by large calculation amount in the feature extraction process may be encountered. For this, the motor control system adopts a hierarchical computing strategy, optimizing computing resource allocation through feature importance evaluation. In specific implementation, a three-level feature extraction framework is constructed, wherein a first level rapidly extracts basic features by using a simplified algorithm, a second level calculates complete features on a longer time scale, and a third level performs fine analysis on key events. For example, in a normal working state, the system mainly compensates by means of temperature trend and first-order angle characteristics, the calculation load is small, and when the temperature violent change (the change rate exceeds 2 ℃ per minute) or the angle drift abnormality (the drift rate exceeds 0.5 ℃ per minute) is detected, the complete characteristic extraction flow is activated, and the calculation intensive operations such as wavelet analysis, spectrum analysis and the like are included. The hierarchical computing mechanism ensures the accuracy of feature extraction and obviously improves the real-time response capability of the system.
And S210, performing secondary compensation on the primary compensation angle value based on the accurate compensation parameter to obtain the accurate compensation angle value, and updating the motor control parameter based on the accurate compensation angle value.
Referring to step S107, the motor control system performs accurate compensation.
S211, calculating a real-time angle difference value between the accurate compensation angle value and the preliminary compensation angle value.
The real-time angle difference value represents the numerical deviation between two levels of compensation results, the calculation period refers to the time interval for calculating the difference value, the difference value statistical characteristics comprise statistics such as mean value, standard deviation and extremum, the difference value trend represents the change rule of the angle deviation along with time, and the threshold value judgment condition refers to the difference value standard for triggering the system response.
The motor control system needs to monitor the difference of the two-stage compensation effects in real time. The motor control system firstly synchronously acquires an accurate compensation angle value and a preliminary compensation angle value in each control period, then calculates algebraic difference values of the accurate compensation angle value and the preliminary compensation angle value, performs unit conversion and dimension unification, then performs sliding window analysis on the difference values of a plurality of continuous periods, calculates short-term and long-term statistical characteristics, and finally compares a calculation result with a preset evaluation index to judge the stability of a compensation effect.
In some embodiments, the calculation and analysis of the angle difference can be realized in various ways, alternatively, the motor control system can adopt a multi-scale difference analysis method, firstly, calculate the instantaneous difference value in a micro scale, establish a high-frequency difference value sequence, then average through a window to obtain the trend characteristic of a mesoscale, finally build the performance index of a macro scale by using accumulated statistics to form a complete difference evaluation system, alternatively, the motor control system can also adopt an adaptive weight analysis strategy, dynamically adjust the weight coefficient calculated by the difference value according to the intensity of the angle change, focus on the instantaneous difference value in a rapid movement stage, and focus on the long-term drift in a steady state stage. It will be appreciated that other analysis methods may also be employed, such as differential assessment based on spectral analysis, and the like, and are not limited in this regard.
In practical applications, the problem of misalignment of the judgment caused by noise interference of the difference calculation may be encountered. In this regard, the motor control system employs a robust difference evaluation algorithm that improves computational reliability through multiple filtering and statistical testing. In the concrete implementation, a three-level data processing flow is designed, namely a first level uses median filtering to remove sporadic abnormal values, a second level uses low-pass filtering to extract main trend characteristics, and a third level uses exponential weighted moving average to calculate a stable difference value. For example, when the system detects that the variance of the difference sequence suddenly increases (exceeds 3 times the normal value), the average window width is automatically prolonged, and the margin of the abnormal value judgment is increased, ensuring the stability of the difference calculation. Through the multiple protection mechanism, the influence of noise interference on difference judgment is effectively avoided.
And S212, when the real-time angle difference value is larger than the compensation adjustment threshold value, reducing the data capacity of the compensation buffer area.
The capacity adjustment strategy comprises an adjustment step length, an adjustment frequency and a boundary condition, the data cleaning mechanism refers to a data screening and deleting rule when the capacity is reduced, and the system response time refers to a time interval from exceeding the threshold value to completing adjustment.
The motor control system needs to dynamically optimize the storage resources according to the compensation effect. Specifically, the motor control system firstly compares the real-time angle difference value with a preset adjustment threshold value (such as 0.1 degree), triggers a buffer capacity adjustment process when the difference value exceeds the threshold value for a plurality of continuous periods, then calculates a new capacity target value according to a preset shrinkage proportion (such as 20 percent reduction), then performs data cleaning, preferentially retains the latest data and key feature point data, and finally reorganizes a storage structure to ensure the continuity and the integrity of the data.
In some embodiments, the dynamic adjustment of the buffer capacity can be achieved in various ways, alternatively, the motor control system can adopt a progressive capacity adjustment strategy, firstly evaluate the importance distribution of the current data, establish the data retention priority ranking, then gradually reduce the capacity in batches, evaluate the system performance after each reduction, finally gradually reach the target capacity value on the premise of ensuring the compensation effect, alternatively, the motor control system can also adopt an adaptive partition management method to divide the buffer area into a core data area and an expansion data area, and when the capacity needs to be reduced, the low-priority data of the expansion area is cleaned preferentially, and the stability of the core area is maintained. It will be appreciated that other capacity adjustment methods may be used, such as dynamic storage management based on data compression, and the like, and are not limited herein.
In practical application, the problem of unstable compensation effect after capacity adjustment may be encountered. In this regard, the motor control system employs a safety rollback mechanism that ensures the reliability of the adjustment process through performance monitoring. In the specific implementation, a multi-stage capacity adjustment scheme is established, wherein the first stage is temporary adjustment, the system response is observed in a short time (such as 10 seconds), the second stage is medium-term verification, the compensation effect is evaluated in a longer period (such as 1 minute), and the third stage is permanent adjustment, so that the new capacity setting is solidified after stabilization is confirmed. For example, after the system performs the capacity reduction operation, the data before adjustment and the configuration parameters are recorded at the same time. If a decrease in compensation accuracy (an increase in error of more than 50%) is found during verification, the system will immediately revert to the pre-adjustment state and record the cause of the adjustment failure in the log. The adjustment strategy with the protection mechanism ensures that the stability of control performance is maintained while the storage efficiency is optimized.
In some embodiments, the motor control system performs a policy adjustment for accurate compensation, that is, the motor control system calculates a rate of change of the real-time angle difference when the real-time angle difference is greater than a compensation adjustment threshold, determines a target response period for secondary compensation based on the rate of change, and adjusts the data capacity of the compensation buffer to the number of data packets in one target response period.
The change rate indicates the change speed of the real-time angle difference value along with time, the target response period indicates the shortest time interval required by completing secondary compensation, the data capacity adjustment indicates the dynamic optimization of the storage space of the compensation buffer area, the number of data packets indicates the total data quantity collected in the target response period, the compensation adjustment threshold value indicates the angle difference value judgment standard for triggering the system to respond, and the angle difference value characteristics comprise characteristic parameters such as amplitude, frequency, phase and the like.
The motor control system needs to optimize the compensation response speed according to the dynamic characteristic of the angle difference value. The motor control system firstly calculates real-time angle difference values of a plurality of continuous sampling points, calculates a first derivative of the continuous sampling points by adopting a central difference method to obtain a change rate, then estimates the shortest time required for reaching expected compensation accuracy through a response time prediction model based on the change rate, defines the time as a target response period, calculates the number of data packets required in the period according to the data sampling frequency, and finally dynamically adjusts the capacity of a compensation buffer area according to a calculation result to enable the capacity of the compensation buffer area to be accurately matched with the data requirement of the target response period.
In some embodiments, response optimization can be achieved in a variety of ways, alternatively, the motor control system can employ an adaptive response optimization strategy, firstly, a dynamic model of angle difference is established to analyze the change characteristics and stability of the angle difference, then a nonlinear mapping function is designed based on the change characteristics to map the change rate to an optimal response period, finally, parameters of the mapping function are continuously optimized through a feedback correction mechanism, alternatively, the motor control system can employ a predictive control method, a predictive model is trained by utilizing historical data, response time required by compensation is estimated in advance, and cache capacity is dynamically adjusted accordingly. It will be appreciated that other optimization methods may be employed, such as adaptive adjustment based on fuzzy control, etc., and are not limited herein.
In practical applications, a problem may be encountered that the response period estimation is inaccurate, resulting in unstable compensation effects. In this regard, the motor control system employs a multi-model fusion strategy that improves estimation accuracy by integrating a plurality of predictive models. In specific implementation, a double-layer structure comprising a quick response model and an accurate response model is constructed, wherein the quick response model uses simplified linear prediction for preliminary estimation of response period, and the accurate response model considers the nonlinear characteristics of the system and accurately predicts the required time through a state observer. For example, when it is detected that the rate of change of the angle difference exceeds 0.1 degrees/second, the system first gives a rough estimate using the fast model and then runs the precise model in sync in the background for correction. If the prediction difference of the two models exceeds 20%, triggering an exception handling mechanism, and temporarily keeping the current cache capacity unchanged until a more reliable prediction result is obtained.
In the embodiment of the application, a double-layer compensation framework integrating rapid compensation and accurate compensation is innovatively provided, and technologies such as real-time data acquisition, time sequence analysis and self-adaptive parameter adjustment are combined, so that the compensation effect can be continuously optimized while the real-time response capability of the system is ensured. By establishing the mapping relation between the temperature change characteristics and the angle drift, the system can accurately predict and compensate the temperature influence, and the problems of low compensation precision, response lag, poor adaptability and the like in the traditional method are effectively solved. Meanwhile, by adopting a dynamic data management and feature extraction strategy, the high-efficiency utilization of computing resources is realized, and the reliable operation of the compensation algorithm in an actual industrial environment is ensured. The system also has self-learning and optimizing capabilities, and can continuously improve the compensation effect according to the historical data, so that the motor control system can operate with high precision and high reliability in a complex temperature environment.
The following describes a motor control system in the embodiment of the present application from the perspective of hardware processing, please refer to fig. 3, which is a schematic diagram of a physical device of the motor control system in the embodiment of the present application.
It should be noted that the structure of the motor control system shown in fig. 3 is only an example, and should not impose any limitation on the functions and the application scope of the embodiment of the present invention.
As shown in fig. 3, the motor control system includes a CPU301 that can perform various appropriate actions and processes, such as performing the methods described in the above embodiments, according to a program stored in a ROM302 or a program loaded from a storage section 308 into a RAM 303. In the RAM303, various programs and data required for the system operation are also stored. The CPU301, ROM302, and RAM303 are connected to each other through a bus 304. I/O interface 305 is also connected to bus 304.
Connected to the I/O interface 305 are an input section 306 including an audio input device, a push button switch, and the like, an output section 307 including a liquid crystal display (LiquidCrystalDisplay, LCD) and an audio output device, an indicator lamp, and the like, a storage section 308 including a hard disk, and the like, and a communication section 309 including a network interface card such as a LAN (LocalAreaNetwork ) card, a modem, and the like. Translated from Korean
{METHODS AND SYSTEMS FOR DETECTING NETWORK INTRUSIONS USING FEDERATED LEARNING BASED ON BLOCKCHAIN}
The present disclosure relates to a system and method for detecting network intrusions using blockchain-based federated learning.
The concept of the Internet of Things (IoT) has been developed to improve people's lives by providing various intelligent network applications and gadgets in various fields. Over the past few years, the development of the Internet of Things (IoT) has integrated computers, devices, businesses, vehicles, and even neighbors, thereby improving the convenience of people's daily lives.
IoT is also a network system built on public standards for exchanging information. Including multiple sensors in an IoT embedded system allows for real-time data collection from remote physical devices.
Service provisioning has become part of the capabilities of many participants in IoT networks, especially end devices, due to the advancement of wireless technologies and IoT (Internet of Things) devices. These devices are increasingly capable of collaborating to provide processing and storage services to other entities connected to the network.
The vast amount of data collected from end devices can lead to intelligent and automated decision-making and efficient management of IoT networks. However, as many devices and devices commonly used in the real world are connected to the Internet, concerns about cybersecurity risks are also raised. Security refers to a system that protects personal information from falling into the hands of malicious parties due to intrusion, leakage, or cyberattacks, while privacy refers to the ability of users to control, access, and regulate their personal information. Real-time IoT systems are at risk of unwanted intrusion, critical attacks, or errors, so security and privacy are top priorities.
In addition, the amount and sensitivity of information shared by some devices in IoT networks may exacerbate security and privacy issues above, thus increasing the need for decentralized solutions for data management. In addition, current intrusion detection systems (IDS) are set up to identify specific types of attacks and are unable to adapt to new threats.
Accordingly, the present disclosure aims to propose solutions to solve the aforementioned problems.
In order to achieve the above-mentioned purpose, a system for detecting network intrusions using blockchain-based federated learning is presented. The system may include one or more federated learning clients, one or more federated learning distributors, and one or more aggregation servers. The one or more federated learning clients may obtain a learning model for detecting network intrusions, and perform learning on the learning model using collected data to generate updated model weights. The one or more aggregation servers may aggregate the updated model weights to generate an updated learning model. The one or more federated learning distributors may distribute the updated learning model to one or more federated learning clients.
The learning model can be acquired by one or more federated learning clients approved by the smart contract.
The updated model weights generated by the one or more federated learning clients can be transmitted to the one or more aggregation servers via the one or more federated learning distributors.
The updated model weights may be aggregated by one or more aggregation servers using the FedAvg algorithm.
The one or more federated learning clients can obtain an updated learning model, perform learning on the updated learning model using the collected data, and additionally update model weights for the updated learning model.
In order to achieve the above-mentioned object, a method for detecting a network intrusion is provided, which is performed by a system for detecting a network intrusion using blockchain-based federated learning, including one or more federated learning clients, one or more federated learning distributors, and one or more aggregation servers. The method may include a step in which the one or more federated learning clients acquire a learning model for detecting a network intrusion, and perform learning on the learning model using collected data to generate updated model weights; a step in which the one or more aggregation servers aggregate the updated model weights to generate an updated learning model; and a step in which the one or more federated learning distributors distribute the updated learning model to the one or more federated learning clients.
The learning model can be acquired by one or more federated learning clients approved by the smart contract.
The updated model weights generated by the one or more federated learning clients can be transmitted to the one or more aggregation servers via the one or more federated learning distributors.
The updated model weights may be aggregated by one or more aggregation servers using the FedAvg algorithm.
The method may further include a step of allowing the one or more federated learning clients to obtain an updated learning model, perform learning on the updated learning model using the collected data, and additionally update model weights for the updated learning model.
According to one disclosure of this specification, security and privacy of IoT networks can be ensured by a blockchain-based architecture that enables federated learning and improves intrusion detection in IoT networks.
