### 📜 Full Specification & Deep Scrape Text
Title
A Parametric Equivalent Magnetic Network Modeling Method for Multi-objective Optimization of Permanent Magnet Motors

Abstract
Translated from Chinese
The invention discloses a parametric equivalent magnetic network modeling method for multi-objective optimization of a permanent magnet motor. Type permanent magnet motor modeling and optimization to provide reference research. First, divide the disordered area and regular area of the magnetic field lines in the motor, build the dynamic grid model of the disordered area, and build the magnetic circuit model of the ordered area; then connect the dynamic grid model and the magnetic circuit model to establish the parametric equivalent magnetic field of the motor. Network model, solve the equations simultaneously with nonlinear matrices, solve the magnetic potential of each node, and obtain the torque characteristics of the motor; then use the parameterized equivalent magnetic network model to perform variable sensitivity analysis on the average torque and torque ripple, and select high-sensitivity variables , establish the response surface model of average torque and torque ripple respectively, and substitute the response surface model into the multi-objective optimization algorithm to obtain the Pareto front and determine the optimal parameter combination.

Description
Multi-objective optimization parameterized equivalent magnetic network modeling method for permanent magnet motor
Technical Field
The invention relates to a multi-objective optimization parameterized equivalent magnetic network modeling method for a permanent magnet motor, and belongs to the field of electromagnetic field calculation.
Background
The surface-mounted permanent magnet motor has excellent dynamic performance and is very suitable for a DC/AC motor in a servo system. The key of the performance is the optimization means. The traditional single-target optimization aims at one variable optimization at one time, the method is simple to operate and has certain effect, but influence conflicts among multiple parameters cannot be avoided. Multi-objective optimization methods are commonly used to improve the interaction between parameters, which are solved by Pareto optimality sets, i.e. optimal solution sets. The multi-objective optimization can balance the selected parameter variables, optimize various performance parameters simultaneously, and avoid the influence among a plurality of factors. However, due to the Finite Element Analysis (FEA), the multi-objective optimization has the disadvantages of large time consumption, complex operation and the like. Therefore, a response surface method is proposed to reduce excessive finite element analysis by applying a proxy model. Nevertheless, global optimization still has the disadvantage of being too time-consuming to simulate due to the multi-dimensionality of the sampling points.
An Equivalent Magnetic Network (EMN) model is used as a substitution method of finite element analysis, and the method has the advantages of high analysis speed, low calculation cost and the like. By considering the influence of the spatial harmonic content, the EMN model accuracy based on the grid method can be compared favorably with finite element analysis. However, the EMN model has not been innovatively applied in the aspect of motor structure optimization. By carrying out parameterized equivalent magnetic network modeling on the surface-mounted permanent magnet motor, repeated modeling operation is not needed, the calculation principle is simple, the precision is high, the simulation time consumption is short, higher design efficiency is achieved, the electromagnetic parameters such as motor torque and the like can be rapidly solved under multivariable conditions, and the high-efficiency performance optimization design of the surface-mounted permanent magnet motor is realized by utilizing a multi-objective optimization algorithm.
Disclosure of Invention
The invention aims to provide a multi-objective optimization parameterized equivalent magnetic network modeling method for a permanent magnet motor, which mainly comprises the steps of dividing the magnetic conductance of a dynamic grid in a disordered magnetic line region in the motor, equivalent the magnetic conductance of a magnetic circuit in a regular magnetic line region and establishing and solving a magnetic network matrix equation. And completing sensitivity analysis of a plurality of structural variables and establishing a response surface model by using a parameterized equivalent magnetic network model, and determining an optimal parameter combination by using a multi-objective optimization algorithm to realize rapid multi-objective optimization of the permanent magnet motor.
In order to achieve the purpose, the invention adopts the technical scheme that: a surface-mounted permanent magnet motor multi-objective optimization parameterized equivalent magnetic network modeling method comprises the following steps:
step 1, dividing regions of disorder and rule of magnetic lines in a motor;
step 2, constructing a dynamic grid model of a disordered region of magnetic force lines in the motor;
step 3, constructing a magnetic circuit model of a magnetic line regular region in the motor;
step 4, connecting the dynamic grid model and the magnetic circuit model, and establishing a parameterized equivalent magnetic network model of the motor;
step 5, simultaneously solving an equation by a nonlinear matrix, solving the magnetic potential of each node, and further obtaining the torque characteristic of the motor;
step 6, selecting an optimization variable, determining an optimization target, and using a parameterized equivalent magnetic network model to complete parameter sensitivity analysis;
step 7, selecting a high-sensitivity variable, and respectively establishing response surface models of average torque and torque ripple;
and 8, substituting the response surface model into a multi-objective optimization algorithm to obtain the pareto frontier and determine the optimal parameter combination.
Furthermore, the surface-mounted permanent magnet motor is a 48-slot/44-pole three-phase motor and consists of a stator, an air gap, a rotor permanent magnet and a rotating shaft; the stator comprises a stator yoke part, a stator tooth part, a stator pole shoe, a stator slot and an armature winding, a stator core is made of a silicon steel sheet B20AT1500, and the armature winding adopts a fractional slot centralized winding mode; the air gap is between the stator and the rotor, and the thickness of the air gap is 1 mm; the rotor is of a coreless cylindrical structure and only comprises a permanent magnet and a rotating shaft, the surface of the cylindrical rotating shaft is provided with a groove and is pasted with the permanent magnet made of N42UH, the section of the pasted permanent magnet is approximately rectangular, the pasted permanent magnet is uniformly arranged on the surface of the rotating shaft by a Halbach permanent magnet array, and a main permanent magnet in the array is clamped and embedded in the groove on the surface of the rotating shaft so as to position and install an auxiliary permanent magnet and reduce the influence of manufacturing tolerance on assembly; the motor rotating shaft is made of stainless steel 304 which is a non-magnetic material, is in a solid cylinder shape, is provided with a groove for positioning on the surface, and is coaxially connected with the rotor.
Further, in the step 1, a magnetic force line distribution cloud chart in the motor is obtained by adopting finite element software, the disordered region of the magnetic force lines in the motor is mainly concentrated in a stator pole shoe and an air gap, and the region has more space harmonics; the magnetic line regular region is mainly concentrated on the stator yoke part and the stator tooth part, and the magnetic performance of the rotor permanent magnet is strong and is positioned under the Halbach array, so that the magnetic line trend in the rotor permanent magnet is regular, and the magnetic leakage is negligible; the rotor rotating shaft adopts a non-magnetic material, so the distribution of magnetic lines of force can be equivalently regarded as the distribution of magnetic lines of force in the air, and modeling is not carried out.
Further, in the step 2, the specific process of dynamic grid modeling for the disordered region of the magnetic force line in the motor is as follows: according to the size of a pole shoe and the size of an air gap of the motor, a cross-shaped magnetic conduction grid with variable length and width is adopted for subdivision, the influence of magnetic leakage is considered, the air gap between the pole shoe and the pole shoe is simultaneously subdivided in the circumferential direction, the distribution of two grids is strictly limited to respective regional boundaries, the size is strictly set according to respective regional specifications, and the grid shape of a corresponding region of the pole shoe is only influenced when the pole shoe is changed after the quantity is fixed; the modeling of the air gap part needs to keep consistent quantity and width with the upper pole shoe grid in the circumferential direction, and the grid height is judged according to the air gap length alone. When the width of the pole shoe grid is changed, the width of the grid in the air gap needs to be updated along with the change of the width of the pole shoe grid, so that the magnetic conduction connection relation between the upper grid and the lower grid is constant.
Further, in step 3, the specific process of modeling the magnetic circuit in the magnetic line regular region in the motor is as follows: for the stator tooth part and the yoke part, performing magnetic conductance equivalent treatment by adopting a universal magnetic circuit model, wherein a single tooth part is equivalent to a single magnetic conductance, and the stator yoke part is equivalent in a segmented manner according to the number of teeth to establish connection magnetic conductance among teeth; and for the rotor permanent magnet, each permanent magnet block is equivalent respectively according to the Halbach magnetizing direction, a radial magnetic conductance is established in the main permanent magnet, a tangential magnetic conductance is established in the auxiliary permanent magnet, and the permanent magnet magnetic conductances are connected at the nodes in sequence according to the flow rule of Halbach magnetic lines.
Further, in the step 4, the bottom node of the magnetic conductance of the stator tooth part is sequentially connected with the upper node of the stator pole shoe grid, and the upper node of the air gap grid between the stator pole shoes is vacant; the bottom grid nodes of the air gap grid are connected with the main permanent magnet permeance in the rotor Halbach permanent magnet array according to the corresponding relation, and whether the mapping area of the main permanent magnet on the air gap grid is larger than a half is judged according to the basis, and the bottom permeance of the air gap grid above the auxiliary permanent magnet is not connected in a vacant mode; and the position of the motor rotor needs to be updated, the rotating angle needs to be judged again, and the connection relation between the air gap grid and the magnetic conductance of the rotor main permanent magnet is reset.
Further, in the step 5, a matrix equation G · F of the flux guide G, the magnetomotive force F, and the magnetic flux Φ is established, and the magnetic induction intensity between two points is calculated from the node magnetic potential difference, and the formula is: b is i,j ＝(F(i)-F(j))·G(i,j)/S i,j . Introducing a B-H curve of nonlinear parameters of the iron core, obtaining a magnetic permeability value through interpolation during iterative calculation, updating the magnetic permeability by adopting a super-relaxation iterative algorithm, and calculating the new value of the magnetic permeability value and the last value of the magnetic permeability valueAnd calculating value and weighting iteration. When the magnetic density difference delta B of the tooth part between two times of iterative calculations is less than or equal to 0.5%, the iteration is considered to be converged, the rotor position is updated, and the next rotor position angle is calculated; after one electric angle period is calculated, electromagnetic parameters such as a motor flux linkage phi and a back electromotive force E are calculated through the magnetic density of the tooth part; under the condition of load, sinusoidal current is added into an armature winding to generate sinusoidal alternating tooth magnetomotive force, and further the output torque of the motor can be calculated.
Further, in step 6, 8 parameter variables of the stator yoke thickness, the stator tooth width, the stator tooth length, the pole shoe height, the notch width, the main permanent magnet length, the auxiliary permanent magnet width and the pole arc coefficient are selected, the average torque and the torque ripple are subjected to variable sensitivity analysis by changing the magnetic conductance value of the magnetic circuit and adjusting the magnetic conductance grid shape by using the parameterized equivalent magnetic network model, and 4 high-sensitivity variables are selected.
Further, in step 7, using a Box-Behnken Design test method to sample the selected 4 high-sensitivity variables for 29 times, calculating average torque and torque ripple of the designed 29 parameter combination method in a magnetic network model, generating a response surface model of the average torque and the torque ripple in Design Expert software, and generating a multivariate correlation coefficient R 2 The closer to 1, the smaller the p value is, the higher the accuracy of the model is; further according to R 2 And adjusting the number of variables in the response surface model according to the p value so as to improve the fitting precision of the model.
Further, in step 8, a multi-objective differential evolution algorithm (MODE-RMO) based on a sorting mutation operator is introduced by using a response surface model of average torque and torque ripple, and external records of branch distribution solutions are divided by mutation, intersection and selection, and the average distance between two solutions is analyzed by using a crowding distance, so that the most excellent individual solution is guaranteed to survive to the next iteration. And finally, obtaining a pareto frontier of the non-dominated solution set, and determining the optimal non-dominated solution by using the constraint of the optimization objective function.
The invention has the following beneficial effects:
1. in the invention, the surface-mounted permanent magnet motor is comprehensively modeled by respectively using the mesh subdivision and magnetic circuit magnetic conductance models, and meanwhile, the high precision of the finite element method and the low consumption of the magnetic circuit method are considered, thereby being beneficial to improving the calculation accuracy and efficiency of the equivalent magnetic network.
2. According to the invention, the cross-shaped magnetic conductance grid with adjustable length and width is adopted for local subdivision, the grid shape in the area is equivalently changed when the structure of the modeling area is changed, repeated modeling is avoided when parameters are changed, and the model universality and the dynamic property are improved.
3. In the invention, the grids in the air gap area and the grids in the pole shoe area are fixed with nodes, and when the pole shoe structure influences the pole shoe grids, the air gap grids are adjusted with the same width, so that the stability of the magnetic conduction connection relation is ensured;
4. in the invention, the connection relation between the grids of the air gap area and the rotor permanent magnet is judged through the mapping area, so that the error of adjusting the air gap magnetic conductance according to the mapping area is avoided, and the model calculation accuracy is improved.
5. According to the invention, the parameter-adjustable equivalent magnetic network model is utilized to carry out multi-objective optimization design, so that the simulation time consumption is short, the design efficiency is high, the electromagnetic parameters such as motor torque and the like are rapidly solved under multivariable conditions, and the structure optimization design of the surface-mounted permanent magnet motor is favorably and efficiently realized.

Detailed Description
The technical solution in the embodiments of the present invention will be clearly and completely described below with reference to the accompanying drawings in the embodiments of the present invention.
In order to be able to illustrate the advantages of the present invention more simply and clearly, the following description is made in detail with reference to a specific surface-mount permanent magnet motor: FIG. 1 is a schematic diagram of the motor topology, wherein 1 is a stator yoke part, and 2-1 is a stator tooth part; 2-2 is stator tooth pole shoe, 2-3 is air gap between stator tooth pole shoes, 3 is winding, 4 is air gap between stator and rotor, 5-1 is main permanent magnet in Halbach array, 5-2 is auxiliary permanent magnet in Halbach array, 6 is non-magnetic rotating shaft; the embodiment of the invention relates to a 48-slot/44-pole three-phase motor which consists of four parts, namely a stator, an air gap, a rotor permanent magnet and a rotating shaft; the stator comprises a stator yoke part, a stator tooth part pole shoe, a stator slot and an armature winding, a stator core is made of a silicon steel sheet B20AT1500, and the armature winding adopts a fractional slot centralized winding mode; the air gap is between the stator and the rotor, and the thickness of the air gap is 1 mm; the rotor is of a coreless cylindrical structure and only comprises a permanent magnet and a rotating shaft, the surface of the cylindrical rotating shaft is provided with a groove and is pasted with the permanent magnet made of N42UH, the section of the pasted permanent magnet is approximately rectangular, the pasted permanent magnet is uniformly arranged on the surface of the rotating shaft by a Halbach permanent magnet array, and a main permanent magnet in the array is clamped and embedded in the groove on the surface of the rotating shaft so as to position and install an auxiliary permanent magnet and reduce the influence of manufacturing tolerance on assembly; the motor rotating shaft is made of stainless steel 304 which is a non-magnetic material, is in a solid cylinder shape, is provided with a groove for positioning on the surface, and is coaxially connected with the rotor.
The flowchart shown in fig. 9 is implemented by the following steps:
step 1, dividing the disordered and regular regions of magnetic lines in the motor.
Fig. 2 is a magnetic line analyzing diagram of a motor used in the embodiment of the present invention. In the distribution of magnetic force lines, the disordered region of the magnetic force lines in the motor is mainly concentrated in an air gap between a stator tooth part pole shoe and a stator and a rotor, the region is a key region for electromagnetic energy conversion, and the magnetic flux of the motor is distorted by uneven air magnetic conductance, so that the trend of the magnetic force lines is complicated and irregular, and a large amount of magnetic flux leakage between teeth and space harmonic exist; the magnetic line regular region in the motor is mainly concentrated on the stator tooth part, the stator yoke part and the rotor permanent magnet, the region is a path of magnetic flux guiding air gaps, the shape is regular, basically no magnetic flux leakage exists, the trend of the magnetic line is regular, and the magnetic line is in the same direction.
And 2, constructing a dynamic grid model of the disordered region of the magnetic force lines in the motor.
According to the size and the air gap size of a stator tooth part pole shoe of the motor, a dynamically adjustable cross-shaped magnetic conduction grid is adopted for subdivision, the influence of magnetic leakage is considered, the grid subdivision is simultaneously carried out on the air gap between the stator tooth part pole shoe and the pole shoe in the circumferential direction, the distribution of two grids is strictly limited to respective regional boundaries, the size is strictly set according to respective regional specifications, and the grid shape of a corresponding region of the stator tooth part pole shoe is only influenced when the structure of the stator tooth part pole shoe is changed after the grid number is fixed; the number and the width of the air gap part modeling are required to be consistent with those of the pole shoe grids of the stator tooth part on the upper layer in the circumferential direction, the grid height is judged according to the air gap length alone, and when the width of the pole shoe grids of the stator tooth part is changed, the width of the grids in the air gap is required to be updated along with the grid height, so that the magnetic conduction connection relation between the grids on the upper layer and the grids on the lower layer is ensured to be constant.
FIG. 4 is a diagram of a magnetic network model constructed by dynamic meshing of the present invention, and FIG. 5 is a diagram of a magnetic network model constructed by dynamic meshing of the present invention with a partial enlargement; according to the actual size of the modeling area, the interdental leakage flux and the magnetic line loop are considered at the same time, wherein the interdental leakage flux and the magnetic line loop comprise the height of the pole shoe, the length of the pole shoe, the width of the notch, the outer diameter of the air gap, the height of the air gap and the like, and different mesh generation schemes are selected in different areas correspondingly. in the formula, L a Is the axial length, w cell Is the grid width, h cell Is the grid height, μ 0 Is the magnetic permeability of vacuum, mu r Is the relative magnetic permeability of ferromagnetic materials. And simultaneously considering the influence of magnetic leakage, meshing the air gaps between the stator tooth part pole shoes and the pole shoes in the circumferential direction, wherein the two meshes are strictly distributed on respective region boundaries, the size is strictly set according to respective region specifications, and the mesh shape of the corresponding region is only influenced when the structure of the stator pole shoes is changed after the number of the meshes is fixed.
The region with complex magnetic field of the stator part is an air gap 2-3 between a pole shoe 2-2 and a pole shoe of the stator tooth part, and the heights of the subdivision grids are all h 1 The grid width is divided equally by the modeling area width, 1 row and 2 columns of equal-width grids are arranged in the air gaps between the pole shoes, 1 row and 9 columns of equal-width grids are arranged in the pole shoes, 9 upper nodes of the grids in the pole shoes are sequentially connected with 2-1 lower nodes of the stator teeth, and 2 upper nodes of the air gap grids between the pole shoes are not connected in a vacant mode.
The air gap 4 is an important place for energy conversion of the permanent magnet motor and is also the region with the most complex magnetic field. Through reasonable design, 2 layers of grids are divided for the air gap 4, the number of the air gap grids is the same as that of the lower layer grids of the stator, and the total number of the air gap grids is the least common multiple 528 of 48 slots/44 poles, so that the symmetrical equality of the grids is ensured. The number of the air gap grids is consistent with that of the stator lower grids, the widths of the air gap grids are also completely consistent, and the air gap upper grids are correspondingly connected with the stator lower grids. On the other hand, the air gap lower layer grid is connected with the rotor permanent magnet. The rotor is provided with a Halbach array permanent magnet array which consists of a main permanent magnet 5-1 and an auxiliary permanent magnet 5-2. The main permanent magnet 5-1 is magnetized in the radial direction, and the auxiliary permanent magnet 5-2 is punched in the tangential direction, so that the effect of enhancing the unilateral air gap magnetic field is achieved. For the Halbach permanent magnet array, because the auxiliary permanent magnet only generates tangential magnetic lines of force in practice, the auxiliary permanent magnet 5-2 is not connected with the lower node of the air gap 4 grid, and only the main permanent magnet 5-1 generating tangential magnetization is connected with the air gap 4 grid within the width range of all the main permanent magnets 5-1. When the grid width of the pole shoe of the tooth part of the stator is changed, the grid in the air gap needs to be updated with the change of the width, so that the magnetic conduction connection relation between the upper grid and the lower grid is constant.
And 3, constructing a magnetic circuit model of the magnetic line regular region in the motor.
For the stator part of the motor, the trend of the magnetic lines of force in the stator yoke part 1 and the stator tooth part 2-1 is regular, basically no magnetic leakage exists, and the magnetic lines of force are in the same direction. For the stator tooth part, modeling of a general magnetic circuit magnetic conductance model is carried out according to the structural parameters, and the magnetic conductance calculation formula is as follows:
wherein μ is the magnetic permeability of the iron core, S is the sectional area in the magnetizing direction, l is the magnetizing length t Is tooth length, mu 0 Is the magnetic permeability of vacuum, mu r Is the relative permeability of the ferromagnetic material, w is the structure width, L a Is the axial length.
The magnetic circuit permeance of the stator yoke part is equivalent, the number of teeth is equivalent in a segmented mode, and a connecting permeance between teeth is established, wherein a calculation formula of the connecting permeance is the same as that of the teeth; and nodes at two ends of the yoke part magnetic guide are respectively connected with upper end nodes of the correspondingly connected tooth part magnetic guide. For the rotor permanent magnet, according to the Halbach magnetizing direction, each permanent magnet block is subjected to magnetic conductance equivalence respectively, radial magnetic conductance is established in the main permanent magnet, tangential magnetic conductance is established in the auxiliary permanent magnet, the calculation formula is the same as the stator magnetic conductance calculation formula, the permanent magnet is approximately regarded as air magnetic conductance, and the relative magnetic conductance is set to be 1. Meanwhile, a magnetic conductance path is considered, and according to the flow rule of Halbach magnetic force lines, the lower end node of the radial magnetic conductance of the main permanent magnet is connected with the tangential magnetic conductance node of the auxiliary permanent magnet, so that an interconnected magnetic conductance network among the permanent magnets is established.
Step 4, connecting the dynamic grid model and the magnetic circuit model, and establishing a parameterized equivalent magnetic network model of the motor;
the bottom node of the stator tooth magnetic conductance is sequentially connected with the upper node of the stator tooth pole shoe grid, and the upper node of the air gap grid between the stator tooth pole shoes is vacant; the bottom grid nodes of the air gap grid are connected with the main permanent magnet permeance in the rotor Halbach permanent magnet array according to the corresponding relation, and whether the mapping area of the main permanent magnet on the air gap grid is larger than a half is judged according to the basis, and the bottom permeance of the air gap grid above the auxiliary permanent magnet is not connected in a vacant mode; and the position of the motor rotor needs to be updated, the rotating angle needs to be judged again, and the connection relation between the air gap grid and the magnetic conductance of the rotor main permanent magnet is reset.
Because the stator pole shoe area uses dynamic mesh subdivision, the magnetic conductance model of the stator tooth part 2-1 is connected with 9 meshes in the first row of the corresponding tooth lower pole shoe 2-2 and the relation is fixed, and meanwhile, the meshes of the tooth lower pole shoe 2-2 are fixedly connected with the meshes of the air gap 4. For the grids in the air gap 4, the connection relationship between the grids is fixed, and the connection relationship between the grids and the stator pole shoe 2-2 is also fixed, so that when the rotor rotates along the Z-axis circumferential direction, only the magnetic conduction connection relationship between the air gap and the rotor changes along with different rotation angles, and therefore the method for determining the connection between the rotor Halbach permanent magnet array and the air gap grids is the key for establishing a rotating magnetic network model. When the rotor rotates to a specific angle, the upper nodes of the radial magnetic conductance of the main permanent magnet 5-1 are respectively connected with the corresponding magnetic conductance in the mapping area, and whether the mapping area of the main permanent magnet on the air gap grid is larger than a half is judged according to the criterion; in the range of which about 6 to 7 air gap meshes are connected, and in the range of the auxiliary permanent magnet about 6 to 7 air gap meshes are also connected, which remain empty. When the rotor permanent magnet rotates by an angle step, the air gap 4 grid node in the coverage range connected with the main permanent magnet 5-1 changes, and the connection relation between the rotor main permanent magnet permeance and the air gap grid needs to be updated continuously in the rotation process of the motor.
Fig. 6 is a schematic diagram of dynamic grid change when parameters of the invention change, and after an equivalent magnetic network model of the motor is established by combining a grid and a magnetic circuit model, the parameterization function of the invention can be realized by dynamically adjusting the size of the grid and the magnetic conductance value of the magnetic circuit. For parametric grid adjustment, the dynamic adjustment of variables such as the width of a slot, the height of a pole shoe, the length of an air gap and the like can be mainly realized. As shown in fig. 6, as the pole piece height increases, the height of the entire row of grids in the pole piece layer increases to match the new pole piece height, while the grid width in the slots lengthens and the grid width in the pole piece decreases as the slot width becomes larger, reducing the length of the pole piece. When the stator grid is dynamically adjusted according to the parameterization requirement, the principle that the boundaries of the grid and the modeling area are kept unified needs to be ensured, namely the grid of the boundary which is overlapped with the modeling area needs to ensure that the boundaries of the edge cannot generate position deviation, and meanwhile, the heights and the widths of all grids in the area are processed in an equal part, so that the equality of a grid model is kept, and the defect of repeated modeling during variable adjustment is avoided. In addition, when the stator part grids change in width, the grid width in the air gap needs to be adjusted correspondingly, the grid widths of the upper area and the lower area are ensured to be consistent, and the grid magnetic conductance is fixedly connected. For the magnetic conductance adjustment of the parametric magnetic circuit, the dynamic adjustment of variables such as the thickness of a stator yoke, the tooth width of a stator, the tooth length of the stator, the height of a permanent magnet, the pole arc coefficient and the like can be mainly realized. The parameterization of the trend rule of the magnetic force lines in the region is directly realized by adjusting the sectional area or the length in the magnetic conductance calculation formula, only the magnetic conductance values of the magnetic circuits among partial nodes are changed, and the judgment of the connection relation of the nodes is not influenced.

And 6, selecting an optimization variable, determining an optimization target, and completing parameter sensitivity analysis by using a parameterized equivalent magnetic network model.

As can be seen from fig. 7(b), for the comprehensive sensitivity coefficient, the tooth width, the notch width, the auxiliary permanent magnet width, and the pole arc coefficient have higher comprehensive sensitivity, and therefore, the four sets of parameters are integrated into a high sensitivity coefficient, and the modeling of the response surface is performed. And the rest of the stator yoke thickness, the stator tooth length, the stator pole shoe height and the main permanent magnet length have relatively low sensitivity coefficients, and a single-parameter optimization method is adopted for the rest of the stator yoke thickness, the stator tooth length, the stator pole shoe height and the main permanent magnet length. And 8, substituting the response surface model into a multi-objective optimization algorithm to obtain the pareto frontier and determine the optimal parameter combination.
A response surface model of average torque and torque ripple is utilized, a multi-target differential evolution algorithm based on a sequencing mutation operator is introduced, and MODE-RMO is adopted in the invention. TheThe key to the model is the differential evolution of the rank-based mutation operators. MODE-RMO combines fast non-dominated sorting and congestion distance and speeds convergence speed. And further carrying out rapid non-dominant sorting and congestion distance sorting on the population. First, members with a dominance of zero will be placed in a separate list Q, and these members belong to the non-dominated solution set. Secondly, the average distance between the two solutions is analyzed by using the crowding distance, the absolute normalized difference of the two adjacent solutions is calculated, and the population density is predicted. Finally, according to the population ranking, the most elite individuals in the population will survive to the next generation. Repeating the above process until convergence and producing the optimum value of the pareto front,
fig. 7(d) is a schematic diagram of the resulting pareto front surface. It can be seen that the parameterized magnetic network matches well with the pareto frontier obtained from finite elements. The reason for the offset is mainly that the EMN gets a smaller average torque than the finite element analysis results. The particle locations include information of the solution set, and the important zone divides high-quality particles from low-quality particles. Based on the pareto front surface, the predicted optimal average torque is 266.1n.m, the torque ripple is 1.04n.m, and the torque performance is greatly improved compared with the initial design that the average torque is 252.6n.m and the torque ripple is 1.87 n.m.
Fig. 8(a) is a comparison diagram of no-load back-emf before and after optimization. It can be seen that the back emf amplitude of the initial design is about 170V, the back emf amplitude of the optimized design is increased by about 15V, and the back emf obtained by finite element analysis and EMN is substantially the same in the initial design and the optimized design. The difference in the waveform peaks is caused by human error in the equivalent magnetic circuit calculation and the air gap junction permeability calculation. Fig. 8(b) is a comparison diagram with experimental no-load back-potential, comparing EMN, FEA and no-load line potential for realizing measurement, although error in phase potential is slightly increased in line potential calculation, it can still be well matched, and calculation accuracy is high.
Fig. 8(c) is a comparison graph of cogging torque before and after optimization, which demonstrates the reduction in cogging torque. The peak value of the optimized torque ripple is reduced from 1.9N.m to 1.3N.m, and the effectiveness of torque ripple suppression is shown. Further, fig. 8(d) is a schematic diagram of torque comparison before and after optimization. The result shows that the average torque is improved to 268.3N.m from the initial 252.6N.m, the average torque is improved by 15.7N.m, the torque ripple is reduced from 1.87N.m to 1.21N.m, and the torque performance is basically better predicted within the allowable error range compared with the predicted result. This difference is mainly due to the finite order of the response surface function. On the other hand, in the initial design and the optimized design, the EMN calculation result is better matched with the finite element analysis result in the waveform and the period. However, EMN yields an average torque slightly lower than FEA, about 0.65n.m, due to the difference in back emf magnitude caused by mesh roughness and finite element fine subdivision. FIG. 8(e) is a schematic diagram of the experimentally measured Torque showing the measured Torque at rated load, with an average measured Torque of about 253N.m and an average Torque of about 268.3N.m for EMN. This difference is mainly caused by mechanical and stray losses, which are neglected in the EMN modeling. The torque ripple in the experiment, although affected by the sensor noise, still exhibited a smooth output torque, demonstrating the effectiveness of the optimization process.
In conclusion, the multi-objective optimization parameterized equivalent magnetic network modeling method for the permanent magnet motor comprises the steps of dividing disordered and regular regions of magnetic force lines in the motor, adopting dynamic mesh subdivision with parameterized characteristics for the disordered regions, adopting a conventional magnetic circuit magnetic conductance equivalent model for the ordered regions, connecting the dynamic mesh model with the magnetic circuit model, and establishing a parameterized equivalent magnetic network model of the motor; solving an equation by simultaneous nonlinear matrixes, solving the magnetic potential of each node, and further obtaining the torque characteristic of the motor; the method comprises the steps of carrying out variable sensitivity analysis on average torque and torque ripple by changing a magnetic circuit magnetic conductance value and adjusting the shape of a magnetic conductance grid through a parameterized equivalent magnetic network model, selecting high-sensitivity variables, respectively establishing response surface models of the average torque and the torque ripple, substituting the response surface models into a multi-objective optimization algorithm to obtain pareto frontier, determining optimal parameter combinations, and respectively carrying out comparison verification with finite element analysis and experimental results. The invention firstly carries out parameterized equivalent magnetic network modeling suitable for multi-objective optimization aiming at the surface-mounted permanent magnet motor, and the provided scheme can provide reference research for modeling and optimization of the permanent magnet motor.
Although the present invention has been described in terms of the preferred embodiment, it is not intended that the invention be limited to the embodiment. ### 📜 Full Specification & Deep Scrape Text
Title
Multi-objective optimization method for groundwater pollution monitoring network

Abstract
A multi-objective optimization method for groundwater pollution monitoring network, which mainly includes four steps: groundwater numerical value simulation, groundwater vulnerability assessment, the establishment of the monitoring network optimization model, and the solving of the optimization model. The core of the method is to establish a multi-objective optimization model aimed at establishing the least monitoring wells, monitoring the maximum pollutant concentration, and monitoring the maximum regional vulnerability value. Solving the optimization model by the algorithm and considering the relationship between the quality error and the number of monitoring wells comprehensively to determine the well number and location of the monitoring network.

Description
This application is the continuation application of International Application PCT/CN2018/092473 filed on 22 Jun. 2018 which claims priority to Chinese Application No. CN201710963185.X filed on 16 Oct. 2017, the entire contents of each of which are hereby incorporated by reference.
TECHNICAL FIELD
The present invention belongs to the field of groundwater environment monitoring, and particularly relates to a multi-objective optimization method for groundwater pollution monitoring network based on the susceptibility and status of the groundwater pollution.
BACKGROUND ART
Groundwater is an important part of water resources and has gradually become an important source of drinking water in China. However, with the increase of human activities and the rapid development of social and economic production, groundwater resources are seriously polluted. In order to ensure the security of groundwater, it is necessary to establish a comprehensive groundwater monitoring network to obtain effective groundwater information.
Due to the concealment, deep burial depth, and slow water circulation, the self-purification ability of groundwater is rather poor. Once contaminated, it is difficult to recover, and the cost of repair is high. Therefore, prevention of groundwater pollution is more important than treatment, and it is necessary to monitor the areas with high pollution risks. Especially for the monitoring system of groundwater source area, while understanding the status of groundwater quality, monitoring the areas with high pollution risks can play a role of early warning. Decision makers can timely grasp pollution trend through monitoring data, formulate effective measures to prevent further spread of pollutants, minimize pollution hazards, and greatly ensure the safety of the wellhead.
At present, most groundwater monitoring networks have problems such as irrational spatial layout and redundancy or inadequacy of monitoring wells. Even if it costs a lot of money and resources, it cannot obtain sufficient and effective groundwater information. It is therefore necessary to optimize existing groundwater monitoring networks to establish groundwater monitoring systems with minimal cost to obtain adequate information. At present, there are numerous studies of optimization methods of groundwater monitoring networks at home and abroad, including statistical methods such as hydrogeological analysis, Kriging, Kalman filtering, and so on, optimization methods based on groundwater simulation, and combination of different methods, for example, multi-objective planning combined with geostatistical methods.
These methods are mainly based on hydrogeological conditions or the distribution of pollutants to optimize the monitoring network, and rarely consider the groundwater susceptibility. Some research on layout of monitoring wells based on groundwater vulnerability does not quantitatively determine the number and location of monitoring wells. Therefore, current research is difficult to quantitatively optimize the number and location of the monitoring network while considering groundwater vulnerability and pollution distribution.
CONTENTS OF THE INVENTION
In order to solve the above problems existing, the present invention provides a multi-objective optimization method for pollution monitoring network which is more suitable for groundwater source.
The multi-objective optimization method for groundwater pollution monitoring network provided by the present invention comprises: S 1 According to the yearbook, drilling or field pumping test data and empirical values, establish a hydrogeological conceptual model, select characteristic pollutants, simulate three-dimensional groundwater flow field and solute transport, and get the distribution situation, migration and conversion process of characteristic pollutants in the groundwater of the workplace; S 2 Determine the indicator system for workplace vulnerability assessment, determine the score and weight of each indicator, and evaluate the vulnerability of the workplace; S 3 Based on the groundwater vulnerability assessment results, initially establish a workplace monitoring network, then establish a multi-objective optimization model for the workplace pollution monitoring network; S 4 Solve multi-objective optimization model and combine the quality error analysis to optimize the well number and location of the monitoring network.
Compared with the prior art, the multi-objective optimization method for groundwater pollution monitoring network provided by the present invention has the following beneficial effects:
Know the groundwater polluting status in workplace through groundwater simulation, delineate the vulnerable area through groundwater vulnerability assessment, establish and solve the multi-objective optimization model with the goal of least number of monitoring wells, maximum sum of pollutant concentration monitored, and maximum sum of vulnerability scores at selected monitoring sites, to optimize all targets simultaneously and obtain the optimized well number and location of the monitoring network. The monitoring network optimized by this method can detect the most seriously polluted and the most vulnerably polluted areas, and improve the effectiveness and advancement of monitoring data.
DESCRIPTION OF FIGURES
In order to illustrate the embodiment of the present invention more clearly, the drawings used in the embodiment will be briefly described below.
FIG. 1 is a flowchart of a multi-objective optimization method for groundwater pollution monitoring network according to the embodiment of the present invention;
FIG. 2 is a detailed flowchart of groundwater vulnerability assessment.
SPECIFIC EMBODIMENTS FOR CARRYING OUT THE INVENTION
In order to make the objects, technical solutions, and advantages of the present invention more comprehensible, the present invention will be further described in details below with reference to specific embodiments and the accompanying drawings.
In order to solve the problem that the existing optimization method is hard to quantitatively optimize the monitoring network when considering the groundwater vulnerability, the present invention selects the multi-objective optimization method, and uses the groundwater vulnerability and pollutant concentration as decision variables in the multi-objective optimization model, thereby the groundwater vulnerability and pollution distribution are considered simultaneously, and analyzing the result of the multi-objective optimization model to quantitatively optimize the well number and location of the monitoring network.
As shown in FIG. 1 , the multi-objective optimization method for groundwater pollution monitoring network provided by the present invention comprises:
S 1 . According to a yearbook, drilling or field pumping test data and empirical values, establish a hydrogeological conceptual model, select characteristic pollutants, simulate three-dimensional groundwater flow field and solute transport, and get the distribution situation, migration and conversion process of characteristic pollutants in the groundwater of the workplace;
Said hydrogeological conceptual model includes aquifer and topsoil layer. In one embodiment, the conceptual model in S 1 is to generalize the geological layer into four layers, from top to bottom includes: topsoil layer, pore phreatic aquifer, pore weak confined aquifer, and pore confined aquifer; select nitrate as the characteristic pollutant according to the condition of the pollution source discharge and the groundwater quality monitoring data; construct the three-dimensional groundwater numerical model, and simulate the distribution of nitrate in the region and the future migration and transformation.
S 2 . Determine the indicator system for workplace vulnerability assessment, determine the score and weight of each indicator, and evaluate the vulnerability of the workplace;
As shown in FIG. 2 , the step specifically includes:
S 201 : According to the hydrogeological characteristics and pollution conditions of the groundwater source area, establish a indicator system of groundwater vulnerability assessment suitable for workplaces containing groundwater sources;
S 202 : Uniformly quantify each indicator, establish scoring rules, and score each indicator according to the scoring rules;
S 203 : Determine the weight of each indicator;
S 204 : Perform groundwater vulnerability assessment of the workplace.
In one embodiment, the indicator system of vulnerability assessment in S 2 is divided into essential vulnerability and special vulnerability. The indicators of essential vulnerability include depth to water, recharge, aquifer medium, topography and impact of the vadose zone media. The special vulnerability indicators include impact range of pumping well group, land use type and pollution source. The data of depth to water, aquifer medium, and so on can be obtained from local geological survey data or by drilling. Using the groundwater simulation software to simulate the groundwater flow field when pumped and unpumped water respectively, comparing the flow direction and flow velocity of the streamline under the two scenarios, and drawing the changed area of the groundwater flow field flowing to the water source under two scenarios by ArcGIS. The ratio of the area of variation range of the streamline when pumping water compared to when not pumping water to the well number in the range is impact range of the pumping well group. The land use type is obtained through analysising the land use map of the workplace. The indicator score of pollution source is given according to the pollutant discharge amount released per unit area, which is calculated based on the relevant data obtained from the yearbook and pollution source survey.
In S 2 , the essential vulnerability indicator score refers to the indicator score in the DRASTIC method, and the score grading standards of the special vulnerability indicators including impact range of pumping well group, land use type, and pollution source are shown in Table 2. Different land type regions set different scores; the pollution source indicator is graded according to emission amount of pollution source; the indicator score of the impact range of pumping well group is determined by two parts, firstly, the value is taken within 1 to 5 according to the size of the impact range, and then based on the evaluation result of the essential vulnerability, multiplied by the coefficient corresponding to the highest level of the essential vulnerability within the impact range of pumping well group (see Table 3), and the calculation formula is as follows: The indicator score of impact range of pumping well group=size score of impact range of pumping well groupx coefficient
In S 2 , the weight of each indicator is determined by using an analytic hierarchy process, and the process includes stratifying the evaluation system, setting the groundwater vulnerability as the first layer, namely the target layer; and the second layer is the criterion layer, which includes two factors, essential vulnerability and special vulnerability respectively; and the third layer is the decision-making layer, and this layer includes the specific indicators of the essential vulnerability and special vulnerability; constructing a judgment matrix of indicators of each layer; performing single order and consistency test of each layer according to the judgment matrix; performing total order and consistency test of the layers; and the product of the weight of each indicator in the decision-making layer and the target weight of the corresponding criterion layer is the weight of each indicator on the groundwater vulnerability.
Weight sum of the scores and weights of each indicator using ArcGIS to get the vulnerability assessment results of the workplace. The vulnerability is divided into five levels: lower, low, medium, high and higher, according to the vulnerability score, and different levels of vulnerability are displayed in different colors in the ArcGIS to present a partition map of groundwater vulnerability.
S 3 . Based on the groundwater vulnerability assessment results, initially establish a workplace monitoring network, and establish a multi-objective optimization model for the workplace pollution monitoring network;
In one embodiment, the method for initially establishing the workplace monitoring network in S 3 is: Determining the area and the initial density of each vulnerability level region according to the vulnerability assessment results, wherein the initial density of the monitoring wells required by different vulnerability levels is listed in Table 4. The number of monitoring wells initially set in the region with each vulnerability level is not less than the product of the area and density of the corresponding region, and the existing 6 monitoring wells and 34 pumping wells are integrated to form an initial monitoring network of 60 wells.
The multi-objective optimization model for the monitoring network in S 3 is: (1) the minimum number of monitoring wells; (2) the maximum sum of pollutant concentration monitored; and (3) the maximum sum of vulnerability scores at all selected monitoring sites. The specific formulas are: Objective functions are as follows:
min Z 1 =Σ j∈J Σ i∈Q j X i (1)
max Z 2 =Σ j∈J Σ i∈Q j V i X i (2)
max Z 3 =Σ j∈J Σ i∈Q j Y i X i (3)
Constrained functions are as follows:
N j *≥N j ≥1, j∈J (4)
N j =Σ i∈Q j X i , j∈J, i∈Q j , Q j ∈I (5)
N j *=[ S j ×M j ], j∈J (6)
X i =[0,1], i∈I (7)
Wherein, Z 1 is the number of monitoring wells; Z 2 is the mass concentration of pollutants monitored, mg/L; Z 3 is vulnerability score at monitoring site; Q j is the set of location numbers of monitoring well in the j-th partition; Xi is a binary decision variable, indicating whether the i-th monitoring well is selected, the value is 1 when the monitoring well is selected, and 0 is not selected; V i is the groundwater vulnerability score at the i-th monitoring well location; Y i is the mass concentration of groundwater pollutants the i-th well monitored, mg/L; N j is the number of monitoring wells selected in the j-th partition; S j is the area of the j-th partition, km 2 ; M j is the density of the monitoring wells corresponding to the groundwater vulnerability level of the j-th partition prokm 2 ; N j * is the upper limit of the number of monitoring wells in the j-th partition, and the value is the smallest integer greater than the product of S j and M j ; I is the set of location numbers of all monitoring well; and J is the set of partition numbers of regional vulnerability.
Wherein, constrained function N j *≥N i ≥1, j∈J constrains the maximum and minimum number of monitoring wells in each partition, ensuring that there are monitoring wells in each partition without over-aggregation.
S 4 . Solve multi-objective optimization model and combine the quality error analysis to optimize the well number and location of the monitoring network.
In one embodiment, the multi-objective optimization model in S 4 is calculated by NSGA-II. The calculation process is: generate the initial population firstly, read the concentration data obtained from the solute transport simulation and the vulnerability score obtained from the vulnerability assessment to calculate the objective function values, which include the number of monitoring wells, the sum of pollutant concentration value monitored, and the sum of vulnerability scores at selected monitoring sites. Calculate the non-dominated sorting and focus distance of the corresponding population according to the calculated objective function values, select, cross, and mutate to generate the next child, merge the child and the parent population, perform the NSGA-II optimization iterative calculation until the maximum iteration number is reached, exit the cycle, and finally obtain the Pareto optimal solution designed by the multi-objective optimization for groundwater pollution monitoring network. The whole process is implemented by running code programmed by MATLAB.
The calculated Pareto optimal solution reflects the trade-off relationship between the number of monitoring wells and the vulnerability score and the nitrate concentration monitored. The solution results show appropriate range of the monitoring well number and optimal layout of the monitoring network for different number of monitoring wells within the numerical range.
The quality error analysis process in S 4 is: according to the pollutant concentration (for example, nitrate concentration) at the optimal monitoring well location of different monitoring wells solved by NSGA-II, using ordinary Kriging method to calculate the concentration value of unknown nodes, and estimated spatial distribution of pollutants corresponding to the optimal layout scheme of different monitoring wells is obtained. Comparing with the total mass concentration of pollutants estimated by interpolation using monitoring concentration of all wells (such as nitrate concentration), calculating the corresponding quality error, fitting the relationship between the different well number and the quality error, and the corresponding quantity of the monitoring well within the acceptable error range is the recommended well number of optimized monitoring network. In one embodiment, after quality error analysis in S 4 , when within 15.00% is considered to be an acceptable quality error, the number of optimal monitoring wells is 12, and there is at least one monitoring well in each partition. The monitoring wells are mainly distributed in areas with high vulnerability and high nitrogen concentration of nitrate(s), which ensures the monitoring purpose and accuracy, and compared with the initial monitoring network which composed of 60 wells, the monitoring cost is reduced by 80%.
The Multi-objective optimization method for groundwater pollution monitoring network provided by the embodiment of the present invention can be applied to the optimization of the groundwater monitoring network with the groundwater source and the pollution source area.
The objects, the technical solutions and the beneficial effects of the present invention are described in detail by the above embodiments. However, the above is only the specific embodiments of the present invention, and is not intended to limit the present invention. Any modifications, equivalent substitutions, improvements, and so on made within the spirit and principles of the present invention are intended to be included within the scope of the present invention.

## 648. [CN112183719B] An intelligent detection method for total nitrogen in effluent based on multi-objective optimization-fuzzy neural network
- **Patent ID / App No**: `CN112183719B`
- **Source**: Google Patents
- **URL**: [https://patents.google.com/patent/CN112183719B/en](https://patents.google.com/patent/CN112183719B/en)
- **AI Relevancy Score**: N/A (UNAUDITED)

### 📋 Abstract
> An intelligent detection method for total nitrogen in effluent based on a multi-objective optimization-fuzzy neural network belongs to the field of sewage treatment and aims at solving the problems that the total nitrogen concentration in effluent is difficult to detect in real time and the accuracy of a predicted result is low in the sewage treatment process. Aiming at a multi-level learning objective function of a network, the intelligent detection method optimizes the network structure and parameters by adopting a multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm with global optimization capability, establishes a proper fuzzy neural network detection model, and solves the problem of poor generalization capability of a fuzzy neural network based on a single objective function; experimental results show that the method improves the prediction precision of total nitrogen in the effluent, ensures that the total nitrogen in the effluent can be accurately obtained in real time in the sewage treatment process, and simultaneously ensures the low-cost requirement in the sewage treatment plant.

### 📜 Full Specification & Deep Scrape Text
Title
An intelligent detection method for total nitrogen in effluent based on multi-objective optimization-fuzzy neural network

Abstract
An intelligent detection method for total nitrogen in effluent based on a multi-objective optimization-fuzzy neural network belongs to the field of sewage treatment and aims at solving the problems that the total nitrogen concentration in effluent is difficult to detect in real time and the accuracy of a predicted result is low in the sewage treatment process. Aiming at a multi-level learning objective function of a network, the intelligent detection method optimizes the network structure and parameters by adopting a multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm with global optimization capability, establishes a proper fuzzy neural network detection model, and solves the problem of poor generalization capability of a fuzzy neural network based on a single objective function; experimental results show that the method improves the prediction precision of total nitrogen in the effluent, ensures that the total nitrogen in the effluent can be accurately obtained in real time in the sewage treatment process, and simultaneously ensures the low-cost requirement in the sewage treatment plant.

Description
Intelligent detection method for total nitrogen in effluent based on multi-objective optimization-fuzzy neural network
Technical Field
On the basis of analysis of the running characteristics of the urban sewage treatment process, the intelligent detection of the total nitrogen concentration of the effluent is realized from the perspective of improving the fuzzy neural network optimization algorithm by establishing the intelligent detection model of the total nitrogen of the effluent based on the fuzzy neural network and simultaneously adjusting the parameters and the structure of the detection model based on the multi-target particle swarm optimization algorithm. According to the intelligent total nitrogen detection method for the water outlet based on the multi-objective optimization-fuzzy neural network, in an actual process, a learning objective function of the network can be fully optimized, the prediction precision of the network is improved by improving the generalization capability of the fuzzy neural network, and the more accurate total nitrogen detection precision of the water outlet is realized, and the intelligent total nitrogen detection method for the water outlet based on the multi-objective optimization-fuzzy neural network belongs to the field of water treatment.
Background
Years 2019, chinese Water resource publication shows: the total national water consumption in 2019 is 6021.2 hundred million cubic meters, which is 5.7 hundred million cubic meters longer than that in 2018. Along with the acceleration of urban process in China, the demand of China for fresh water resources is continuously increased, so that the sewage generation amount is increased, and therefore, sewage treatment becomes one of important work in recent years in China. The sewage treatment capability of China is greatly improved from the large-scale construction of the sewage treatment plant in the 80 s of the 20 th century to the present. The sewage treatment capacity of urban sewage treatment plants in 2019 is more than 2.1 hundred million cubic meters per day, and the method plays a positive role in preventing and controlling water pollution and protecting environment. Therefore, the method has wide application prospect on the research results of the sewage treatment process.
With the improvement of sewage treatment technology, the pollution of organic matters in sewage is suppressed, but the pollution of water is still serious due to the excessive discharge of nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus and the like. Wherein, the increase of nitrogen content is one of the main factors causing the deterioration of water quality and eutrophication, and the total nitrogen content of the effluent in sewage treatment is a basic index for measuring the effluent quality of a sewage treatment plant. Meanwhile, the total nitrogen content is used as a measurement index on a plurality of national standards such as urban sewage recycling landscape environmental water quality. Therefore, the accurate and rapid detection of the total nitrogen content in water has great significance for preventing and controlling water pollution and recycling. Currently, sewage treatment plants mainly detect total nitrogen concentration by chemical experimental means. Although the method can ensure more accurate detection precision, the method has high requirements on the operation environment and long detection time, and cannot meet the requirements of real-time detection. In recent years, the on-line instrument detection can realize the automatic detection of the water sample of the effluent, but the instrument purchase and instrument maintenance cost is higher. Therefore, how to realize low-cost and high-precision detection by using informatization technology is a key of research. Due to the nonlinear approximation capability and learning capability of the artificial neural network, the nonlinear system in the sewage treatment process can be effectively modeled, and a novel method is provided for sewage outlet water quality detection. Therefore, the invention has important practical significance in improving the detection precision of the total nitrogen concentration of the effluent.
The invention designs an intelligent detection method for total nitrogen concentration of effluent based on a multi-objective optimization-fuzzy neural network, which utilizes a partial least square algorithm to extract characteristic variables, establishes a detection model based on the fuzzy neural network, adopts a multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm with global optimization capability to optimize a multi-stage learning target of the fuzzy neural network to train the model so as to improve the generalization performance of the model, improves the detection precision of total nitrogen of the effluent, and provides an effective method for realizing accurate detection of total nitrogen of the effluent and reducing the measurement cost from the improvement of the generalization capability of the model so as to realize the actual demands of sewage treatment plants.
Disclosure of Invention
The invention has obtained the overall optimization algorithm based on multiple target particle swarms trains the intelligent detection method of total nitrogen of water outlet of the fuzzy neural network, this method adopts the least square algorithm to extract the characteristic variable in numerous process variables and confirm the main variable correlated with total nitrogen of water outlet; the fuzzy neural network is constructed by utilizing the multi-level learning target of the fuzzy neural network and simultaneously optimizing the parameters and the structure of the model by utilizing a multi-target particle swarm algorithm, so that the problem of poor generalization capability of the traditional fuzzy neural network is solved, the real-time measurement of total nitrogen in effluent is realized, and the detection precision is good.
The invention adopts the following technical scheme and implementation steps:
1. the intelligent detection method for total nitrogen in effluent based on the multi-objective optimization-fuzzy neural network is characterized by comprising the following steps:
step 1: feature variable selection

step 4: intelligent detection of total nitrogen concentration of effluent
The trained intelligent detection model of total nitrogen of the effluent is utilized to add the dosage, ORP in anaerobic, di-good last orthophosphate, pH of a water inlet cell and ammonia nitrogen NH of the water inlet cell 3 N, anoxic last nitrate nitrogen NO 3 And N, taking test samples of seven variables of effluent COD of the primary sedimentation tank as input of a detection model, and performing inverse normalization on the output of the detection model to obtain a detection value of total nitrogen concentration of the effluent.
The invention mainly comprises the following steps:
(1) Aiming at the problem that the total nitrogen content of the effluent is difficult to measure in real time, the invention provides an intelligent detection method for the total nitrogen of the effluent based on a fuzzy neural network, which aims at the long detection period of the total nitrogen of the effluent in the current sewage treatment;
(2) Aiming at the problem that a single learning target is difficult to improve the generalization capability of a fuzzy neural network, the invention provides a multi-level generalization capability evaluation index, which is used as an objective function for constructing model parameters and adjusting a structure to make up the defect of the single target;
(3) According to the multistage network learning function, the parameters and the structure of the model are simultaneously optimized by adopting an improved multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm, so that the constructed model has proper training precision and network structure.

Detailed Description
The experimental data are from a water quality analysis table of a sewage treatment plant in 2020; respectively taking water flow, ORP in anaerobic condition, ORP before hypoxia, and NO in last nitrate nitrogen of hypoxia 3 N, an aerobic pre-DO, an aerobic mid-DO, a two-aerobic DO, a water inlet cell pH, a water inlet cell SS, a water inlet cell COD, a water inlet cell ammonia nitrogen NH 3 Effluent C of N and primary sedimentation tankThe actual detection data of OD, external reflux flowmeter, dosing amount, two good end orthophosphate and residual sludge discharge amount are experimental sample data, and 500 groups of available data are left after abnormal experimental samples are removed, wherein 350 groups are used as training samples, and the other 150 groups are used as test samples.

Claims
Translated from Chinese
1. An intelligent detection method for total nitrogen in effluent based on multi-objective optimization-fuzzy neural network. By establishing an intelligent detection model based on fuzzy neural network, the multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to complete the structure and parameter adjustment of the fuzzy neural network detection model to achieve Real-time detection of total nitrogen concentration in effluent is characterized by including the following steps:
Step 1: Feature variable selection
Step 1.1: Analyze the sewage treatment process, and use the least squares method to extract characteristic variables from multiple process variables that affect the total nitrogen concentration of the effluent; determine the dosage, anaerobic ORP, diphosphate orthophosphate, and influent water. Chamber pH, inlet chamber ammonia nitrogen NH 3 N, anoxic final nitrate nitrogen NO 3 N, and primary sedimentation tank effluent COD are the seven key characteristic variables that affect the total nitrogen concentration of the effluent;
Step 1.2: The seven characteristic variables obtained in step 1.1 are normalized to [0,1] respectively, and the output variable effluent total nitrogen is normalized to [0,1];
Step 2: Establish a model for intelligent detection of total nitrogen in effluent water

The number of neurons is P, the number of neurons in the regular layer is Q, the number of neurons in the output layer is 1, P and Q are both positive integers between [2,15], and P=Q; set N as a training sample The number of effluent total nitrogen detection models is x(n)=[x 1 (n), x 2 (n),…, x 7 (n)], x 1 (n) is the The volume of dosing in the nth sample, x 2 (n) is the ORP concentration in the anaerobic medium in the nth sample after normalization, x 3 (n) is the concentration of ORP in the nth sample after normalization Phosphate concentration, x 4 (n) is the pH value of the water inlet chamber in the nth sample after normalization, x 5 (n) is the ammonia nitrogen NH 3 N concentration in the water inlet chamber in the nth sample after normalization, x 6 (n) is the anoxic final nitrate nitrogen NO 3 N concentration in the nth sample after normalization, x 7 (n) is the COD concentration of the primary sedimentation tank effluent in the nth sample after normalization, and the output is is the actual concentration of total nitrogen in the effluent in the nth sample after normalization, n=1,2,...,N.
