Claims
A quantum circuit determining method for determining a quantum circuit according to a quantum circuit design task, performed by a computer device forming a hybrid device environment including a classical computer and a quantum computer, the method comprising:
sampling (101), by the classical computer, an initial circuit unit pool according to an initial sampling manner to determine K groups of circuit units, K being a positive integer,
and constructing and generating K candidate quantum circuits based on the K groups of circuit units, wherein each group of circuit units comprises a plurality of circuit units for constructing and generating a candidate quantum circuit, a candidate quantum circuit has a multi-layer structure, each layer includes a plurality of filling positions for filling a circuit unit, the plurality of filling positions in a same layer are connected to one another in a preset manner, and a gap in a candidate quantum circuit is filled with circuit units being single-bit quantum gates so that a set of the single-bit quantum gates filling the gap proves an identity matrix,
determining (102), by the quantum computer, a performance evaluation index corresponding to the K candidate quantum circuits, wherein the performance evaluation index is an operation result of an objective function (204), wherein the objective function is specified according to the quantum circuit design task;
updating (103), by the classical computer, the sampling manner and a circuit unit in the initial circuit unit pool based on the performance evaluation index, to determine an updated sampling manner and an updated circuit unit pool;
sampling (104, 208), by the classical computer, the updated circuit unit pool according to the updated sampling manner to determine updated K groups of circuit units, and constructing and generating updated K candidate quantum circuits based on the updated K groups of circuit units; and
in response to a cycle termination condition being satisfied, determining (105), by the classical computer, a target quantum circuit from the updated K candidate quantum circuits.
The method according to claim 1, wherein the sampling an initial circuit unit pool according to an initial sampling manner to determine K groups of circuit units, and constructing and generating K candidate quantum circuits based on the K groups of circuit units comprises:
constructing (201) an initial probability model, the initial probability model comprising p × c parameters, p representing a maximum number of circuit units, and c representing a total number of circuit units in the initial circuit unit pool;
sampling (202) the initial circuit unit pool K times based on the initial probability model, to determine the K groups of circuit units, each time of sampling being performed to determine one group of circuit units; and
constructing and generating (203) the K candidate quantum circuits based on the K groups of circuit units.
The method according to claim 2, wherein the updating the sampling manner and a circuit unit in the initial circuit unit pool based on the performance evaluation index, to determine an updated sampling manner and an updated circuit unit pool comprises:
computing (205) first gradient information and second gradient information based on the performance evaluation index, the first gradient information being gradient information of a model parameter of the initial probability model, and the second gradient information being gradient information of a circuit parameter of the circuit unit in the initial circuit unit pool;
updating (206) the model parameter of the initial probability model based on the first gradient information, to determine an updated probability model; and
updating (207) the circuit parameter of the circuit unit in the initial circuit unit pool based on the second gradient information, to determine the updated circuit unit pool.
The method according to claim 3, wherein the computing first gradient information and second gradient information based on the performance evaluation index comprises:
computing a derivative of the objective function relative to the model parameter of the initial probability model, to determine the first gradient information; and
computing a derivative of the objective function relative to the circuit parameter of the circuit unit in the initial circuit unit pool, to determine the second gradient information.

computing K operation results of the objective function respectively corresponding to the K candidate quantum circuits; and
determining the performance evaluation index based on the K operation results.

determining a candidate quantum circuit with a largest generation probability from the updated K candidate quantum circuits, wherein the generation probability of the candidate quantum circuit is a proportion of the number of same candidate quantum circuit among the number of updated K candidate quantum circuits; and
determining the candidate quantum circuit with the largest generation probability as the target quantum circuit.

Detailed Description
To make the objects, technical solutions and advantages of the present application more clear, embodiments of the present application will be described in further detail below with reference to the accompanying drawings.
Cloud technology (cloud technology) refers to a hosting technology for unifying series of resources such as hardware, software, network and the like in a wide area network or a local area network to realize calculation, storage, processing and sharing of data.
The cloud technology is a general term of network technology, information technology, integration technology, management platform technology, application technology and the like applied based on a cloud computing business model, can form a resource pool, is used as required, and is flexible and convenient. Cloud computing technology will become an important support. Background services of the technical network system require a large amount of computing and storage resources, such as video websites, picture-like websites and more web portals. With the high development and application of the internet industry, each article may have its own identification mark and needs to be transmitted to a background system for logic processing, data in different levels are processed separately, and various industrial data need strong system background support and can be realized through cloud computing.
Cloud technology relates to basic technologies such as cloud computing, cloud storage, databases and big data, and cloud applications provided based on the cloud technology include medical cloud, cloud internet of things, cloud security, cloud calling, private cloud, public cloud, hybrid cloud, cloud games, cloud education, cloud conference, cloud social contact, artificial intelligent cloud service and the like. With the development of cloud technology and the application of cloud technology in different fields, more and more cloud applications will appear.
Generally, a system constructed based on cloud technology includes a server and a terminal. The server may be an independent physical server, a server cluster or a distributed system formed by a plurality of physical servers, or a cloud server providing basic cloud computing services such as a cloud service, a cloud database, cloud computing, a cloud function, cloud storage, a Network service, cloud communication, a middleware service, a domain name service, a security service, a CDN (Content Delivery Network), a big data and artificial intelligence platform. The terminal may be, but is not limited to, a smart phone, a tablet computer, a laptop computer, a desktop computer, a smart speaker, a smart watch, and the like. The terminal and the server may be directly or indirectly connected through wired or wireless communication, and the application is not limited herein.
A quantum computer (quantum computer) is a machine that performs calculations using the principles of quantum mechanics. Based on the superposition principle of quantum mechanics and quantum entanglement, the quantum computer has stronger parallel processing capability and can solve the problem that some classical computers are difficult to calculate. The zero resistance property of superconducting qubits and the manufacturing process close to that of integrated circuits make the quantum computing system constructed by using superconducting qubits one of the most promising systems for practical quantum computing at present.
Quantum processor refers to a quantum computer processor, i.e., a processor of a quantum computer. The quantum processor may include one or more quantum chips.
A quantum chip (or referred to as a superconducting quantum chip) is a central processing unit of a quantum computer and is a core component of the quantum computer. The quantum chip integrates quantum circuits on a substrate, and further bears the function of quantum information processing. In view of the development process of the conventional computer, the research on the quantum computer needs to be integrated to realize commercialization and industrial upgrading after overcoming the bottleneck technology. Superconducting systems, semiconductor quantum dot systems, micro-nano photonics systems, and even atomic and ionic systems, all want to go the path of chipization. From the development point of view, superconducting quantum chip systems are technically moved in front of other physical systems; the traditional semiconductor quantum dot system is also an object of research, because after all, the traditional semiconductor industry has developed well, for example, once a semiconductor quantum chip breaks through a threshold value of fault-tolerant quantum computation in the phase-coherent time and the control precision, the traditional semiconductor quantum dot system is expected to integrate the existing achievement of the traditional semiconductor industry, and the development cost is saved.
In view of the advantages of quantum computers, quantum computers may be used for some processing and computation in future systems built based on cloud technology to provide better services.
Before the technical solutions of the present application are introduced, some key terms referred to in the present application are explained.
1. Quantum computing: based on the quantum-logic computational approach, the basic unit of storage data is a quantum bit (qubit).
2. Quantum bit: basic unit of quantum computation. Conventional computers use 0 and 1 as the basic units of the binary system. Except that quantum computation can process 0 and 1 simultaneously, the system can be in a linear superposition state of 0 and 1: phi>＝α|0>+β|1>Here, α and β represent the complex probability amplitude of the system at 0 and 1.Their modulus squared | α 2 ，|β| 2 Representing the probabilities at 0 and 1, respectively.
3. Quantum wires: one representation of a quantum general purpose computer represents a hardware implementation of a corresponding quantum algorithm/program under a quantum gate model.
4. Hamilton amount: a matrix describing the hermitian conjugate of the total energy of the quantum system. The hamiltonian is a physical word, an operator describing the total energy of the system, usually denoted by H.
5. The eigenstate: for a Hamiltonian matrix H, the equation is satisfied: the solution of H | ψ > ═ E | ψ > is referred to as the eigenstate | ψ > of H, with the eigenenergy E. The ground state corresponds to the eigenstate where the quantum system has the lowest energy.
6. Neural network Architecture Search (NAS for short): in the key field of automatic Machine Learning (AutoML for short), various different underlying technical schemes such as reinforcement Learning, genetic algorithm and microstructural search are utilized to achieve the purpose of automatically searching and constructing a neural network topology and structure with excellent performance by a computer.
7. Quantum Architecture Search (QAS) is a generic term for a series of tasks and protocols that attempt to automate and program the structure, pattern, and arrangement of Quantum wires. Conventionally, the work of quantum structure search usually adopts greedy algorithm, reinforcement learning or genetic algorithm as its core technology.
8. Quantum classical mixture calculation: the inner layer is calculated by using the quantum wire, and the outer layer is calculated by using a calculation mode of adjusting the parameters of the variable-component quantum wire by using a traditional classical optimizer, so that the advantages of quantum calculation can be exerted to the maximum extent, and the calculation method is believed to be one of important directions with potential for proving the advantages of the quantum.
9. Quantum approximation Optimization Algorithm (Quantum approximation Optimization Algorithm, QAOA for short): one particular quantum wire structure assumes that the quantum states produced by such quantum wires can be used to approximate the results of a NP (Non-deterministic Polynomial) fully combinatorial mathematical optimization problem, which is a classical mixed-quantum computational paradigm. The definition of this particular quantum wire is as follows:
wherein H c ，H b Mixer and phase hamilton quantities, gamma and beta are variation parameters. In general, H c The same as the objective function we want to optimize. Phi 0 >Is an initial wave function which is easy to prepare, and is usually in a direct integral state
And | ψ > is the objective state wave function. P represents the number of layers of the QOA assumed arrangement, the larger P is, the closer to adiabatic approximation is, the closer to the theoretical result is the objective wave function, and the better the approximation effect is.
10. Maximum cut (max cut) problem: a typical complexity is NP-complete graph theory combinatorial optimization problem, which is also the problem that the QOA algorithm was used for solving at first. MAX CUT refers to finding a node bisection scheme that maximizes the sum of the number of edges (or edge weights) across two nodes, for a graph given node and edge connections.
11. NISQ (noise Intermediate-Scale Quantum): recent medium-scale noisy quantum hardware is the current stage and focus of research in the development of quantum computing. This stage of quantum computation cannot be applied as an engine for general purpose computation for a while due to size and noise limitations, but results beyond the strongest classical computer have been achieved on part of the problem, which is often referred to as quantum dominance or quantum dominance.
12. Quantum Error cancellation (Quantum Error cancellation): corresponding to Quantum Error Correction (Quantum Error Correction), the method is a series of Quantum Error mitigation and noise suppression schemes with smaller resource cost under hardware in the NISQ era. The resources required are significantly reduced compared to a complete quantum error correction, while possibly only being suitable for specific tasks, not for general purpose solutions.
13. Variational-Quantum-intrinsic solver (Variational-Quantum-eigenresolver, VQE for short): the estimation of the ground state energy of a specific quantity of subsystems through a variation line is also a typical quantum classical hybrid calculation paradigm, and has wide application in the field of quantum chemistry.
One of the more conventional schemes for constructing quantum wires is to use genetic algorithms. The basic method is that after a part of the circuit structure of the quantum circuit is fixed, a gene algorithm is adopted to find the next optimal circuit structure, and a complete quantum circuit is finally constructed by repeating the process for many times. However, the genetic algorithm itself has the problems of large calculation amount and low efficiency, so that the construction of the quantum line is very complicated and inefficient. Furthermore, the schemes are less versatile, such as requiring genetic algorithms that select different variants for different quantum computing tasks.
The present application provides a technical solution for constructing a Quantum wire, which may be referred to as a Differential Quantum Architecture Search (DQAS) scheme (or a Quantum structure Search framework). Under the micro quantum structure search framework provided by the application, the design problems of different types of quantum lines are highly abstracted and unified, so that the framework has extremely strong universality, and the important problems of a plurality of sub-fields can be solved without modification. For example, the quantum wire constructed by the framework can be used in a plurality of sub-fields of quantum computation and quantum information processing, including but not limited to preparation of quantum states, design of quantum wires, quantum compiling, optimal variation structure searching, quantum error suppression and the like. The framework can be adopted to automatically design and find the optimal quantum circuit structure and circuit parameters, thereby realizing the multi-target, full-automatic and end-to-end quantum circuit automatic design.

The line parameters of the quantum lines are variation parameters, and the variation parameters refer to that the line parameters of the quantum lines are updatable (namely, adjustable and modifiable), so that the line parameters of the quantum lines can be updated through an optimizer to achieve the purpose of optimizing the objective function. By treating an arbitrary quantum wire as being stacked from a series of unitary matrices, our search scheme is not limited to hypothetical wire search of the classical mixed computation paradigm of quanta, but is applicable to a wider range of problems with or without wire parameters. That is, we can also use this scheme to find the optimal quantum wire design for a fully discrete quantum gate arrangement, which is compatible with the presence or absence of the variation parameters of the wire itself.

In order to embed the parameters controlling the quantum wire structure into the continuous domain, the present application considers the process of wire unit selection that makes up the quantum wire as being controlled by a probabilistic model. This probability model P may be a sufficiently generic energy model or an autoregressive (autoregressive) network. In an example, the simplest layer-by-layer discrete distribution can be selected to describe the process of selecting the line units from the line unit pool for quantum line construction. This probability model has a continuous parameter α, whereby the structure parameter k of discrete integers, which determine the structure of the corresponding quantum wire, can be sampled from the probability model P (k, α).

Before describing the embodiments of the method of the present application, the operating environment of the method is described. The quantum wire structure determination method provided in the embodiments of the present application may be implemented by a classical Computer (such as a PC (Personal Computer)), for example, by the classical Computer executing a corresponding Computer program to implement the method; the method can also be executed in the environment of a mixed device of a classical computer and a quantum computer, for example, the classical computer executes steps of line sampling, parameter updating, line selection and the like, and the quantum computer executes steps of determining performance evaluation indexes (such as an objective function) corresponding to candidate quantum lines, and the like, because the quantum lines are directly deployed on the quantum computer to execute, compared with the quantum lines simulated on the classical computer, the corresponding performance evaluation results should be better theoretically.
In the following method embodiments, for convenience of description, only the execution subject of each step is described as a computer device. It should be understood that the computer device may be a classical computer, or may include a hybrid execution environment of a classical computer and a quantum computer, which is not limited in this application.
Referring to fig. 1, a flow chart of a method for determining a quantum wire according to an embodiment of the present application is shown. The execution subject of each step of the method can be computer equipment. The method comprises the following steps (101-105):
step 101, sampling K groups of line units from the initial line unit pool according to an initial sampling mode, and constructing and generating K candidate quantum lines, where K is a positive integer.
The line unit pool comprises a plurality of selectable line units. In the present embodiment, a wire unit is a basic unit constituting a quantum wire, and a quantum wire may include one or more wire units. In the case where the quantum wire includes a plurality of wire units, the connection relationship between the respective wire units may be defined or designed in advance. In one example, a quantum wire is a multi-layer structure, each layer includes a wire unit, and the layers are connected in sequence, for example, the output result of a wire unit of a certain layer can be used as the input data of a wire unit of the next layer, and further calculation or processing is performed through the wire unit of the next layer. In another example, a quantum wire is a multi-layer structure, each layer containing one or more sites to be filled for filling the wire units. In the case where a plurality of positions to be filled are included in the same layer, the positions to be filled may be connected in advance in a predetermined manner.
Alternatively, for some basic operations that may be involved in a quantum computing task, a corresponding one of the line units is designed for each basic operation. For example, a line unit may be a single-bit quantum gate, a layer of quantum gates, or a time-dependent evolution of a hamiltonian, which is not limited in the embodiments of the present application.
The sampling mode refers to a mode of selecting line units from a line unit pool. One or more line units are selected from the line unit pool in each sampling, and the one or more line units selected in each sampling form a group of line units, namely each group of line units comprises at least one line unit. In the embodiment of the present application, each group of wire units is used to construct a candidate quantum wire. In addition, the line cells included in each group of line cells are repeatable. That is, the sampling process is put back to ensure that each line unit is reusable in the finally constructed quantum line.
For example, the initial line unit pool includes 5 line units with numbers of 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively. Assume that 3 samples are taken from the initial pool of line cells in an initial sampling manner to obtain 3 groups of line cells. Suppose that a set of line units obtained by sampling for the 1 st time comprises 3 line units with the serial numbers of 2, 1 and 3 in sequence, a set of line units obtained by sampling for the 2 nd time comprises 3 line units with the serial numbers of 2, 1 and 1 in sequence, and a set of line units obtained by sampling for the 3 rd time comprises 3 line units with the serial numbers of 2, 1 and 4 in sequence. Then, 3 candidate quantum wires are constructed and generated according to the sampling result.
And step 102, determining performance evaluation indexes corresponding to the K candidate quantum lines.
The performance evaluation index is a parameter for quantitatively evaluating the performance of the candidate quantum wire. In the embodiment of the present application, the performance evaluation indexes corresponding to the K candidate quantum wires are parameters for evaluating the comprehensive performance or the average performance of the K candidate quantum wires, and reflect the overall situation or the average situation of the respective performances of the K candidate quantum wires.
In an exemplary embodiment, an objective function is employed to characterize the performance evaluation index described above. The objective function is a mathematical function used to calculate whether the quantum wire generated by the construction achieves the task optimization goal. For example, as introduced above, different objective functions may be set for different quantum wire design tasks.
And 103, updating the sampling mode and the line units in the line unit pool based on the performance evaluation indexes to obtain an updated sampling mode and an updated line unit pool.
The performance evaluation index is used for guiding the adjustment of the sampling mode and the line parameters of the line unit so as to sample candidate quantum lines with better performance. On one hand, updating the sampling mode based on the performance evaluation index to optimize the sampling mode and select a better combination scheme of the line units from the line unit pool; on the other hand, the line units in the line unit pool are updated based on the performance evaluation indexes, for example, the line parameters of the line units are updated, so that the performance of a single line unit is optimized, and the overall performance of the constructed quantum line is further promoted.
And step 104, sampling K groups of line units from the updated line unit pool according to the updated sampling mode, and constructing and generating K candidate quantum lines.
The sampling process in step 104 is the same as or similar to the sampling process described in step 101, except that the sampling mode and the line parameters of the line units in the line unit pool are updated, and in step 104, K groups of line units are sampled from the updated line unit pool according to the updated sampling mode.
The number of times of sampling in step 104 may be the same as or different from the number of times of sampling in step 101. For example, in the case where the number of times of sampling in step 104 is the same as the number of times of sampling in step 101, K in step 104 is also equal to 10, as K in step 101 is equal to 10. For another example, in the case where the number of times of sampling in step 104 is different from the number of times of sampling in step 101, K is equal to 10 in step 101 and K is equal to 8 in step 104. Because the probability model corresponding to the sampling mode tends to be converged in the circulation process, the value of the sampling number K of each round is reduced in a self-adaptive manner, and the performance can be kept while the computing resources are effectively saved.
After the step 104, the steps 102 to 104 may be executed in a loop to continuously update the optimized sampling manner and the optimized line parameters, so as to construct a better candidate quantum line, and the loop process is stopped until the loop termination condition is satisfied.
The cycle stop condition is a condition that is set in advance to trigger the stop of the above cycle process. Illustratively, the loop abort condition includes, but is not limited to, at least one of: the last K candidate quantum wires generated are the same, the same number of sub-wires with the same number larger than the threshold number exist in the last K candidate quantum wires generated, the performance evaluation indexes corresponding to the last K candidate quantum wires generated meet the set index requirement, the execution times of the cycle process reach the set times, and the like, which is not limited in the embodiment of the present application.
In step 105, a target quantum wire is determined from the K candidate quantum wires generated last time when the loop termination condition is satisfied.
The target quantum line is a quantum line determined from the K candidate quantum lines generated last, and the target quantum line may be one selected from the K candidate quantum lines generated last. In the embodiments of the present application, the target quantum wire is the quantum wire generated for the final structure to achieve a certain predetermined quantum wire design task.
In an exemplary embodiment, from among the K candidate quantum wires generated last time, a candidate quantum wire whose generation probability is the largest is determined; the candidate quantum line with the highest generation probability is determined as the target quantum line. The generation probability of a candidate quantum wire may be a ratio of the number of the candidate quantum wires in the K candidate quantum wires. For example, the number of candidate quantum wires generated at the last time is 10, 9 of which are the same (denoted as quantum wire a), and the other 1 is different from the other 9 (denoted as quantum wire B). Then, the probability of generation of the quantum wire a is 9/10 ═ 0.9, the probability of generation of the quantum wire B is 1/10 ═ 0.1, and the quantum wire a can be selected as the final target quantum wire.
In summary, for different types of quantum line design problems, a target quantum line for solving the corresponding problem can be constructed by using the technical scheme of the present application, so that the different types of quantum line design problems are highly abstracted and unified, and the scheme has strong universality and universality.
In addition, compared with the defects of large calculation consumption and slow convergence existing in the genetic algorithm, the technical scheme of the application only needs to determine the performance evaluation index corresponding to the candidate quantum circuit obtained by sampling, and then synchronously updates the sampling mode and the circuit units in the circuit unit pool based on the performance evaluation index, so that the candidate quantum circuit with better performance can be quickly constructed, the calculation amount is reduced, and the efficiency of finally determining the target quantum circuit is improved.
Please refer to fig. 2, which shows a flowchart of a method for determining a quantum wire according to another embodiment of the present application. The execution subject of each step of the method can be computer equipment. The method comprises the following steps (201-211):
step 201, constructing an initial probability model, wherein the probability model comprises p × c parameters; where p represents the maximum number of line units and c represents the total number of line units in the pool of line units.
In the embodiment of the present application, a probabilistic model may be used as a sampling method to sample and obtain a plurality of groups of line units from a line unit pool. The probability model is a parameter-containing probability model which comprises p × c parameters; where p represents the maximum number of line units and c represents the total number of line units in the pool of line units.
The maximum number of line units is the maximum number of line units that can be included in a target quantum line that is finally constructed and generated to achieve a predetermined quantum line design task. For example, if the maximum number of line units is 6, the actual number of line units included in the target quantum line generated by the final configuration should be less than or equal to 6, in which case, one group of line units acquired by sampling each time may include 6 line units, or may include less than 6 line units. In one example, the number of line units included in the target quantum line is a predetermined number, for example, if the number of line units included in the target quantum line is specified to be 6 in advance, then a group of line units obtained by sampling each time includes 6 line units. In this case, the maximum number of line units is the predetermined number, and the predetermined number may be determined according to the number of design layers or the number of positions to be filled of the target quantum line.
The line unit pool comprises a plurality of line units. As described above, any quantum wire can be regarded as being formed by stacking a series of unitary matrices, and thus the cell pool of wires can include equivalent wires corresponding to a plurality of unitary matrices. The line unit pool may also be referred to as an operator pool or other names, which is not limited in the embodiments of the present application.
In the embodiment of the present application, it is assumed that the model parameter of the probabilistic model is α, and α includes p × c parameters. For example, α can be regarded as a matrix of p rows × c columns, where the element in the ith row and the jth column in the matrix represents the probability of filling the jth line cell in the line cell pool at the ith to-be-filled position of the target quantum line, i is a positive integer less than or equal to p, and j is a positive integer less than or equal to c.
Step 202, based on the initial probability model, sampling the initial line unit pool for K times, and obtaining a group of line units each time, thereby obtaining K groups of line units.
In each sampling process, a structure parameter k is generated based on the model parameter α of the probability model P (k, α), and the structure parameter k may include a plurality of discrete values for representing the line units obtained by the sampling. For example, the line unit pool includes 5 line units with numbers of 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively, the configuration parameter k includes (2, 1, 3), and it indicates that a group of line units sampled from the line unit pool includes 3 line units with numbers of 2, 1, and 3 in sequence. When the model parameters α of the probabilistic model P (k, α) are the same, the structural parameters k generated by sampling any two times may be the same or different. For example, the structural parameters k generated by two sampling operations are the same and are (2, 1, 3); for another example, the structural parameter k generated by two sampling operations before and after the sampling operation is different, where the former operation is (2, 1, 3) and the latter operation is (2, 1, 4).
In addition, assuming that the number of line parameters of each line unit in the line unit pool is l, a line parameter pool may be maintained, where the line parameter pool includes the line parameters of each line unit in the line unit pool at each to-be-filled location, that is, the line parameter pool includes p × c × l parameters.
Step 203, constructing and generating K candidate quantum wires based on the K groups of wire units.
For each set of line cells sampled, a candidate quantum line is constructed accordingly. The connection relationship between the line units may be predefined or designed, and this is not limited in the embodiments of the present application.
And step 204, determining performance evaluation indexes corresponding to the K candidate quantum lines, wherein the performance evaluation indexes are operation results of the objective function.

For example, by calculating gradient information of the target function with respect to the line parameters of the target quantum line, the line parameters of the target quantum line are also updated by using a gradient descent algorithm, so as to continuously optimize the line parameters of the target quantum line, thereby improving the performance of the target quantum line.
And step 211, obtaining the target quantum circuit with optimized parameters under the condition that the adjustment stopping condition is met.
The adjustment suspension condition is a condition that is set in advance to trigger the stop of the adjustment of the line parameter of the target quantum line. Illustratively, the adjustment abort condition includes, but is not limited to, at least one of: the performance evaluation index of the target quantum circuit reaches a preset index, the number of times of adjusting the circuit parameter of the target quantum circuit reaches a set number, and the like, which is not limited in the embodiment of the present application.
In the embodiment of the present application, the target quantum wire with optimized parameters is a quantum wire generated in the final structure and used for achieving a certain predetermined quantum wire design task.
In an exemplary embodiment, after constructing the generated K candidate quantum wires, the following steps are further included: for the jth line unit in the ith candidate quantum line, acquiring the line parameter of the jth line unit from the line parameter pool according to the position of the jth line unit in the line unit pool and the position of the jth line unit in the ith candidate quantum line; the line parameter pool comprises line parameters of each line unit in the line unit pool at each position to be filled; i is a positive integer less than or equal to K, and j is a positive integer. The line parameter pool may include p × c sets of line parameters, the (i, j) th set of line parameters is a line parameter when the jth line unit in the line unit pool is filled to the ith position to be filled, i is a positive integer less than or equal to p, and j is a positive integer less than or equal to c.
By the method, the line parameters of the line units are bound with the positions to be filled by the parameter binding mechanism, so that the line parameters of each line unit can be simply and efficiently acquired from the line parameter pool after new candidate quantum lines are constructed and generated. In addition, when the line parameters of each line unit in the line unit pool are updated based on the second gradient information, the line parameters stored in the line parameter pool need to be updated synchronously, so that the accuracy of the line parameters acquired from the line parameter pool is ensured.
In an exemplary embodiment, for a more stable training process, training techniques that arise in NAS and broader machine learning field studies may be introduced and developed, including but not limited to early stop, multi-start, line variation parameter pre-heating training, training verification dataset separately optimizing two sets of parameters, post-processing and grid search of better training results, progressive layer-by-layer training, adding a running average of an objective function as a baseline (baseline) to reduce estimation variance during montecary gradient estimation, line parameters adding random noise to smooth energy loss, adding regular and penalty terms to support multiple objectives at the objective function, smaller-scale agent tasks and migratory learning, etc.
The more important is the addition of the regular term, and since the model parameters of the probabilistic model determine the sampling times and the probability of each line unit, the regular term based on the model parameters can be defined correspondingly, so that certain types of line units (such as a single-bit quantum gate) are encouraged, that is, the sampling times and the probability of the line units of the type are promoted; alternatively, some types of line units (e.g., two-bit quantum gates) are suppressed, i.e., the number and probability of sampling for that type of line unit is reduced. For example, the following regularization term is added to the objective function L, and the objective function L after the regularization term is added can be represented as Δ L:
where c represents the number of line units in the pool of line units, p is the number of locations to be filled, p (k) i K) is the probability of filling the kth line cell at the ith candidate fill position, λ is the weight of the regularization term, and q represents the number of two-bit quantum gates in the line cell.
The self-defined regular term mode is introduced, so that the sampling flexibility and controllability of the line unit are improved, the performance of the finally constructed and generated quantum line is improved, and the quantum noise level of the quantum line is reduced.
In summary, the technical solution provided by the embodiment of the present application widens the search domain of the quantum line to a continuous space, so that automatic differentiation and random gradient descent are possible, which greatly reduces the consumption of computing resources, and simultaneously, convergence can be better ensured.
In addition, in the parameter optimization process, the model parameters and the line parameters can be simultaneously optimized based on the two gradient information by calculating the first gradient information and the second gradient information, so that a multi-objective parameter optimization scheme is realized, and the quantum line construction efficiency is favorably improved.

Please refer to fig. 4, which shows a flowchart of a method for determining a quantum wire according to another embodiment of the present application. The execution subject of each step of the method can be computer equipment. The method comprises the following steps (401-403):
step 401, select N line units from a line unit pool, where the line unit pool includes a plurality of line units, each line unit is an equivalent quantum line corresponding to a unitary matrix, and N is an integer greater than 1.
The line unit pool comprises a plurality of selectable line units. In the present embodiment, a wire unit is a basic unit constituting a quantum wire, and a quantum wire may include one or more wire units. In the case where the quantum wire includes a plurality of wire units, the connection relationship between the respective wire units may be defined or designed in advance. In one example, a quantum wire is a multi-layer structure, each layer includes a wire unit, and the layers are connected in sequence, for example, the output result of a wire unit of a certain layer can be used as the input data of a wire unit of the next layer, and further calculation or processing is performed through the wire unit of the next layer. In another example, a quantum wire is a multi-layer structure, each layer containing one or more sites to be filled for filling the wire units. In the case where a plurality of positions to be filled are included in the same layer, the positions to be filled may be connected in advance in a predetermined manner.
Alternatively, for some basic operations that may be involved in a quantum computing task, a corresponding one of the line units is designed for each basic operation. For example, a line unit may be a single-bit quantum gate, a layer of quantum gates, or a time-dependent evolution of a hamiltonian, which is not limited in the embodiments of the present application.
In the embodiments of the present application, the quantum wires are divided into wire units as a granularity, and one quantum wire may be formed by connecting a plurality of wire units according to a certain connection manner. Thus, to construct a quantum wire for performing some quantum computing task, a number of wire units may be selected from a pool of wire units.
In a possible embodiment, N line units are selected from a pool of line units in some sampling manner. The sampling mode refers to a mode of selecting line units from a line unit pool. Each sampling selects N line units from the line unit pool, and the N line units selected by the sampling form a group of line units, namely each group of line units comprises N line units. In addition, the line unit included in the N line units is repeatable. That is, the sampling process is put back to ensure that each line unit is reusable in the finally constructed quantum line.
In an exemplary embodiment, the sampling manner may be a probabilistic model, and regarding a manner of sampling and obtaining the line unit through the probabilistic model, reference may be made to the description in the above embodiments, and details are not described here again.
In step 402, line parameters corresponding to the N line units are determined, where the line parameters are used to define operations performed by the line units, and the line parameters are updatable.
For a line unit, the line unit has corresponding line parameters, which define the operation performed by the line unit. That is, the operation performed by a line unit is related to the line parameters of the line unit, in addition to the structure of the line unit. After N line units are selected from the line unit pool in step 401, the structure of each line unit is established, and then line parameters of each line unit are acquired through step 402.
In the embodiment of the present application, the line parameter of the line unit is a variation parameter, that is, the line parameter of the line unit is updatable (i.e., adjustable and modifiable), so that the line parameter of the line unit can be updated if necessary to improve the performance of the line unit.
In an exemplary embodiment, a line parameter pool may be maintained that includes line parameters for each line unit in the line unit pool at each location to be filled. And for the ith line unit in the N line units, acquiring the line parameters of the ith line unit from a line parameter pool according to the position to be filled of the ith line unit. By the mode, the line parameters of the line units are bound with the positions to be filled by the parameter binding mechanism, so that the line parameters of each line unit can be simply and efficiently acquired from the line parameter pool when the quantum line is constructed and generated.
In step 403, a generated quantum wire is constructed based on the N wire units and the wire parameters corresponding to the N wire units.
After obtaining the N line units and the line parameters corresponding to the N line units, a quantum line is constructed and generated, wherein the quantum line includes the N line units, and the line parameters of the quantum line include the line parameters corresponding to the N line units. In addition, the connection relationship between the line units may be predefined or designed, which is not limited in the embodiments of the present application.
In an exemplary embodiment, as shown in fig. 5, the step 403 further includes the following steps:
step 404, determine the performance evaluation index corresponding to the quantum wire.
The performance evaluation index is a parameter for quantitatively evaluating the performance of the quantum wire. In an exemplary embodiment, an objective function is employed to characterize the performance evaluation index described above. The objective function is a mathematical function used to calculate whether the quantum wire generated by the construction achieves the task optimization goal. For example, as introduced above, different objective functions may be set for different quantum wire design tasks.
Step 405, based on the performance evaluation index, calculates target gradient information, which is gradient information of the line parameters of the quantum line.
In the embodiment of the present application, target gradient information is obtained by calculating gradient information of the target function with respect to the line parameters of the quantum lines, and the target gradient information is used to guide updating of the line parameters of the quantum lines.
In one example, the derivative of the objective function with respect to the line parameters of the quantum line is calculated, resulting in target gradient information. Illustratively, the derivative formula employed to calculate the target gradient information is:
wherein,
represents the derivative of the objective function L with respect to the line parameter θ of the quantum line U (k, θ).
Step 406, updating the line parameters of the quantum line based on the target gradient information to obtain an updated quantum line.
For example, the line parameters of the quantum line are updated by adopting a gradient descent algorithm so as to continuously optimize the line parameters of each line unit, thereby improving the overall performance of the quantum line.
In the embodiment of the present application, since the objective function is a differentiable function, the corresponding gradient information can be calculated in a derivation manner, so that the line parameters can be updated and optimized by using a gradient descent algorithm, so as to continuously improve the performance of the quantum line.
In summary, according to the technical scheme provided by the embodiment of the present application, a quantum line is regarded as being formed by stacking equivalent quantum lines corresponding to a series of unitary matrices, so that the quantum line is divided into individual line units, an optional line unit is provided by constructing a line unit pool, and a line unit is selected from the line unit pool to construct the quantum line, thereby realizing a search of a micro-quantum structure and providing a quantum line construction scheme with strong universality and universality.
In addition, since the line parameters of each line unit included in the quantum line are updatable, the performance of the quantum line can be improved by updating (i.e., adjusting) the line parameters. Furthermore, as the target function corresponding to the quantum line is a differentiable function, the corresponding gradient information can be calculated in a derivation mode, so that the line parameters can be updated and optimized by adopting a gradient descent algorithm, and the performance of the quantum line is continuously improved.
In addition, compared with the method for constructing the quantum circuit by adopting the genetic algorithm, the genetic algorithm searches a part of circuit structure with local optimization section by section, so that the finally constructed complete quantum circuit has the problem of non-overall optimization.
It should be noted that, for the details not described in detail in this embodiment, reference may be made to the description in the other embodiments above.
Next, an experimental case in which the micro quantum structure search framework provided by the present application is applied to a specific quantum line design problem will be described. Three types of problems are considered respectively to show the application and the prospect of the search framework of the micro quantum structure.
Case one, GHZ (Greenberger Horne-Zeiling) quantum state preparation and Bell state circuit design.
In the following example, we adopt the operator pool and coding scheme as single-bit and two-bit quantum gates, and the kind of quantum gate and the number of qubit lines in it determine the composition of the operator pool.
The GHZ quantum state is defined as
This state, known as the schrodinger cat state, has many applications in both theoretical and quantum information practice. The micro quantum structure search framework provided by the application can automatically design a corresponding quantum state preparation line. The target function is the inner product of the quantum line output state and the theoretical GHZ state. By gradually reducing the number p of trained gates and searching in a manner of ensuring performance, it can be ensured that a qualified preparation route with the minimum required number of sub-gates is found, and the specific route is as shown in fig. 6. The parameter π/2 is completely learned by the framework itself.
The Bell state is four orthogonal entangled states formed by two bits and plays an important role in quantum invisible state and compression coding. The respective quantum wires should map 4 different measurement basis states to the corresponding encoded Bell-state entangled states, respectively. The problem is therefore a complete line learning problem, not just single quantum state preparation. The inner product of the target states or the expectation of the observed quantities XX, ZZ can be used as the target function, while 4 different input state evaluations are required as the total target function. The specific route obtained by automatic search is shown in fig. 7. In this example, the framework utilizes only a discrete pool of non-parameter operators, i.e., no variable line parameters.
Case two, quantum error suppression (quantum error mitigation).
The line components of the quantum Fourier transform and the assumed quantum noise model which are frequently generated in quantum computation are utilized to show the potential application of the micro-quantum structure search scheme in the field of quantum error correction. By filling the quantum Fourier transform circuit on a 3-bit system and a 4-bit system, the fidelity of an output state is improved.
The quantum error suppression strategy employed here is: the gaps in the quantum wires fill the single-bit quantum gates, so that the set of these quantum gates gives the identity matrix. Therefore, on the premise of not changing the corresponding matrix of the quantum circuit, the attenuation noise of the waiting bit can be effectively reduced, and the coherent noise which is difficult to inhibit can be converted into simple Poillion noise. In accordance with this strategy, we adopt a line design coding scheme, i.e. a pool of operators V formed by different types of single-bit gates and placeholders U whose search depth p is equal to the number of original line slot positions. E.g., p 6 for a 3-bit qubit fourier transform line and p 12 for a 4-bit line.
This comparative baseline of error correction effect is the attempt to fill the equivalent of 1 quantum gate in the corresponding consecutive gap, and we have found that this framework can search for lines with higher fidelity than this knowledge-based conventional sense scheme. In fact, the search of the micro quantum structure can effectively sense a certain long-range correlation in the quantum circuit, so that the single gap can be filled with non-identity, and further improvement of the fidelity is realized.
Specifically, for a 3-bit quantum fourier transform line, the fidelity corresponding to the original line, the expert line, and the automatically designed line of the framework is 0.33, 0.55, and 0.6, respectively. And for a 4-bit quantum fourier transform line, the fidelity corresponding to the original line, the expert line, and the automatically designed line of the framework are 0.13, 0.41, and 0.45, respectively. It can be seen that the error correction circuit designed by the framework automatically suppresses the quantum noise better than the circuit design of human experts. The automatic line design is completely independent of any prior knowledge and is generated from scratch. (the corresponding quantum error correction design and specific fidelity values depend on the assumed quantum noise model, which is assumed in this example to be that for each column of quantum gate gaps there is a bit inversion noise of p 0.02 and for each quantum line slot there is a bit inversion noise of p 0.2.)
3-bit and 4-bit original lines, the error correction lines found by the framework are shown in fig. 8 to 11, respectively. The grey quantum gate in the error correction circuit is a result intelligently filled after the micro quantum structure searching framework is trained.
Case three, a line configuration search of the QAOA type.
QOA is a very important quantum classical hybrid computational paradigm and has strong physical significance and connection with quantum annealing. Therefore, under the condition of the same depth and the same line parameters, finding the quantum line arrangement with stronger approximation capability has important application value (for showing quantum superiority) and theoretical significance (for cross-contrasting and understanding with important concepts in quantum annealing). In such a problem, the end-to-end environment adopts a typical MAX CUT combinatorial optimization problem, and the operator pool adopts a strategy of combining a hamiltonian time-containing rendering layer and a common single-bit quantum gate layer. In the simplest case, the operators considered include a Hadamard gate layer, a single bit x, y, z rotation layer (which is equivalent to e) iHθ Where H ═ Σ i X i X may also be replaced by Y, Z operator) and
layers, where ij represents the edges of the graph in the problem. These basic components we refer to as H-layer, rx-layer, ry-layer, rz-layer, zz-layer, respectively. It should be noted that xx-layer and yy-layer can be generated using the basic component construction described above and are therefore redundant items. The end-to-end objective function setting is the expectation of the Hamilton quantity corresponding to MAX CUT in the quantum line output state, which is the same as the traditional QOA。
By this framework we can find a configuration and corresponding parameters such that the corresponding quantum wire construction can be simultaneously adapted to a set of graph instances resulting from a certain distribution, e.g. a regular graph. The quantum wire structure thus found is an optimal solution for approximating different graphs with the same scheme as much as possible. We can automatically search for the same layout of QOA, i.e., H-layer, zz-layer, rx-layer, zz-layer, rx-layer, as shown in FIG. 12. That is, in the case where the range of the drawing is relatively wide and the number of layers is small, the framework shows that the alternate arrangement of QAOAs is really the best choice for the approximation effect, and this also shows that the framework has a function of certain theoretical search in addition to its strong applicability.
As shown above, the search framework of the micro-quantum structure provided by the present application can be widely applied to various quantum computing and quantum information problems, especially to the automated design of quantum wires in various situations. This end-to-end micro-design, independent of any assumptions about the line structure, opens up many possibilities for quantum line design. Theoretically, the method combines completely new programming paradigms such as quantum programming, differential programming and probability programming, and can be used for exploring and finding potential efficient quantum structures beyond the existing knowledge accumulation. In practice, this framework shows good performance and excellent results in quantum state preparation, quantum wire decomposition and compilation, quantum error correction, and variation quantum structure search. The microminiature methodology and the high universality of the framework ensure that the scheme is simple and efficient, and simultaneously can consider the characteristics of a native quantum gate, connection topology, noise and the like of real quantum hardware.
Specifically, we have demonstrated that the micro-quantum structure search framework provided by the present application can achieve the following:
1. and automatically designing a multi-bit GHZ quantum state preparation line.
2. And (4) automatically realizing the discrete gate decomposition of the given quantum line and finishing the design of the Bell state mapping line.
3. Certain quantum error suppression is realized on a quantum Fourier transform line, and an error correction strategy exceeding the experience of the existing experts is found.
4. The assumption that the QOA arrangement structure is used as a quantum line solution is spontaneously found only through the MAX CUT combined optimization problem environment, and a Hamiltonian sub-block arrangement mode with better performance can be searched in a specific problem.
Generally, compared with other schemes, the technical scheme provided by the application has the following advantages:
1. universality: we have for the first time fully outlined and abstracted the important problem of quantum structure search and put forward for the first time a fully generic end-to-end solution.
2. Calculating efficiency: the scheme is the first differentiable automatic design scheme of quantum wires, which can consume less computing resources, such as time, hardware and the like, and can obtain similar or obviously better results of other schemes.
3. Multiple targets: the scheme can optimize a plurality of targets simultaneously, so that the hardware is friendly, and quantum error correction and the like are considered to be better embedded into the overall framework.
4. Results beyond prior knowledge experience: the framework is applied to a specific quantum computing problem, a series of results reaching or exceeding the existing knowledge accumulation are obtained by purely depending on machine learning without depending on the assumption of proprietary knowledge in any field, and the great potential of the scheme is displayed.
The technical scheme of the application is favorable for accelerating the quantum line design with stronger adaptability at the present stage. The typical disadvantages of quantum hardware in the nissq era are short coherence time and large quantum noise, and accordingly, we need to reduce the depth of a quantum line and the number of two-bit quantum gates as much as possible under the condition of fully considering the specific characteristics of the quantum hardware. Because the two-bit quantum gate often has bigger noise than the single-bit quantum gate, the number of the two-bit quantum gate is reduced while the performance is ensured, and the influence of quantum noise can be effectively relieved. The micro-quantum structure search framework provided by the application can well solve the multi-target line design problem, thereby obtaining advantages in quantum computing commercial application.
In addition, the application to quantum hardware evaluation is possible in a medium-short period, and the application in practical production comprises the VQE or QOA hypothesis optimization assisted by micro quantum structure search, so that better results can be obtained by using fewer quantum resources, and the corresponding product can be used for solving the combination optimization problem or the ground state energy simulation of quantum chemistry. Meanwhile, the search of the micro-quantum structure can also effectively play a design potential on the quantum compiling technology stack and the quantum error suppression, so that the corresponding line is more stable to quantum noise.

Title
Gate formation on a quantum processor

Abstract
In a general aspect, a gate is formed for a quantum processor. In some implementations, an arbitrary program is received. The arbitrary program includes a first sequence of quantum logic gates, which includes a parametric XY gate. A native gate set is identified, which includes a set of quantum logic gates associated with a quantum processing unit. A second sequence of quantum logic gates corresponding to the parametric XY gate is identified, which includes a parametric quantum logic gate. Each of the quantum logic gates in the second sequence is selected from the native gate set. A native program is generated. The native program includes a third sequence of quantum logic gates. The third sequence of quantum logic gates corresponds to the first sequence of quantum logic gates and includes the second sequence of quantum logic gates. The native program is provided for execution by the quantum processing unit.

BACKGROUND
The following description relates to gate formation for a quantum processor.
Quantum computers can perform computational tasks by storing and processing information within quantum states of quantum systems. For example, qubits (i.e., quantum bits) can be stored in and represented by an effective two-level sub-manifold of a quantum coherent physical system. A variety of physical systems have been proposed for quantum computing applications. Examples include superconducting circuits, trapped ions, spin systems, and others.
