Detailed ways
The implementation of the present invention is described below through specific examples and in conjunction with the accompanying drawings, and those skilled in the art can easily understand other advantages and effects of the present invention from the content disclosed in this specification. The present invention can also be implemented or applied through other different specific examples, and various modifications and changes can be made to the details in this specification based on different viewpoints and applications without departing from the spirit of the present invention.
Before introducing the present invention, the abbreviations and key terms involved in the present invention are defined as follows:
Deep learning: Deep learning was proposed by Hinton et al. in 2006 and is a new field of machine learning. Deep learning was introduced into machine learning to bring it closer to the original goal - artificial intelligence. Deep learning is to learn the internal laws and representation levels of sample data. The information obtained in these learning processes is of great help to the interpretation of data such as images and text. Its ultimate goal is to enable machines to have the ability to analyze and learn like humans, and to be able to recognize data such as images and text.
Convolutional Neural Network: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a feedforward neural network. Its artificial neurons can respond to surrounding units within a part of the coverage area, and it has excellent performance for large-scale image processing. Generally, the basic structure of CNN includes a convolutional layer and a pooling layer, one of which is a feature extraction layer, the input of each neuron is connected to the local receptive field of the previous layer, and the local area is extracted. Characteristics. Once the local feature is extracted, the positional relationship between it and other features is also determined; the second is the feature map layer, each calculation layer of the network is composed of multiple feature maps, each feature map is a plane, All neurons on the plane have equal weights. The feature map structure uses the sigmoid function with a small influence function kernel as the activation function of the convolutional network, so that the feature map has displacement invariance. In addition, since neurons on a mapping plane share weights, the number of free parameters of the network is reduced. Each convolutional layer in the convolutional neural network is followed by a calculation layer for local averaging and secondary extraction. This unique two-time feature extraction structure reduces the feature resolution.
Reinforcement learning: Reinforcement learning (RL), also known as reward learning and evaluation learning, is an important machine learning method that has many applications in the fields of intelligent control robots and analysis and prediction. Reinforcement learning is that the agent (Agent) learns in a "trial-and-error" way, and the behavior is guided by rewards obtained through interaction with the environment. The goal is to enable the agent to obtain the maximum reward. Reinforcement learning is different from supervised learning in connectionist learning. , mainly manifested in the teacher's signal. The reinforcement signal provided by the environment in reinforcement learning is an evaluation of the quality of the generated action, rather than telling the reinforcement learning system how to generate the correct action. Since the external environment provides little information, the agent must learn from its own experience. In this way, knowledge is acquired in an action-evaluation environment, and action programs are improved to suit the environment.
Value Iteration Network: In order to solve the problem of poor generalization ability in deep reinforcement learning, Value Iteration Networks (VINs) introduces a Value Iteration Module (VI Module) with planning capabilities. A planning module is added to the general policy representation, and the introduced space assists the solution of the policy, making the learned optimal policy more generalizable.
FIG. 1 is a schematic structural diagram of a cross-domain federated learning model based on a value iterative network in the present invention.
As shown in Figure 1, a cross-domain federated learning model based on the value iterative network of the present invention includes:
The data preparation unit 101 is used to use the path planning field of the grid map as the training environment, and use the observation states of two different parts in the same map as the respective inputs of the two fields of federated learning. In a specific embodiment of the present invention, the two Two different partially observed states s(i, j) and s′(i, j) are used as the input of two domains, domain A and domain B, respectively.
Specifically, the data preparation unit 101 uses path planning in a grid map with obstacles randomly set as the experimental field, where the state observations input to the model include the current position, target position and grid map image. Specifically, for each state s(i,j) in each trajectory, a state observation image of size (2*m*n) is generated, and the first channel of the image encodes the presence of grid map obstacles (1 for obstacles, 0 otherwise), while the second channel encodes the target position (1 at the target, 0 otherwise). A complete observation vector consists of a map and a state s(i, j). Furthermore, for each input state, an action annotation needs to be generated as an expert policy, denoting the action decision that the optimal path policy will take in that state. In the grid map field of the present invention, there are 8 executable actions in the action space: {East, West, North, South, Northeast, Northwest, Southeast, Southwest}.
The complexity of grid domain planning generally depends on the number of obstacles and their distribution on the grid map. Therefore, grid maps with different numbers of obstacles and different sizes can be used as different training domains for federated learning. For example, the two domains are grid maps with sizes of 8*8 and 16*16 respectively, and obstacles with a ratio of 30% or 50% are randomly placed. In addition, many other application fields, such as navigation, warehouse scheduling, etc., can be matched to grid maps with different complexity, so Federated-VIN is effective for various planning fields.
Prediction accuracy in the present invention is defined by calculating the proportion of successful trials among all trials for each network corresponding domain. Thus, for each state in the test set, the predicted action is considered successful if it is the same as the expert action.
The Federated-VIN network establishment unit 102 is used to establish a Federated-VIN network structure based on VIN (Value Iteration Networks, value iteration network), and construct a full connection between the source domain and the target domain value iteration module, and each connection weight corresponds to the source domain and the value iteration network. The similarity of the pair of actions between target domains and define a new loss function based on the newly constructed Federated-VIN network.
In a specific embodiment of the present invention, the Federated-VIN network establishment unit 102 establishes the Federated-VIN network structure, and the Federated-VIN has a value iteration module (VI) with planning capability, and the Federated-VIN network establishment unit 102 constructs the source field and the target field The connection of the VI module, because each convolution channel of the Q learning layer in the VIN network corresponds to the Q function Q(s, a) of a specific action a in the field, contains policy planning information about the field. In the present invention, a fully connected network is constructed between the action channels of the Q learning layer in the two domains. Each connection weight of the fully connected bridge corresponds to the similarity of the pair of actions between the source domain and the target domain, and has a high similarity Sexual cross-domain actions are assigned larger weights. Therefore, the Federated-VIN network can automatically learn the action similarity between two domains, which reduces the human cost of manually selecting similar action pairs for transfer.
The invention establishes the connection in the VI module, and realizes the confidentiality of the original data of both parties in the federated learning. Since the prediction goals of the two fields are to learn the optimal path from the starting point to a given goal point, the state observations of the two fields are different, but part of the policy prediction knowledge learned through VIN overlaps. Therefore, based on VIN, it is possible to realize the growth of both parties' models by using part of the observations and network hidden knowledge of both parties without sharing the original input data. The method of Federated-VIN in the present invention is to firstly encrypt policy information through VI modules in their respective fields, and then exchange knowledge through full-connection bridges to establish the similarity of action pairs and communicate, and use full-connection weights to transfer shared information in an encrypted state. part of the knowledge. Because the original state observation data has not been exchanged, what is exchanged is only part of the information shared by the VI module after learning, so the data privacy protection is achieved. Then, the two parties use different parts of the observation data they own as input to iteratively train the model, Exchange parameters, update parameters. Based on the knowledge transfer of Federated-VIN, the two parties cannot inversely deduce the observation characteristics that the other party has but not their own, so the data privacy is still protected.
For single-domain VIN, the loss function can be expressed by cross-entropy loss:
For the Federated-VIN of the present invention, a new joint loss function about the two fields is defined, and the learning objective of the fully connected weight is added, and LFVIN is expressed as:
L FVIN (θ A , θ B , θ t ) = L A (θ A , θ t ) + L B (θ B , θ t )
Among them, θ t represents the weight of the full connection, and A and B represent the two fields of federated learning, respectively. Specifically, L i (θ i , θ t ) represents the objective function when each domain is updated: L i (θ i , θ t )=L i (θ i )+L t (θ i , θ t ), where L t (θ i , θ t ) represents the loss function of fully connected weights in Federated-VIN, which can be defined as a square difference loss, for example, for domain A: L t (θ A , θ t )=||θ B -F(θ A , θ t )|| 2 , the same is true for the backward update of domain B: L t (θ B , θ t )=||θ A -F(θ B , θ t )|| 2 .
The value iteration execution unit 103 first performs forward calculation on the VIN of the two fields during training, and implements several iterations through the VI module. In each iteration step, according to the Federated-VIN federated network, input part of the observed features of the two fields into the network, And calculate the respective action prediction results forward through VIN.
Forward calculation is performed on the VIN of the two domains. In each iterative step, according to the Federated-VIN federated network, the respective partial observation states I of the two domains are input and the respective action prediction results π A and π B are obtained through forward calculation.
In traditional reinforcement learning, the value iteration algorithm is a commonly used and effective iterative solution algorithm for calculating the optimal value function V * and the optimal policy π * . In each iteration, the V and Q functions are updated according to the Bellman equation:
in,
Q n (s, a) = R (s, a) + γ∑ s tP (s'|s, a)V n (s').
The characteristic of the value iterative network VIN is that it uses a derivable convolutional neural network to approximate the process of realizing the traditional value iterative algorithm. The specific structure of the VI module in the present invention is shown in Figure 2. Each iteration of this module can be approximated as the value function V n and reward function R of the previous iteration are calculated by convolution and maximum pooling calculation to simulate the value based on the Bellman equation Iterative algorithm process; in the convolution calculation layer, each feature map corresponds to the result of the Q function corresponding to a specific action a in the field, and the number of feature maps in the convolution layer is consistent with the number of action spaces. And the convolution kernel parameter in the convolutional layer just corresponds to the state transition probability function in the value iteration. Therefore, the Q function obtained by convolution calculation can be expressed as:
After the result of the convolution calculation is obtained, the maximum pooling operation is performed on the Q values of different channels, that is, the maximum pooling layer realizes V n+1(s) = max a Q n (s, α), and this step iteratively updates the V function . In the next iteration, in the same way, the Vn obtained in this step and the reward function R are superimposed and passed to the convolution layer and the maximum pooling layer, so that K steps are cycled to realize the iterative update of the value function I for K times. Then such VI The module has the function of value iteration, and the CNN network can learn parameters through the existing backward updating (BP) algorithm.
The backward updating unit 104 is used for backward calculation and updating of network parameters, and alternately backward updating the VIN parameters and full connection parameters of the two domains according to the newly defined loss function. That is, the backward update unit 104 adopts an alternate update method, first fixes the network parameters of the source domain for Federated-VIN, and updates the target domain parameters according to the joint loss function; then fixes the network parameters of the target domain, and updates the source domain parameters according to the joint loss function; finally The VIN parameters of the two domains are fixed as non-trainable parameters, and the fully connected bridge parameters in Federated-VIN are updated, so as to achieve the purpose of alternately updating the training process and mutual utilization of knowledge federated learning.
In Federated-VIN, the VIN of the two domains is represented by a CNN network structure. After the forward calculation, the loss function L FVLN (θ A , θ B , θ t ) is optimized end-to-end, and then the backpropagation update of the network is realized. , so as to learn the joint parameters, such as the optimal learning method through stochastic gradient descent. For single domain VIN, the corresponding gradient of L i (θ i ) can be obtained as follows:
Based on this gradient, the network parameters θ A , θ B , and θ t are updated sequentially in Federated-VIN through backward calculation. That is to fix the network parameter θ B of domain B first, update the parameter θ A of the target domain according to the loss function L A (θ A , θ t ); then fix the network parameter θ A of the target domain A, and update the parameter θ A of the target domain according to the loss function L B (θ B , θ t ) Update the source domain parameter θ B ; finally fix the VIN parameters of the two domains as non-trainable parameters, and update the fully connected bridge parameter θ t in Federated-VIN. Iteratively train models, exchange parameters, and alternately update parameters. Finally, Federated-VIN learns the optimal strategy close to the expert's labeling strategy, so as to achieve the purpose of mutual use of knowledge for federated learning.
FIG. 3 is a flow chart of the steps of a cross-domain federated learning method based on a value iterative network in the present invention. As shown in Figure 3, a cross-domain federated learning method based on the value iterative network of the present invention includes the following steps:
In step S1, by using the path planning domain of the grid map as the training environment, two different partial observation states in the same map are used as the respective inputs of the two domains of federated learning.
Specifically, in step S1, the path planning in the grid map with random obstacles is adopted as the experimental field, where the state observation input to the model includes the current position, the target position and the grid map image. Specifically, for each state s(i,j) in each trajectory, a state observation image of size (2*m*n) is generated, and the first channel of the image encodes the presence of grid map obstacles (1 for obstacles, 0 otherwise), while the second channel encodes the target position (1 at the target, 0 otherwise). A complete observation vector consists of a map and a state s(i, j). Furthermore, for each input state, an action annotation needs to be generated as an expert policy, denoting the action decision that the optimal path policy will take in that state. In the grid map field of the present invention, there are 8 executable actions in the action space: {East, West, North, South, Northeast, Northwest, Southeast, Southwest}.
Step S2, establish a Federated-VIN network structure based on VIN (Value Iteration Networks, value iteration network), and build a full connection between the source domain and the target domain value iteration module, and each connection weight corresponds to the pair between the source domain and the target domain. Action similarity, and define a new loss function based on the newly constructed Federated-VIN network.
In a specific embodiment of the present invention, in step S2, the Federated-VIN network structure is first established, the Federated-VIN network has a value iteration module (VI) with planning capabilities, and then the connection between the VI modules of the source domain and the target domain is constructed , since each convolution channel of the Q learning layer in the VIN network corresponds to the Q function Q(s, a) of a specific action a in the field, which contains policy planning information about the field, in the present invention, in the two fields Q learning A fully connected network is constructed between the various action channels of the layer. Each connection weight of the fully connected bridge corresponds to the similarity of the pair of actions between the source domain and the target domain. The cross-domain actions with higher similarity are assigned larger Weights. Therefore, the Federated-VIN network can automatically learn the action similarity between two domains, which reduces the human cost of manually selecting similar action pairs for transfer.
The invention establishes the connection in the VI module, and realizes the confidentiality of the original data of both parties in the federated learning. Since the prediction goals of the two fields are to learn the optimal path from the starting point to a given goal point, the state observations of the two fields are different, but part of the policy prediction knowledge learned through VIN overlaps. Therefore, based on VIN, it is possible to realize the growth of both parties' models by using part of the observations and network hidden knowledge of both parties without sharing the original input data. The method of Federated-VIN in the present invention is to firstly encrypt policy information through VI modules in their respective fields, and then exchange knowledge through full-connection bridges to establish the similarity of action pairs and communicate, and use full-connection weights to transfer shared information in an encrypted state. part of the knowledge. Because the original state observation data has not been exchanged, what is exchanged is only part of the information shared by the VI module after learning, so the data privacy protection is achieved. Then, the two parties use different parts of the observation data they own as input to iteratively train the model, Exchange parameters, update parameters. Based on the knowledge transfer of Federated-VIN, the two parties cannot inversely deduce the observation characteristics that the other party has but not their own, so the data privacy is still protected.
For the Federated-VIN of the present invention, a new joint loss function about the two fields is defined, and the learning objective of the fully connected weight is added, and LFVIN is expressed as:
L FVIN (θ A , θ B , θ t ) = L A (θ A , θ t ) + L B (θ B , θ t )
Among them, θ t represents the weight of the full connection, and A and B represent the two fields of federated learning, respectively. Specifically, L i (θ i , θ t ) represents the objective function when each domain is updated: L i (θ i , θ t )=L i (θ i )+L t (θ i , θ t ), where L t (θ i , θ t ) represents the loss function of fully connected weights in Federated-VIN, which can be defined as a square difference loss, for example, for domain A: L t (θ A , θ t )=||θ B -F(θ A , θ t )|| 2 , the same is true for the backward update of domain B: L t (θ B , θ t )=||θ A -F(θ B , θ t )|| 2 .
Step S3, during training, first perform forward calculation on the VIN of the two fields, and implement several iterations through the VI module. In each iteration step, according to the Federated-VIN federated network, input part of the observed characteristics of the two fields into the network, and pass the VIN Calculate the respective action prediction results forward. It is used to perform forward calculations on the VI modules of the two fields during training, and perform several value iterations on the VI modules
That is to say, in step S3, forward calculation is performed on the VINs of the two domains, and at each iterative step, according to the Federated-VIN federated network, the partial observation states of the two domains are input, and the respective action prediction results are obtained through the forward calculation π A and π B .
The characteristic of the value iterative network VIN is that it uses a derivable convolutional neural network to approximate the process of realizing the traditional value iterative algorithm. The specific structure of the VI module in the present invention is shown in Figure 2. Each iteration of this module can be approximated as the value function V n and reward function R of the previous iteration are calculated by convolution and maximum pooling calculation to simulate the value based on the Bellman equation Iterative algorithm process; in the convolution calculation layer, each feature map corresponds to the result of the Q function corresponding to a specific action a in the field, and the number of feature maps in the convolution layer is consistent with the number of action spaces. And the convolution kernel parameter in the convolution layer just corresponds to the state transition probability function in the value iteration. Therefore, the Q function obtained by convolution calculation can be expressed as:
After the result of the convolution calculation is obtained, the maximum pooling operation is performed on the Q values of different channels, that is, the maximum pooling layer realizes V n+1 (s)=max a Q n (s, a), and this step iteratively updates the V function . In the next iteration, in the same way, superimpose the V n obtained in this step and the reward function R into the convolution layer and the maximum pooling layer, so that the K steps are cycled to realize the iterative update I of the K value function. The VI module has the function of value iteration, and the CNN network can learn parameters through the existing backward updating (BP) algorithm.
In step S4, the network parameters are updated by backward calculation, and the VIN parameters and full connection parameters of the two domains are updated alternately and backwards according to the newly defined loss function. That is, the alternate update method is adopted. For Federated-VIN, the network parameters of the source domain are first fixed, and the target domain parameters are updated according to the loss function; then the network parameters of the target domain are fixed, and the source domain parameters are updated according to the loss function; finally, the VIN parameters of the two domains are fixed. , as a non-trainable parameter I to update the fully connected bridge parameters in Federated-VIN, so as to achieve the purpose of alternately updating the training process and mutual use of knowledge federated learning.
In Federated-VIN, the VIN of the two domains is represented by a CNN network structure. After the forward calculation, the loss function L FVIN (θ A , θ B , θ t ) is optimized end-to-end, and then the backpropagation update of the network is realized. , so as to learn the joint parameters, such as the optimal learning method through stochastic gradient descent. For single domain VIN, the corresponding gradient of L i (θ i ) can be obtained as follows:
Based on the gradient, the network parameters θ A , θ B , and θ t are updated sequentially in Federated-VIN through backward calculation. That is to fix the network parameter θ B of domain B first, update the parameter θ A of the target domain according to the loss function L A (θ A , θ t ); then fix the network parameter θ A of the target domain A, and update the parameter θ A of the target domain according to the loss function L B (θ B , θ t ) Update the source domain parameter θ B ; finally fix the VIN parameters of the two domains as non-trainable parameters, and update the fully connected bridge parameter θ t in Federated-VIN. Iteratively train models, exchange parameters, and alternately update parameters. Finally, Federated-VIN learns the optimal strategy close to the expert's labeling strategy, so as to achieve the purpose of mutual use of knowledge for federated learning.
To sum up, a cross-domain federated learning model and method based on the value iteration network of the present invention establishes a similar relationship between domains by constructing a full connection between the value iteration modules of the source domain and the target domain, and can End-to-end automatic learning of the similarity is used as a bridge for the utilization of federated learning knowledge, and an alternate learning when training the model is proposed, so that the two fields can use internal knowledge and improve each other, thereby improving the prediction accuracy of their respective optimal strategies , compared with the existing independent value iteration network, the present invention can overcome the defects of high computational complexity and cost consumption that rely on large-scale data training in a single field, and compared with traditional transfer learning, it can achieve Under the premise, data privacy is protected, and the data of both parties is used to achieve model effect growth.

## 686. [KR20210010193A] Big Data system that detects and sends teaching activity on a web browser to a web server
- **Patent ID / App No**: `KR20210010193A`
- **Source**: Google Patents
- **URL**: [https://patents.google.com/patent/KR20210010193A/en](https://patents.google.com/patent/KR20210010193A/en)
- **AI Relevancy Score**: N/A (UNAUDITED)

### 📋 Abstract
> The present invention relates to a big data system which detects and transmits teaching and learning activities on a web browser to a web server. More specifically, the present invention relates to a method which detects teaching and learning activities, which are an interaction between users and web educational content, and a big data system which detects and transmits teaching and learning activities on a web browser by converting detected data into data of a Javascript object notation (JSON) code to transmit the same to the web server. To this end, the big data system which detects and transmits teaching and learning activities on a web browser comprises: a data extraction unit; a data acquisition unit; a language analysis unit; a learning data analysis unit; an access sensing means; a data storage unit; an error detection unit; and a data collection server.

Translated from Korean
Big Data system that detects and sends teaching activity on a web browser to a web server}
The present invention relates to a big data system that detects teaching and learning activities on a web browser and transmits them to a web server. More specifically, a method of detecting teaching and learning activities, which is an interaction between a user and web education content, on a web browser, and It relates to a big data system that detects teaching and learning activities on a web browser that converts data into JSON (Javascript object notation) data and transmits it to a web server and transmits it to a web server.
As it enters a highly information-oriented society, rapid progress is being made in technologies related to providing, searching, processing, and sharing information.
In this regard, in the form of learning, in the existing collective education form where a large number of students are gathered in a physical space and classes are conducted with one or two teachers using the same textbook, individualized customized learning using Internet or mobile technology It is being converted into form.
This trend has developed in various forms such as e-learning, m-learning, and u-learning (ubiquitous-learning) since the 2000s.
In such a web-based learning form using the Internet, mobile, etc., a professor adopts and uses a web-based learning management system in order to more easily manage the learning of a large number of students.
This web-based learning management system provides a variety of learning courses, such as educational materials and lecture materials for the learning process, to a large number of students, and the results are verified by the professor, and then the systematic curriculum and the learning process to be provided. It is making it possible to establish.
Since such a conventional web-based learning management system simply obtains the result of education completion confirmation and incorrect answer, it is difficult to use it for the purpose of updating a better curriculum and learning process by referring to it.
In addition to the above-described results, various information such as learning status, process, duration of study, number of problem solving and problem solving attempts, etc., must be acquired so that the establishment of the learning process can be easily updated. Do.
However, with the development of modern technology, various web browser applications are being provided, and not only one type of web browser is used among various web browser applications, but a computer supported by each web browser is used by many students. There is a problem with technology development because the language must be used to access the web browser and extract data.
Accordingly, there is a need to develop a technology capable of easily accessing each web browser developed in various computer languages, unifying them and converting them into a single language to collect data.

The purpose is to provide a big data system.
In addition, you can easily access one or more web browsers using various computer languages, and detect teaching and learning activities on a web browser that can be obtained by unifying and converting learning data provided in each computer language into one language. The purpose is to provide a big data system that transmits to the server.

Title
Bi-directional translation service using text information restoration technology

Abstract
Translated from Korean
A method for providing a two-way translation service between print and Braille according to a first embodiment of the present invention comprises: (a) a step of determining whether a character corresponding to a translation target is Braille or print; (b) a step of classifying words constituting a received character into at least one category among Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols, and inputting each classified word into a Braille conversion model learned by artificial intelligence and outputting it as print or Braille, thereby performing a translation between print and Braille; and (c) a step of providing the translated character to a user terminal; wherein, in step (c), if the character to be translated is print, Braille is provided to a terminal of a visually impaired person, and if the character to be translated is Braille, print is provided to a terminal of a teacher.

Description
Translated from Korean
Method for providing a bidirectional translation service using text information restoration technology {BI-DIRECTIONAL TRANSLATION SERVICE USING TEXT INFORMATION RESTORATION TECHNOLOGY}
The present invention relates to a method for providing a two-way translation service using character information restoration technology. More specifically, it relates to providing a two-way translation service using character information restoration technology that bidirectionally translates Braille and Korean, enabling non-face-to-face chat-based learning guidance for the visually impaired. This service is particularly useful for general professors or teachers who do not know Braille when teaching visually impaired students.
According to a 2021 survey by the Ministry of Health and Welfare, the number of registered visually impaired people was 252,000, the third largest number after those with physical disabilities and those with hearing and speech disabilities.
However, the reality is that most facilities in South Korea are designed or primarily used by people without disabilities. This isn't limited to facilities. Even in education, the most basic provision we should have, people with disabilities face significant limitations compared to those without disabilities.
While the pandemic has led to a rise in non-face-to-face education platforms, there are currently no service platforms available for real-time, non-face-to-face education for people with visual impairments. Therefore, education has traditionally been conducted primarily via phone or video conferencing platforms.
However, visually impaired people have difficulty with web accessibility because the location and functions of the video conferencing service menus differ from one video conferencing platform to another, starting from the process of clicking on a link to participate in a video conference, and it is difficult for them to become familiar with and participate in various functions in a short period of time.
Furthermore, the current video conferencing platforms, primarily for video conferencing, lack the ability to share class materials, making it difficult to review materials mid-class. Furthermore, there are limitations in managing attendance and students who drop out during class. Furthermore, when receiving remote instruction from a teacher, students can only perceive the teacher's voice, making it difficult to provide seamless feedback to the teacher in person, even if they have questions during class.
Additionally, in the case of chat, although video conferencing platforms also have chat functions, real-time communication is impossible because screen readers (devices that read the screen) used by visually impaired people cannot read chat conversations.
Furthermore, while many existing services offered translation services from Braille to print, there were no two-way services that allowed for reverse translation of the converted print back into Braille. This was because, in the process of translating from the more informative (print) side to the less informative (Braille) side, a single Braille word could be interpreted as multiple Korean, English, other foreign languages, or symbols, increasing the likelihood of mistranslation. Consequently, while there were services that provided one-way communication between teachers and visually impaired students, there were none that enabled simultaneous communication between the two parties.
The purpose is to provide a two-way translation service using text information restoration technology that allows real-time feedback from teachers by utilizing a class chat function based on a Braille AI engine and reverse Braille AI engine that utilize real-time sentence conversion technology rather than simple character conversion using artificial intelligence technology, including a real-time class facial recognition function and learning guidance through non-face-to-face chat for the visually impaired.
However, the technical task that this embodiment seeks to achieve is not limited to the technical task described above, and other technical tasks may exist.
As a technical means for achieving the above-described technical task, a method for providing a two-way translation service between print and Braille according to a first embodiment of the present invention comprises: (a) a step of determining whether a character corresponding to a translation target is Braille or print; (b) a step of classifying words constituting a received character into at least one category among Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols, and inputting each classified word into a Braille conversion model learned by artificial intelligence and outputting it as print or Braille, thereby performing a translation between print and Braille; and (c) a step of providing the translated character to a user terminal; wherein, in step (c), if the character to be translated is print, Braille is provided to a terminal of a visually impaired person, and if the character to be translated is Braille, print is provided to a terminal of a teacher.
In addition, the input characters include Korean, English, other foreign languages, and at least one of symbols, and the symbols include letter symbols, mathematical symbols, and special symbols.
In addition, the step (b) includes: (b-1) a step of classifying and separating input words constituting the input characters into one of Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols; (b-2) a step of inputting each separated input word into one of a Korean character transliteration model, an English character transliteration model, other foreign language transliteration model, and a symbol transliteration model according to a classified category, and outputting an output word composed of Braille or print; and (b-3) a step of listing and combining output words according to the order of the input words constituting the characters input in the step (b-1) to complete the translation; and the symbol transliteration model includes a character symbol transliteration model, a mathematical symbol transliteration model, and a special symbol transliteration model.
In addition, the above Korean Braille model is pre-trained by inputting learning data including a corpus pair for Korean and Braille into at least one of an unsupervised learning model, a supervised learning model, and a reinforcement learning model.
In addition, the English Braille model is pre-trained by inputting learning data including corpus pairs for English and Braille into at least one of an unsupervised learning model, a supervised learning model, and a reinforcement learning model.
In addition, the above-mentioned foreign language Braille model is pre-trained by inputting learning data including corpus pairs for other foreign languages and Braille into at least one of an unsupervised learning model, a supervised learning model, and a reinforcement learning model.
In addition, the symbol-braille model is pre-trained by inputting learning data including corpus pairs for symbols and Braille into at least one of an unsupervised learning model, a supervised learning model, and a reinforcement learning model.
In addition, Korean words, English words, and other foreign language words and symbols can be defined as the same single Braille, but in the corpus pairs of each category consisting of the corpus pairs for the Korean and Braille, the corpus pairs for the English and Braille, the corpus pairs for the other foreign language and Braille, and the corpus pairs for the symbols and Braille, one Braille can be included in corpus pairs of multiple categories, but there are no duplicate Brailles within one corpus pair.
In addition, in the step (b-1), if the character is Braille, the character is input into a character information restoration model, and the Braille characters constituting the character are classified into one of the categories of Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols and output.
In addition, in the step (b-1), the character information restoration model is trained to classify the sentence written in Braille into Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols by considering the context of the sentence.
In addition, the character information restoration model generates a translation combination of the Braille characters placed before and after a Braille character at a specific location constituting a character, and classifies each Braille character into one of Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols so that among the generated translation combinations, a translation combination that fits the context or has dictionary meaning is created.
In addition, the step (a) includes a step in which the teacher terminal provides an electronic file composed of Korean to the server, the server extracts text from the electronic file, and determines whether the text is in print or Braille, and the step (c) includes a step in which the teacher terminal converts the Korean provided into Braille and provides the converted text to the user terminal.
In addition, the step (a) includes a step of providing Braille input by the user terminal into a chat window to the server, and the step (c) includes a step of converting the Braille input by the user terminal into print and providing it to the chat window of the teacher terminal.
A device for providing a two-way translation service using a character information restoration technology comprises: a memory for storing a program for providing a two-way translation service using a character information restoration technology; and a processor for executing the program, wherein the method comprises: (a) a step of determining whether a character corresponding to a translation target is Braille or print; (b) a step of classifying words constituting a received character into at least one category among Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols, and inputting each classified word into a Braille conversion model learned by artificial intelligence and outputting it as print or Braille, thereby performing a translation between print and Braille; and (c) a step of providing the translated character to a user terminal; wherein, in step (c), if the character to be translated is print, Braille is provided to a terminal of a visually impaired person, and if the character to be translated is Braille, print is provided to a terminal of a teacher.
The present invention provides a two-way translation service using a character information restoration technology including a real-time class facial recognition function and learning guidance through class chat based on a braille AI engine and a reverse braille AI engine with real-time sentence conversion technology for the visually impaired.
The present invention can be usefully used by people who do not know Braille when communicating with visually impaired people.

First, referring to FIG. 1, the structure of a method for providing a two-way translation service using a character information restoration technology according to one embodiment of the present invention will be described.
According to FIG. 1, a method for providing a two-way translation service using a character information restoration technology according to one embodiment of the present invention may include a server (100), a terminal for the visually impaired (200), and a teacher terminal (300). In this case, the teacher terminal (300) may be a teacher terminal.
Referring to FIG. 2 below, the structure of a server for providing a two-way translation service using a character information restoration technology according to one embodiment of the present invention will be described.
According to FIG. 2, a server according to one embodiment of the present invention includes a memory (110), a processor (120), and a communication module (130). However, the structure of the server (100) is not limited thereto.
The memory (110) can store at least one of information and data input to the communication module (130), information and data required for functions performed by the processor (120), and data generated according to the execution of the processor (120). The memory (110) should be interpreted as a general term for a non-volatile storage device that maintains stored information even when no power is supplied and a volatile storage device that requires power to maintain the stored information. In addition, the memory (110) can perform a function of temporarily or permanently storing data processed by the processor (120). The memory (110) may include a magnetic storage media or a flash storage media in addition to a volatile storage device that requires power to maintain the stored information, but the scope of the present invention is not limited thereto.
The memory (110) stores a two-way translation service program using character information restoration technology, and the processor (120) receives information entered by the visually impaired terminal (200) within the online education service and links it to the program. The name of the program is set for convenience of explanation, and the name itself does not limit the program's functions.
The processor (120) is configured to execute a program stored in the memory (110). The processor (120) may include various types of devices that control and process data. The processor (120) may refer to a data processing device built into hardware that has a physically structured circuit to perform a function expressed by a code or instruction included in the program. In one example, the processor (120) may be implemented in the form of a microprocessor, a central processing unit (CPU), a processor core, a multiprocessor, an application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC), a field programmable gate array (FPGA), etc., but the scope of the present invention is not limited thereto.
The processor (120) is configured to perform detailed processes of a two-way translation service using character information restoration technology as described below.
The communication module (130) can transmit and receive information with an external database or external device. Here, the external device may be a terminal for the visually impaired (200) or a teacher's terminal (300). The communication module (130) may include a device including the hardware and software necessary to transmit and receive signals, such as control signals or data signals, with other network devices via wired or wireless connections.
The communication module (130) transmits a two-way translation service program using a character information restoration technology stored in the memory (110) provided by the processor (120) of the server (100) to an external database or external device so that the program can be linked.
The terminal (200) for the visually impaired may include a smartphone, tablet PC, notebook (laptop), or desktop computer with a screen capable of inputting information. However, the terminal (200) for the visually impaired is not limited to these. The terminal (200) for the visually impaired may transmit written content to the teacher terminal (300) via the server (100), view feedback provided by the teacher terminal (300) from the server (100), and input additional tasks.
The teacher terminal (300) may include a smartphone, tablet PC, laptop, or desktop computer with a screen capable of inputting information. However, the teacher terminal (300) is not limited to these. The teacher terminal (300) receives the content written by the visually impaired terminal (200) from the server (100) and transmits feedback on the writing to the visually impaired terminal (200) via the server (100).
Referring to FIG. 3 below, an outline of a method for providing a two-way translation service using a character information restoration technology according to one embodiment of the present invention will be described.
Referring to FIG. 3, the present invention allows a visually impaired student to write in Braille and transmit it to a server (100), and the server (100) converts the Braille into print using a translation engine and transmits it to a teacher's terminal (300), and the teacher transmits feedback written in print to the server (100), and the server (100) converts the print feedback into Braille feedback and transmits it to the visually impaired student's terminal (200).
Referring to FIG. 4 below, a detailed description will be given of a process for providing a two-way translation service using a character information restoration technology according to one embodiment of the present invention.
First, a visually impaired person, special education teacher, or general teacher inputs Braille into the chat window, or a special education teacher or general teacher uploads an electronic file in Korean (S411, S412, S413).
A visually impaired person, special education teacher, or general teacher can input Braille or print characters into a chat window using a terminal for the visually impaired (200) or a teacher terminal (300), and a special education teacher or general teacher can upload an electronic file in Korean. In this case, the input characters may include Korean characters, English, other foreign languages, or symbols. In addition, if a special education teacher or general teacher uploads an electronic file, the text can be extracted from the electronic file to determine whether the text is in print or Braille.
Next, it is determined whether the character to be translated is Braille or print (S420).
The server (100) can determine whether characters entered in a chat window by a visually impaired person, special education teacher, or general teacher using a visually impaired person's terminal (200) or a teacher's terminal (300) are Braille or print.
Next, the words that make up the received text are classified into categories such as Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols, and then the classified words are input into a Braille conversion model trained by artificial intelligence to perform translation (S430).
The S430 process will be explained with reference to Figures 5 and 6 below.
The following Figure 5 is an exemplary diagram showing a method for providing a two-way translation service using a character information restoration technology according to one embodiment of the present invention, translating Braille into print.
According to Fig. 5, if the character is determined to be Braille in process S420, the character written in Braille is distinguished into Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols using a character information restoration engine (S431).
At this time, the character information restoration model can learn to classify sentences written in Braille into Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols by considering the context of the sentence. At this time, the symbols can include character symbols, mathematical symbols, and special symbols. In addition, the character information restoration model can generate a translation combination with the Braille characters placed before and after a Braille character at a specific position that constitutes a character, and classify each Braille character into one of Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols so that among the generated translation combinations, the translation combination that fits the context or has dictionary meaning is selected. In other words, it can be said to be an engine that infers which words should come before and after the Braille characters placed at a specific position to form a meaningful word or sentence by combining the Braille characters before and after the Braille character.
For example, assuming that the Braille represents the English word "SOMETHING", if the word "ET" in the middle is recognized, the Braille placed before "ET" can be interpreted as "한" or "SOM". At this time, the character information restoration engine can compose the word combinations "한+ET" and "SOM+ET" and check whether the result fits the context and forms a meaningful word, so it can interpret the word combination as "SOM+ET". If it interprets it as "한", the Braille may be recognized as "한ETHING", resulting in an incorrect translation.
Next, the Braille characters, categorized into Korean, English, and other foreign languages and symbols, are converted into their respective print characters using a Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbol reverse braille engine (S432). Next, each print character is combined and converted into a sentence written in the aforementioned print characters (S433).
For example, if Braille containing Korean, English, and other foreign languages and symbols is entered, categorized into Korean, English, and other foreign languages and symbols, and these words are converted using their respective reverse Braille engines, the results are "World Health Organization," "WHO," and ":." Arranging these words in their original order yields the print-written "WHO: World Health Organization."
The following Figure 6 is an exemplary diagram showing a method for providing a two-way translation service using a character information restoration technology according to one embodiment of the present invention, translating ink characters into Braille.
According to Figure 6, if a word or sentence is determined to be a print character in process S420, the print character is divided into Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols (S434). Next, the Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols are converted into Braille using a Braille engine (S435). Next, the individual Braille characters are combined and converted into Braille feedback (S436).
For example, when entering "WHO: World Health Organization" in ink, you can classify it into Korean (World Health Organization), English (WHO), and symbols (:), convert these words into their respective Braille engines, and then arrange the words in their original order to obtain a sentence written in Braille.
In this process, the Korean character divination model, the English character divination model, the other foreign language divination model, and the symbol divination model may have been pre-trained by inputting training data including corpus pairs for Korean and Braille, corpus pairs for English and Braille, corpus pairs for other foreign languages and Braille, and corpus pairs for symbols and Braille into at least one of the unsupervised learning model, the supervised learning model, and the reinforcement learning model. At this time, the symbol divination model may include a character symbol divination model, a mathematical symbol divination model, and a special symbol divination model.
And in each braille model, the pair of corpora that are the target of learning correspond one-to-one. For example, in the case of the Korean braille model, one Korean word corresponds one-to-one to one Braille word, in the case of the English braille model, one English word corresponds one-to-one to one Braille word, and in the case of the symbol braille model, one symbol corresponds one-to-one to one Braille word. However, in reality, one Braille word can have at least two or more meanings among Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols. In other words, in the case of the conventional braille-to-reverse braille model, there are cases where the Braille word has ambiguous meaning, and in such cases, the translation is often not performed properly. However, the present invention can perform an accurate translation by dividing a word into Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols, and implementing a braille model that matches the divided words one-to-one. In other words, and Korean words, English words, other foreign language words, and symbols can be defined as the same single Braille, but in the corpus pairs of each category consisting of the corpus pairs for Korean and Braille, the corpus pairs for the above English and Braille, the corpus pairs for other foreign languages and Braille, and the corpus pairs for symbols and Braille, one Braille word can be included in the corpus pairs of multiple categories, but there are no duplicate Braille words within one corpus pair.
If Korean, English, and other foreign languages and symbols are not pre-trained as Braille and corpus pairs, the same Braille characters may be interpreted as different print characters. This will be explained with reference to Figures 7 through 11 below.
Figures 7 and 8 are examples of word pairs that have two or more meanings when the same Braille character is used as a stressor.
Figures 9 and 10 are examples showing sentences that can have two or more meanings when the same Braille character is emphasized.
Figure 11 is an example diagram showing a common reverse dot error in a sentence that mixes Korean, English, other foreign languages, and punctuation marks.
According to Figures 7 and 8, the problem that occurs because one Braille character has different meanings in Korean, English, and other foreign languages and symbols is shown.
For example, as shown in (a) of Figure 7, the Braille notation for "어!", which is a combination of Hangul and a symbol, and the Hangul "억" are identical. Accordingly, when the Braille is used as in the Braille examples of Figures 9 (a) and (b), if the print conversion is performed in a state learned by a corpus pair, it can be interpreted as "Bring it from the Tangsuyuk sauce bu"어!" or "Bring it from the Tangsuyuk sauce bu"육"." However, if the examples are not learned in advance as corpus pairs, they can be interpreted as meaningless sentences, such as "Bring it from the Tangsuyuk sauce bu"육" or "Bring it from the Tangsuyuk sauce bu"어!".
As another example, as shown in (b) of Fig. 7, the Korean letter "거" and the symbol "$" have the same Braille notation. Therefore, when the Braille is used as in the Braille examples in (c) and (d) of Fig. 9, if converted to print while trained by a corpus pair, it can be interpreted as "$100 is expensive" or "Spiders are arthropods." However, if the examples are not trained in advance as corpus pairs, they can be interpreted as meaningless sentences such as "거100 is expensive" or "$미 is arthropods."
As another example, as shown in (a) of Fig. 8, the Braille notation for "He/", which is a combination of English and special symbols, and the English "He still" are identical. Accordingly, when the Braille is used as in the Braille example of (a) of Fig. 10, if converted to print while trained by a corpus pair, it can be interpreted as "He "still" meets his wife." However, if the examples are not trained in advance as corpus pairs, they can be interpreted as meaningless sentences, such as "He "/" meets his wife", as in (b) of Fig. 10.
As another example, as shown in (b) of Fig. 8, the combination of a number symbol and a special symbol, "'8", and the special symbol "double quotation mark (")" have the same Braille notation. Therefore, when the Braille is used as in the Braille example of (c) of Fig. 10, if converted to print while trained by a corpus pair, it can be interpreted as "hundreds of people." However, if the examples are not trained in advance as a corpus pair, they can be interpreted as a meaningless sentence, such as '8hundreds of people'8, as in (d) of Fig. 10.
According to Fig. 11, (a) and (b) of Fig. 11 are sentences containing Korean, English, other foreign languages, and symbols. Fig. 11 (a) is a Braille sentence indicating "STEP1, STEP2 are basic learning courses." If this is emphasized in print, the Braille corresponding to "STEP1, STEP2" and "다.", which are marked in red in the first sentence, may be incorrectly emphasized as "ㅎ?尸?1, ?尸?2" and "??", respectively. Accordingly, the sentence may become an incorrect sentence as "ㅎ?尸?1, ?尸?2 are basic learning courses??". In addition, if another sentence "The next step is STEP2" is emphasized, it may be incorrectly interpreted as "The next step is ㅎ?尸?2??".
Next, if the Braille corresponding to the sentence in (b) of Fig. 11, "After completing the first day's study material of Tip Part 1 of the study method, review with TEST-previous questions," is emphasized in print, the Braille corresponding to "Tip," "Part 1," "TEST-," and "yo." highlighted in red may be incorrectly emphasized as "ㅎ설두", "ㅎㅅ루1", "ㄹㅎ설??", and "?F", respectively. As shown in Figures 7 through 11 above, the reason a single Braille character can have multiple meanings in print is because, with only 63 dot shapes available in Braille, the duplication of dot shapes is inevitable. An artificial intelligence model according to an additional embodiment of the present invention is a Korean-Braille bidirectional translation engine using a sequence-to-sequence model or a transformer including an encoder and a decoder module, wherein input characters can be converted into numbers through an embedding layer before being input to the sequence-to-sequence model. At this time, the encoder sequentially compresses all word information in an input sentence to create a single context vector, and the decoder translates the context vector to sequentially output words, and the context vector can have a size of hundreds of dimensions or more.
Additionally, the encoder and decoder have multiple RNNs (Recurrent Neural Networks) built inside, and can utilize the LSTM (Long-Short Term Memory) structure or the GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit) structure to solve the vanishing gradient problem.

## 688. [KR20210115265A] An Implementation Method for the Adaptive Learning System Based on Artificial Neural Network Technology
- **Patent ID / App No**: `KR20210115265A`
- **Source**: Google Patents
- **URL**: [https://patents.google.com/patent/KR20210115265A/en](https://patents.google.com/patent/KR20210115265A/en)
- **AI Relevancy Score**: N/A (UNAUDITED)

### 📋 Abstract
> Translated from Korean This method is an adaptive learning method that increases learning efficiency by using artificial intelligence technology in study papers or reference materials in the technical field. The artificial intelligence system used is applied when learners encounter sentences that they do not understand while reading reference books or specialized books, or when they do not understand the sentences while solving practice problems in related subjects. It is a method of decomposing the sentence into components and then displaying several easy use cases to help understand each element sequentially. This artificial intelligence system consists of three artificial neural networks. The first artificial neural network is a system that inputs a sentence of a learning target and then decomposes it to output several components (terms). The second is an artificial neural network that outputs standardized terms when inputting terms with similar expressions. Of course, if you input a 'standard term', the output will be the same as the input. Third, the artificial neural network is a recurrent neural network that outputs 'standard terms' as input and easily understandable fact information. For example, in the case of 'Galileo asserted that the earth revolves around the sun', the result of the parsing is 'Galileo', 'Earth', 'Sun', 'Around', 'Rotates', and 'Assert'. do. If you enter the first item 'Galileo', 'Galileo made a telescope several times', 'Galileo observed the movement of stars with a telescope', 'Galileo knew that the sun was bigger than the Earth', 'Galileo was a small star' I found out that it revolves around this big star' is the output of the artificial neural network at the end. This artificial intelligence system can be called an adaptive learning method because the learning items or learning target sentences are different depending on the learner.

> Translated from Portuguese EQUIPMENT FOR EXPERIMENTAL PRACTICES FOR CONTROLLING ACTUATORS AND ACQUIRING SENSOR DATA IN REAL TIME This equipment is an interface for real-time experimental practices that enables the acquisition of sensor data and actuator commands for conducting educational experiments in the areas of mathematics and natural sciences (physics, chemistry and biology) and their technologies. ### 📜 Full Specification & Deep Scrape Text
Title
EQUIPMENT FOR EXPERIMENTAL PRACTICES FOR ACTUATOR CONTROL AND REAL-TIME SENSOR DATA ACQUISITION

Abstract
Translated from Portuguese
EQUIPMENT FOR EXPERIMENTAL PRACTICES FOR CONTROLLING ACTUATORS AND ACQUIRING SENSOR DATA IN REAL TIME This equipment is an interface for real-time experimental practices that enables the acquisition of sensor data and actuator commands for conducting educational experiments in the areas of mathematics and natural sciences (physics, chemistry and biology) and their technologies. In practice, this interface allows teachers and students to monitor and interact in real time with data acquisition and actuator control so that a single experiment can be shared and viewed by everyone during in-person classes. This device facilitates such practices, because once the interface is built, the user has a “plug and play” system for connecting various sensors and actuators for presentations and demonstration of experimental practices.

Description
Translated from Portuguese
[001] The present invention relates to an interface for real-time experimental practices and hardware that enables the acquisition of data from sensors and commands to actuators to carry out educational experiments in the areas of mathematics and natural sciences (physics, chemistry and biology) and their technologies.
[002] In practice, this interface allows teachers and students to monitor and interact in real time with data acquisition and actuator control so that a single experiment can be shared and viewed by everyone during face-to-face classes. This device facilitates such practices, because once the interface is built, the user has a “plug and play” system for connecting various sensors and actuators for presentations and experimental practices.
[003] The present invention is an equipment for experimental teaching practices with sensors and actuators that has an input for testing various devices. Currently, what we have are suggestions for teaching experiments, in which each experiment requires the assembly of different circuits for the operation of the sensor or actuator that will be used, in addition to the need to test a new hardware configuration for each new experiment. As a consequence, the user, in order to be willing to set up a teaching experiment involving sensors and actuators, needs time and knowledge of electronics and some programming language.
[004] This equipment has a single piece of hardware that, connected to the computer, has a single input for connecting sensors and actuators. In this way, we can perform and test several educational experiments in a plug-and-play format on the same circuit, optimizing time and without burdening the user with the need for programming and knowledge of electronics.
[005] The teaching of Natural Sciences is strengthened by the implementation of experimental practices, the elucidation of concepts and the interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary contextualization. These learning situations can be greatly favored by the use of Information and Communication Technologies - ICTs, since they constitute instrumental bases capable of allowing various methodological possibilities and are increasingly present in the daily life of schools. However, while on the one hand the use of these technologies in pedagogical environments is recognized as legitimate, on the other hand it is limited by several factors. Among these are issues such as the lack of technical knowledge of the teacher in the area of ICTs, making it difficult to include technologies as learning instruments; the lack of time available to set up experiments; the lack of physical space and materials in schools that allow the experiments to be carried out.
[006] Several studies point to the use of the Arduino platform as a useful tool for teaching mathematics and natural sciences, however each author shows a different assembly and configuration of this device for each experiment to be carried out. These facts make the use of this tool unfeasible in everyday life and often in lesson planning.
[007] The proposed interface has the innovation of providing a single connection for various types of sensors and actuators without the need to assemble a new electrical diagram for each new experiment, which makes it viable to use it effectively in classrooms for pedagogical purposes and not just academic purposes for research and production of articles. Thus, the proposed interface overcomes all of the aforementioned limiting factors by using hardware that is simple to build/acquire and low cost, capable of promoting the use of ICTs in the development of teaching mathematics and natural sciences effectively.
[008] The invention can be better understood through the following detailed description, in accordance with the attached figures where: FIGURE 01 represents the hardware scheme for building the interface. FIGURE 02 represents the flowchart of the programming logic. FIGURE 03 represents the interface displayed for the user to choose the sensors and actuators connected to the interface. FIGURE 04 represents the distance sensor SR04. FIGURE 05 represents the LED scheme as an actuator. FIGURE 06 represents the image of the physical interface for connecting sensors and actuators. FIGURE 07 represents the implementation scheme of the SVD. FIGURE 08 represents the initial screen of the data visualization system. FIGURE 09 represents the temperature data acquisition screen over time.
[009] The present invention is an interface for real-time experimental practices. It is a hardware that enables the acquisition of data from sensors and commands to actuators for conducting educational experiments in the areas of mathematics and natural sciences (physics, chemistry and biology) and their technologies. In practice, this interface allows the teacher and students to monitor in real time the acquisition of data and control of actuators so that a single experiment can be shared and viewed by everyone during face-to-face classes. This device facilitates such practices, because once the interface is built, the user has a “plug and play” system for connecting several sensors and actuators for presentations and conducting experimental practices. The interface consists of an Arduino nano board: control and data acquisition board; a 10 Kw potentiometer; a used to control actuators; a push button: for resetting; a USB A input: connector for interfacing; a USB cable (AM-BM): connection field between the interface hardware and the computer; a plastic box; support for the hardware; a tripod: support for the plastic box;
[009] FIGURE 01 shows the connections required to build the interface.
[010] FIGURE 02 demonstrates the programming logic, since in addition to the hardware it was necessary to develop programming logic for the integrated circuit to activate different actuators or capture data from different sensors according to the user's needs.
[011] FIGURE 03 shows how the user can access the different sensors/actuators through the interface.
[012] FIGURE 04 and Figure 05 demonstrate the connection of sensors/actuators and the male connector for connection to the interface.
[013] FIGURE 06 represents the real-time data visualization system (DVS) is a software that enables the display of graphs from sensors connected to real-time data acquisition hardware. This system was implemented using the JAVA language and its development was based on the following functional requirements: RF01. The DVS must capture data from the interface and illustrate them graphically in real time. RF02. It must have a button to start data capture; RF03. It must have a button to pause data capture; RF04. It must have a button to restart data capture. And non-functional requirements: RNF01. It must contain fonts that facilitate data reading; RNF02. It must be operational in Linux and Windows; RNF03. It must be implemented in JAVA; RNF04. It must have easy-to-navigate windows.
[009] To implement the SVD, distance and temperature sensors and an LED were used as an actuator. These, in turn, respond to a physical or chemical stimulus, for example, temperature sensors (transducers) convert the temperature into an electrical signal, which can be interpreted by Arduino and sent to the microcomputer. Thus, stimuli from the environment were initially captured by the sensors. Then, the Arduino controller receives (reads) the information from the sensor, sends (writes) this information to Java and applies the data coming from Arduino to the graph through the JfreeChart library.
[010] The link between Java and Arduino was established through a specific class, where the serial port settings were determined. Thus, every second or 1,000 milliseconds, data is captured and shown on the graph, since the lowest value accepted for time is 1 millisecond, while the maximum time consists of 8,388,480 microseconds.
[011] Communication between Java and the computer's serial port was established through Java's RXTX library. It is an RXTX serial communication API for reading and writing to serial ports, and has been ported to Windows, Linux and Mac.
[012] FIGURE 07 shows the main screen where all the sensors and actuators that the user can choose to perform an experiment are available.
[013] FIGURE 08 shows a 45-second period of data acquisition from a temperature sensor. On this screen, it is possible to observe two buttons in the lower center. The first (on the left PPeettiiççããoo887700213900003049361301,,ddee2259//0041//22002139,,ppáágg.. 190//4272 to the right) is a start/pause button, that is, one can start data acquisition during an explanation or pause to better elucidate the phenomenon. The second button is a restart button, that is, the user can clear the graph on the screen and restart data acquisition. Finally, the data captured from the sensor during the experiment can be presented simultaneously.

The technology disclosed relates to a system and method of exporting learned features between federated endpoints whose learning is confined to respective training datasets. The system includes logic to access a first training dataset to train a first federated endpoint and a second training dataset to train a second federated endpoint. The first and second training datasets have first and second sample sets that share one or more shared sample features. The shared sample features are common between the first and second sample sets. The system includes logic to train a first generator on the first federated endpoint. The system includes logic to use the first trained generator for a second inference on a second performance task executed on the second federated endpoint.

FIELD OF THE TECHNOLOGY DISCLOSED
The disclosed system and method are in the field of machine learning. To be more specific, technology disclosed relates to using artificial intelligence and machine learning for federated transfer learning.
BACKGROUND
The subject matter discussed in this section should not be assumed to be prior art merely as a result of its mention in this section. Similarly, a problem mentioned in this section or associated with the subject matter provided as background should not be assumed to have been previously recognized in the prior art. The subject matter in this section merely represents different approaches, which in and of themselves can also correspond to implementations of the claimed technology.
Insufficient data can result in weak performance by machine learning models. In many applications such as healthcare, data related to same users or entities such as patients are maintained by separate departments in one organization or separate organizations resulting in data silos. A data silo is a situation in which only one group or department in an organization can access a data source. Raw data regarding the same users from multiple data sources cannot be combined due to privacy regulations and laws. Examples of different data sources can include health insurance data, medical claims data, mobility data, genomic data, environmental or exposomic data, laboratory tests and prescriptions data, trackers and bed side monitors data, etc. Therefore, in many real-world situations either raw data or labeled training data from different sources cannot be combined to train powerful machine learning models that can provide insights and predictions for providing better services and products to users.
An opportunity arises to train high performance machine learning models by utilizing different and heterogenous data sources without sharing data across computing devices.
