The identity authentication in this embodiment includes: detecting and analyzing identity identification and authentication mechanism measures, password security management, account lock setting options, account security management and evaluating; the access control includes: detecting and analyzing default sharing settings, whether they comply with the principle of least authorization, detecting and analyzing privileged user management, file system security features, and network service security, and evaluating; the security audit includes: detecting and analyzing system logs, audit policies and evaluating. The intrusion prevention in this embodiment includes: detecting and analyzing patch management, vulnerability risks and evaluating. The malicious code prevention of this embodiment includes: detecting and analyzing malicious code software management and evaluating. The resource control of this embodiment includes: detecting and analyzing resource control strategies and evaluating. The security risks of the application system of this embodiment include: security function design, security weaknesses, and weaknesses in security deployment. The detection and analysis of input validation in this embodiment includes: detecting whether the application verifies all input data, whether all input data verifies the length, range, format, type, whether there is dependence on the user-side verification code, whether the application trusts the data written to the Web page, whether to filter or convert all codes and system command content in the user-submitted data, whether to verify the data at the access point when transferring data between different trust boundaries, detecting whether the application system uses an independent database account, assigns the minimum library, table and field permissions, detects whether the database prohibits or deletes unnecessary stored procedures, whether to shield database error messages, analyzes whether there is or may be unverified data written to the Web page, using unverified input to generate SQL queries, using unsafe data access coding technology to increase SQLInjection threats, using deny methods instead of allow to filter input, using input files or URLs (Uniform Resource Locator) or user names to make security decisions, and relying on one or more problems in client verification. The detection and analysis of identity authentication in this embodiment includes: detecting whether the user name and password are sent in plain text on an unprotected channel, whether there is a special encryption method for sensitive information, whether the certificate is stored, and if it is stored, how to store and protect it, whether to implement strong passwords, what kind of password policy is implemented, whether identity authentication has added secondary authentication, whether to perform graphic verification codes or SMS verification codes, how to verify credentials, how to identify authenticated users after the first login, and analyzing whether there is or may be authentication credentials or authentication cookies transmitted on unencrypted network links, causing credential capture or session attacks, and whether there is unauthorized access caused by weak passwords and account policies. The detection and analysis of authorization in this embodiment includes: detecting whether necessary behavioral audits have been conducted, what kind of access control is used at the application entry point, whether the application uses roles, and if roles are used, whether the granularity is fine enough for access control and audit purposes, detecting whether the application restricts access to system resources, detecting whether database access is restricted, how to authorize the database, analyzing whether unauthorized roles and accounts are used, whether sufficient role granularity is provided, and whether system resources are restricted to specific application identities. The detection and analysis of configuration management in this embodiment includes: detecting how to protect the remote management interface, how to protect the configuration storage, whether the sensitive configuration data is encrypted, whether to separate the administrator privileges, whether to use the process and service accounts with the lowest privileges, whether to manage the management IP with whitelist policy, analyzing whether to store the configuration confidential information in plain text including the connection string and the service account certificate, analyzing whether to protect the appearance of the application configuration management including the management interface, analyzing whether to use the unauthorized process account and service account, analyzing whether the installation script deletes the data directory and the file name is fixed, configuring the file extension, and analyzing whether the directory permissions are improperly set. The detection and analysis of sensitive data in this implementation includes: detecting whether confidential information is stored in permanent storage, how to store sensitive data, whether sensitive data is transmitted on the network, whether sensitive data is disaster-prepared, analyzing whether to save when confidential information is not needed, whether to store confidential information in plain text in the code, and whether to transmit sensitive data in plain text on the network. The detection and analysis of session management in this embodiment includes: detecting how to generate session cookies, how to exchange session identifiers, how to protect session status when crossing networks, how to protect session status to prevent session attacks, how to protect session status storage, whether the application limits the lifetime of the session, how the application uses session storage for identity authentication, analyzing whether the session identifier is transmitted on an unencrypted channel, whether the lifetime of the session is extended, whether it is stored in an unsafe session state, and whether the session identifier is located in the query string. The detection and analysis of encryption technology in this embodiment includes: detecting what algorithm and encryption technology are used, whether the application uses a custom encryption algorithm, detecting how long the key is, how to protect it, detecting how often the key is changed, how to publish the key, analyzing the use of custom encryption methods, whether the wrong algorithm or a key with too short a length is used, whether the key is not protected, and whether the same key is used for an extended time period. The detection and analysis of exception management in this embodiment includes: detecting how the application handles error conditions, whether the exception is allowed to propagate back to the client, whether the application displays too much information to the client, where the application records the detailed resources of the exception, whether the log file is safe, and analyzing whether all input parameters are verified and whether too much information is displayed to the client. The detection, auditing and logging of this embodiment include: detecting whether the application determines the main activities to be audited, whether the application is audited across all layers and servers, how to protect the log files, analyzing whether there are no logins that have failed to be audited, whether the audit files are not protected, and whether the audit is not conducted across the application layers and servers. The detection and analysis of habit problems in this embodiment include: detecting programming habits, analyzing whether the programmer likes to modify the program directly on the server, causing the editor to generate multiple backup files on the server, whether the file may expose the program code, and analyzing whether the programmer saves sensitive information including database passwords in the file. The penetration test of this embodiment includes: within the permitted and controllable range, using controllable hacker intrusion techniques that do not cause irreparable losses, launching attacks on the network and system, invading the system to obtain confidential information, and forming a report based on the intrusion process and details. The patch check, account password, and network service check of this embodiment can be checked through a vulnerability scanning tool. The virus protection check can be performed through a malicious code killing tool. The local policy check can be checked by viewing the local security policy, checking the script, and configuring the scanning tool. The detection and analysis of database username and password management includes: detecting and analyzing user permission settings, password policy settings, and redundant account management. The detection and analysis of database access control in this embodiment includes: detection and analysis of access IP address control and communication security configuration. The detection and analysis of data security in this embodiment includes: detection and analysis of sensitive information storage methods and database backup. The detection and analysis of database security audit in this embodiment includes: detection and analysis of login log audit and operation log audit. The detection and analysis of physical security boundaries in this embodiment includes: detection and analysis of whether security boundaries are set to protect the security of sensitive information, dangerous information, and information processing facilities. The detection and analysis of physical entrance control in this embodiment includes: detection and analysis of whether the security area is protected by entrance control and whether it is ensured that only authorized personnel are allowed to access. The detection and analysis of security protection of offices, rooms, and facilities includes: detection and analysis of whether physical security measures are adopted in offices, rooms, and facilities. The detection and analysis of security protection against external and environmental threats includes: detection and analysis of whether physical security measures are adopted to prevent natural disasters, malicious attacks or accidents. The detection and analysis of work control in secure areas includes: detection and analysis of whether physical protection measures and guidelines for work in secure areas are designed and applied. The detection and analysis of delivery and handover areas includes: detection and analysis of whether access points including handover areas and other points where unauthorized personnel enter the office are controlled, whether they are isolated from information processing facilities, and whether unauthorized access is avoided. The detection and analysis of equipment placement and protection include: detection and analysis of whether the equipment is placed and protected, whether environmental threats and hazards are reduced or avoided, and whether unauthorized access is reduced or avoided. The detection and analysis of supporting equipment include: detection and analysis of whether the equipment is protected and whether the equipment is protected from power failure or termination caused by the failure of supporting facilities. The detection and analysis of cabling security include: detection and analysis of whether the power and communication cables that transmit data or support information services are protected and whether they are protected from interception or destruction. The detection and analysis of equipment maintenance include: detection and analysis of whether the equipment is properly protected and whether the continuous availability and integrity of the equipment are ensured. The detection and analysis of asset movement include: detection and analysis of whether equipment, information, and software cannot be taken out of the organization before authorization. The detection and analysis of off-site equipment and asset security include: detection and analysis of whether security measures are taken for assets outside the site and whether the different risks of working outside the organization's site are considered. The detection and analysis of safe disposal or reuse of equipment include: detection and analysis of whether all items of equipment containing storage media are checked and whether any sensitive information and registered software are deleted or securely overwritten before disposal. The detection and analysis of unattended user equipment include: detection and analysis of whether unattended user equipment is protected. The detection and analysis of the strategy of clearing the desktop and screen includes: detection and analysis of whether the strategy of clearing the files and removable storage media on the desktop is adopted, and whether the strategy of clearing the screen of the information processing facility is adopted. The detection and analysis of the middleware username and password management includes: detection and analysis of user permission settings, password policy settings, and redundant account management. The detection and analysis of the middleware security audit includes: detection and analysis of login log audit and operation log audit. The detection and analysis of the middleware intrusion prevention strategy includes: detection and analysis of SSL protection activation, default port modification, and application server socket number limit.
Furthermore, the information collection and analysis of the present embodiment includes: retrieving one or more materials from policy documents, rules and regulations and process management records, information system overall description documents, information system detailed description documents, information system security protection level classification reports, security requirements analysis reports, information system security overall plans, security status evaluation reports, information system security detailed design plans, user guides, operation steps, network diagrams, and configuration management documents; analyzing the basic information, management framework, network and equipment deployment, business types and characteristics, business data, user scope, and user type of the information system; conducting comprehensive analysis and collation; analyzing the industry characteristics, supervisory agencies, business scope, geographical location, background information, contact methods, organizational management structure, management strategies, department settings, the role of departments in business operation terminals, job responsibilities, physical environment, network topology, hardware equipment deployment, scope and boundaries, business types and characteristics, business processes, and business security protection levels of the information system; and forming an information system basic situation analysis report.
The determination of the evaluation object in this embodiment includes: detecting information system information, analyzing the entire unit information system and the business system involved, identifying and describing the overall structure of the information system according to the basic situation analysis report of the information system, the description content includes the identification of the information system, the physical environment of the information system, the network topology of the information system, and the connection status of the external boundary of the information system, providing a network topology diagram, identifying and describing the boundary of the information system, and describing the boundary connection mode of the information system and other networks, including the use of optical fiber, wireless, and dedicated lines. The devices describing the boundary include one or more of firewalls, routers, and servers. If there is a shared device at the boundary connection of the information system, the device is classified into a relatively high-level information system. For information systems that have not been divided into regions, they are divided and described according to the actual situation of the information system. The description content includes regional division, the main business applications of each region, business processes, the boundaries of the region, and the connection between them. The nodes of the information system are described with regions as clues, and the computer hardware devices, network hardware devices, communication lines, and application system software in each region are described, and the connection status between each node is explained. Computer hardware devices include server devices, client devices, printers, and storage. Network hardware equipment includes: switches, routers, and adapters; organize the above descriptions to determine the evaluation information system and describe it. The description is based on the network topology of the information system, using a general-to-specific description method. First, describe the overall structure, then describe the external boundary connection status and the main boundary equipment, and then describe the network area composition, business functions, and related equipment nodes of the information system; analyze each business system, analyze the importance of the business system and its related equipment and components, determine the evaluation object, and describe it according to the category of the business system, including network, network equipment, servers, hosts, and application systems. Use a list to describe each type of evaluation object, including the area to which the evaluation object belongs, the equipment name, purpose, equipment information, and spot check instructions. Determining the evaluation indicators includes: obtaining the classification results of the information system based on the basic situation analysis report of the information system, including the business information security protection level and the system service security protection level, and deriving the combination of ASG (A system service assurance class, S business information security class, G basic requirements class) security protection measures that the information system should take; selecting the corresponding level of security requirements as evaluation indicators according to the standards, including the selection of the three types of ASG security requirements, and describing each business system separately, and the description content includes the classification results of the business system and the selection of indicators. Determining the evaluation content includes: determining the one-way evaluation content and the system evaluation content, analyzing the basic situation analysis report of the information system, the evaluation object, evaluation indicators, and evaluation tool access points of the evaluation plan, combining the evaluation indicators and the evaluation object, and then combining the evaluation object with the evaluation method, combining the evaluation indicators at all levels with the specific evaluation object and explaining the evaluation method, forming the evaluation implementation unit, combining the evaluation indicators and the evaluation object to explain the single evaluation implementation work content, and compiling the corresponding evaluation content according to the evaluation tool access points. The one-way evaluation content includes evaluation indicators, evaluation objects, evaluation methods, and evaluation implementation. According to the evaluation methods of relevant standards, combined with the actual situation of the information system and evaluation experience, determine the system evaluation content, and output the single evaluation implementation and system evaluation implementation parts of the evaluation plan. The development of the evaluation guide includes: describing a single evaluation object including the name, IP address, purpose, and management personnel of the evaluation object according to the test tool access point, single evaluation implementation, and system evaluation implementation; determining the evaluation activities including evaluation items, evaluation methods, operation steps, and expected results according to the single evaluation implementation and system evaluation implementation; and outputting the evaluation guide of the evaluation plan; the evaluation items refer to the requirements of the evaluation object in the use case in the standard, and the evaluation methods include: interviews, document retrieval and review, configuration inspection, tool testing, and on-site inspection and review; each evaluation item corresponds to one or more evaluation methods. Operation steps include commands or steps executed in the evaluation activities. If tool testing is involved, the requirements of the detection equipment and tools are described, including the model, specifications, and version of the tool. The expected results include the results obtained under normal circumstances according to the operation steps and the evidence obtained. Preparation of an assessment plan includes: extracting the source of the project, the overall information construction of the unit where the information system is located, and the connection status with other systems of the unit according to the entrusted assessment agreement and the basic situation analysis report of the information system; listing the standards on which the assessment activities are based according to the level assessment implementation requirements in the level protection process; estimating the assessment workload according to the entrusted assessment agreement and the information system situation, and estimating according to the number of nodes configured for detection and the access points and test content of the tool test; preparing a specific assessment plan based on assessment experience and the scale of the information system, including personnel division of labor and time arrangements. The assessment should avoid the business peak period of the information system; forming a preliminary draft of the assessment plan based on the above content and the content obtained from the tasks of the plan preparation activity, and outputting the assessment plan after review and confirmation.
Preparation for the implementation of the assessment includes: confirming the resources required for the assessment, including supporting personnel and assessment conditions, and updating the assessment plan or assessment procedure as required. On-site assessment and result recording include: checking whether the systems, policies, and operating procedures required by the standards are complete, checking whether there are complete records of system implementation, including computer room entry and exit registration records, electronic records, and registration records for the use of key equipment in high-level systems, reviewing and analyzing documents, and checking the integrity of documents and the internal consistency between files; checking whether the configuration of application systems, host systems, database systems, and network equipment is correct based on the assessment result records, and whether they are consistent with documents, related equipment, and components, and verifying the content of the document review, including log auditing; if the system receives an invalid command and cannot complete the configuration check, an error test is performed; for the network Verify the connection rules based on the network connection; test the system according to the evaluation plan, including vulnerability scanning based on network detection and host audit, website vulnerability scanning, database vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, performance testing, intrusion detection, and protocol analysis; detect personnel behavior, technical facilities, and physical environment status according to the actual situation of the information system to judge the security awareness of personnel, business operations, management procedures, and the security of the system's physical environment, and evaluate whether the corresponding level of security requirements have been met, record the evaluation results of management security evaluation, record the network, host, and application evaluation results of technical security evaluation, record the physical security evaluation results of technical security evaluation, and the test results after tool evaluation. Result confirmation and data return include: summarizing evaluation records, summarizing problems, evidence, and evidence sources found in the evaluation, supplementing evaluations of missed content and content that needs further verification, and recording the summary of problems found in the evaluation, evidence, and evidence sources. The determination of single evaluation results includes: testing each evaluation item. If the evaluation item is applicable, the multiple evaluation results actually obtained during the evaluation are compared with the expected evaluation results. The conformity between each evaluation result and the expected result is determined. The evaluation results of each evaluation item corresponding to the evaluation implementation are obtained to determine whether they are in compliance or not. Based on the judgment of all evaluation results, the evaluation results of the evaluation item are comprehensively judged to determine whether they are in compliance, partially in compliance or not, and the single evaluation records and results are output. The summary analysis of single evaluation results includes: summarizing the single evaluation results of the corresponding evaluation indicators of different evaluation objects at different levels, including the number of evaluation items and the number of items that meet the requirements. The overall assessment includes: for single assessment items that are non-compliant or partially compliant with the assessment object, analyze whether other security controls related to the assessment can be associated with it, what kind of association can occur, and whether the effects of these associations can make up for the shortcomings of the assessment item; analyze whether other assessment objects at other levels related to the assessment item can be associated with it, what kind of association can occur, and whether the effects of these associations can make up for the shortcomings of the assessment item; analyze whether other assessment objects in other areas related to the assessment item can be associated with it, what kind of association can occur, and whether the effects of these associations can make up for the shortcomings of the assessment item; analyze the security of the overall structure of the information system from a security perspective, and analyze the rationality of the overall security prevention of the information system from a system perspective; output the overall assessment results of the information system. The formation of security assessment conclusions includes: combining the individual assessment results with the overall assessment results to summarize and analyze the individual assessment results of each assessment object in the physical security, host security, and application security levels, and counting the compliance situations; analyzing the security risks and reasons for the assessment items that do not meet the requirements to the information system, and judging the impact on the overall protection capabilities of the information system; based on the results of the summary analysis of the individual assessment results, if there are assessment items that do not meet the requirements, it is judged that the information system does not meet the basic security protection capabilities of the corresponding level; if all assessment items meet the requirements, it is judged that the information system meets the basic security protection capabilities of the corresponding level; and outputting the level assessment conclusion. The preparation of the evaluation report includes: making improvement suggestions from the perspective of system security for the security risks existing in the information system; preparing the evaluation report according to the evaluation plan, single evaluation records and results, single evaluation result summary analysis, overall evaluation structure, and grade evaluation conclusion; forming a corresponding evaluation report according to the number of information systems; providing a list of evaluation documents and single evaluation records, and the judgment of the single evaluation results of each evaluation item; reviewing and confirming the evaluation report according to the evaluation agreement, relevant documents, original evaluation records and auxiliary information, and outputting the information system grade evaluation report. Security strategy includes: draft design, review, implementation, training, deployment, monitoring, reinforcement, re-evaluation, revision, and ensuring the timeliness and effectiveness of security strategy through management. The security technology system is the basis of the information system framework, including: network security, host security, terminal security, application security, data security, and security integrated management platform. Guided by the security strategy, a complete security technology protection system with coordinated parts is established from the multi-level perspectives of network security protection, host system security protection, application security protection, terminal security protection, and data security protection. The security organization and management system is based on the overall security strategy and cooperates with the security technology system. The operation guarantee system includes: security operation and maintenance management, daily operation guarantee, security emergency response, and data system backup. Security operation and maintenance management includes: network security operation and maintenance management, host security operation and maintenance management, and application security operation and maintenance management. Network security operation and maintenance management includes: unified operation authentication, authorization, and auditing of the entire network system, using dynamic passwords to authenticate equipment maintenance operations on the network system, encrypting and transmitting operation commands, and only authorized users can maintain and manage network equipment. At least two levels of equipment operation permissions are set for the equipment administrator of the network system, and the corresponding settings are set with the operation commands. Management and maintenance operations that exceed the authority are prohibited, and only authorized operations are performed; the operation and maintenance operations of the network system must be audited, and the audit content includes: operation commands, operators, and operation time to ensure that authorized users perform authorized operations.
Further, the host security operation and maintenance management of this embodiment includes: the host system performs unified operation authentication, authorization, and audit. Application security operation and maintenance management includes: the application system performs unified operation authentication, authorization, and audit. Data system backup includes: formulating backup strategies and recovery goals according to data backup requirements, the importance of the business system, and the recovery cost, regularly backing up the server data according to the backup strategy, including the operating system, database, and files, and storing the system's data backup media off-site according to the importance of the data. The off-site backup data at least includes all the original data of the business system and the static data required for the recovery system. Data recovery supports multiple platforms, and the entire system is quickly restored through disaster recovery tapes. Recovery goals include: tolerable data loss and tolerable system recovery time. Physical security assessment includes: assessing the physical security settings corresponding to the information system, including assessing the selection of physical locations, physical access control, anti-theft and anti-destruction, lightning protection, fire protection, waterproofing, moisture resistance, anti-static, temperature and humidity control, power supply, and electromagnetic protection configuration. Network security assessment includes: router/switch assessment, anti-virus system assessment, host system security assessment, application security assessment, and data security assessment. Router/switch evaluation includes: evaluation of router/switch response to important operations, including evaluation of structural security domain network segmentation, network access control, network security audit, boundary integrity check, and network device protection configuration. Antivirus system evaluation includes: evaluation of antivirus system response to important operations, including evaluation of structural security and network segmentation, network security audit, network current prevention, malicious code prevention, and network device protection configuration. Host system security evaluation includes: evaluation of operating system response to important operations, including evaluation of token use, account authentication, password management, login restrictions, identity identification and authentication, subject and object access control, user authorization, security audit, alarm, monitoring, system protection, malicious code protection, residual information protection, and resource control configuration. Operating systems include: Windows system and LINUX operating system. The evaluation of Windows system includes the evaluation of whether the account and password settings are strong enough, including the evaluation of account selection or setting, password length, composition, life cycle, evaluation of whether the desktop application software has a legitimate source, whether to set a screen saver, evaluation of registry security settings, SMP (Symmetric Multi-Processor) service, RPC (Remote Procedure Call) service, security latest patch anti-virus software installation, system resource allocation. The evaluation of LINUX operating system includes: evaluation of operating system response to important operations, including evaluation of token usage, account authentication, password management, login restrictions, identity identification and authentication, subject and object access control, user authorization, security audit, alarm, monitoring, system protection, malicious code protection, residual information protection, resource control supported versions, local buffer overflow vulnerability, installation of the latest security patch, whether irrelevant services are off or there are no unnecessary services, account password, RootPATH (the path of the root file system on the NFS server) environment variable, trust relationship with other hosts, system reinforcement TCP/IP protocol stack configuration. Application security assessment includes: checking and assessing the identity and authentication of the application system, access control of subjects and objects, user authorization, security audit, residual information protection, and resource control. Data security assessment includes: checking the data integrity and confidentiality of the application system, and data backup.
The network security construction of this embodiment includes: security isolation of external boundaries, boundary protection of internal security domains, protection within security domains, network performance protection, and network access control.
The security isolation of the external boundary includes: the boundary protection of the region's external Internet and external units to achieve secure access control and intrusion prevention, prevent unauthorized access from the outside, detect and block the detection and attack behavior on the network, and ensure the security logical isolation of the boundary.
Boundary protection of the internal security domain includes: implementing secure access control and intrusion prevention, preventing unauthorized access from users/businesses in low-security domains, detecting and blocking probing and attacking behaviors on regional application system networks, and ensuring secure logical isolation of boundaries.
Protection within the security domain includes: users/services in the same security domain must use VLAN (Virtual Local Area Network), access control, MPLS-VPN (Multiprotocol Label Switching-Virtual Local Area Network), integrated security technology of network equipment and other means to achieve secure access for internal users/services. VLAN or firewall and other technologies are used within the application system network to achieve secure isolation of different application systems, follow the principle of minimizing access, ensure secure access between application systems, avoid unrestricted access between internal systems, and prevent internal security incidents from spreading through "springboards". Firewalls used for internal security access control can be shared with firewalls at the boundaries of regional application system networks.
Network performance protection includes: statistical analysis of network traffic, application access, etc., using NetFlow, Netstream, Sflow and other technologies to collect, analyze, monitor, record and audit network traffic and network access. It has the ability to protect network performance, prevent PC terminal malware and non-compliant user behavior from abusing network resources, and ensure the reasonable use of network resources and normal user access to internal application systems.
Network access control includes: achieving comprehensive network access control for user PCs, achieving full integration with the company's PKI/CA (public key infrastructure/certificate authority) certificate system, so that only authorized users can access the network, forming a unified authentication system for network access and application system access for the entire unit. The network access control method should adopt a centralized authentication method. Achieve integration with terminal security technical requirements, so that only PC terminals that meet terminal security specifications can access the network to ensure endpoint security.
The operating system reinforcement of this embodiment includes: enabling the operating system password policy, forcing passwords to meet complexity requirements and changing passwords regularly, establishing an independent account for each administrator, modifying the default remote operation and maintenance port, using single user-level control for the administrator's remote login address, setting illegal login policies, and setting audit policies; setting important file permission control policies, deleting unnecessary default shares; disabling unnecessary services and ports, updating system vulnerability patches, and renaming system default accounts; allocating permissions according to the roles of management users, separating management user permissions, and granting management users the minimum permissions required; separating the permissions of privileged users of the operating system and database system, restricting terminal logins according to actual conditions, limiting the maximum or minimum usage limit of system resources by a single user, detecting the system's service level, and issuing an alarm if the system's service level drops below a pre-defined minimum value, setting a forced shutdown of the remote system, setting ownership of the files or objects to be retrieved, setting a local login to this computer, setting a network access to this computer, enabling TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) filtering, enabling the system firewall, enabling SYN (Synchronize Sequence Number) filtering, and enabling TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) filtering. Numbers synchronization sequence number) attack protection, enable the screen saver, set the Microsoft network server suspension time, shut down the service, modify the SNMP service password, shut down invalid startup items, and shut down the Windows AutoPlay function.
The network/security device reinforcement of this embodiment includes: renaming the default accounts of network devices and security devices, setting a higher password length and strategy, using a single user-level control for the remote login address, setting up an independent user account for each device administrator, canceling the telnet mode, using a secure remote management login method including SSH, canceling the default useless services or protocols, setting bandwidth allocation priority, configuring port-level access control, setting application layer filtering, setting network traffic control, setting login failure processing strategy, adjusting and planning the network topology environment; the database reinforcement includes: checking the current configuration of the database, reinforcing the account, authorization, password, log, strategy, and patch respectively, assigning different accounts to different administrators, deleting or locking invalid accounts, restricting super administrator remote login, minimizing permissions, limiting the length and complexity of the default password, limiting the default password generation cycle, limiting password reuse, enabling logging functions, recording user operations on the device, recording system security events, and database audit strategies.
The establishment and improvement of the information security management system implemented in this document include: establishing and implementing a security management system that meets the requirements of the corresponding level in accordance with standard specifications.
The establishment and improvement of the information security management system of this embodiment also includes: implementing information security responsibilities, establishing an information security work leading group, an information security management department or an information security responsibility department, clarifying information security work, determining security positions, implementing personnel, and clarifying the information security responsibilities of the leading organization, responsible departments, and personnel; implementing the personnel security management system, formulating a management system for personnel recruitment, leaving the post, assessment, and education and training, implementing specific measures of the management system, and conducting security reviews, training, assessments, and security and confidentiality education for security position personnel; implementing the system construction management system, establishing information system classification filing, solution design, product procurement and use, password use, software development, project implementation, acceptance and delivery, grade assessment, and security service management systems, and clarifying work content, work methods, work processes, and work requirements; implementing the system operation and maintenance management system, establishing computer room environment safety, storage media safety, equipment and facility safety, security monitoring, network security, system security, malicious code prevention, password protection, backup and recovery, and incident handling management systems, formulating emergency plans, and conducting regular drills.
For this implementation, corresponding systems, strategies, operating procedures, etc. can be formulated according to GB/T22239-2008.
The standards of this embodiment may include, but are not limited to, the following standards: ISO31000 risk management standard, ISO27001:2013 information security management system, GB-T 20984-2007 information security technology information security risk assessment specification, GB-T20269-2006 information system security management requirements, GB-T 20282-2006 information system security engineering management requirements, GB/T9361-2000 computer site security requirements, GB/T 18336-2015 information technology security technology information technology security assessment criteria, "Information Security Level Protection Management Measures" (Public Notice [2007] No. 43), "Notice on Strengthening Information Security Risk Assessment Work for National E-Government Engineering Construction Projects" (Development and Reform Commission [2008] No. 2071), GB/T 22239-2008 Information Security Technology Information System Security Level Protection Basic Requirements, GB/T 22239-XXXX Information Security Technology Network Security Level Protection Basic Requirements (Level Protection 2.0).
The scanning strategies implemented in this paper include: WEB vulnerability scanning, system vulnerability scanning, weak password scanning, special high-risk vulnerability scanning (such as MS17-010, log4j2 vulnerability) and other one or more scanning strategies. You can also select a specific vulnerability knowledge base to generate a dedicated strategy. You can edit the IP, domain name, port, vulnerability template, number of concurrent connections, etc. You can select a template scanning strategy; perform PoC (Proof of Concept) or vulnerability retest on the target system to check whether the target system has security vulnerabilities. Do not use FuZZ scanning to reduce the impact of scanning; the port range can be set according to the settings or needs.
The vulnerabilities of this embodiment include but are not limited to: SQL injection vulnerabilities, XSS vulnerabilities, weak passwords, arbitrary file upload vulnerabilities, directory traversal vulnerabilities, arbitrary command execution vulnerabilities, sensitive information leakage, etc. The above-mentioned vulnerabilities are all vulnerabilities; different vulnerabilities have different repair or configuration methods, for example: the key to solving SQL injection vulnerabilities is to strictly check all data that may come from user input and use the principle of least privilege for database configuration. To solve the file upload vulnerability, it is necessary to strictly limit and verify the uploaded files, prohibit uploading files with malicious code, and limit the execution permissions of related directories to prevent webshell attacks. Improper configuration includes but is not limited to: the existence of default accounts, default sharing is not closed, startup items are not closed, etc. Imprecise configuration includes but is not limited to: not limiting the idle disconnection time of remote login, not limiting the remote login IP address, etc.
The logical tests in the penetration test of this embodiment include but are not limited to: 1. Registration: one is malicious registration, and the other is account traversal; 2. Login: One situation is that there is no verification code on the login interface and it can be directly blasted, the second situation is that there is a verification code but it can be bypassed, and the third situation is that the third-party account login can be bypassed; 3. Overstepping authority: The problem of horizontal overstepping authority occurs on the same role. The system only verifies the role that can access the data, and does not subdivide the users within the role, nor does it subdivide the subset of data, because there is a lack of a corresponding relationship between users and data. Since horizontal permission management is caused by the lack of a data-level access control in the system, horizontal permission management can also be called "data-based access control"; vertical permission problems occur on different roles. Generally speaking, high-authority roles can access the resources of low-authority roles, while low-authority roles are prohibited from accessing the resources of high-authority roles. If a user who originally belongs to a low-authority role can obtain the ability of a low-authority role through some methods, a vertical overstepping authority vulnerability occurs; 4. Transaction: Orders can be maliciously modified, such as modifying the purchase quantity and unit price to form a logical vulnerability of the total amount at an ultra-low price.
A network security protection system based on a unit unit according to an embodiment of the present invention includes:
Vulnerability scanning module: determine the plan, configure the strategy, back up the system, implement the scan, analyze the results, scan again, fix the vulnerability, conduct a second review, and scan again. According to the security vulnerability knowledge base, detect the security risks and vulnerabilities of any one or more information assets in the network protocol, network service, and network equipment, analyze and identify the vulnerabilities that may be used by intruders to illegally enter the network or illegally obtain information assets, and remind that when receiving the host scanning instruction or performing the host scanning, the host data is backed up first. If the server is a dual-machine hot standby system, one of them is scanned in one scanning session. The scanning object strategy is adjusted for hosts or network devices with special requirements. A single host scanning method for a certain system is adopted, and one IP is scanned each time. The next IP is scanned after the scan is completed. The scanning time of the equipment scanning the production network segment is adjusted to a time period that does not affect the business.
Baseline inspection module: collects login information of network devices, security devices, operating systems, databases, and middleware in the target information system, logs in to the target device to check the device configuration, records the configuration information, conducts configuration security analysis, logs in to the network devices, security devices, operating systems, databases, and middleware one by one based on the collected login information, tests the accuracy of the login information collection and the permissions of the provided accounts, analyzes whether all security configuration inspection contents can be covered, and forms a baseline inspection report;
Check the network and security equipment modules: check equipment management (such as console, ssh (Secure Shell), management IP, AAA (Authentication, Authorization, Accounting), account management, authentication and authorization, login method, log audit, service port optimization, security protection (such as SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol), protocol encryption, address spoofing, etc.), security policy rationality, including checking the operating system unit, checking the database unit, checking the Web (World Wide Web) server, and the middleware unit;
Full-flow threat analysis module: Utilizes threat data intelligence and the collected full-network traffic to analyze internal compromised hosts, external attacks, internal violations, and internal risks, analyzes, determines, and traces incidents, and analyzes asset information and related statistical data within the current network;
Intranet asset discovery module: sort out the host assets and WEB servers of the intranet information system, and dynamically manage the intranet asset ledger throughout its life cycle, including: host asset service discovery unit, Web service discovery unit, and asset visualization display unit;
Emergency response module: monitors security issues in business systems, traces attacks at the Internet level through big data analysis, analyzes the causes of security incidents, traces the sources of incidents, classifies security incidents, defends against attacks through big data analysis and security threat intelligence, discovers unknown and dangerous network behaviors, and locates the source of attacks;
Emergency drill module: analysis and judgment. If it is judged to be a suspected computer virus outbreak, determine whether it is a system problem. If it is a system problem, start the system emergency plan. If it is not a system problem, determine whether it is a virus outbreak. If it is a virus outbreak, execute the notification process. If it is not a virus outbreak, determine whether it has network transmission. If it is judged to have network transmission, determine whether it is necessary to isolate the infected host. If it is judged to be isolated, disconnect the host network connection and start the system emergency plan. Determine whether it is necessary to execute anti-virus measures. If it is judged that it is not necessary to isolate, directly determine whether it is necessary to execute anti-virus measures. If it is judged that it is necessary to execute anti-virus measures, determine whether it will cause damage to system data. If it is judged that it will cause damage to the system, perform anti-virus measures after backing up the system. If it is judged that it will not cause damage to the system, directly execute anti-virus measures. After execution, determine whether the virus has been cleared. If it is judged that no anti-virus measures are needed, directly determine whether the virus has been cleared. If it is judged that the virus has been cleared, restore the network connection of the isolated host and execute the notification process. If the virus still exists after the anti-virus measures are executed, continue to execute new virus detection and killing measures until the virus is cleared.
The penetration test modules include: Web penetration test unit and advanced penetration test unit. Web penetration test unit: simulates real security attacks to discover potential ways for hackers to invade information systems, including: information collection, remote overflow, password guessing, local overflow, enterprise user-side attacks, man-in-the-middle attacks, Web scripts and application testing. The advanced penetration test unit includes: combining information security best practices, simulating targeted attacks, using Internet-side assets or internal untrusted/semi-trusted areas as penetration entrances, simulating hacker intranet attacks to obtain the highest permissions or sensitive data on the intranet for further penetration testing, including evaluating the status of external assets, finding intranet access points and using available intranet access points in Internet assets, and deploying jump servers to penetrate the internal network;
The safety operation and maintenance module includes: daily safety operation and maintenance unit, important moment safety assurance unit, and periodic safety inspection unit;
Daily security operation and maintenance units include: security policy optimization, security product operation and maintenance, and security assessment;
Security strategy optimization: Check and improve whether the security control strategy is effective and reasonable, including: research, plan formulation, strategy optimization, and report output;
Security product operation and maintenance includes: equipment operation security monitoring, equipment operation security audit, equipment and policy backup and update;
Security assessment includes: timely discovering security vulnerabilities in information systems through security scanning assessment, rectifying vulnerabilities in Windows, Linux servers and security devices, conducting security scans of information assets during non-business peak hours based on applications and in combination with the security vulnerability knowledge base, not using scan methods that contain denial of service, and immediately stopping the scan if the scanning system does not respond during the scan process, analyzing the situation to determine the cause, restoring the system, and adjusting the scan strategy before scanning;
The security assurance unit at important moments includes: proactively detecting the assets exposed by users on the external network before major holidays, forming an asset list, conducting precise vulnerability scans based on the asset discovery results, conducting comprehensive inspections for specific vulnerabilities, and notifying major security incidents including one or more of high-risk system vulnerabilities, high-risk worm viruses, and malicious intrusions and attacks, providing one or more of the following information: event type, scope of impact, solution, and prevention plan, conducting comprehensive security inspections and security reinforcements on important systems, and retesting the security reinforcement results to confirm that security issues are promptly and effectively repaired; during holidays, real-time alarm monitoring and log analysis of firewalls, Web application firewalls, IDS/IPS (Intrusion Detection Systems/Intrusion Prevention Systems), load balancing, web anti-tampering systems, and network security audit systems, monitoring antivirus software and detection and killing records, monitoring and log analysis of the status of application systems and database systems and business platforms, and promptly investigating and analyzing if attacked or one or more intrusion accidents are discovered, tracing and analyzing the source and cause of the accident, proposing solutions based on the investigation causes and accident situations, and recording accidents, accident analysis, solutions, and tracing plans;
The periodic safety inspection unit includes: periodic safety product inspection, periodic safety strategy optimization suggestions;
The risk assessment module includes: network security assessment unit, host security assessment unit, application security assessment unit, terminal security assessment unit, data security assessment unit, physical security assessment unit, middleware security assessment unit, and management security assessment unit;
The network security assessment unit includes: analyzing the organization's network topology, security domain planning, VLAN division, network equipment configuration, security equipment configuration, and security protection measures; conducting security assessments on the physical network structure, logical network structure, and network equipment; discovering security and network load issues in the network structure, security and anti-attack issues in network equipment; assessing the current security status of the network; and discovering existing security, rationality, and efficiency issues;
The host security assessment unit includes: analyzing the operating system, account, authentication, authorization, network service, system log, patch upgrade, virus protection, and local security policy, discovering security vulnerabilities and potential safety hazards in system configuration and operation, and conducting analysis and assessment based on business application and security baseline configuration, including identity authentication, access control, security audit, intrusion prevention, malicious code prevention, and resource control;
Application security assessment includes: conducting security assessment of the application system based on the account, authentication, authorization, audit, performance resources, backup and recovery, and penetration testing of the application system, detecting and analyzing input verification, identity authentication, authorization, configuration management, sensitive data, session management, encryption technology, exception management, audit and log records, customary problems, and finding security vulnerabilities and potential safety hazards of the application system;
The terminal security assessment unit includes: checking patches, account passwords, network services, virus protection, and local security policies. It assesses the security status of the terminal based on patch upgrades, virus protection, account passwords, network services, and local security policies, and finds security vulnerabilities and potential safety hazards of the terminal.
The data security assessment unit includes: detection and analysis of database username and password management, database access control, login authentication method, data security, security vulnerability inspection, patch management, database security audit, and assessment of data security status based on data confidentiality, integrity, and availability, to find possible security vulnerabilities and potential safety hazards at the data level;
The physical security assessment unit includes: detection and analysis of physical security boundaries, physical entrance control, detection and analysis of security protection of offices, rooms, and facilities, detection and analysis of security protection of external and environmental threats, secure area work control, delivery and handover areas, equipment placement and protection, supporting equipment, cabling safety, equipment maintenance, asset movement, off-site equipment and asset safety, safe disposal or reuse of equipment, unattended user equipment, clearing desktop and screen policies, and assessing the security of the network computer room based on the physical environment of the computer room, access control, power supply, cable laying, equipment placement, labeling specifications, and computer room system;
The middleware security assessment unit includes: detecting and analyzing middleware username and password management, middleware security audit, login authentication method, communication confidentiality, resource control, middleware intrusion prevention strategy, and assessing whether the installation and deployment of the middleware and the implementation of configuration parameters meet the application operation security requirements;
The management security assessment unit includes: evaluating the current status of information security management based on security organization, security system, security personnel, security operation and maintenance, security emergency response, and security training, and identifying possible security risks and gaps.
The information system level protection assessment module includes: level protection gap assessment unit, security assurance system design unit, level protection assessment unit, and information system software rectification unit;
The level protection gap assessment unit includes the following processes: information collection and analysis, preparation of tools and forms, determination of assessment objects, determination of assessment indicators, determination of assessment tool access points, determination of assessment content, development of assessment guidelines, preparation of assessment plans, preparation of assessment implementation, on-site assessment and result recording, result confirmation and data return, determination of single assessment results, summary and analysis of single assessment results, overall assessment, formation of security assessment conclusions, and preparation of assessment reports;
The security assurance system design unit includes: analyzing the weaknesses and risks of the current network and information system through the information system level protection gap assessment unit, making security rectifications, completing the topology design of the corresponding products, implementing security technical measures, and improving the security management system; combining the results of the information system level protection gap assessment unit, in accordance with the information security level protection requirements, and formulating the information security system framework according to the actual situation;
The information security system framework includes: security strategy, security technology system, operation guarantee system, security organization and management system;
The three systems of security strategy and security technology system, operation guarantee system, and security organization and management system interact with each other.
The three major systems of security technology system, operation guarantee system, and security organization and management system are constructed under the guidance of security strategy, transforming various elements formulated in the security strategy into technical implementation methods and management and operation guarantee means to achieve the goals formulated in the security strategy;
The level protection assessment unit includes: testing and evaluating the level protection status of information system security, including the security control assessment and assessment analysis of the implementation and configuration of the basic security controls required by the level protection of information security in the information system, and the overall assessment of the overall security of the information system. The description of the security control assessment is organized in the form of work units. The work units include security technology assessment and security management assessment. The security technology assessment includes: physical security assessment, network security assessment, host system security assessment, application security assessment, data security assessment and multi-level security control assessment; the security management assessment includes: security management organization assessment, security management system assessment, personnel safety system assessment, system construction management assessment, system operation and maintenance management assessment and multi-level security control assessment;
The information system software rectification unit includes: analyzing the weaknesses and risks of the current network and information system through the gap assessment report of the level protection gap assessment unit, including the weaknesses and risks of the operating system, database, and network security equipment, checking and reinforcing the operating system, database, and network security equipment one by one according to the security configuration reinforcement specifications of the equipment, and formulating relevant risk avoidance measures, including operating system reinforcement, network/security equipment reinforcement, database reinforcement, and establishment and improvement of information security management system;
The Internet threat detection and active response module includes: providing risk assessment, real-time monitoring, tampering disposal, and emergency confrontation for Internet services to regain greater security;
Risk assessment includes: assessing exposure, vulnerability, and content security as a baseline, conducting regular and continuous reviews, regularly monitoring asset changes, and continuously analyzing the risks introduced by new assets;
Real-time monitoring includes: real-time monitoring of page tampering, 0day (vulnerability information that is known or disclosed before the system vendor knows and releases relevant patches), web trojans, black links, DNS (Domain Name System), and availability security events, and generating reports to notify users in a timely manner;
Tampering disposal includes: quickly replacing the tampered site through DNS technology;
Emergency response includes: cloud-based emergency response to protect sensitive data.
Furthermore, the baseline check module of this embodiment also includes: based on the best practices of the baseline check at each level of network equipment, security equipment, operating system, database, and middleware, a configuration check is performed on the target information system, the configuration status of the current equipment is recorded, the current security configuration status is analyzed, and the gaps in security configuration are identified and recorded with reference to the security baseline, and a baseline check report is formed based on the overall gap analysis of the baseline check and the current situation of the information system.
Furthermore, the operating system inspection unit of this embodiment includes: basic information inspection, patch management, user account, password security, permission management, log and audit, system service port inspection, security protection, and network protocol security.
Furthermore, the database checking unit of this embodiment: checks account security, checks database connection security, checks database security component configuration, checks log configuration, and checks communication protocols.
Furthermore, the present embodiment checks the Web server and the middleware unit: management application restriction check, directory listing check, prohibition of access to files outside the Web directory check, message body size of http requests, default port check, error level redirection, prohibition of list display files, prevention of denial of service attacks, default installation of useless files, hiding of version numbers and sensitive information, account management, authentication and authorization, log configuration, communication protocols, equipment and security requirements.

Furthermore, the detection of external attacks in this embodiment includes: reverse sequence attack detection, Web attack situation analysis, and password brute force attack detection.
Furthermore, the anti-sequence attack detection of this embodiment includes: analyzing and discovering the number of anti-sequence attack behaviors of internal services and the situation of each anti-sequence attack behavior.

Furthermore, the Web attack situation analysis of this embodiment analyzes the situation of the internal server being attacked through traffic analysis, and analyzes the situation distribution of the overall Web attack types, detailed information of each attack method and the results of the attack.
Furthermore, the attack results of this embodiment include: attack warning, attack capture, and prompt.
Furthermore, the password blasting attack detection of this embodiment detects the number of password blasting attacks suffered by different servers every day, the type of service, the email exposure attack situation, the remote management service blasting attack situation and the database service blasting attack situation.
Furthermore, the detection of internal violations in this embodiment includes: exposure surface detection, illegal external connection detection, malicious DNS (Domain Name System) analysis, ACL (Access Control Lists) combing, weak password detection, abnormal login detection, and unconventional service analysis.
Furthermore, the exposure surface detection of this embodiment analyzes the illegal attack surface information in the current network through big data analysis.
Furthermore, the illegal attack surface information of this embodiment includes: attack surface statistics information, newly added attack surface information, attack surface change information, and attack surface information.
Furthermore, the illegal external connection detection of this embodiment analyzes illegal external connection information within the environment.
Furthermore, the malicious DNS analysis of this embodiment monitors and analyzes the DNS of internal network requests through traffic analysis, and analyzes the credibility of the internal DNS in combination with threat intelligence to discover the malicious DNS requests and detailed information existing inside.
Furthermore, the ACL of this embodiment analyzes the access relationship of all existing IPs in the current network, including the access relationship of different ports from the source IP to the destination IP, analyzes the ACL control in the network, and handles unreasonable internal ACLs.
Furthermore, the weak password detection and analysis of this embodiment discovers the status of weak passwords of internal servers, reports the total number of weak passwords, the number of passive statistical discoveries, the number of dictionary matching discoveries and the number of active discoveries, and detects and analyzes information on weak passwords for mail services, remote management services, and database services.
Furthermore, the information of weak passwords of the mail service, remote management service, and database service of this embodiment includes: affected accounts, weak passwords, affected servers, protocols, and detection time.
Furthermore, the abnormal login detection of this embodiment includes: detecting abnormal behavior of the internal server, including: abnormal details of external login to the internal server, abnormal login details, and non-working hours login details.
Furthermore, the unconventional service analysis of this embodiment includes: remote control service, proxy service, RegeoryTunnel (intranet penetration tunnel) service detection and discovery, HTTP (Hyper Text Transfer Protocol) proxy detection and discovery, SOCKS (Protocol for sessions traversal across firewallsecurely) proxy detection and discovery, Teamview/IRC (professional remote connection tool/(Internet Relay Chat)) detection and discovery, analysis of the time of connection service, source IP of connection service, destination IP of connection service and service type.
Furthermore, the event analysis of this embodiment includes: by discovering compromise events, WEB attack events, internal abnormal information, using network penetration information, and combining cloud threat situations, determining whether the nature of the event is a true malicious attack behavior and analyzing the cause of the event.
Furthermore, the event tracing of this embodiment tracks and traces the malicious attack events, analyzes the physical location of the attacker, the evidence of the attacker's behavior, and the methods commonly used by the attacker.
Furthermore, the host asset service discovery unit of this embodiment includes: scanning and discovering new assets, asset changes, new ports, port changes, identifying operating systems, IP addresses, domain names, and outputting asset information reports.
Furthermore, the Web service discovery unit of this embodiment includes: analyzing and discovering ports, Web servers, development languages, some pre-WAF information, and Web service conditions. Further, the network attack incident emergency drill unit of the present embodiment includes: analysis and judgment. If it is judged to be a malicious attack incident on an external website, the attack source IP address is located according to the system log, firewall log, network log, network traffic analysis, and web page anti-tampering system analysis, and it is judged whether the attack source can be determined. If the attack source cannot be determined, it is judged whether the attack source type can be determined. At the same time, according to the system security status, it is judged whether it is tampering, SQL (Structured Query Language) injection, XSS (Cross Site Scripting) cross-site scripting attack, Trojan horse, illegal intrusion or one or more malicious attacks. If it is judged that there is a malicious attack, whether the web page anti-self-tampering system has been tampered with is detected. If it has been tampered with, the cause of the vulnerability is detected. If it has not been tampered with, the IDS (intrusion detection system intrusion detection system) Whether the system detects intrusion, if intrusion is detected, verification is performed; if no intrusion is detected, whether the type of attack source can be determined; if the type of attack can be determined, whether the vulnerability can be restored and repaired; if the type of attack source cannot be determined, the emergency plan is initiated; if it is determined that the vulnerability can be restored and repaired, then the vulnerability is restored and repaired; if it is determined that the vulnerability cannot be restored and repaired, then the emergency plan is initiated; after restoring and repairing the vulnerability, it is determined whether the attack continues; if it is determined that the attack continues, the source of the attack is determined and the emergency plan is initiated at the same time; if it is determined that the attack does not continue, the notification process is executed; if the attack source IP address or attack path cannot be located, or the attack network path cannot be closed after analysis, the emergency plan (in the case of system unavailability) is initiated and notified.

Password guessing uses brute force attacks and dictionaries to guess passwords.

The information collection and analysis of this embodiment includes: baseline check and vulnerability scanning. The baseline check of this embodiment includes: performing a baseline check on the system to discover security holes and weak links in servers, network devices, and security devices, and identifying, analyzing, repairing, and testing the discovered vulnerabilities.
Vulnerability scanning includes scanning the system for vulnerabilities, checking network protocols, network services, and various information assets in network devices for security risks and vulnerabilities, performing security vulnerability detection and analysis on network devices, and assisting in the rectification of vulnerabilities.
Further, the information collection and analysis in the level protection gap assessment unit of this embodiment includes: retrieving one or more materials in policy documents, rules and regulations and process management records, information system overall description documents, information system detailed description documents, information system security protection level classification report, security needs analysis report, information system security overall plan, security status evaluation report, information system security detailed design plan, user guide, operation steps, network diagram, configuration management document, analyzing the basic information, management framework, network and equipment deployment, business types and characteristics, business data, user scope, user type of the information system, conducting comprehensive analysis and collation, analyzing the industry characteristics, competent authorities, business scope, geographical location, background information, contact methods, organizational management structure, management strategy, department settings, the role of departments in business operation terminals, job responsibilities, physical environment, network topology, hardware equipment deployment, scope and boundaries, business types and characteristics, business processes, and business security protection levels of the information system, and forming an information system basic situation analysis report.
