Detailed Description
The technical solutions in the embodiments of the present application will be clearly and completely described below with reference to the drawings in the embodiments of the present application, and it is obvious that the described embodiments are only a part of the embodiments of the present application, and not all of the embodiments. All other embodiments, which can be derived by a person skilled in the art from the embodiments given herein without making any creative effort, shall fall within the protection scope of the present application.
The service data access method in the embodiment of the present application may perform validity check on the check certificate (i.e., the first check certificate) that is matched with the service access request and is mentioned in the embodiment of the present application based on a cloud technology, so as to obtain a validity check result. When the validity check result indicates that the first check certificate has validity, a service response result corresponding to the service access request can be obtained from a service server corresponding to a service application through the intelligent gateway, and the method and the device are suitable for the field of cloud security in the cloud technology.
The Cloud technology (Cloud technology) is a hosting technology for unifying series resources such as hardware, software, network and the like in a wide area network or a local area network to realize calculation, storage, processing and sharing of data. Cloud technology (Cloud technology) is based on a general term of network technology, information technology, integration technology, management platform technology, application technology and the like applied in a Cloud computing business model, can form a resource pool, is used as required, and is flexible and convenient. Cloud computing technology will become an important support. Background services of the technical network system require a large amount of computing and storage resources, such as video websites, picture-like websites and more web portals. With the high development and application of the internet industry, each article may have its own identification mark and needs to be transmitted to a background system for logic processing, data in different levels are processed separately, and various industrial data need strong system background support and can only be realized through cloud computing.
The Cloud Security (Cloud Security) refers to a generic name of Security software, hardware, users, organizations and Security Cloud platforms applied based on a Cloud computing business model. The cloud security integrates emerging technologies and concepts such as parallel processing, grid computing and unknown virus behavior judgment, abnormal monitoring of software behaviors in the network is achieved through a large number of meshed clients, the latest information of trojans and malicious programs in the internet is obtained and sent to the server for automatic analysis and processing, and then the virus and trojan solution is distributed to each client.
It should be understood that the main research directions for cloud security include:
1. the cloud computing security mainly researches how to guarantee the security of the cloud and various applications on the cloud, including the security of a cloud computer system, the secure storage and isolation of user data, user access authentication, information transmission security, network attack protection, compliance audit and the like;
2. the cloud of the security infrastructure mainly researches how to adopt cloud computing to newly build and integrate security infrastructure resources and optimize a security protection mechanism, and comprises the steps of constructing a super-large-scale security event and an information acquisition and processing platform through a cloud computing technology, realizing the acquisition and correlation analysis of mass information, and improving the handling control capability and the risk control capability of the security event of the whole network;
3. the cloud security service mainly researches various security services, such as anti-virus services and the like, provided for users based on a cloud computing platform.
Referring to fig. 1, fig. 1 is a schematic structural diagram of a network architecture according to an embodiment of the present disclosure. As shown in fig. 1, the network architecture may include a server 100, a management user terminal 300, and a user terminal cluster. The user terminal cluster may comprise one or more user terminals, where the number of user terminals will not be limited. The user terminal cluster may specifically include a user terminal 200a, a user terminal 200b, a user terminal 200c, …, and a user terminal 200 n. As shown in fig. 1, the user terminals 200a, 200b, 200c, …, and 200n may be respectively connected to the server 100 via a network, so that each user terminal may interact with the server 100 via the network.
Wherein, each user terminal of the user terminal cluster may include: the intelligent terminal comprises an intelligent terminal with a service data access function, such as a smart phone, a tablet computer, a notebook computer, a desktop computer, wearable equipment, an intelligent home, and head-mounted equipment. It should be understood that each user terminal in the user terminal cluster shown in fig. 1 may be installed with a service application and a target application (i.e., a security management client, for example, iOA client), and when the security management client runs in each user terminal, data interaction may be performed with the server 100 shown in fig. 1. The security management client herein may include a proxy component with request interception functionality.
The business application (i.e., business application client) herein may be a social client, an office client, a search client (e.g., browser client), a multimedia client (e.g., video client), an entertainment client (e.g., game client), an education client, a live client, a news client, a shopping client (e.g., e-commerce client), and the like. Here, the service application (i.e., trusted application) refers to an application bearer which is trusted by the management user corresponding to the security management client through the management user terminal 300 shown in fig. 1 and can access the internal service system, and includes an application name, an application MD5 (an information digest algorithm), signature information, and the like.
The administrative user terminals 300 herein may each include: the intelligent terminal comprises an intelligent terminal with a service data access function, such as a smart phone, a tablet computer, a notebook computer, a desktop computer, wearable equipment, an intelligent home, and head-mounted equipment. The management user terminal 300 may be operated with the security management client. It is understood that, in the management user terminal 300, the user accessing the security management client through the user account 1 may be referred to as a management user (e.g., user a) in the embodiment of the present application. At this time, the management user terminal 300 may implement data interaction with the server 100 through the security management client. Here, the administrative user may create a user account for accessing the security management client through the administrative user terminal 300, and configure a zero trust access policy (e.g., a first zero trust access policy) according to user account information corresponding to the user account.
As shown in fig. 1, the server 100 in this embodiment may be a server corresponding to the security management client, that is, a security management server (e.g., iOA backend server). The server 100 may be an independent physical server, a server cluster or a distributed system formed by a plurality of physical servers, or a cloud server providing basic cloud computing services such as a cloud service, a cloud database, cloud computing, a cloud function, cloud storage, a network service, cloud communication, a middleware service, a domain name service, a security service, a CDN, a big data and artificial intelligence platform, and the like.
It is understood that, in the embodiment of the present application, a user who accesses the security management client through the user account (e.g., user account 2) created by the management user may be referred to as an accessing user (e.g., user b). In the embodiment of the application, one user terminal can be arbitrarily selected from the user terminal cluster shown in fig. 1 as a target user terminal corresponding to an access user. For example, the embodiment of the present application may use the user terminal 200a shown in fig. 1 as a target user terminal. At this time, the target user terminal may implement data interaction with the server 100 through the security management client.
It should be understood that the service data access method provided in the embodiment of the present application may be based on the security management client, break through a traditional zone-based trust control manner, grant access rights by using a "4T principle" based on Trusted identity (Trusted identity), Trusted device (Trusted device), Trusted application (Trusted application) and Trusted link (Trusted link), and force all accesses to be authenticated, authorized and encrypted, thereby truly practicing a "zero trust" design concept, and thus, it may be effectively ensured that data information of an enterprise where an access user is located can be securely accessed no matter where and when the access user is located, and further, deployment flexibility and access experience of the access user may be improved, so as to improve overall security of office of the enterprise.
In the aspect of credible identity, the security management client can adapt to identity authentication modes of different enterprises and support a plurality of verification modes such as enterprise WeChat code scanning, LDAP authentication, HTTP authentication, local identity, domain identity and the like; in the aspect of trusted equipment, the safety management client can support self-defined compliance datum lines and comprehensive safety protection capability, including virus killing, vulnerability repair, system safety reinforcement, compliance detection, data protection, threat response and the like; in the aspect of trusted application, the security management client can allow trusted applications in the white list to access authorization services, and intercept access when discovering malicious processes; in the aspect of a trusted link, a service server corresponding to service application is hidden through a front trusted access gateway (namely an intelligent gateway), all accesses are forced to be authenticated, authorized and encrypted, and meanwhile, the problem of unsmooth or slow access of cross-border cross-carrier managers is solved by combining a self-developed long and short connection mode and a global network acceleration service, so that the safety and stability of the link are guaranteed. The intelligent gateway in the embodiment of the present application may be a complex network interconnection device (i.e., a computer device) that implements network interconnection above a network layer, where the computer device may be a user terminal, a server, a base station, or the like, and is not limited herein.
It should be understood that the service data access method according to the embodiment of the present application may check a service access request transmitted through a Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), and optionally, the method may also check a service access request transmitted through a User Datagram Protocol (UDP).
The TCP protocol can be controlled serially, and in a Windows operating system of a user terminal (for example, a computer terminal), the process and the connection can be acquired through a driving layer, the process and the connection can also be acquired through a virtual network card, and a zero trust access strategy can be controlled; in a Mac operating system of a user terminal (for example, a computer terminal), tunnel limitation can be performed through a mechanism applied by a system white list; in a user terminal (e.g., a smart phone), an Android Vpnservice expansion interface (an expansion interface of a virtual network card) may be used to add an expansion logic of a white list providing a network traffic forwarding service. An application whitelisting mechanism in the Ios operating system and the macos operating system may be used to instruct the system description file to configure the whitelisting application.
The trusted process management of the Udp protocol may be controlled asynchronously. It should be appreciated that the Windows operating system may acquire the service access request asynchronously, and block the warning asynchronously according to the zero trust access policy. Firstly, when it is determined that an access user has a trusted identity and an operating system of a target user terminal used by the access user is legal, the service access request can be forwarded, then an access process in the service access request is monitored through a security management client operated by the operating system, when the access process is not matched with a zero-trust access policy, the access user or a management user can be warned, and then automatic audit or manual audit is performed on the service access request. Trusted process management of the Udp protocol for other operating systems may be controlled by configuration services provided by the system, for example, a macos operating system and an ios operating system may configure a white list application via a system configuration description file. An Android vpnservice expansion interface (an expansion interface of a virtual network card) may be used to add a control logic of a white list providing a network traffic forwarding service.
For easy understanding, please refer to fig. 2, and fig. 2 is a schematic diagram of a scenario for performing data interaction according to an embodiment of the present application. As shown in fig. 2, the user terminal 20A in this embodiment may be a user terminal corresponding to an access user (e.g., a user b), the user terminal 20A may operate a security management client, and the user terminal 20A may be any one user terminal in the user terminal cluster shown in fig. 1, for example, a user terminal 200A. The intelligent gateway 20B shown in fig. 2 may be a network interconnect device associated with the security management client. The security management server 20C shown in fig. 2 may be a server corresponding to the security management client, and the security management server 20C may be the server 100 shown in fig. 1. The service server 20D shown in fig. 2 may apply a corresponding service server for the service accessed by the user b.
It should be understood that the user b in the embodiment of the present application may access the security management client executed by the user terminal 20A through the user account (e.g., the user account 2) created by the management user (e.g., the user a) of the security management client. At this time, the user terminal 20A may determine the terminal device information of the user terminal 20A, and further may send the terminal device information to the security management server 20C, so that the security management server 20C authenticates the access right of the user b, and when it is determined that the user b has the access right, may return the login credential configured for the user b and the user account information of the user b to the user terminal 20A, so that the user terminal 20A encrypts and stores the login credential and the user account information. When the user terminal 20A receives the user account information, a policy synchronization instruction for sending to the security management server 20C may be generated based on the user account information, so that the security management server 20C may issue a zero-trust access policy associated with the user b. The zero trust access policy here may be configured for user b for the administrative user of the security management client.
It should be understood that the user b may perform a trigger operation with respect to the service application running in the user terminal 20A, so that the user terminal 20A may generate a service access request associated with the service application (e.g., retrieval application). The triggering operation may include a contact operation such as a click or a long press, or may also include a non-contact operation such as a voice or a gesture, which is not limited herein. For example, the service access request may be a service access request associated with the retrieval application (e.g., browser a), in other words, the service access request may be generated by the user b when a certain service access site is retrieved through browser a.
At this time, the user terminal 20A may intercept the service access request based on the proxy component in the security management client. When a service access request associated with a service application is intercepted, the user terminal 20A may determine, by the security management client, a first check credential matched with the service access request based on a first zero trust access policy issued by the security management server 20C. The first zero trust access policy refers to a zero trust policy configured for an access user (e.g., user b) by an administrative user at an administrative user terminal with the granularity of the access user.
Further, the user terminal 20A may send the service access request and the first check certificate to the intelligent gateway 20B shown in fig. 2. It should be appreciated that the intelligent gateway may forward the received service access request and the first verification credential to the security management server 20C. At this time, the security management server 20C may extract the verification assistance parameter associated with the business application from the first verification credential. The verification auxiliary parameters may include a maximum number of uses of the first verification certificate, a validity period, and an error code. The maximum number of uses here refers to the maximum number of times the proxy component can be used within the validity period. The error code may be used to identify the use status of the first check credential, for example, when the value is 0, the error code may be used to identify the use status of the first check credential as a usable status, and when the value is a non-zero value, the error code may be used to identify the use status of the first check credential as an unusable status. The validity duration is determined based on the stored timestamp in the first proof-reading and a time threshold range of the first proof-reading (i.e., a threshold range including a first threshold and a second threshold). The storage time stamp can be expressed by unix epoch time stamp, wherein the unix epoch time stamp represents the number of seconds from 1, 0 min 0 s to the present in 1970. For example, 8/19/2020, 12: 00: a timestamp of 00 may be denoted as 1597809600 seconds.
For example, if the storage timestamp in the first check certificate is 1597809600 seconds (i.e., 8/19/2020/12: 00: 00), and the time threshold of the first check certificate is [3600 seconds-7200 seconds ], the valid duration of the first check certificate may be 8/19/2020/13: 00: 00-14: 00: 00.
it should be understood that the security management server 20C may perform validity check on the first check certificate based on the check auxiliary parameter to obtain a validity check result. If the validity check result indicates that the first check certificate does not have validity, the security management server 20C may notify the intelligent gateway 20B to interrupt the service access request, so that the user B cannot access the service server 20D, and further cannot obtain data information in the service application. It is to be understood that the security management server 20C may also generate an exception notification corresponding to the error code based on the error code of the first check certificate, so as to return the exception notification to the user terminal 20A through the intelligent gateway 20B. For example, the exception alert notification may be "no access to the website. "
If the validity check result indicates that the first check certificate has validity, the security management server 20B may forward the acquired service access request to the service server 20D through the intelligent gateway, so that the service server 20B may determine a service response result corresponding to the service access request. At this time, the service server 20D may return the service response result to the intelligent gateway 20B, so that the intelligent gateway 20B returns the service response result to the user terminal 20A. Further, the user terminal 20A may output the service response result to an application display interface corresponding to the service application.
It can be seen that the user terminal 20A may intercept a service access request associated with a service application through the security management client, so that the first verification credential of the intercepted service access request may be determined. Further, the user terminal 20A may send the first verification credential to the security management server 20C through the intelligent gateway 20B, so that the security management server 20C performs validity verification. When the verification is successful, the security management server 20C may allow the service access request to be forwarded to the service server 20D through the intelligent gateway 20B, and when the verification is failed, the security management server 20C may interrupt the service access request through the intelligent gateway 20B, and refuse to access the service server 20D, so that the security risk of data leakage may be reduced, and the security of access may be improved.
The specific implementation manner supporting the service access request to access the service server when the legal verification result indicates that the first verification certificate is legal may refer to the following embodiments corresponding to fig. 3 to 9.
Further, please refer to fig. 3, where fig. 3 is a schematic flowchart of a service data access method according to an embodiment of the present application. As shown in fig. 3, the method may be performed by a user terminal running a security management client. The ue may be any one ue in the ue cluster shown in fig. 1, for example, the ue 200 a. The method may comprise at least the following steps S101-S103:
step S101, when a service access request associated with a service application is intercepted, a first verification certificate matched with the service access request is determined through a security management client based on a first zero trust access policy issued by a security management server corresponding to the security management client.
Specifically, the access user corresponding to the user terminal may be a user account (e.g., user account 2) created by an administrative user (e.g., user a) of the security management client, and a user (e.g., user b) accessing the security management client. It should be appreciated that when the accessing user performs a triggering operation with respect to a business application, the user terminal may generate a business access request associated with the business application in response to the triggering operation. At this time, the proxy component in the security management client may intercept the service access request, and the user terminal may determine, through the security management client, a first verification credential matched with the service access request based on a first zero trust access policy issued by a security management server corresponding to the security management client.
For ease of understanding, please refer to fig. 4, where fig. 4 is a timing diagram illustrating an access user accessing a security management client according to an embodiment of the present application. As shown in fig. 4, a user terminal in this embodiment may be a user terminal corresponding to an access user (e.g., user b), where the user terminal may operate a security management client, and the user terminal may be any one user terminal in the user terminal cluster shown in fig. 1, for example, the user terminal 200 a. The security management server shown in fig. 4 may be a server corresponding to the security management client, and the security management server may be the server 100 shown in fig. 1.
The security management client (e.g., iOA client) may support various verification methods such as enterprise WeChat code, LDAP authentication, HTTP authentication, local identity, Domain identity, TOKEN, etc. to determine the trusted identity of the accessing user accessing the management client. It should be understood that, in the process that the access user accesses the security management client through the user terminal, the security management server may push the zero-trust access policy bound to the access user to the security management client, so as to implement policy control with the access user as a granularity, thereby improving the security of access.
It will be appreciated that the security management client may include an interface process and a host service process. For example, the interface process may be an iooagui interface process and the host service process may be an iooaent host service process. When the access user accesses the security management client through the user terminal, the user terminal may determine terminal device information of the user terminal. The terminal device information here may be device identification information (e.g., deviceid) and machine information. The machine information may include a system operating system type, an operating system version number, and the like.
Further, the user terminal may execute step S410 shown in fig. 4, and submit the terminal device information to the security management server through the interface process, so that the security management server executes step S411 to authenticate the access right of the access user, thereby obtaining an authentication result. The authentication result may be used to instruct the security management server to obtain user account information configured for the access user by the management user of the security management client when it is determined that the access user has the access right, and further configure a login credential for the access user based on the user account information. The user account information herein may include user identification information (e.g., user ID) of the accessing user and a user name (e.g., chinese name). Further, the security management server may execute step S412 to return the login credentials and the user account information to the user terminal. At this time, the user terminal may perform step S413 to encrypt and store the received login credential and the user account information.
And when the user account information is acquired, the user terminal generates a policy synchronization instruction for sending to the security management server based on the interface process and the main service process. Wherein the policy synchronization instruction may be used to instruct the security management server to generate a policy identification list associated with the accessing user. The policy identification list comprises Y pieces of first identification information; y may be a positive integer. It can be understood that, when the user account information is obtained, the user terminal may trigger a policy pull instruction for obtaining the first zero trust access policy of the access user through the interface process, and then may execute step S414, transmit the policy pull instruction to the main service process, and control the main service process to generate a policy synchronization instruction in response to the policy pull instruction. At this time, the user terminal may perform step S415 to transmit the policy synchronization command to the security management server.
Further, the security management server may execute step S416, and based on the policy synchronization instruction, obtain Y first zero trust access policies configured by the administrative user for the access user, and further may generate a policy identifier list based on the obtained Y first zero trust access policies. At this time, the security management server may perform step S417 to return the policy identifier list to the user terminal. It should be understood that the user terminal may execute step S418, and compare the first identification information with the second identification information of the local identification list in the security management client through the main service process, so as to obtain a comparison result. The comparison result may include the first identification information that is determined in the policy identification list and is the same as the second identification information.
The user terminal may obtain target identification information in the policy identification list, and then execute step S419 to send the target identification information to the security management server, so that the security management server obtains a second zero trust access policy corresponding to the target identification information. The target identification information may be the first identification information remaining in the policy identification list except the first identification information that is the same as the second identification information. Further, the security management server may execute step S420 to return a second zero trust access policy to the user terminal. At this time, the user terminal adds the target identification information corresponding to the second zero trust access policy to the local identification list, and may further perform step S421 to display the second zero trust access policy through the interface process.

It should be understood that, if the access user is a user who accesses the security management client for the first time, the local identifier list is not generated in the security management client operated by the user terminal corresponding to the access user. At this time, the user terminal takes all the first identification information in the policy identification list shown in table 1 as target identification information (e.g., identification information 1, identification information 2, identification information 3, identification information 4, and identification information 5), and further sends the target identification information to the security management server, so that the security management server can obtain a second zero trust access policy corresponding to the target identification information, for example, a zero trust access policy 1 corresponding to identification information 1, a zero trust access policy 2 corresponding to identification information 2, a zero trust access policy 3 corresponding to identification information 3, a zero trust access policy 4 corresponding to identification information 4, and a zero trust access policy 5 corresponding to identification information 5. At this time, the user terminal may acquire the first identification information remaining in addition to the identification information 1 and the identification information 2, i.e., the identification information 3, the identification information 4, and the identification information 5, in table 1. At this time, the user terminal may determine the 3 pieces of identification information as target identification information, and further send the target identification information to the security management server, so that the security management server may obtain a second zero-trust access policy corresponding to the target identification information, for example, a zero- trust access policy 3 corresponding to the identification information 3, a zero-trust access policy 4 corresponding to the identification information 4, and a zero-trust access policy 5 corresponding to the identification information 5. Further, the security management server may return the 3 second zero trust access policies to the user terminal. At this time, the user terminal may add the target identification information corresponding to the 3 second zero trust access policies to the local identification list shown in table 2, and may further display the 3 zero trust access policies through the interface process.
For ease of understanding, please further refer to fig. 5, where fig. 5 is a schematic diagram of a scenario in which a management user configures a zero-trust access policy according to an embodiment of the present application. As shown in fig. 5, a user a corresponding to the embodiment of the present application may be a management user corresponding to a security management client, a user terminal corresponding to the user a may be referred to as a management user terminal, and the management user terminal may be the management user terminal 300 shown in fig. 1.
As shown in fig. 5, the terminal interface 500 in the embodiment of the present application may be a terminal interface corresponding to a security management client (e.g., iOA client) executed by a management user terminal. Wherein, the control 1 (e.g., "enable zero trust office" control) can be used to control the on and off of the zero trust borderless office function; control 2 (e.g., a "policy management" control) may be used to indicate the configuration of a zero trust access policy (e.g., a first zero trust access policy); control 3 (e.g., a "save settings" control) may be used to indicate that the relevant settings are saved.
It should be understood that the user a may perform a trigger operation on the widget 1 in the terminal interface 500, so as to control the starting of the zero-trust borderless office function, and further may perform a trigger operation on the widget 3, so as to save the setting of the starting of the zero-trust borderless office function this time. Further, a plurality of user accounts created by the management user may be displayed in the terminal interface 510, where the user accounts may be individual user accounts or group user accounts, which is not limited herein. It is understood that the user a may configure a zero trust access policy associated with the trusted application in zone 1 of the terminal interface 510, and of course, the user a may also configure a zero trust access policy associated with the business system in zone 2 of the terminal interface 510. After the configuration in the terminal interface 510 is finished, the user a may execute a trigger operation for the control 4 in the terminal interface 510, so as to store the zero trust access policy configured this time.
Further, please refer to fig. 6a, and fig. 6a is a schematic view of a scenario in which an access user accesses a security management client according to an embodiment of the present application. Further, please refer to fig. 7, where fig. 7 is a schematic flowchart illustrating a process that a user terminal determines a first check credential through a security management client according to an embodiment of the present application. As shown in fig. 7, the agent component having a request interception function in this embodiment may obtain configuration information configured for the agent component by a management user of the security management client. The configuration information may include an intelligent gateway address, a white list, and a direct connection list. The service sites in the white list may be service sites accessed by trusted applications; the service site in the direct connection list may be a service site that can be directly accessed without validity check.
When the user terminal intercepts a service access request associated with a service application through the proxy component, the service access request can be analyzed and processed through the security management client, so that access auxiliary parameters in the service access request are obtained. Wherein the access assisting parameter may include a service access site entered in the service application, an access process in the service application, and a request generation timestamp of the service access request.
Further, the user terminal may search for a first zero trust access policy matched with the service access site based on the first zero trust access policy issued by the security management server corresponding to the security management client. When the first zero trust access policy matched with the service access site is not found, if the service access site belongs to the service site in the direct connection list, the user terminal may directly send the service access request to a service server corresponding to the service application. If the service access site does not belong to the service site in the direct connection list, the user terminal may interrupt the service access request.
When the first zero trust access policy matched with the service access site is found (namely, when the matching is successful), the user terminal can use the cache node corresponding to the service access site as a target cache node through the security management client. Further, the user terminal may determine, by the security management client, whether the cache of the target mitigation node is empty, that is, determine whether the number of child nodes included in the target cache node and associated with the service access site is zero. If the cache of the target release node is empty, the target cache node is deleted, and it can be further determined that the search result of the security management client indicates that the search fails, in other words, the security management client does not search the first check credential matched with the service access request.
If the cache of the target mitigation node is not empty, that is, the target cache node may include Z child nodes associated with the service access site, the user terminal may obtain the first child node from the Z child nodes based on the valid duration corresponding to each check credential. One child node may correspond to one check certificate, and one check certificate may correspond to one valid duration; here Z may be a positive integer.
For example, the target cache node may include 3 child nodes, specifically, child node 1, child node 2, and child node 3. The valid duration of the check certificate 1 corresponding to the child node 1 may be 13 of 8, 19 and 2020: 00: 00-13: 30: 00, the valid duration of the check certificate 2 corresponding to the child node 2 may be 14 of 8, 19 and 2020: 30: 00-15: 30: 00, the valid duration of the check certificate 3 corresponding to the child node 3 may be 15 of 8, 19 and 2020: 00: 00-17: 00: 00. at this time, the user terminal may act as the first child node based on obtaining the child node 1.
Further, the user terminal may determine the verification credential corresponding to the first child node as the first to-be-matched credential, and may further determine a time interval value between the request generation timestamp and a storage timestamp corresponding to the first to-be-matched credential. It should be understood that the user terminal may determine the first to-be-matched certificate matching the service access request as the first check certificate based on the time interval value. For example, the first certificate to be matched determined in the embodiment of the present application may be the check certificate 1 corresponding to the child node 1, and the storage timestamp corresponding to the check certificate 1 may be 1597809600 seconds, that is, 8/19/2020, 12: 00: 00. the time threshold ranges from [3600 seconds to 5400 seconds ]. The first threshold of the proof 1 may be 3600 seconds, and the second threshold of the proof 1 may be 5400 seconds.
If the time interval value belongs to the time threshold range, the user terminal may parse the first to-be-matched certificate to obtain the cache data corresponding to the first to-be-matched certificate; the cache data may include a service cache site and a cache process corresponding to the service cache site. When the service cache site is the same as the target site information and the cache process is the same as the access process in the service auxiliary information, the user terminal may delete the first certificate to be matched from the security management client, and may further use the first certificate to be matched as the first certificate to be matched with the service access request.
It should be understood that, in this embodiment of the present application, the cache data of each verification credential may be stored in a Key-value distributed manner, where the cache type of the verification credential corresponding to each child node may be a memory cache and stored in a map structure, where Key may be: the service caching site (i.e. request url information) and the caching process md5 are in the format: "target domain name (IP): port "; the value may be: and when the verification certificate is applied, the service cache site is the server response information of the service cache site corresponding to the key. For easy understanding, please refer to table 3, where table 3 is a cache parameter table of the check certificate provided in the embodiment of the present application.
TABLE 3
As shown in Table 3 above, the parameter url may be of STRING type, format: "target domain name (IP): port "; the parameter ticket refers to a verification certificate; the parameter validstartoffset refers to a time period (representing a difference interval between the stored timestamp and the reusable time period) for which the check voucher can be repeatedly used, and is a left segment of a closed interval, such as 0 (unit: second); the parameter valindedffset refers to the right segment of the closed time interval (representing the difference interval between the time interval and the storage time stamp) for which the proof certificate can be repeatedly used, such as 1800 (unit: second), which represents 30 minutes; the parameter effect _ cnt refers to the valid number of times that the check certificate can be cached (sent to the proxy component for caching); the parameter error refers to an error code, which can identify whether the check certificate is available, and the value is 0 if the check certificate is available; the parameter startTime refers to a store timestamp, of the type Unix epoch timestamp (representing the total number of seconds from 1970, 1, 0 minutes, 0 seconds to the present).
For example, if the request generation timestamp of the service access request is 1597813800 seconds, i.e., 8/19/2020, 13: 10: 00, the security management client may determine that the time interval value between the request generation timestamp and the storage timestamp of check credential 1 (e.g., 1597809600 seconds) is 4200 seconds. The user terminal may determine, through the security management client, that the time interval value belongs to a time threshold range (e.g., [3600 seconds-5400 seconds ]) of the verification credential 1, at this time, the user terminal may parse the verification credential 1 to obtain cache data corresponding to the verification credential 1; the cache data may include a service cache site and a cache process corresponding to the service cache site. When the service cache site is the same as the service access site and the cache process is the same as the access process in the service auxiliary information, the user terminal may delete the check certificate 1 from the security management client, and may further use the check certificate 1 as the first check certificate matched with the service access request.
If the time interval value does not belong to the time threshold range and the time interval value is smaller than the first threshold, the ue may determine that the search result of the security management client indicates that the search fails, in other words, the security management client does not find the first check credential matching the service access request.
For example, if the request generation timestamp of the service access request is 1597811400 seconds, i.e., 8/19/2020, 12: 30: 00, the security management client may determine that the time interval value between the request generation timestamp and the storage timestamp of check document 1 (e.g., 1597809600 seconds) is 1800 seconds. The ue may determine, by the security management client, that the time interval value does not belong to a time threshold range of check credential 1 (e.g., [3600 seconds-5400 seconds ]), and the time interval value is smaller than the first threshold (e.g., 3600 seconds), at this time, the ue may determine that the security management client does not find the first check credential matching the service access request.
If the time interval value does not belong to the time threshold range and is greater than the second threshold, the ue may determine the first to-be-matched certificate as a failed-check certificate and delete the failed-check certificate. For example, if the request generation timestamp of the service access request is 1597816800 seconds, i.e., 8/19/2020, 14: 00: 00, the security management client may determine that the time interval value between the request generation timestamp and the storage timestamp of check document 1 (e.g., 1597809600 seconds) is 7200 seconds. The user terminal may determine, through the security management client, that the time interval value does not belong to the time threshold range of the check credential 1 (e.g., [3600 seconds-5400 seconds ]), and the time interval value is greater than the second threshold (e.g., 5400 seconds), at this time, the user terminal may determine the check credential 1 as an invalid check credential and delete a child node (e.g., child node 1) corresponding to the invalid check credential.
Further, the user terminal may determine whether the target cache node has a node next to the first child node. When the next child node of the first child node does not exist in the target cache node, the user terminal may determine that the security management client does not find the first verification credential matching the service access request. When a next child node (e.g., child node 2) of the first child node exists in the target cache node, the user terminal may determine the next child node of the first child node as a second child node, acquire a second to-be-matched credential (e.g., check credential 2) corresponding to the second child node, and determine the second to-be-matched credential as the first check credential when the second to-be-matched credential matches the service access request. The matching process of the second credential to be matched and the service access request may refer to the matching process of the first credential to be matched and the service access request, and will not be further described herein.
As shown in fig. 7, when the search result of the security management client indicates that the search is failed, that is, the security management client does not find the first check credential matching the service access request based on the first zero trust access policy, the user terminal may generate a credential application request for applying for the second check credential through the security management client. The credential application request may include the login credential and an access process characteristic corresponding to an access process in the service application. The access process characteristics are access process characteristics corresponding to the access process collected by the security management client, wherein the access process characteristics may include process md5, digital signature information, path, copyright information, process name, and the like.
Further, the user terminal may send the credential application request to a security management server, and at this time, in order to reduce network latency and effectively relieve a request pressure of the security management server in a distributed deployment environment, the security management server may configure, based on the login credential and the access process feature, X verification credentials associated with the access process for the security management client; x herein may be a positive integer; each proof of verification may include a range of time thresholds that do not overlap with each other. At this time, the security management server may return the X check credentials to the security management client, so that the security management client determines valid durations corresponding to the X check credentials based on a time threshold range in the X check credentials and storage timestamps of the X check credentials, and caches the check credentials corresponding to each valid duration to a cache node of the service access site, so as to search for a first check credential matched with the service access request.
Therefore, in the embodiment of the application, the service access request initiated at the user terminal can be intercepted by the proxy component in the security management client, so that the access user can be used as the granularity, the first verification certificate matched with the service access request is determined by the security management client based on the first zero trust access strategy associated with the access user, the access position, the access time and the used user terminal of the access user do not need to be concerned, and the first verification certificate is subjected to validity verification by the security management server subsequently to control whether the access user can access the service server, so that the deployment flexibility is improved, and the access security is improved.
Step S102, the first verification certificate is forwarded to a security management server through an intelligent gateway associated with the security management client, so that the security management server conducts validity verification on the first verification certificate based on a verification auxiliary parameter corresponding to the first verification certificate, and a validity verification result is obtained.
In particular, the user terminal may forward the first verification credential to the security management server through an intelligent gateway associated with the security management client. At this time, the security management server may extract the verification assistance parameter associated with the business application from the first verification credential. The verification auxiliary parameters may include a maximum number of uses of the first verification certificate, a validity period, and an error code. Further, the security management server may perform validity check on the first check certificate based on the check auxiliary parameter, so that a validity check result may be obtained, and the validity check result may be returned to the intelligent gateway.
It should be understood that the security management server may extract the verification auxiliary parameter associated with the service application from the first verification certificate, and perform validity verification on the service access request based on the verification auxiliary parameter. For example, the security management server may check whether the first check certificate has a formatting error such as missing format. If the first verification certificate has a formatting error, the intelligent gateway is informed to return an abnormal prompt notice of parameter error to the user terminal; if the first check certificate has no formatting error, the security management server can detect the validity of the first check certificate, that is, detect whether the first check certificate is within the valid duration and exceeds the maximum use times; if the detection result determines that the first check certificate is invalid, the security management server may notify the intelligent gateway to return an abnormal prompt notification that the check certificate is invalid to the user terminal. If the detection result determines that the first verification certificate is valid, the legal verification result of the security management server can indicate that the first verification certificate is legal.
Therefore, the security management server in the embodiment of the application can perform validity check on the first check certificate matched with the service access request to obtain a legal check result, the legal check result can indicate that the validity of the first check certificate is determined, if the legal check result indicates that the first check certificate does not have the validity, the security management server can inform the intelligent gateway of interrupting the service access request based on the reason of the check failure, and generate an abnormal prompt notice used for sending to the user terminal to inform the access user of the reason of the failure in accessing the service server, so that the access experience of the access user can be improved.
And step S103, when the legal verification result indicates that the first verification certificate has the legality, acquiring a service response result corresponding to the service access request through the intelligent gateway, and outputting the service response result to an application display interface corresponding to the service application.
It should be understood that, when the validity check result indicates that the first check certificate has validity, the security management server may notify the intelligent gateway to forward the service access request to the service server corresponding to the service application. At this time, the service server may obtain a service response result corresponding to the service access request, and may further send the service response result to the intelligent gateway, so that the intelligent gateway returns the service response result to the user terminal. And when receiving the service response result, the user terminal can output the service response result to an application display interface corresponding to the service application.
Therefore, when the legal verification result indicates that the first verification certificate has the legality, the safety management server can allow the service access request to be sent to the service server through the intelligent gateway, so that the user terminal can access the service server and obtain a service response result corresponding to the service access request, and therefore the access safety is improved.
Further, please refer to fig. 8, where fig. 8 is a schematic flowchart of a service data access method according to an embodiment of the present application. As shown in fig. 8, the method may be executed by a user terminal running a security management client, an intelligent gateway associated with the security management client, a security management server corresponding to the security management client, and a service server corresponding to a service application, where the user terminal may be any one user terminal in the user terminal cluster shown in fig. 1, for example, the user terminal 200 a. The security management server may be the server 100 shown in fig. 1 described above. The method may comprise at least the following steps S201-S213:
step S201, an agent component of a safety management client operated by a user terminal sends a configuration information acquisition instruction to the safety management client;
step S202, the user terminal returns the configuration information associated with the configuration information acquisition instruction to the proxy component through the security management client;
step S203, when the agent component intercepts a service access request which is sent by the user terminal and is associated with the service application, the user terminal sends the service access request to the security management client, so that the security management client searches a first verification certificate matched with the service access request based on a first zero trust access strategy issued by a security management server corresponding to the security management client;
step S204, when the security management client side does not find a first verification certificate matched with the service access request based on the first zero trust access strategy, the user terminal sends a certificate application request to the security management server;
step S205, the security management server configures X verification certificates associated with the access process for the security management client based on the login certificate in the certificate application request and the access process characteristics corresponding to the access process in the service application, and returns the X verification certificates to the security management client;
step S206, the user terminal obtains a first verification certificate matched with the service access request from the returned X verification certificates through the security management client;
step S207, the user terminal sends the first verification certificate to the intelligent gateway through the agent component;
step S208, the intelligent gateway forwards the first check certificate to a security management server;
step S209, the safety management server checks the validity of the first checking certificate based on the checking auxiliary parameter extracted from the first checking certificate and associated with the service application, and obtains a valid checking result;
step S210, the safety management server returns a legal verification result to the intelligent gateway;
step S211, when the legal verification result indicates that the first verification certificate has validity, the intelligent gateway forwards the service access request to a service server corresponding to the service application, so that the service server obtains a service response result corresponding to the service access request;
step S212, the service server returns a service response result corresponding to the service access request to the intelligent gateway;
step S213, the intelligent gateway returns the service response result to the user terminal, so that the user terminal outputs the service response result to the application display interface corresponding to the service application based on the security management client.
For specific implementation of steps S201 to S213, reference may be made to the description of steps S101 to S103 in the embodiment corresponding to fig. 3, which will not be described herein again.
Further, please refer to fig. 9, where fig. 9 is a timing chart of a service data access method according to an embodiment of the present application. As shown in fig. 9, a user terminal in this embodiment may be a user terminal corresponding to an access user, where the user terminal may operate a security management client, the security management client may include an agent component having a request interception function, and the user terminal may be any one of the user terminals in the user terminal cluster shown in fig. 1, for example, the user terminal 200 a. The intelligent gateway shown in fig. 9 may be an intelligent gateway associated with the security management client, the security management server shown in fig. 9 may be a server corresponding to the security management client, and the security management server may be the server 100 shown in fig. 1. The service server shown in fig. 9 may be a service server corresponding to a service application.
The user terminal may execute step S910 through the security management client, and submit terminal device information of the user terminal to the security management server, at this time, the security management server may execute step S911 to authenticate the user right of the access user, and when the authentication is successful, may execute step S912, and return the login credential configured for the access user and the acquired user account information to the user terminal. When the user terminal obtains the user account information, step S913 may be executed to send a policy synchronization instruction to the security management server according to the user account information, so that the security management server may execute step S914 to obtain a second zero trust access policy corresponding to the target identification information, and further may execute step S915 to return the second zero trust access policy to the user terminal.
For specific implementation of the access flow corresponding to steps S910 to S912 and the policy synchronization flow corresponding to steps S913 to S915 in this embodiment, reference may be made to the description of steps S410 to S421 in the embodiment corresponding to fig. 4, and details are not repeated here.
The user terminal may execute step S916 by the proxy component to send a configuration information obtaining instruction to the security management client, so that the security management client may execute step S917 to return the configuration information when obtaining the configuration information. It should be appreciated that the user terminal may execute step S918 via the proxy component to send the intercepted service access request to the security management client. When the security management client does not find the first check credential matching the service access request, step S919 may be executed to send a credential application request to the security management server, so that the security management server may execute step S920 to return X check credentials. Further, the user terminal may execute step S921 through the security management client, and return the first verification certificate matching with the service access request. The user terminal may perform step S922 through the proxy component, and send the first verification credential to the intelligent gateway, so that the intelligent gateway performs step S923 to forward the first verification credential to the security management server. Further, the security management server may execute step S924 to perform validity check on the first check certificate to obtain a validity check result, and further execute step S925 to send the validity check result to the intelligent gateway. When the validity check result indicates that the first check certificate has validity, the intelligent gateway may perform step S926, forward the service access request to the service server, so that the service server performs step S927, and return a service response result corresponding to the service access request. Further, the intelligent gateway may execute step S928, and return the service response result to the user terminal.
The proxy access flow corresponding to steps S916 to S928 in the embodiment of the present application may refer to the description of steps S201 to S213 in the embodiment corresponding to fig. 4, and is not described again.

The matching certificate determining module 11 is configured to determine, by the security management client, a first verification certificate matching the service access request based on a first zero trust access policy issued by the security management server corresponding to the security management client when the service access request associated with the service application is intercepted.
The safety management client comprises an agent component with a request interception function;
the matching certificate determination module 11 includes: the system comprises a parsing processing unit 111, a strategy searching unit 112, a target node determining unit 113, a time interval value determining unit 114 and a matching certificate determining unit 115.
The analysis processing unit 111 is configured to, when a service access request associated with a service application is intercepted by the proxy component, perform analysis processing on the service access request through the security management client to obtain an access auxiliary parameter in the service access request; the access auxiliary parameters comprise service access sites recorded in the service application, access processes in the service application and request generation timestamps of service access requests;
the policy searching unit 112 is configured to search, based on a first zero trust access policy issued by a security management server corresponding to a security management client, a first zero trust access policy matched with a service access site;

the time interval value determining unit 114 is configured to obtain a first child node from the Z child nodes based on the valid duration corresponding to each verification certificate, determine the verification certificate corresponding to the first child node as a first certificate to be matched, and determine a time interval value between the request generation timestamp and the storage timestamp corresponding to the first certificate to be matched;
the matching certificate determining unit 115 is configured to determine, as the first verification certificate, the first to-be-matched certificate that matches the service access request based on the time interval value.
Wherein the first to-be-matched credential includes a first threshold associated with a store timestamp and a second threshold, and the second threshold is greater than the first threshold;
the matching credential determination unit 115 includes: a time threshold range determining subunit 1151, a cache data determining subunit 1152, a deleting subunit 1153, a matching credential determining subunit 1154, a first determining subunit 1155, an invalidating credential deleting subunit 1156, a second determining subunit 1157, and a third determining subunit 1158.
The time threshold range determining subunit 1151, configured to determine a time threshold range including the first threshold and the second threshold;
the cached data determining subunit 1152, configured to, if the time interval value belongs to the time threshold range, parse the first to-be-matched credential to obtain cached data corresponding to the first to-be-matched credential; the cache data comprises a service cache site and a cache process corresponding to the service cache site;
the deleting subunit 1153 is configured to delete the first to-be-matched verification certificate from the security management client when the service cache site is the same as the service access site and the cache process is the same as the access process in the service auxiliary information;
the matching certificate determining subunit 1154 is configured to use the first to-be-matched certificate as the first verification certificate matching the service access request.
The first determining subunit 1155 is configured to determine that the security management client does not find the first check credential matched with the service access request if the time interval value does not belong to the time threshold range and is smaller than the first threshold.
The revocation certificate deleting subunit 1156 is configured to determine the first to-be-matched certificate as a revocation certificate and delete the revocation certificate if the time interval value does not belong to the time threshold range and is greater than the second threshold;
the second determining subunit 1157 is configured to, when a next child node of the first child node exists in the target cache node, determine the next child node of the first child node as a second child node, acquire a second to-be-matched credential corresponding to the second child node, and when the second to-be-matched credential is matched with the service access request, determine the second to-be-matched credential as a first check credential;
the third determining subunit 1158 is configured to determine that the security management client does not find the first check credential matching the service access request when the next child node of the first child node does not exist in the target cache node.
For specific implementation manners of the time threshold range determining subunit 1151, the cache data determining subunit 1152, the deleting subunit 1153, the matching credential determining subunit 1154, the first determining subunit 1155, the invalid credential deleting subunit 1156, the second determining subunit 1157, and the third determining subunit 1158, reference may be made to the description that the service access request matches the first check credential in the embodiment corresponding to fig. 7, which will not be described again here.

the service result obtaining module 13 is configured to, when the validity check result indicates that the first check certificate has validity, obtain, through the intelligent gateway, a service response result corresponding to the service access request, and output the service response result to an application display interface corresponding to the service application.

the device information sending module 15 is configured to send the terminal device information to the security management server through an interface process of the management client, so that the security management server authenticates an access right of an access user to obtain an authentication result; the authentication result is used for indicating the security management server to configure a login certificate for the access user based on the user account information configured for the access user by the management user when the access user is determined to have the access right;
the encryption storage module 16 is configured to obtain a login credential and user account information returned by the security management server, and encrypt and store the login credential and the user account information.

the synchronization instruction sending module 17 is configured to generate a policy synchronization instruction for sending to the security management server based on the interface process and the main service process when the user account information is obtained; the policy synchronization instruction is used for instructing the security management server to generate a policy identification list associated with the access user; the strategy identification list comprises Y pieces of first identification information; y is a positive integer.

the policy returning module 20 is configured to receive, through the host service process, a second zero trust access policy returned by the security management server, add target identification information corresponding to the second zero trust access policy to the local identification list, and display the second zero trust access policy through the interface process.
