Some of the terms referred to herein are described below to facilitate understanding by those skilled in the art.
1. A process, in a narrow definition, refers to an instance of an executing application program, such as may also be referred to as an application process, and in a broad sense is understood to be a running activity of a program with a certain independent functionality with respect to a certain data set.
The concept of a process has two main points:
(1) A process is an entity. Each process has its own address space, typically including a text region, a data region, and a stack. Wherein the text region stores code executed by the processor; the data area stores variables and dynamically allocated memory used during process execution; the stack area stores the instructions and local variables of the active procedure call.
(2) A process is an "executing program", where the program is, for example, an executable program with a suffix name exe, which is an inanimate entity that can become an active entity only if the processor gives the program life (operating system execution), which may be referred to as a process.
2. Zero trust is a security concept that is not essentially the same dimensional concept as traditional security products/devices, but because the zero trust architecture is landed, it will cooperate with traditional security products/devices, and even there may be situations where some traditional security products/devices are replaced.
Zero trust can be understood literally, namely, the trust chain is not trusted to any object, and in particular, in an access control system, the trust chain is established from person (user), terminal, resource and the like to the resource under the assumption that the person (user), terminal, resource and the like are not trusted, so that the resource security and trust request is realized, network attack is blocked, and network security is improved.
The following describes the design concept of the present application.
As described above, in the current service access control, a region-based trust control mechanism is generally adopted in the related art, after confirming that the network location of the user is trusted, the device is allowed to enter the network, and once the device enters the network, the device can access an internal network service through any application in the device, that is, once the device is trusted and enters the network, any code executed by the device has access authority of a service system, in the process, the execution code of the application process may be tampered maliciously, some malicious codes also have the capability of penetrating the network to invade the service system, and at the moment, the intranet service accesses the device which is focused only to initiate access, but not the application process which is thinned to the device, so that the access control mechanism in the related art cannot detect that the application process is tampered to cause some advanced threats or virus Trojan to permeate the service system, so that the access control mechanism in the related art has a large network security risk and the effectiveness of access control is lower.
In view of this, an embodiment of the present application provides an access control method, specifically, when a terminal initiates a service access request, the terminal may obtain process feature information of an application process (for example, referred to as a target application process) for initiating the service access request, and then perform trusted verification on the process feature information, where performing trusted verification on the process feature information is equivalent to performing trusted verification on a target application process, and only when the process feature information for identifying the target application process passes the trusted verification, an authorization credential is issued to the target application process, that is, the terminal may obtain authorization information corresponding to the target application process. Further, the access control unit can authenticate the service access request initiated by the terminal by using the authorization information and send the authentication result to the access gateway, so that the access gateway releases or intercepts the service access request initiated by the target service process according to the authentication result, thereby realizing effective control of the service access request.
Compared with an access control mechanism in the related art, the scheme is integrated with a zero trust mechanism, namely, the application process initiating the service access request is not trusted by default, based on the zero trust mechanism, the authorization and verification management mechanism of the application process is increased, a strong management strategy and security inspection capability of the application process are provided, the access control granularity is refined to each application process in the equipment, the validity of the process source initiating the access can be verified, under the strong management verification strategy, the security threat of some advanced threats or virus Trojan penetration service systems caused by the fact that the application process is tampered can be effectively detected and prevented, and thus, the execution of malicious codes is greatly reduced, the effectiveness of access control is improved, the security risk of the service systems is reduced, and the network security is enhanced.
It should be noted that, the access control method provided by the embodiment of the present application mainly relates to Cloud technology (Cloud technology), and the technology refers to a hosting technology for unifying serial resources such as hardware, software, network, etc. in a wide area network or a local area network, so as to implement calculation, storage, processing and sharing of data. Similarly, the technology is a generic term of network technology, information technology, integration technology, management platform technology, application technology and the like based on cloud computing business model application, can form a resource pool, and is flexible and convenient as required. Cloud computing technology will become an important support. Background services of technical networking systems require a large amount of computing, storage resources, such as video websites, picture-like websites, and more portals. Along with the high development and application of the internet industry, each article possibly has an own identification mark in the future, the identification mark needs to be transmitted to a background system for logic processing, data with different levels can be processed separately, and various industry data needs strong system rear shield support and can be realized only through cloud computing.
Further, in the Cloud technology field, the access control method provided by the embodiment of the application is mainly applied to Cloud computing (Cloud computing), cloud Security (Cloud Security) and Cloud storage (Cloud storage). The related art will be described below.
(1) Cloud computing (clouding) is a computing model that distributes computing tasks over a resource pool of large numbers of computers, enabling various application systems to acquire computing power, storage space, and information services as needed. The network that provides the resources is referred to as the "cloud". Resources in the cloud are infinitely expandable in the sense of users, and can be acquired at any time, used as needed, expanded at any time and paid for use as needed. As a basic capability provider of cloud computing, a cloud computing resource pool is established, where a cloud computing resource pool is called a cloud platform for short, and is generally called an Infrastructure AS A SERVICE (IaaS) platform, and multiple types of virtual resources are deployed in the resource pool for external clients to select for use. The cloud computing resource pool mainly comprises: computing devices (which are virtualized machines, including operating systems), storage devices, network devices. Cloud Computing is a product of fusion of traditional computer and network technology developments such as Grid Computing (Grid Computing), distributed Computing (Distributed Computing), parallel Computing (Parallel Computing), utility Computing (Utility Computing), network storage (Network Storage Technologies), virtualization (Virtualization), load balancing (Load Balance), and the like. With the development of the internet, real-time data flow and diversification of connected devices, and the promotion of demands of search services, social networks, mobile commerce, open collaboration and the like, cloud computing is rapidly developed. Unlike the previous parallel distributed computing, the generation of cloud computing will promote the revolutionary transformation of the whole internet mode and enterprise management mode in concept.
(2) Cloud Security (Cloud Security) refers to a generic term for Security software, hardware, users, institutions, and secure Cloud platforms based on Cloud computing business model applications. Cloud security fuses emerging technologies and concepts such as parallel processing, network computing, unknown disease behavior judgment and the like, acquires the latest information of Trojan horse and malicious programs in the Internet through abnormal monitoring of a large number of netlike clients on software behaviors in the network, sends the latest information to a server for automatic analysis and processing, and distributes solutions of viruses and Trojan horse to each client.
The main research directions of cloud security include: ① Cloud computing security, namely, how to guarantee security of cloud and various applications on the cloud, including cloud computer system security, security storage and isolation of user data, user access authentication, information transmission security, network attack protection, compliance audit and the like; ② Clouding of a safety infrastructure, mainly researching how to build and integrate safety infrastructure resources by adopting cloud computing, and optimizing a safety protection mechanism, wherein the cloud computing technology is used for constructing a super-large-scale safety event and an information acquisition and processing platform, realizing acquisition and association analysis of mass information, and improving the control capability and risk control capability of the whole-network safety event; ③ Cloud security services, mainly research on various security services provided for users based on cloud computing platforms, such as anti-virus services and the like.
(3) Cloud storage (cloud storage) is a new concept which extends and develops in the concept of cloud computing, and a distributed cloud storage system (hereinafter referred to as a storage system for short) refers to a storage system which provides data storage and service access functions for the outside through functions such as cluster application, grid technology, a distributed storage file system and the like, and a large number of storage devices (storage devices are also called storage nodes) of different types in a network are combined to work cooperatively through application software or an application interface. At present, the storage method of the storage system is as follows: when creating logical volumes, each logical volume is allocated a physical storage space, which may be a disk composition of a certain storage device or of several storage devices.
In order to better understand the technical solution provided by the embodiments of the present application, some simple descriptions are provided below for application scenarios applicable to the technical solution provided by the embodiments of the present application, and it should be noted that the application scenarios described below are only used to illustrate the embodiments of the present application, but not limited thereto. In the specific implementation, the technical scheme provided by the embodiment of the application can be flexibly applied according to actual needs.
Referring to fig. 1a, fig. 1a shows an access control system to which the technical solution of the embodiment of the present application is applicable, where the access control system includes an access control unit and an admission gateway, the access control unit includes an authentication module and an access control module, and in a specific network topology, the access control unit and the admission gateway may be integrated on one server, or may be integrated on different servers respectively, that is, the access control unit and the admission gateway may be understood as two logic functional units, which is not limited by the specific physical implementation of the embodiment of the present application.
The main functions of the access control unit include: authentication and authorization of the user and terminal identity, and continuous access control including establishment and deployment of access control policies, dynamic security detection and dynamic guard response. The access control management background can provide centralized management capability, and main functions include: user management, terminal management, resource management, policy management, and the like.
An admission gateway, which is a system that is externally exposed and directly accessible to users (i.e., terminals), has the main functions of forwarding user requests and intercepting user requests. The user request is forwarded by authentication and authorization forwarding for access unauthorized requests, and the resource access forwarding for user requests which are authorized correctly, and the interception is interception and blocking for user requests which are forbidden to access so as to prevent the user requests from continuing to access to the network back end.
The access control unit is positioned at the control layer, the access control unit positioned at the control plane can realize the control functions of authentication, authorization, verification, authentication and the like in the access control, the access gateway is positioned at the data layer, and the access gateway positioned at the data layer can realize the decision of forwarding or intercepting the user request. In this way, the control channel and the data channel are separated, so that mutual influence after blocking can be prevented as much as possible, and the function of each logic function module in access control can be realized more reasonably.
Referring to fig. 1b in combination with fig. 1a, fig. 1b is an application scenario to which the technical solution in the embodiment of the present application is applicable, that is, the access control method in the embodiment of the present application may be applied to the application environments shown in fig. 1a and fig. 1 b. As shown in fig. 1b, the application scenario is composed of a terminal system, an access control system and a service system. The terminal system includes an intra-enterprise terminal (in fig. 1b, terminal 110-1 and terminal 110-2 are taken as examples) and an external-enterprise terminal (in fig. 1b, terminal 110-3 and terminal 110-4 are taken as examples); the access control system comprises an access control unit 120 and an admission gateway 121; the service system is composed of a plurality of service servers (in fig. 1b, the service server 130-1, the service server 130-2, and the service server 130-3 are taken as examples), and an enterprise public cloud service, an enterprise private cloud service, and an enterprise local service can be implemented through the service system, that is, the service system can provide a public cloud service, a private cloud service, and a local service, and can also provide a hybrid cloud service (not shown in fig. 1 b).
The access control system is deployed between the terminal system and the service system, the access control unit 120 can authenticate and authorize each terminal, and can authenticate the service access request initiated by the service system, and the admission gateway 121 passes or intercepts the service access request sent by the terminal according to the authentication result of the access control unit 102, which is equivalent to adding a layer of admission control mechanism between the terminal and the service system, so that direct coupling between the terminal and the service system can be avoided, and thus, the service access request initiated by the terminal can be effectively controlled. Each terminal may communicate with access control unit 100 and admission gateway 121, and admission gateway 121 may communicate with each service server in the service system, the communication network between each terminal and access control unit 100 and admission gateway 121, and the communication network between admission gateway 121 and each service server, including but not limited to a wide area network, a metropolitan area network, or a local area network.
Public clouds (Public clouds) generally refer to clouds that can be used by third party providers for users, the Public clouds can be generally used through the Internet, and may be free or low-cost, the core attribute of the Public clouds is shared resource services, and the Public clouds have many examples and can provide services in the whole Public network which is open today.
A Private Cloud (Private Cloud) is a Cloud infrastructure created with software and hardware resources within a firewall for organizations or departments within an enterprise to share resources within a data center. A private cloud is created, and in addition to hardware resources, there is typically cloud equipment (IaaS, infrastructure AS A SERVICE) software. Private cloud computing also includes three levels of cloud hardware, cloud platform, cloud services. In contrast, cloud hardware is a user's own personal computer or server, rather than a data center of a cloud computing vendor. Private cloud computing serves only friends and relatives to individuals, and staff and clients and suppliers to businesses, so personal or business's own personal computers or servers are sufficient to provide cloud services.
Hybrid clouds (Hybrid clouds) merge public and private clouds, and are the main mode and development direction of Cloud computing in recent years. Private clouds are mainly for enterprise users, and for safety reasons, enterprises prefer to store data in the private clouds, but at the same time wish to obtain computing resources of public clouds, in which case hybrid clouds are increasingly adopted, and mix and match the public clouds and the private clouds to obtain the best effect.
Taking the terminal 110-1 as an example based on the application scenario shown in fig. 1b, in the embodiment of the present application, when a user uses the terminal 110-1 to initiate a service access request to a service system, the terminal 110-1 obtains process feature information of an application process for initiating the service access request, and then performs trusted verification on the process feature information, one possible verification manner is asynchronous inspection verification, specifically, sending the process feature information to the access control unit 120 to perform trusted verification on the process feature information through the access control unit 120, and another possible verification manner is local verification, that is, the terminal 110-1 may use a trusted process list (also referred to as a process whitelist) cached in advance from the access control unit 120 to match the process feature information to implement trusted verification on the process feature information. When the process characteristic information passes the trusted verification, corresponding authorization information can be obtained, wherein the authorization information is used for indicating that the application process of the initiated service access request is a trusted application process authenticated by the system, and the authorization information can indicate that the application process is a trusted process and is safe.
Further, when sending the service access request to the admission gateway 121, the terminal 110-1 may send the issued authorization information to the admission gateway 121 together, where the admission gateway 121 may send the service access request (specifically, for example, access link information in the service access request) and the authorization information to the access control unit 120 together, so that the access control unit 120 authenticates the sent service access request together according to the authorization control information, which is actually equivalent to authenticating an application process that initiates the service access request, and when the authentication is passed, it indicates that the application process that initiates the service access request is actually a security process that is authenticated by trust, so that the service access request may be forwarded to a corresponding service server in the service system to achieve security access to the service system, and when the authentication is not passed, it indicates that there is a security risk in the application process that initiates the service access request, and at this time, the service access request may be intercepted (for example, discarded) and dangerous prompt information may be returned to the terminal 110-1, so as to notify that the application process that initiates the service access request may be potentially appear in a security risk, so that a potential network user can find and process in time.
In the processing process of the service access request, the application process initiating the service access request is taken as the detection and control granularity, the fine-granularity access control mechanism provides a strong management strategy for security inspection of the application process, and the validity of the process source initiating the access is verified, so that the validity of the access control can be improved, the security risk of a service system is reduced, and the security performance of the service system is enhanced.
Based on the service access control of the application scene, the traditional region-based trust control mode is broken, forced access must be authenticated and authorized based on a strong management strategy for an application process, so that a user (such as enterprise staff) can safely access service resources in an enterprise wherever and when using any equipment, service access can be effectively detected and controlled, flexibility and access experience are good, security risks such as data leakage are reduced, and the security of the enterprise office is improved.
The access control unit 120, the admission gateway 121, and each service server in the service system (i.e., the service server 130-1, the service server 130-2, and the service server 130-3) may be an independent physical server, or may be a server cluster or a distributed system formed by a plurality of physical servers, or may be a cloud server that provides cloud services, cloud databases, cloud computing, cloud functions, cloud storage, network services, cloud communication, middleware services, domain name services, security services, CDNs (Content Delivery Network, content distribution networks), and basic cloud computing services such as big data and artificial intelligent platforms. The terminal devices 110-1, 110-2, 110-3, and 110-4 may be, but are not limited to, notebook computers, desktop computers, all-in-one machines, smart phones, tablet computers, and the like.
In order to further explain the technical solution provided by the embodiments of the present application, the following details are described with reference to the accompanying drawings and the detailed description. Although embodiments of the present application provide the method operational steps shown in the following embodiments or figures, more or fewer operational steps may be included in the method, either on a routine or non-inventive basis. In steps where there is logically no necessary causal relationship, the execution order of the steps is not limited to the execution order provided by the embodiments of the present application. The methods may be performed sequentially or in parallel as shown in the embodiments or the drawings when the actual processing or the apparatus is performed.
The access control method provided by the embodiment of the application mainly relates to a terminal for initiating a service access request and an access control unit for authenticating the service access request, and can be realized in an application scene shown in fig. 1a or fig. 1b, and the access control method provided by the embodiment of the application is described below from the angles of the terminal and the access control unit respectively.
Referring to fig. 2, the terminal is, for example, any one of the intra-enterprise terminals or the external-enterprise terminals in the application scenario shown in fig. 1 b. The flow shown in fig. 2 is described as follows.
Step 201: and responding to the access triggering operation, and initiating a service access request through the target application process.
When a user needs to request a resource from a service system, that is, when the user needs to access the service system, a specific trigger operation may be performed on the terminal, for example, the trigger operation is referred to as an access trigger operation, for example, the access trigger operation is an input operation performed by the user to input a specified URL (Uniform Resource Locator ) address, or for example, the access trigger operation is a click operation performed by the user to click on a specified folder inside an enterprise, or the like.
In a specific implementation process, a user generally performs an access trigger operation on an application installed in a terminal, where the application is, for example, an office application or other applications used in an enterprise, and after detecting the access trigger operation, an application process corresponding to the application may be called to initiate a service access request, for example, an application process that initiates the service access request is called a target application process, it may be understood that different applications may have different application processes, and the same application may also include different application processes. Wherein an "application process" of an application, which may also be referred to as a process, is an instance of the application in the process of running.
Step 202: and acquiring process characteristic information of the target application process.
Each application process has its corresponding process feature information, and the process feature information of one application process is information for identifying the application process and is unique for identifying the application process, that is, the process feature information corresponding to the application process has uniqueness. In a specific implementation, the process characteristic information of the application process may include one or more combinations of information such as a process identifier (e.g., a process name), process signature information, a process MD5 (MESSAGE DIGEST algoritm 5, a fifth version of a message digest Algorithm), a process sha256 (an Algorithm), a process version number, and so on. For example, the process characteristic information of the application process with the process name "wehaha. Exe" is shown in fig. 3, and the information of the process name of the application process, the application name of the application, the applicable operating system, the process signature information, the process MD5, the process version, the process sha256, and the like is shown in fig. 3.
Step 203: and when the process characteristic information passes the trusted verification, obtaining authorization information corresponding to the target application process.
The authorization information corresponding to the target application process is used for indicating that the corresponding target application process is a trusted application process verified by the system, the corresponding application process can be indicated to be a trusted process through the authorization information, and the corresponding application process is indicated to be safe, that is, the authorization information can be regarded as identity credentials of the trusted application process, so the authorization information can be called as authorization information and process authorization credentials, or the authorization information of the process can be called as a bill or a process bill, and the authorization information of the process is equivalent to a pass of the application process in the process of accessing the service system.
In the embodiment of the application, the process characteristic information of the target application process initiating the service access request needs to be subjected to the trusted verification, and the process characteristic information is subjected to the trusted verification, which is equivalent to the trusted verification of the corresponding target application process, so that when the process characteristic information passes the trusted verification, the corresponding target application process passes the trusted verification. The trusted verification may also be called security verification or security authentication, for example, that is to verify the security of the target application process by the process characteristic information.
In a specific implementation process, the process feature information may be verified in a plurality of ways, and for the terminal, one possible verification way is asynchronous inspection verification, and another possible verification way is local verification, and the two verification ways are described below in conjunction with fig. 4. Referring to fig. 4, steps 401 to 404 (i.e., step 401, step 402, step 403, step 404) illustrate the asynchronous inspection verification process, and steps 401, step 405, and step 406 illustrate the local verification process. The following is a detailed description.
Step 401: and obtaining the process characteristic information of the target application process.
This step is the same as the implementation of step 202 described above and will not be repeated here.
Step 402: and sending the process characteristic information to an access control unit so as to perform trusted verification on the process characteristic information through the access control unit.
The asynchronous inspection verification refers to that the terminal sends the process characteristic information to other devices (such as an access control unit) for verification at different places, and after the access control unit receives the process characteristic information, the process characteristic information can be verified in a trusted manner in some possible manners, and several possible verification manners are provided below.
Mode 1:
The access control unit locally stores a second process list, which may be a trusted process list, for example referred to as white list, and the corresponding second process list may also be an untrusted process list, for example referred to as black list. The access control unit may match the process feature information with a locally stored trusted process list and an untrusted process list, and if it is determined that the process feature information exists in the white list, it may be considered as a trusted process, that is, it indicates that the trusted process has passed, and if it is determined that the process feature information exists in the black list, it may be considered as an untrusted process, that is, it indicates that the trusted process has failed.
In another possible case, the process characteristic information does not exist in the white list and the black list, and can be called as a "gray process" at this time, that is, the system does not clearly determine whether the system is a trusted white process or an untrusted black process, and at this time, the access control unit can output the identification result of the "gray process" to the user, for example, to the terminal or directly display the identification result to the administrator, so that the user can determine the identification result by himself. Or under the scene of strong security requirements, such as a banking system, a financial system, a secret-related system and the like, the system can directly consider the gray process as an unreliable process, namely, the gray process and the black process are processed in the same mode, so that the system security can be ensured as much as possible.
In the mode 1, the access control unit performs local verification on the process feature information through the locally stored process list, so that the verification efficiency is high, and the locally stored process list is set by an administrator according to enterprise properties and enterprise requirements in advance, for example, so that the filtering verification mode can meet the requirements of actual service scenes as much as possible, and the verification effectiveness is high.
Mode 2:
The access control unit can purchase cloud verification services of some third party verification platforms or can establish a cooperative relationship with the cloud verification services, based on the cloud verification services, the access control unit can call a cloud query interface, send process characteristic information to the cloud verification platform corresponding to the cloud query interface, and determine whether the process characteristic information passes trusted verification according to second verification result information sent by the cloud verification platform. That is, the access control unit can perform remote auxiliary verification through the third party verification platform, so that the verification work of the access control unit itself can be reduced, the processing load of the access control unit is reduced, and the third party verification platform is generally of a verification structure with stronger professionals, so that the effectiveness of the trusted verification of the process characteristic information can be improved to a certain extent.
Mode 3:
The access control unit sends the process characteristic information to the security detection analysis platform so as to carry out security detection on the running behavior of the target application process according to the process characteristic information through the security detection analysis platform, and determines whether the process characteristic information passes the trusted verification according to the detection result output by the security detection analysis platform. The security detection analysis platform is a service system for providing security management, such as SOC (Security Operations Center, security operation center), SIEM (Security Information EVENT MANAGEMENT, security information and event management), MSS (Managing security services, management security service), etc., and may be integrated in the access control unit, or may be integrated in other servers in a distributed manner, or may be a separate analysis platform. That is, the security detection analysis platform can determine the target application process according to the process feature information, and further dynamically detect the running process of the target application process, for example, perform security related trusted verification on the target application process according to the running log data in the last period of time of the target application process, so that the target application process can be effectively and reliably verified.
After the access control unit performs the trusted verification on the process feature information in any mode, a final verification result can be obtained, and the verification result is represented by first verification result information, wherein the first verification result information is used for indicating whether the process feature information passes the trusted verification, for example, the first verification result information is used for indicating that the process feature information passes the trusted verification, or the first verification result information is used for indicating that the process feature information does not pass the trusted verification. Further, the first verification result information may be returned to the terminal.
Step 403: and receiving first verification result information sent by the access control unit.
After receiving the first verification result information sent by the access control unit, the terminal can determine whether the target application process which initiates the service access request currently is safe and credible according to the indication.
Step 404: and receiving authorization information corresponding to the process characteristic information, which is sent by the access control unit.
When the access control unit determines that the process characteristic information passes the trusted verification, the access control unit may also issue a corresponding authorization credential for the target application process, and in a possible implementation manner, the access control unit may generate corresponding authorization credential information according to the process characteristic information and send the generated authorization credential information to the terminal, so as to implement verification and trust of the target application process, for example, refer to the authorization credential information as authorization information.
Step 405: and matching the process characteristic information with a first process list stored locally.
The first process list stored in the terminal may be downloaded and cached from the access control unit in advance, the first process list may be a process white list or a process black list, and the embodiment of verifying the credibility of the process feature information by the terminal using the first process list is similar to the embodiment of performing credibility verification by the access control unit through the locally stored second process list described above, so the implementation of step 405 may refer to the description of mode1 described above, and will not be repeated herein.
Step 406: if the matching result shows that the process characteristic information belongs to a white process, namely the process characteristic information is positioned in a trusted process list, authorization information corresponding to the process characteristic information is generated.
If the process characteristic information is trusted, the target application process is indicated to be safe and trusted, and at the moment, the terminal can issue authorization information for the target application process by itself, and of course, the terminal generates corresponding authorization information for the target application process according to a trust mode agreed with the access control unit, for example, the corresponding authorization information is obtained by encrypting the process characteristic information according to an encryption algorithm agreed with the access control unit.
The above describes two ways of asynchronous inspection verification and terminal local verification, and in the implementation process, the two ways can be alternatively implemented to perform single verification or can be simultaneously implemented to perform double verification, so that the embodiment of the application is not limited.
For the two ways of asynchronous inspection verification and terminal local verification described above, after the terminal or the access control unit obtains the trusted verification result for the process characteristic information, the verification result can be output to the user, so that the user can perform final manual confirmation conveniently. For example:
For the local verification of the terminal and the verification mode by the access control unit, after obtaining the trusted verification result of the device on the process characteristic information, the terminal can display a result confirmation interface, wherein the result confirmation interface comprises the trusted verification result of the process characteristic information. Further, the user may choose whether to approve the verification result of the device according to his actual cognition and understanding, specifically, the user may perform a confirmation operation (for example, referred to as a first confirmation operation) with respect to the result confirmation interface, the terminal may obtain the user confirmation result in response to the first confirmation operation, and then use the user confirmation result as a final verification result, that is, update the foregoing trusted verification result of the process feature information obtained by the device with the user confirmation result. The method can meet the actual knowledge of the end user on the application process as much as possible by a secondary confirmation mode of the end user, and further improves the verification effectiveness.
For the asynchronous verification mode of the access control unit, after the access control unit obtains the trusted verification result aiming at the process characteristic information, a management operation interface can be displayed, the management operation interface comprises the trusted verification result of the process characteristic information, an administrator of the access control unit can carry out secondary verification on the verification result of the access control unit in a manual verification mode, thus the administrator can carry out verification operation (such as second verification operation) aiming at the management operation interface, the access control unit responds to the second verification operation to obtain the administrator verification result, and then the administrator verification result is used for updating the trusted verification result of the process characteristic information obtained by verification of the control gateway. The secondary verification mode of the management end is also used for further improving the verification effectiveness.
The above description of two ways of performing trusted authentication on the process feature information is illustrated by fig. 4, and in a specific implementation process, the process feature information may also be verified in a dual-terminal verification manner.
First, in addition to the process feature information sent to the access control unit, the terminal may send the user account information logged in by itself and the access link information corresponding to the service access request to the process feature information.
Further, the access control unit may perform the trusted verification on the process feature information by using the method described above and obtain the verification result, and in another embodiment, the access control unit may not perform the trusted verification on the process feature information.
Then, the access control unit determines the terminal logged in by the account information associated with the access control unit according to the user account information. Furthermore, the access control unit sends the process characteristic information and the access link information to the associated terminal, or if the access control unit verifies the process characteristic information, the verification result and the process characteristic information and the access link information can be sent to the associated terminal.
And after receiving the process characteristic information and the access link information (which can also comprise a verification result of the process characteristic information by the access control unit), the associated terminal can display the process characteristic information to a user, and the user of the associated terminal can select whether the process characteristic information is determined to be credible or not by himself, so that the associated terminal is triggered to generate user decision information and return the user decision information to the access control unit, wherein the user decision information is used for indicating whether the process characteristic information passes the credible verification. In this process, the access control unit sends the authentication result of the access control unit to the user together, which is equivalent to a certain risk prompt for the user, if the user does not follow the authentication result of the access control unit and makes a decision on the contrary by itself, the security problem occurring in the later stage for the user can be borne by the user by himself, so in one embodiment, if the authentication result of the access control unit is opposite to the user decision information, the access control unit can store the user decision information in association with the user account information and the access link information corresponding to the user decision information, on one hand, the user decision information can be directly adopted when the user encounters such authentication subsequently, on the other hand, the user decision information can be recorded so as to analyze the reason and divide responsibility when the security accident occurs subsequently, and the like.
In the above embodiment, the associated account information corresponding to the user account information may be the user account information itself, for example, the user logs in the user account information of the user at the computer end and the mobile phone end at the same time, when the service access request is initiated at the computer end, the access control unit may further send the relevant process feature information and the access link information to the mobile phone end, so that the user performs the second verification at the mobile phone end, that is, performs the second verification through another terminal having the same login identity, so that the effectiveness and security of the access control may be further improved through the dual-terminal verification method.
In another embodiment, the associated account information corresponding to the user account information is other user account information different from the user account information, for example, account information of other users in the same group as the user is used, for example, account information of a company administrator, or account management information of a user's upper part is used, and the like, so that an audit role is added through the associated terminal, and the effectiveness and safety of access control can be further improved through a dual-terminal verification mode.
Step 204: and sending the service access request and the authorization information to an access gateway so as to pass or intercept the service access request through the access gateway according to the authentication result of the service access request, wherein the service access request is authenticated through the authorization information.
After obtaining the authorization information, the terminal may assemble the service access request and the authorization information and then send the service access request and the authorization information to the access gateway, for example, reassemble the service access request and the authorization information into one piece of information according to a transmission protocol between the terminal and the access gateway and then send the information to the access gateway, so that the access gateway can correctly receive the service access request and the corresponding authorization information sent by the terminal.
After receiving the service access request and the corresponding authorization information, the access gateway can send the service access request and the corresponding authorization information to the access control unit for authentication, specifically, for example, the access connection information and the authorization information corresponding to the service access request are sent to the access control unit, further, the access control unit uses the authorization information to authenticate the service access request, for example, decrypts the authorization information according to a contracted decryption algorithm, and then, whether the authorization information is in a valid period is also needed to be judged, if both the two verification methods are in conformity, the current service access request can be considered to be safe, namely, the authentication of the service access request is passed, and the access gateway can be informed of the authentication result.
The access gateway can process the service access request according to the authentication result returned by the access control unit. Specifically, when authentication is passed, the admission gateway may distribute the service access request to the corresponding service server, so as to obtain the corresponding resource from the service server and forward the corresponding resource to the terminal, or directly send the corresponding resource to the terminal by the service server. When the authentication is not passed, the service access request can be intercepted, for example, the service access request can be directly discarded, and meanwhile, dangerous prompt information can be returned to the terminal so as to inform the user of the terminal that the security risk exists or the target application process of the current initiation service access request is illegal.
In the embodiment of the application, the application process is taken as the granularity of access control, the availability of each application can be ensured through the fine-granularity access control mechanism, and the risk management and control are carried out from the source of the accessed process, so that the effectiveness of the access control can be effectively improved, and the security of the whole business system can be improved.
In the embodiment of the application, on the basis of the access control of the application process, the permission verification can be performed on the user, and the following example is shown.
In one embodiment, the user account information and an application identifier of an application to which the target application process belongs are sent to an access control unit, so that whether an account corresponding to the user account information has permission to use the application indicated by the application identifier or not is determined through the access control unit, a first permission matching result sent by the access control unit is received, and then the application indicated by the account corresponding to the user account information has permission to use the application identifier is determined according to the first permission matching result. That is, the user permission can be judged first for the usable application, and the application which is not used by the user permission is not supported to initiate the service access request, so that the user permission can be verified, the resource leakage is avoided, and the access safety is improved.
In another embodiment, the user account information and the resource identification information of the target resource to be accessed corresponding to the service access request are sent to the access control unit, so that whether the account corresponding to the user account information has permission to access the target resource or not is determined through the access control unit, a second permission matching node sent by the access control unit is received, and then the account corresponding to the user account information is determined to have permission to access the target resource according to a second permission matching result. That is, the resources which the user has permission to access can be verified, so that the user permission can be verified, the resource leakage is avoided, and the access security is improved.
In order to facilitate understanding of those skilled in the art, the following description will be given with reference to the accompanying drawings.
Referring to fig. 5, fig. 5 illustrates a process of asynchronously checking process feature information in a terminal by an access control unit in an access control system, and a flow shown in fig. 5 is described as follows.
Step 501: and the terminal initiates a service access request through the target application process and obtains process characteristic information of the target application process.
Step 502: the terminal sends the process characteristic information to the access control unit so as to carry out asynchronous verification on the process characteristic information through the network control unit.
Step 503: the access control unit performs trusted verification on the process characteristic information.
Step 504: upon determining that the process feature information has passed the trusted verification, the access control unit generates authorization information corresponding to the target application process, which may be referred to as a "ticket", for example.
Step 505: the access control unit transmits the generated authorization information to the terminal.
Step 506: the terminal sends the service access request and the authorization information to an admission gateway in the service control system.
Step 507: and the admission gateway sends the received service access request and the received authorization information to the access control unit for authentication.
After receiving the service access request and the authorization information sent by the terminal, the admission gateway needs to authenticate the service access request and the authorization information, specifically, requests the access control unit to authenticate the service access request and the authorization information.
Step 508: the access control unit authenticates the service access request according to the authorization information to obtain an authentication result, wherein the authentication result indicates that the authentication is passed or failed.
Step 509: the access control unit sends the authentication result to the admission gateway.
And when the authentication is determined to pass according to the authentication result, the access gateway forwards the service access request to the service server so as to request corresponding resources from the service server.
On the other hand, if the access gateway determines that the authentication is not passed according to the authentication result, the access gateway directly intercepts the service access request locally to realize the security control of network access.
Step 510: and when the authentication is determined to pass according to the authentication result, the access gateway forwards the service access request to the service server so as to request corresponding resources from the service server.
Referring again to fig. 6, fig. 6 illustrates a process of jointly verifying process feature information by an access control unit and a terminal in an access control system, and a flow shown in fig. 6 is described as follows.
Step 601: and the terminal initiates a service access request through the target application process and obtains process characteristic information of the target application process.
Step 602: and the terminal performs the credibility verification on the process characteristic information locally.
For example, the terminal may match the process feature information with a local first process list (process white list or process black list) to determine whether the process feature information is located in the process white list or the process black list, so as to determine whether the process feature information passes the trusted verification.
In the local verification, the process characteristic information may not be in the white list or the black list, and at this time, the process characteristic information may be regarded as a "gray process", and for the "gray process", prompt information may be popped out to the user to enable the user to manually confirm the trusted verification result, or in some strong security business scenarios, the "gray process" may also be treated as a black process directly.
Step 603: when the local verification passes, the terminal sends the process characteristic information to the access control unit so as to perform secondary verification through the network control unit, thereby achieving the aim of joint verification.
Step 604: the access control unit performs trusted verification on the process characteristic information.
Step 605: upon determining that the process feature information has passed the trusted verification, the access control unit generates authorization information corresponding to the target application process, which may be referred to as a "ticket", for example.
Step 606: the access control unit transmits the generated authorization information to the terminal.
Step 607: the terminal sends the service access request and the authorization information to an admission gateway in the service control system.
Step 608: and the admission gateway sends the received service access request and the received authorization information to the access control unit for authentication.
After receiving the service access request and the authorization information sent by the terminal, the admission gateway needs to authenticate the service access request and the authorization information, specifically, requests the access control unit to authenticate the service access request and the authorization information.
Step 609: the access control unit authenticates the service access request according to the authorization information to obtain an authentication result, and comfort results indicate that the authentication is passed or failed.
Step 610: the access control unit sends the authentication result to the admission gateway.
Step 611: and when the authentication is determined to pass according to the authentication result, the access gateway forwards the service access request to the service server so as to request corresponding resources from the service server.
On the other hand, if the access gateway determines that the authentication is not passed according to the authentication result, the access gateway directly intercepts the service access request locally to realize the security control of network access.
Referring to fig. 7 again, fig. 7 illustrates a process of independently verifying process feature information by a terminal, and the flowchart illustrated in fig. 7 is described below.
Step 701: and the terminal initiates a service access request through the target application process and obtains process characteristic information of the target application process.
Step 702: and the terminal performs the credibility verification on the process characteristic information locally.
For example, the terminal may match the process feature information with a local first process list (process white list or process black list) to determine whether the process feature information is located in the process white list or the process black list, so as to determine whether the process feature information passes the trusted verification.
In the local verification, the process characteristic information may not be in the white list or the black list, and at this time, the process characteristic information may be regarded as a "gray process", and for the "gray process", prompt information may be popped out to the user to enable the user to manually confirm the trusted verification result, or in some strong security business scenarios, the "gray process" may also be treated as a black process directly.
Step 703: and when the local verification passes, the terminal generates authorization information corresponding to the target application process.
It should be noted that, the manner in which the terminal generates the authorization information needs to be agreed with the access control unit in advance, so that the access control unit can conveniently authenticate the service access request initiated by the terminal according to the authorization information.
Step 704: the terminal sends the service access request and the authorization information to an admission gateway in the service control system.
Step 705: and the admission gateway sends the received service access request and the received authorization information to the access control unit for authentication.
After receiving the service access request and the authorization information sent by the terminal, the admission gateway needs to authenticate the service access request and the authorization information, specifically, requests the access control unit to authenticate the service access request and the authorization information.
Step 706: the access control unit authenticates the service access request according to the authorization information to obtain an authentication result, and comfort results indicate that the authentication is passed or failed.
Step 707: the access control unit sends the authentication result to the admission gateway.
Step 708: and when the authentication is determined to pass according to the authentication result, the access gateway forwards the service access request to the service server so as to request corresponding resources from the service server.
Referring again to another embodiment shown in fig. 8, fig. 8 illustrates a process of performing dual terminal authentication on process feature information by a terminal and an associated terminal associated with the terminal, and the flow shown in fig. 8 is described as follows.
Step 801: and the terminal initiates a service access request through the target application process and obtains process characteristic information of the target application process.
Step 802: and the terminal sends the process characteristic information, the user account information and the access link information corresponding to the service access request to the access control unit.
Step 803: the access control unit performs trusted verification on the process characteristic information to obtain a verification result.
In an implementation, step 803 is an optional step, which may or may not be performed.
Step 804: the access control unit determines a terminal which is logged in by the corresponding association account information according to the user account information, and the terminal is called an association terminal.
Step 805: the access control unit transmits the process characteristic information and the access link information to the associated terminal.
In another embodiment, if step 803 is performed before, the verification result may be sent to the associated terminal together in step 805.
Step 806: the associated terminal outputs (e.g., presents to the user) the process feature information and the access link information and obtains user decision information.
The user decision information is used for indicating whether the process feature information passes the trusted verification, the user decision information is a decision made by a user manually, and indicates an actual selection result of the user, and it is known that the selection result of the user may be the same as or different from the verification result obtained by the access control unit.
Step 807: and the associated terminal sends the user decision information to the access control unit.
Step 808: the access control unit determines whether the process characteristic information passes the trusted verification according to the user decision information.
Step 809: and when the access control unit determines that the process characteristic information passes the trusted verification, generating authorization information and sending the authorization information to the terminal.
Step 810: and the terminal sends a service access request and authorization information to the access gateway.
Step 811: and when the admission gateway determines that the authentication is passed, forwarding the service access request to a service server to request corresponding resources.

## 714. [US11496519B1] Managing security in isolated network environments
- **Patent ID / App No**: `US11496519B1`
- **Source**: Google Patents
- **URL**: [https://patents.google.com/patent/US11496519B1/en](https://patents.google.com/patent/US11496519B1/en)
- **AI Relevancy Score**: N/A (UNAUDITED)

### 📋 Abstract
> Security can be provided for data stored using resources that are deployed in an environment managed by a third party. Physical and logical detection mechanisms can be used to monitor various security aspects, and the resulting security data can be used to identify potential threats to these resources. In some embodiments, suspicious activity can cause resources such as data servers to be automatically and remotely rebooted such that keys stored in volatile memory on those data servers will be lost from those servers, such that an attacker will be unable to decrypt data stored on those servers. Once a determination of safety is made, the keys can be provided to the respective data servers such that data operations can resume.

### 📜 Full Specification & Deep Scrape Text
Title
Managing security in isolated network environments

Abstract
Security can be provided for data stored using resources that are deployed in an environment managed by a third party. Physical and logical detection mechanisms can be used to monitor various security aspects, and the resulting security data can be used to identify potential threats to these resources. In some embodiments, suspicious activity can cause resources such as data servers to be automatically and remotely rebooted such that keys stored in volatile memory on those data servers will be lost from those servers, such that an attacker will be unable to decrypt data stored on those servers. Once a determination of safety is made, the keys can be provided to the respective data servers such that data operations can resume.

Description
BACKGROUND
Cloud computing platforms often provide on-demand, managed computing resources to customers. Such computing resources (e.g., compute and storage capacity) are often provisioned from large pools of capacity installed in data centers. Customers can request computing resources from the “cloud,” and the cloud can provision compute resources to those customers. Technologies such as virtual machines and containers are often used to allow customers to securely share capacity of computer systems. This capacity may be located in various locations that are managed by different entities, however, which can raise concerns about security.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION
The present disclosure relates to methods, apparatus, systems, and non-transitory computer-readable storage media for increasing security for cloud service provider substrate extension resources. A cloud provider network, or “cloud,” refers to a large pool of network-accessible computing resources (such as compute, storage, and networking resources, applications, and services). The cloud can provide convenient, on-demand network access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources that can be programmatically provisioned and released in response to customer commands. Cloud computing can thus be considered as both the applications delivered as services over a publicly accessible network (e.g., the Internet, a cellular communication network) and the hardware and software in cloud provider data centers that provide those services. Some customers may desire to use the resources and services of such cloud provider networks, but for various reasons (e.g., latency in communications with customer devices, legal compliance, security, or other reasons) prefer for these resources and services to be provisioned within their own network (for example on premises of the customer), at a separate network managed by the cloud provider, within a network of a communications service provider, or within another independent network.
In some instances a cloud provider may want to deploy physical resources in a particular region, and may contract with a third party to enable those physical resources to be deployed in a given location. It will often be the case, however, that the cloud provider will not have control over the security of this location. Accordingly, the cloud provider may provide additional physical (and logical) security mechanisms that can monitor for suspicious or unapproved activity with respect to the resources. In some embodiments, the resources may be deployed in a protected area, such as inside a metal cage with locks and tamper sensors. There may be cameras and motion sensors deployed to detect motion or objects in this case, as well as various sensors for detecting movement or tampering. Individual racks or servers in the deployment may also have security mechanisms, such as tamper-evident tags. Security data from these physical devices, as well as data from other physical devices for the location offered by the third party, may be analyzed to attempt to determine potential or actual threats, or suspicious activity, with respect to any aspect of the deployment. In some embodiments there may be logical security mechanisms in place as well, to attempt to determine digital or virtual attacks, etc.
In some embodiments the data from the various security mechanisms can be used to calculate a value such as a health score or risk score. If this score falls outside an acceptable range, a determination can be made that there is a security threat and one or more remediations should be performed. In some embodiments, this includes determining potentially impacted resources and rebooting those resources. For resources such as data servers, data such as customer data may be encrypted using an encryption key that is stored locally in volatile memory. A rebooting of the server would cause this key to be lost from volatile memory, such that an attacker would not be able to decrypt the customer data. Once it is determined, based at least in part upon the security data, that the deployment is safe or not under active threat, the keys can be re-transmitted to the impacted servers to enable the customer data to again be accessed from those devices. Appropriate notifications and alarms can be provided for various types of actual or potential attacks, and in some cases there may be various options provided for remediating the attack.
Various other applications, processes, and uses are presented below with respect to the various embodiments.
FIG. 1 illustrates an example configuration 100 that can be utilized in accordance with various embodiments. This example configuration includes a resource provider environment 102 (or “cloud” environment) and a third party environment 140 . Various other types of environments can be utilized as well as discussed elsewhere herein, such as lower security environments or environments where a resource provider does not have control over various security mechanisms, among other such options. These environments can be managed by a resource provider, customer, or third party provider, among other such options. In some embodiments, the environment may be provided by the resource provider but may have a lower security level than is to be used for a particular resource deployment within that environment. In some embodiments, environment 140 could be contained within resource provider environment 102 . In some embodiment a secured deployment could be managed by a resource provider on behalf of a customer, even if the secured deployment is located within an environment controlled by the customer.
As mentioned above, a customer may have an account with a resource provider, or cloud provider, to store and/or process data using various cloud resources. In some embodiments customer data may be hosted or processed using physical resources 114 , 116 of the resource provider environment. Since these physical resources are located within the resource provider environment 102 , over which the resource provider has complete control, the resource provider can be sure that various security mechanisms are in place, as may be managed by a security manager 106 system or service in that environment. It might be the case, however, that at least some of the physical data for a customer may be located external to the resource provider environment 102 .
For example, a cloud provider might contract with a third party to host resources in a specific location. If a cloud provider hosts data for customers in various locations, it can be desirable to host that data locally to those customers for at least performance reasons, such as to reduce latency of data transmission. It may not be practical or desirable, however, for a cloud provider to purchase real estate to set up data centers at these various location, which would require the purchase, management, and maintenance of various physical devices. In some instances, a cloud provider may contract with a third party to have at least some resources placed in a third party environment 140 , such as a server farm or data center owned or managed by a third party. In some embodiments this environment may be owned or controlled by a customer having data hosted by the cloud provider. In any of these situations, at least some level of access or security of the third party environment will be out of the control of the cloud provider.
For example, a third party environment will often have its own physical security mechanisms in the environment, as may relate to locks, cameras, sensors, and the like. These security mechanisms can feed into a third party security system 146 , which in at least some embodiments can send information about potential security breaches or other security events to the cloud provider and/or impacted customers. It will often be the case, however, that the cloud provider will not have control over the security of the third party environment. For resources housing customer data, proper security can be vital to the cloud provider business. While in at least some instances there will be some level of agreement as to security measures to be put in place, the cloud provider may not have the ability to inspect or verify that these measures are in place and functioning properly. Thus, the cloud provider may wish to provide at least some level of additional security to protect its resources in the third party environment 140 .
In this example, there may be a number of physical servers 158 hosted in a number of server racks 156 and managed by one or more resource managers 154 as discussed in more detail elsewhere herein. In order to restrict access to these resources, the resources may be placed in a cage or other access-restricting mechanism. A cage in one embodiment is a fenced-in environment with a locked door or gate, such that physical access to the racks and servers 158 for the cloud provider is only available to an authorized party having a key to a lock 164 or other access control mechanism of this cage 150 . In some embodiments, a cage can be a metal cage positioned on a floor of a data center managed by a third party. While an employee of the third party may have access to third party resources 142 , 144 , they are restricted from accessing cloud provider resources inside the cage unless provided with such access.
In this example, a cage 150 can have various security mechanisms, which can feed into a cloud manager- specific security manager 152 within the cage 150 . The cage can have a lock 164 or other access detection mechanism on a door or entry into the cage 150 . When the lock is unlocked, or access is able to be obtained through a door that has been opened, information can be sent to the security manager 152 . There can also be one or more access detection mechanisms such as cameras 160 or motion detectors 162 which can detect motion within, or potentially near, the cage 150 . Any motion or movement may cause data to be sent to the security manager 152 , and in the case of a camera video or image data can be captured that can be stored or transmitted to the security manager or resource provider environment. Other mechanisms such as audio or infrared detectors can be used as well in various embodiments.
In at least some embodiments, there can be additional security mechanisms on the individual resources as well. For example, there can be tamper- evident tags 168 or sensors on the individual servers 158 , as well as similar sensors 166 on the racks themselves. In some embodiments these devices can be network-enabled devices that are able to transmit data to the security manager 152 upon any tampering or physical access. In other embodiments, a camera 160 can capture image data that can be analyzed to determine whether the tags remain intact or show evidence of tampering. Other security elements can be used as well, as may include individual locks, touch sensors, and the like.
In various embodiments, data from these various security mechanisms for a given cage 150 can be fed to a security manager 152 in the cage 150 or a security manager 106 in the resource provider environment. In some embodiments, detection of certain security events such as unauthorized access by a person in the cage can be enough to trigger an alarm or security review. In other embodiments, detection of security events such as motion within a cage may be enough to trigger further investigation, such as a notification to security personnel or a request to a security application to analyze video data to attempt to determine a cause of this motion. In some embodiments, there may be a security score or threshold that must be violated for action to be taken. Each security mechanism can have, or generate, a certain score, and the scores for the various security mechanisms can be added up to determine whether the security risk exceeds an acceptable threshold, or whether a security score health falls below a specified threshold, among other such options. In some embodiments, the thresholds may vary by factors such as type of location, type of resource impacted, type of data impacted, etc. In some embodiments, certain actions such as detection of a broken lock or detection of an unauthorized person accessing a server storing customer data may have a high enough score to trigger an alarm or security event regardless of the values of other security mechanisms.
As mentioned, detection of a breach (or potential security breach) may cause certain security actions to occur, such as to sound a security alarm or to dispatch security personnel to the location of the breach. There will be some latency in these actions, however, as it will take some time for personnel to react to the alarm or notification, during which time an attacker could potentially make off with, or corrupt, customer data stored on those servers 158 . Accordingly, approaches in accordance with various embodiments can attempt to further protect customer data on these servers 158 , or other such resources, using encryption keys or other such digital security mechanisms.
