### 📜 Full Specification & Deep Scrape Text
Title
Power grid topology optimization method and system based on search ordering

Abstract
The invention discloses a power grid topology optimization method and system based on search sequencing, wherein the method comprises the steps of obtaining power grid topology structure data and constructing an action space based on the power grid topology structure data; the power grid topological structure data comprises a node set, an edge set and an attribute set; acquiring real-time power grid state data, constructing a self-adaptive double-tower model based on the real-time power grid state data and an action space, and calculating to obtain a candidate action set; constructing a graph attention network and a time sequence graph neural network based on the candidate action set to obtain a sorted candidate action list; and performing multi-objective optimization and decision making based on the ordered candidate action list to obtain the optimal action. The invention not only improves the overall effect of power grid topology optimization, but also enhances the adaptability and decision quality of the system, realizes the rapid optimization of a large-scale power grid system and provides powerful support for practical application by organically combining innovative algorithm construction and various methods.

Description
Power grid topology optimization method and system based on search ordering
Technical Field
The invention belongs to the field of intelligent power grid dispatching and discloses a power grid topology optimization method and system based on search ordering.
Background
The power grid topology optimization is one of key technologies for guaranteeing safe, economical and reliable operation of a power system. With the continuous expansion of the power grid scale, the increasing complexity of the structure and the massive access of new energy and flexible loads, the power grid topology optimization faces unprecedented challenges and opportunities. The power grid topology optimization method based on search sequencing is used as an emerging optimization strategy, has great potential in the aspects of improving the optimization efficiency, adapting to complex power grid structures, dynamic operation environments and the like, and has important research significance in improving the overall performance of the power grid and enhancing the stability and reliability of the system.
Currently, grid topology optimization research is mainly focused on the following aspects: traditional mathematical programming methods such as Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) and nonlinear programming (NLP); heuristic algorithms, such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO); and artificial intelligence based methods such as Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and Graph Neural Network (GNN). These approaches have achieved certain success in certain scenarios, but have many limitations. Although the mathematical programming method can obtain an accurate solution, the calculation complexity is high when dealing with large-scale and non-convex optimization problems, and the real-time optimization requirement is difficult to meet. The heuristic algorithm has wide application range, but is easy to fall into local optimum, and parameter adjustment is difficult. While exhibiting advantages in handling high-dimensional complex problems, artificial intelligence-based approaches face challenges such as poor model interpretability and limited generalization capability.
However, the following key technical problems still remain to be solved in the existing research: first, the dynamics and uncertainty of the grid topology are difficult to model effectively, resulting in optimization results that are difficult to adapt to the real-time changing grid conditions. Secondly, the trade-off among targets in the multi-target optimization problem is difficult to accurately quantify, and the practicability of the optimization result is affected. Again, efficient screening and evaluation of the vast number of possible actions in a large-scale grid system remains a challenge, limiting the improvement of optimization efficiency. In addition, constraint conditions in power grid topology optimization are complex and changeable, and how to meet various operation constraints while guaranteeing optimization efficiency is also a difficult problem. Finally, how to coordinate the topology optimization decisions under different time scales to achieve the balance of short-term and long-term targets is also a problem to be solved in the current research. These technical difficulties severely restrict the practical application and popularization of the power grid topology optimization technology, and development of new optimization methods is needed to overcome these challenges.
Disclosure of Invention
The invention aims to provide a power grid topology optimization method and system based on search ordering, so as to solve the problems in the prior art.
The technical scheme is that the power grid topology optimization method based on search ordering comprises the following steps:
s1, acquiring power grid topological structure data, and constructing an action space based on the power grid topological structure data; the power grid topological structure data comprises a node set, an edge set and an attribute set;
S2, acquiring real-time power grid state data, constructing a self-adaptive double-tower model based on the real-time power grid state data and an action space, and calculating to obtain a candidate action set;
s3, constructing a graph attention network and a time sequence graph neural network based on the candidate action set to obtain a sorted candidate action list;
And S4, performing multi-objective optimization and decision making based on the ordered candidate action list to obtain an optimal action.
A search ordering based power grid topology optimization system comprising:
At least one processor; and
A memory communicatively coupled to at least one of the processors; wherein,
The memory stores instructions executable by the processor for execution by the processor to implement the search ranking based power grid topology optimization method of any of the above-described aspects.
The method has the beneficial effects that through the organic combination of innovative algorithm construction and various methods, the overall effect of power grid topology optimization is improved, the adaptability and decision quality of the system are enhanced, the rapid optimization of a large-scale power grid system is realized, and strong support is provided for practical application.

Detailed Description
As shown in fig. 1, the application provides a power grid topology optimization method based on search ordering, which comprises the following specific steps:
s1, acquiring power grid topological structure data, and constructing an action space based on the power grid topological structure data; the power grid topological structure data comprises a node set, an edge set and an attribute set;
S2, acquiring real-time power grid state data, constructing a self-adaptive double-tower model based on the real-time power grid state data and an action space, and calculating to obtain a candidate action set;
s3, constructing a graph attention network and a time sequence graph neural network based on the candidate action set to obtain a sorted candidate action list;
And S4, performing multi-objective optimization and decision making based on the ordered candidate action list to obtain an optimal action.
In the embodiment, the topology structure of the power grid is dynamically adjusted by acquiring real-time power grid state data and constructing a self-adaptive double-tower model, and various disturbance and faults in the power grid are timely handled, and the self-adaption enables the power grid to better maintain stable operation, so that the large-scale power failure risk caused by faults is reduced; the candidate actions are ordered based on the graph attention network and the time sequence graph neural network, so that the most favorable operation for the power grid operation can be identified more accurately, and the economy, reliability and safety of the power grid can be comprehensively considered in the multi-objective optimization and decision process, so that the optimal configuration of resources is realized. By using the graph attention network and the time sequence graph neural network, complex data of the power grid can be processed and analyzed more efficiently, the degree of automation of the power grid is improved, and the self-adjusting capacity of the power grid in the face of complex environments is enhanced; by constructing and sequencing the candidate action list, the necessity of manual intervention is reduced, so that the optimization and decision process of the power grid is more efficient and accurate, the decision time is shortened, and the response speed of the power grid is improved. According to the embodiment, the optimization strategy is dynamically adjusted according to the real-time data and the power grid state, so that the adaptability of the power grid in the face of emergencies and changing environments is enhanced.
As shown in fig. 2, according to an aspect of the present application, step S1 is further:
S11, acquiring power grid topological structure data and action data affecting the power grid topological structure; the power grid topological structure data comprises a node set, an edge set and an attribute set; the action data comprises action types, affected device ID sets and execution parameter sets;
s12, processing power grid topological structure data by using a graph traversal algorithm, and generating a basic action set based on the action data and the processed power grid topological structure data;
S13, forming an action combination set by adopting a combination optimization algorithm based on the basic action set; based on the action combination set, adopting a heuristic algorithm to obtain an optimized action space;
S14, based on the optimized action space and the predefined constraint condition set, sequentially adopting a constraint propagation algorithm and a decision tree algorithm to obtain a classified action space; based on the classified action space, a heuristic rule engine is adopted to obtain a final optimized action space;
and S15, carrying out structured storage on the finally optimized action space to form a structured data set.
In this embodiment, power grid topology data and action data affecting the power grid topology are obtained, and the power grid topology data is processed by using a graph traversal algorithm to generate a basic action set. This basic set of actions is input into a combinatorial optimization algorithm, resulting in a set of action combinations. And finally, inputting the action combination set into a heuristic algorithm to obtain an optimized action space.
The optimized action space and the predefined set of constraints are input to an adaptive constraint network propagation algorithm. The algorithm first builds a constraint network in which nodes represent variables and edges represent constraint relationships. The value range and constraint strength of each node are then initialized. For each constraint, its violation is calculated and the constraint strength is updated. The algorithm selects the constraint with the highest intensity for propagation, reduces the value range of the related node and propagates the influence to the adjacent node. The process can dynamically adjust the propagation sequence, and preferentially process high-strength constraints until the network converges or reaches the upper iteration limit, and finally generate a constrained action space.
And inputting the constrained action space into a fuzzy decision forest algorithm. The algorithm builds a plurality of decision trees, each tree using a random feature subset. And introducing fuzzy splitting into each node, defining a fuzzy membership function, and allowing the sample part to belong to a plurality of child nodes. During the tree growth process, the algorithm dynamically adjusts the ambiguity. And integrating the results of the fuzzy decision trees by using a weighted voting method, and dynamically adjusting the weight based on the performance of each tree to obtain a classified action space.
And inputting the classified action space and the expert knowledge rule set into a cognitive map enhancement rule engine. The engine first builds an initial cognitive map in which nodes represent concepts, edges represent relationships, and maps expert rules onto the cognitive map. For each input action, activating the relevant nodes on the cognitive map, simulating a cognitive process by using a pulse propagation algorithm, and calculating the activation intensity of each rule. And then dynamically updating the rule weight, re-evaluating each action based on the updated weight, and applying Top-K screening to obtain a final optimized action space.
The optimized action space is stored in a structuring way, and the method specifically comprises the following steps: each action is assigned a unique identifier, forming an action index table. The specific parameters of each action are stored to form an action parameter matrix. Based on the action parameter matrix, a correlation graph is formed to represent the dependency and mutual exclusion relationships between actions. These three components together constitute the final structured dataset.
In a further embodiment, grid topology data and action data that may affect the grid topology are obtained, wherein the grid topology data comprises a set of nodes, a set of edges and a set of attributes, the action data comprises an action type, a set of affecting device IDs and a set of execution parameters;
Processing the power grid topological structure data by using a graph traversal algorithm to generate a basic action set; inputting the basic action set into a combination optimization algorithm to generate an action combination set; inputting the action combination set into a heuristic algorithm to finally obtain an optimized action space;
Inputting the optimized action space and the predefined constraint condition set into an adaptive constraint network propagation Algorithm (ACNP) to generate a constrained action space; then inputting the constrained action space into a Fuzzy Decision Forest (FDF) algorithm to obtain a classified action space; and inputting the classified action space and the expert knowledge rule set into a cognitive map enhancement rule engine (CGRE) to finally obtain the optimized action space.
When ACNP algorithm is used, a constraint network is constructed, nodes represent variables, and edges represent constraint relations. The value range D (i) and the constraint intensity CS (i, j) of each node are initialized. For each constraint C (i, j): calculating constraint violation degree CV (i, j) = |D (i) |D (j) |/|D (i)/(D (j) |), and updating constraint intensity: CS (i, j) =cs (i, j) (1+η×cv (i, j), where η is the learning rate; selecting the constraint with highest intensity for propagation, reducing the value range of the related node, and affecting the adjacent node by the propagation; the propagation order is dynamically adjusted to prioritize the high-strength constraints. Repeating until the network converges or reaches the upper iteration limit, and outputting the action space meeting the constraint.
When using the FDF algorithm, a plurality of decision trees are constructed, each tree using a random feature subset. Introducing fuzzy division into each node to construct a fuzzy membership function mu (x), wherein a sample can partially belong to a plurality of child nodes; during tree growth, the ambiguity θ is dynamically adjusted: θ=θ 0 * (1 - depth / max depth ) ρ , where ρ is the attenuation factor, depth represents the depth of the current node in the decision tree, max depth represents the length of the longest path that the decision tree can generate, and θ 0 represents the initial ambiguity; and integrating the results of the fuzzy decision trees, using a weighted voting method, and dynamically adjusting the weight based on the performance of each tree to obtain a classified action space.
When CGRE algorithm is used, an initial cognitive graph is constructed, nodes represent concepts, and edges represent relationships. Expert rules are mapped onto the initial cognitive map. Activating related nodes on an initial cognitive map CG for each input action in an action space, simulating a cognitive process by using a pulse propagation algorithm, and calculating the activation intensity AS (r) of each rule; dynamically updating rule weights: w (r) =w (r) ×1+ζ×as (r)), where ζ is the update rate; based on the updated weights, re-evaluating each action, and applying Top-K screening to obtain an optimized action space.
And (3) carrying out structural storage on the optimized action space, distributing a unique identifier for each action to form an action index table I, storing specific parameters of each action to form an action parameter matrix M, and representing dependence and mutual exclusion relation between actions to form a correlation graph G ', thereby finally obtaining a structural data set D= { I, M, G'.
In another specific embodiment, the system collects and collates complete topology information of the current grid, generating a grid topology dataset T. The grid topology data set T comprises a set of nodes N: including power stations, substations, load points, etc.; edge set E: representing the connection relation between nodes; attribute set a: various attributes of the nodes and edges (e.g., capacity, impedance, etc.) are recorded.
The system identifies and records all operations that may affect the grid topology, generating the original action set O. Each action O e O contains: action type C: such as switching circuitry, adjusting transformer taps, etc.; affecting the set of device IDs D; execution parameter P: such as switch state, adjustment amplitude, etc.
Based on the power grid topology data set T, a Depth First Search (DFS) or Breadth First Search (BFS) is performed using a graph traversal algorithm, resulting in a basic action set B. By traversing the entire grid topology, possible basic actions (e.g., switching operations, adjusting transformer taps, etc.) are generated for each node and edge. Based on the basic action set B, a combination optimization algorithm is used to obtain an action combination set C, and by generating effective combinations of basic actions, interaction and constraint among the actions are considered. Based on the action combination set C, an optimized action space S is obtained by using a simulated annealing algorithm or a genetic algorithm. And performing preliminary optimization on the action combination by using a heuristic algorithm to generate an action sequence with potential optimization effect.
The optimized action space S is further screened and optimized, and based on the optimized action space S and the predefined constraint condition set, an AC-3 algorithm (arc consistency algorithm) is used to obtain a constrained action space S 1 , so that actions which do not meet basic constraints can be rapidly removed. Based on the constrained action space S 1 , a decision tree algorithm is adopted to obtain a classified action space S 2 , so that actions can be classified and further screened based on conditions such as safety, feasibility and the like. Based on the classified action space S 2 and the expert knowledge rule set R, an optimized action space S' is obtained by using a Rete algorithm, so that the rule set constructed by expert knowledge can be applied to finally evaluate and screen actions.
Storing the optimized action space S' as structured data D, including an action index table I: assigning a unique identifier to each action; action parameter matrix M: storing specific parameters of each action; association diagram G: representing dependency and mutex relationships between actions.
According to the embodiment, through the data preprocessing and the action space construction method, the efficiency and the accuracy of power grid topology optimization are improved. By acquiring the power grid topological structure data and the action data which possibly influence the power grid topological structure, a comprehensive data base is established. This comprehensive data collection ensures the integrity and reliability of the subsequent optimization process. And processing the power grid topological structure data by using a graph traversal algorithm to generate a basic action set, and then gradually optimizing an action space by combining an optimization algorithm and a heuristic algorithm. The multi-level action space construction method not only considers single action, but also considers the effect of action combination, and expands the range of possible solutions. An adaptive constraint network propagation Algorithm (ACNP) is introduced to process and optimize the action space, so that the constraint intensity and the propagation sequence can be dynamically adjusted, complex constraint conditions can be effectively processed, and the generated solution can be ensured to meet the actual operation requirement. And classifying the constrained action space by using a Fuzzy Decision Forest (FDF), and improving the flexibility and accuracy of classification by introducing fuzzy splitting and dynamic adjustment ambiguity. The final optimization is performed by adopting a cognitive map enhancement rule engine (CGRE), and the optimization result which is more intelligent and more in line with the actual operation experience is realized by simulating the human cognitive process and combining expert knowledge.
The method and the device realize efficient construction and optimization of the action space, improve the starting point of the subsequent optimization process, and lay a solid foundation for the whole power grid topology optimization process. In addition, the final structured storage construction comprises construction of an action index table, an action parameter matrix and a correlation diagram, thereby providing convenience for subsequent rapid retrieval and analysis and further improving the operation efficiency of the whole system.
In another embodiment, a multi-level adaptive graph traversal algorithm (MLAGT) may also be used to process the grid topology data T, generating a basic action set B; then inputting the basic action set B into a dynamic weight combination optimization algorithm (DWCO) to generate an action combination set C; and inputting the action combination set C into a self-organizing critical heuristic algorithm (SOCH) to finally obtain an optimized action space S. The method comprises the following steps: initializing a plurality of traversal levels L1, L2, ln, each level corresponding to a different traversal granularity; traversing from the coarsest granularity level L1, and identifying key nodes and edges; performing finer-grained traversal in the next level L2 for each key node; in the traversal process, dynamically adjusting the importance weight W (i) of each node, and based on the connectivity and the load condition; switching between different levels using an adaptive step size λ (t), λ (t) =λ 0 /(1+αt), where t is the number of iterations and α is the decay rate; repeating until the finest granularity level Ln is reached or a stopping condition is met; and generating a basic action set B according to the traversing result and the node weight.
Initializing an action combination set C 0 , and setting an initial temperature T 0 and a cooling coefficient beta; assigning an initial weight w i to each action a i ; in each iteration, generating a new action combination C' according to the current temperature T and the action weight w; calculating objective functions f (C') and f (C); if f (C') < f (C), accepting the new combination; otherwise accepted with probability p=exp ((f (C) -f (C'))/T); updating action weights: w i = w i (1+γ×Δf), where γ is the learning rate and Δf is the objective function improvement amount; reducing the temperature: t=t×β; and repeating until the stopping condition is reached, and outputting the optimal action combination set C.
Initializing an action sequence S 0 , and setting initial energy E 0 and a critical index tau; defining an energy function E (S), and evaluating the advantages and disadvantages of the action sequence; in each iteration, a small disturbance is carried out on the current sequence S, and a new sequence S' is generated; calculating an energy difference Δe=e (S') -E (S); if ΔE < 0, accept the new sequence; otherwise accepted with probability p= (E (S)/E (S')) τ ; updating the critical index: τ=τ 0 log (1+t), where t is the number of iterations; dynamically adjusting the disturbance amplitude to maintain the system in a critical state; repeating until a stop condition is reached; outputting the optimized action sequence S.
As shown in fig. 3, according to an aspect of the present application, step S2 is further:
s21, acquiring real-time power grid state data, and acquiring a dynamic feature vector by adopting a multi-scale time sequence feature extraction algorithm based on the real-time power grid state data;
S22, based on the power grid topological structure data, adopting a self-adaptive spectral clustering enhancement algorithm to obtain a static feature vector;
s23, based on the dynamic feature vector and the static feature vector, adopting a self-adaptive weighted fusion algorithm to obtain a fusion feature vector;
s24, constructing a self-adaptive double-tower model, and inputting the fusion feature vector into a state tower in the double-tower model to obtain a state embedded vector; inputting the finally optimized action space into an action tower in the double-tower model to obtain an action embedded vector set;
s25, based on the state embedded vector and the action embedded vector set, adopting a self-adaptive similarity calculation and dynamic threshold selection algorithm to obtain a candidate action set.
Step S21 is further:
s211, acquiring real-time power grid state data, and extracting a time sequence in the real-time power grid state data;
s212, decomposing the time sequence into preset time scales, and calculating the size of each window by adopting an adaptive window sliding algorithm for each time scale;
s213, calculating statistical characteristics in each window based on real-time power grid state data, and extracting frequency domain characteristics in the statistical characteristics by using wavelet transformation; wherein the statistical features include mean, variance, and kurtosis;
s214, constructing a feature importance evaluation index, and updating the weight of the frequency domain feature based on the feature importance evaluation index;
And S215, splicing the frequency domain features with updated weights to form a final dynamic feature vector.
In a specific embodiment, real-time power grid state data are acquired and processed by adopting a multi-scale time sequence feature extraction algorithm. The algorithm decomposes the input time series data into a plurality of time scales. For each time scale, an adaptive window sliding algorithm is applied, with window size being dynamically adjusted over time scale. Statistical features such as mean, variance, kurtosis, etc. are calculated within each window and frequency domain features are extracted using wavelet transforms. Importance weights are applied to each feature, with an initial value of uniform distribution. And constructing a feature importance evaluation index based on the prediction capability of the feature importance evaluation index to the system state. And periodically updating the feature weights, and splicing the weighted features of all scales to form a final dynamic feature vector.
And processing by using a power grid topology data set and adopting a self-adaptive spectral clustering enhancement algorithm. An initial similarity matrix is constructed based on the physical connections and electrical characteristics between the nodes. An adaptive kernel function is introduced to calculate the Laplace matrix. And solving a generalized eigenvalue problem, and acquiring the first k eigenvectors. Self-organizing maps are applied in feature space to form initial clusters. The fuzzy clustering concept is introduced, allowing the node part to belong to a plurality of clusters. And defining a cluster effectiveness index, and periodically evaluating cluster quality. And if the index is reduced, dynamically adjusting the k value and the kernel function parameter. This process is repeated until convergence or an upper iteration limit is reached. Finally, based on the final clustering result, extracting the static feature vector.
The dynamic feature vector and the static feature vector are input into a dynamic attention fusion network. And constructing a dual-channel neural network, and respectively processing dynamic and static characteristics. In each channel, feature internal relationships are captured using a multi-headed self-attention mechanism, and residual connection and layer normalization are applied. A cross-channel attention module is then constructed, and an attention weight matrix between the dynamic and static features is calculated. The importance of both features is dynamically adjusted using a gating mechanism. And finally fusing the features, applying nonlinear transformation and residual connection, and outputting a final fused feature vector.
And constructing a self-adaptive double-tower model. And inputting the fusion feature vector into a state tower formed by the dynamic structure multi-layer perceptron to obtain a state embedded vector. And inputting the optimized action space into an action tower formed by layered local sensitive hash to obtain an action embedded vector set. The dynamic structure multi-layer perceptron dynamically adjusts the network structure by defining the neuron importance index, removes unimportant neurons, and adds new connections or layers between important layers. Hierarchical locality sensitive hashing divides the action space into multiple levels, each level representing a different granularity, maps actions into multiple buckets using a set of hash functions, builds an inter-layer index structure, allowing fast switching between different granularities.
And using a state embedded vector and a motion embedded vector set, and adopting an adaptive similarity calculation and dynamic threshold selection algorithm. A plurality of similarity measures, such as cosine similarity, euclidean distance, etc., are initialized and an initial weight is assigned. Weighted similarity is calculated and then a kernel density estimation method is used to estimate the similarity distribution. And dynamically determining a threshold value, and selecting actions with similarity larger than the threshold value as candidates. If the candidate set size exceeds a predetermined value, a diversity sampling algorithm is used for screening. And finally updating the similarity weight and outputting a final Top-K candidate action set.
In a further embodiment, real-time power grid state data is acquired, and a multiscale sequential feature extraction algorithm (MSTFE) is adopted for processing to obtain a dynamic feature vector, which specifically includes:
Decomposing the input time sequence R into a plurality of time scales { R 1 , R 2 , ..., R n }; for each scale R i , applying an adaptive window sliding algorithm, window size W '(i) =w' 0 * (1 + β＇ i ), where W ' 0 represents the initial window size and β' i represents the adjustment factor associated with the ith time scale; calculating statistical features (mean, variance, kurtosis, etc.) within each window; extracting frequency domain features using wavelet transform; applying importance weights omega (i) to each feature, wherein initial values are uniformly distributed; based on the prediction capability of the system state, constructing a feature importance evaluation index I (f), and periodically updating feature weights: ω (I) =ω (I) ×1+γ×i (f)), γ being the learning rate; and splicing the weighted features of all scales to form a final dynamic feature vector D.
Processing by using a power grid topology data set and adopting an adaptive spectral clustering enhancement Algorithm (ASCE) to obtain a static feature vector F, wherein the method specifically comprises the following steps:
Constructing an initial similarity matrix S' based on physical connection and electrical characteristics between nodes; introducing an adaptive kernel function K (x, y) =exp (-d (x, y) 2 /(2σ (x) σ (y))), wherein σ (x) and σ (y) are both local scale parameters, and d (x, y) represents the distance between the node and the node y; calculating a laplace matrix l=d "-S", D "being a degree matrix; solving a generalized eigenvalue problem lv=λ 'D "v, acquiring the first k eigenvectors, λ' representing eigenvalues in the generalized eigenvalue problem, v representing eigenvectors; applying self-organizing maps (SOMs) in the feature space to form an initial cluster; introducing a fuzzy clustering concept, allowing a node part to belong to a plurality of clusters, defining a cluster effectiveness index CVI, periodically evaluating the clustering quality, dynamically adjusting k values and kernel function parameters if the CVI is reduced, and repeating until convergence or reaching an iteration upper limit; based on the final clustering result, a static feature vector F is extracted.
Inputting the dynamic feature vector D and the static feature vector F into a Dynamic Attention Fusion Network (DAFN) to obtain a fusion feature vector H, wherein the fusion feature vector H is specifically as follows:
Constructing a dual-channel neural network, and respectively processing a dynamic feature vector D and a static feature vector F; in each channel, capturing the characteristic internal relation by using a multi-head self-attention mechanism, and applying residual connection and layer normalization; constructing a cross-channel attention module, calculating an attention weight matrix A between a dynamic feature vector D and a static feature vector F,
A(i，j) = softmax(Q(D i )K(F j ) T /sqrt(d))；
Wherein Q and K are linear transformations, d represents the dimension of the feature vector;
The importance of two features is dynamically regulated using gating mechanism G:
G = σ(W g [D;F] + b g )；
where σ is a sigmoid function, b g denotes the bias term in the gating mechanism.
Fusion characteristics: h=g (AD) + (1-G) (a T F); apply nonlinear transformation and residual connection: h=h+ffn (H), and the final fusion feature vector H is output.
Constructing a self-adaptive double-tower model, and inputting a fusion feature vector H into a state tower formed by a dynamic structure multi-layer perceptron (DSMLP) to obtain a state embedded vector S emb ; meanwhile, the optimized action space S' is input into an action tower formed by layered local sensitive hashes (HLSH) to obtain an action embedded vector set A emb , which is specifically as follows:
Initializing an MLP structure having a variable width and depth; defining a neuron importance index NI based on the activation frequency and gradient thereof; in each training period, forward propagation calculates loss, backward propagation updates parameters, and evaluates the neuron importance index NI of each neuron; periodically performing structural optimization, removing neurons with neuron importance indexes NI lower than a threshold value, and adding new connections or layers between layers with high NI; using the dynamic Dropout, the Dropout rate is inversely proportional to NI, outputting the final state embedding vector S emb .
Dividing the action space S' into a plurality of layers { L1, L2,., ln }, each layer representing a different granularity; at each layer Li, a set of hash functions h i,j (x) = sign(a i,j T x + b i,j is constructed, where a i,j represents the weight vector in the hash function, and b i,j represents the bias term in the hash function, mapping actions into multiple buckets; constructing an interlayer index structure, and allowing quick switching among different granularities; for the query vector q, searching nearest neighbors from the top layer L1, dynamically determining whether to drill down to the next layer, and based on the matching quality of the current layer; in the searching process, the accuracy is improved by using a Local Sensitive Forest (LSF), a plurality of LSH trees are constructed, the results of the plurality of trees are integrated, and the recall rate is improved; the motion embedded vector set a emb is output.
The state embedded vector S emb and the action embedded vector set A emb are utilized, and an adaptive similarity calculation and dynamic threshold selection Algorithm (ASCDTS) is adopted to obtain a Top-K candidate action set C, specifically:
Initializing a plurality of similarity measures { sim 1 , sim 2 , ..., sim m }, including cosine similarity, euclidean distance and the like; assigning an initial weight w i to each similarity measure sim i ; calculating weighted similarity:
Sim W (S emb , a) = Σ(w i * sim i (S emb , a)),a ∈ A emb 。
Using a Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) method, the similarity distribution P (Sim W ) is estimated, and the threshold θ is dynamically determined: initializing θ 0 =μ+σ, μ and σ being the mean and standard deviation of weighted similarity; in each iteration, θ is adjusted according to the result of the previous round:
θ t = θ t-1 + λ(K - |C t-1 |)；
Where λ is the learning rate, C t-1 is the action set selected in the previous round, and K represents the target size of the candidate action set.
Selecting actions with similarity larger than theta as candidates; and if the candidate set size |C| > K, screening by using a diversity sampling algorithm, greedy selecting the first action, and iteratively selecting the action with the smallest similarity with the selected action set. Updating the similarity weight:
w i = w i * (1 + η * performance(C i ))；
η is the update rate, performance (C i ) is the performance score for the action set selected using sim i , and the final Top-K candidate action set C is output.
In another specific embodiment, a timing algorithm is used for processing real-time power grid state data R, and time sequence characteristics of parameters such as power grid load, voltage and the like are captured; processing a power grid topology data set T by using a graph algorithm, and extracting static characteristics of a network structure; and fusing the dynamic characteristics and the static characteristics to generate a comprehensive characteristic representation, namely a fused characteristic vector H. And constructing a double-tower model, and respectively processing the state characteristics and the action characteristics. Inputting the fusion feature vector H into a state tower, and performing multi-layer perceptron (MLP) to obtain a state embedded vector S emb ; inputting the optimized action space S' into an action tower, and performing Local Sensitive Hashing (LSH) to obtain an action embedded vector set A emb ; based on the state embedded vector S emb and the action embedded vector set A emb , the similarity of the state embedded vector and the action embedded vector is calculated by adopting a cosine similarity and Top-K selection algorithm, and the most relevant candidate action is recalled to obtain Top-K candidate action set C. Thus, the dynamic and static characteristics are combined, and the real-time state and the topological structure of the power grid are comprehensively captured. Meanwhile, an adaptive weighted fusion method is also used for flexibly adjusting the importance of different features; the recall efficiency in a large-scale action space is improved by adopting a double-tower model structure; and the motion characteristics are processed by using the local sensitive hash, so that the calculation efficiency of the model is further improved.
According to the embodiment, the efficiency and the accuracy of power grid state feature extraction and action recall are greatly improved through the dynamic double-tower feature fusion recall model. The real-time power grid state data is processed by adopting a multi-scale time sequence feature extraction algorithm, and the algorithm realizes effective capture of features of different time scales by decomposing a time sequence into a plurality of scales and applying a self-adaptive window sliding algorithm on each scale. Meanwhile, by dynamically adjusting the feature weights, the extracted features can be ensured to accurately reflect the key information of the current power grid state. The method improves the comprehensiveness and adaptability of feature extraction, and provides a more reliable data basis for subsequent decisions. By introducing the self-adaptive kernel function and the fuzzy clustering concept, the analysis capability of the power grid topological structure is improved. This approach can better capture complex relationships in the network, providing a more accurate representation of static features. The dynamic attention fusion network is used, and the effective fusion of dynamic characteristics and static characteristics is realized through the two-channel neural network and a cross-channel attention mechanism. The fusion method not only considers the relation inside the features, but also captures the interaction between different types of features through an attention mechanism, so that a more comprehensive and accurate fusion feature representation is generated. The construction of the self-adaptive double-tower model comprises the application of a dynamic structure multi-layer perceptron and a layered local sensitive hash, so that the flexibility and the efficiency of the model are further improved. The dynamic structure multi-layer perceptron can dynamically adjust the network structure according to the feature importance, and the hierarchical local sensitive hash realizes the efficient indexing and retrieval of large-scale action space. The accuracy and diversity of candidate action selection are ensured through the combination of various similarity measures and dynamic threshold adjustment by using the self-adaptive similarity calculation and dynamic threshold selection algorithm. Not only improves the recall quality, but also maintains the adaptability of the system through dynamic adjustment.
The embodiment realizes accurate sensing and efficient action recall of the power grid state, improves the basis of subsequent decisions, reduces the calculation complexity and provides possibility for real-time optimization of the decisions.

Step S32 is further:
s321, constructing a multiscale dynamic graph attention network based on a dynamic space-time graph and a state embedding vector;
S322, based on the state embedded vector, calculating query, key and value matrix of each attention head in the multi-scale dynamic graph attention network;

In a specific embodiment, a power grid topology data set and historical power grid state data are obtained, and a space-time adaptive graph construction algorithm is adopted for processing. The algorithm initializes the static graph structure based on grid topology data. And carrying out time window division on the historical data, and dynamically adjusting the window size. And in each time window, calculating the dynamic association strength among the nodes, and updating the edge weight. Edges are dynamically added or removed according to the weights. Adaptive threshold control map structure variation is used. And finally, constructing edges of the time dimension, and connecting the same nodes of different time steps to obtain a dynamic time-space diagram.
The dynamic space-time diagram and the state embedding vector are input into a multiscale dynamic diagram attention network. The network defines a plurality of attention headers, each header focusing on a different feature subspace. For each attention header, a query, key, value matrix is calculated, and an attention score is calculated. The time decay factor is introduced and the attention calculation is modified. And calculating output, and fusing the multi-head result by using a gating mechanism. Finally, residual connection and layer normalization are applied to obtain a node representation of attention weighting.
The node representation and candidate action set weighted by attention are used for processing by adopting the self-adaptive space-time diagram convolution network. The network constructs an adaptive graph rolling filter, introducing a dynamic adjacency matrix. A multi-layer network structure is constructed including spatial convolution layers, temporal convolution layers, and combination layers. The outputs of the different layers are aggregated using an attention mechanism. For each candidate action, an action embedding is generated, an action-state pair representation is computed, and a spatiotemporal representation of the action-state pair is obtained.
The spatiotemporal representation of action-state pairs is input into a hierarchical multi-criterion decision network. The network first defines a plurality of evaluation criteria such as security, economy, reliability, etc. And constructing a hierarchical neural network structure, wherein the hierarchical neural network structure comprises a bottom layer sub-network, a middle layer and a top layer. An attention mechanism is applied in each sub-network to dynamically adjust feature importance. Using soft hierarchical decomposition allows the evaluation result portion to flow to non-directly superior nodes. Uncertainty modeling is introduced and the evaluation result is represented by probability distribution. And optimizing network parameters by applying a gradient lifting method. And finally generating a final score and an ordered list of candidate actions.
In a further embodiment, a power grid topology data set T and historical power grid state data H are obtained, and a space-time adaptive graph construction algorithm (STAGBA) is adopted for processing, so as to obtain a dynamic space-time graph G ts , which specifically is:
Based on the grid topology data T, a static graph structure G s is initialized. Dividing a time window of the historical data H, and dynamically adjusting the window size w; within each time window t, calculating the dynamic association strength R (i, j, t) among the nodes, and updating the edge weight: w (i, j, t) =α×w (i, j, t-1) + (1- α) ×r (i, j, t); if W (i, j, t) > θ, adding a temporary edge; if W (i, j, t) < φ, remove the existing edge; using an adaptive threshold:
θ t = θ 0 * (1 + β * var(R))；
φ t = φ 0 * (1 - β * var(R))；
where α represents a smoothing factor, θ represents a threshold for adding a temporary edge; phi represents the threshold for removing the existing edge, beta represents the adaptive threshold adjustment factor;
And constructing a time dimension edge, connecting the same node with different time steps, and outputting a dynamic time-space diagram G ts .
The dynamic space-time diagram G ts and the state embedding vector S emb are input into a multi-scale dynamic diagram attention network (MDGAN), and the obtained attention weighted node representation N att is specifically:
Defining a plurality of attention heads, each head focusing on a different feature subspace; for each attention header h, calculate a query, key, value matrix:
Q h = WQ h * S emb ；
K h = WK h * S emb ；
V h = WV h * S emb ；
Where Q h represents the query matrix for attention header h, K h represents the key matrix for attention header h, V h represents the value matrix for attention header h;
Calculating an attention score: a h = softmax((Q h * K h T ) / sqrt(d k +m)), M is the adjacency matrix mask, d k is the dimension of the key vector.
Introducing a time decay factor: d (t) =exp (- λ×Δt), λ is the decay rate, Δt represents the time difference; modifying the attention calculation: a h ' = A h ×d (t); and (3) calculating and outputting: o h = A h ' * V h ; the multi-headed results are fused using a gating mechanism:
g h = sigmoid(W gh * [O h ;S emb ]) O = Σ(g h * O h )；
residual connection and layer normalization are applied: n att = LayerNorm(O + S emb ).
The node representation N att weighted by the attention and the candidate action set C are used for processing by adopting an adaptive space-time diagram convolution network (ASTGCN) to obtain a space-time representation TS of the action-state pair, specifically:
Constructing an adaptive graph convolution filter: f (X, a) =σ (D -1/2 AD -1/2 XW), where a represents the adjacency matrix, σ represents the activation function, D represents the degree matrix, X represents the node feature matrix, and W represents the weight matrix; introducing a dynamic adjacency matrix A t , and updating in real time according to the current network state; constructing a multi-layer ASTGCN structure, and a space convolution layer: GC s (X t ) = f(X t , A t ); time convolution layer: GC t (X) =conv1d (X), where D (X) represents the result of normalizing the node feature matrix X; and (2) a combined layer: h l = GC s (GC t (H l -1)); the outputs of the different layers are aggregated using an attention mechanism: α l = softmax(v T tanh(WH l + b)) O = Σ(α l * H l ), wherein b represents a bias term; generating an action insert e c for each candidate action C e C; computing action-state pair representation: TS c = FC([O; e c ) to output a spatiotemporal representation TS of the action-state pair.
The space-time representation TS of the action-state pairs is input into a hierarchical multi-criterion decision network (HMCDN) to obtain an ordered candidate action list R C , which is specifically:
Defining a plurality of evaluation criteria { C 1 , C 2 , ..., C m }, such as security, economy, reliability, etc.; constructing a hierarchical neural network structure, and evaluating the bottom sub-network according to each criterion C i ; the middle layer synthesizes the evaluation results of the related criteria; the top layer generates the final composite score. Applying an attention mechanism in each sub-network, dynamically adjusting feature importance; using soft hierarchical decomposition: allowing the evaluation result portion to flow to the indirectly superior node. Uncertainty modeling is introduced, the probability distribution is used for representing the evaluation result instead of a single score, and uncertainty propagation is processed through Monte Carlo sampling. And optimizing network parameters by using a gradient lifting method, and generating a final score and an ordered list R C of the candidate actions.
In another specific embodiment, the grid topology dataset is combined with historical grid state data to construct the timing diagram representation. The timing diagram and state embedding vector are based on capturing importance relationships between nodes using a graph attention network, resulting in an attention weighted node representation. Based on the attention weighted node representation and the candidate action set, modeling dynamic changes of the power grid state by using a timing diagram neural network to obtain a timing representation of the action-state pair. Based on the time sequence representation, the candidate actions are evaluated and sequenced by adopting a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and a sequencing algorithm, and a sequenced candidate action list is obtained.
According to the embodiment, through the graph attention and time sequence graph neural network action evaluation method, accuracy and efficiency of action evaluation in power grid topology optimization are improved. By the application of the space-time self-adaptive graph construction algorithm, accurate modeling of the change of the power grid topological structure along with time is realized by dynamically adjusting a time window and edge weights. Not only is a static topological structure captured, but also dynamic changes in the network are considered, and more comprehensive and accurate graph structure representation is provided for subsequent analysis. The introduction of a multi-scale dynamic graph attention network achieves effective attention to different feature subspaces and time scales through a plurality of attention heads and time attenuation factors. Thus, complex space-time dependency relations in the power grid can be captured, and the accuracy and the expression capacity of node representation are improved. The use of the adaptive space-time diagram convolution network realizes the effective processing of space-time diagram data by constructing an adaptive diagram convolution filter and a dynamic adjacency matrix. The construction of a multi-layer network structure, including spatial convolution layers, temporal convolution layers, and combination layers, enables the model to capture features of both spatial and temporal dimensions simultaneously, thereby generating a more comprehensive representation of motion-state pairs. Finally, the application of the hierarchical multi-criterion decision network realizes the comprehensive evaluation of candidate actions by defining a plurality of evaluation criteria and constructing a hierarchical neural network structure. The flexibility and the robustness of the evaluation are further improved by introducing soft hierarchical decomposition and uncertainty modeling. Not only a plurality of decision criteria are considered, but also the evaluation result is represented by probability distribution, so that uncertainty in the decision process is better processed.
The embodiment realizes accurate evaluation of the power grid action. Not only the static structure and the dynamic change of the power grid are considered, but also the comprehensiveness and the reliability of the evaluation result are ensured by a multi-level and multi-criterion evaluation method. The method improves the accuracy of action evaluation, provides a more reliable basis for subsequent optimization decisions, and simultaneously realizes the rapid evaluation of a large-scale power grid system through an efficient graph neural network structure, thereby providing possibility for real-time decisions.

s41, based on a predefined optimization target set, a dynamic weight self-adaptive fusion algorithm is adopted to obtain a self-adaptive multi-target evaluation function; wherein the optimization objective set includes load balancing, network stability, and energy efficiency;

s411, acquiring an optimization target set, and initializing a target weight vector of the optimization target set;
s412, acquiring historical performance data and current system state data, and constructing an importance index of each target based on the historical performance data and the current system state data;
S413, updating the target weight vector based on the importance index to obtain updated weight, and normalizing the updated weight by using a Softmax function to obtain normalized weight;

In a specific embodiment, an optimization target set is obtained, and a dynamic weight self-adaptive fusion algorithm is adopted for processing. And initializing a target weight vector. Importance indicators for each target are defined based on historical performance and current system state. And constructing an adaptive weight updating rule, and normalizing the updated weight by using a Softmax function. And constructing a fuzzy membership function to represent the satisfaction degree of the scheme on the target. Defining a self-adaptive multi-objective evaluation function, periodically evaluating and adjusting a weight updating strategy. Finally, the self-adaptive multi-objective evaluation function is obtained.
And inputting the power grid operation constraint conditions and the self-adaptive multi-objective evaluation function into a dynamic constraint processing and self-adaptive penalty algorithm. Constraints are classified into hard constraints and soft constraints. For hard constraints, solutions meeting the hard constraints are quickly screened using feasibility rules, and constructing repair operations maps infeasible solutions to feasible domain boundaries. And defining a violation degree function for soft constraint, and constructing an adaptive penalty factor. And constructing an evaluation function with the constraint, dynamically adjusting a penalty strategy, and adding penalty weight to the frequently violated constraint. The constraint classification is periodically reevaluated and, if necessary, switched between hard and soft constraints. And finally obtaining the self-adaptive multi-objective evaluation function with the constraint.
And processing by adopting a co-evolution multi-population particle swarm optimization algorithm by utilizing the constrained self-adaptive multi-objective evaluation function and the ordered candidate action list. A plurality of sub-populations are initialized, each focusing on a particular target or search area. In each sub-population, adaptive inertia weights and acceleration coefficients are applied using an improved speed update rule. A co-evolution mechanism is introduced to periodically exchange elite individuals among sub-populations, and competition-collaboration strategies are used to assess individual fitness. And constructing a diversity maintaining strategy, maintaining the diversity of the pareto front by using the crowding distance, and introducing small-probability mutation to jump out of local optimum. Dynamically adjusting the quantity and the scale of the sub-populations, combining similar sub-populations, and splitting sub-populations with strong exploratory property. An archive policy is applied, maintaining a global non-dominant solution set. The search space is periodically reconstructed, focusing on the potential areas. Finally, the pareto optimal solution set is obtained.
And inputting the pareto optimal solution set into a fuzzy analytic hierarchy process network. And constructing a decision hierarchy structure comprising a target layer, a criterion layer and a scheme layer. In each level, a fuzzy comparison matrix is established. And calculating weights by using an improved eigenvector method, constructing a fuzzy consistency matrix, solving a fuzzy eigenvector equation, and reducing the dimension of the fuzzy weights. Introducing a neural network to process the interlayer relation, learning the interlayer mapping relation by using a BP network, and applying dropout to prevent overfitting. An adaptive membership function is constructed and a Choquet fuzzy integral aggregate multi-criterion evaluation is used. And (5) using sensitivity analysis to evaluate the robustness of the result. And finally, outputting the action with the highest comprehensive score as the optimal action.
In a further embodiment, an optimization target set O is obtained, and a Dynamic Weight Adaptive Fusion Algorithm (DWAFA) is adopted to process the optimization target set O, so as to obtain an adaptive multi-target evaluation function M, which specifically is:
Initializing a target weight vector w= { W 1 ,w 2 ,...,w n },Σw i =1; defining an importance index I (oi) of each target based on the historical performance and the current system state; constructing an adaptive weight updating rule:
w i (t+1) = w i (t) +η* (I(o i ) - w i (t)) +ε* N(0，1) ；
wherein eta is learning rate, epsilon is noise term, and N (0, 1) is standard normal distribution.
Normalizing the updated weights by applying a Softmax function; constructing a fuzzy membership function mu i (x) which represents the satisfaction degree of the scheme x on the target o i ; defining an adaptive multi-objective evaluation function: m (x) =Σ (w i *μ i (x)). The weight update strategy is periodically evaluated and adjusted.
Inputting the power grid operation constraint condition E and the self-adaptive multi-objective evaluation function M into a dynamic constraint processing and self-adaptive penalty algorithm (DCAPA) to obtain a constrained self-adaptive multi-objective evaluation function M c , wherein the method specifically comprises the following steps of:
Classifying constraint conditions E into hard constraints EH and soft constraints ES; for the hard constraint EH, a solution meeting the hard constraint is rapidly screened by using a feasibility rule, a repair operation is constructed, and the infeasible solution is mapped to a feasible domain boundary; for soft constraint ES, define a violation degree function v (x, e i ), construct an adaptive penalty factor:
p(e i , t) = p 0 (e i ) * (1 +γ* t) δ ；
Where t is the number of iterations, γ and δ are adjustment parameters, p 0 (e i ) represents the initial penalty factor.
Constructing an evaluation function with constraint: m c (x) = M(x) -Σ(p(e i , t) * v(x, e i ); dynamically adjusting a punishment strategy, tracking the history of constraint violation, adding punishment weight to the frequently violated constraint, and considering that the constraint is violated more than 10 times in one month when the grid operation constraint is violated. The constraint classification is periodically reevaluated and, if necessary, switched between hard and soft constraints.
The self-adaptive multi-objective evaluation function M c with constraint and the ordered candidate action list R C are used for processing by adopting a co-evolution multi-population particle swarm optimization algorithm (CEMPSO) to obtain a pareto optimal solution set P, which is specifically as follows:
A plurality of sub-populations P 1 ,P 2 ,...,P k are initialized, each focusing on a particular target or search area. In each sub-population P i , an improved speed update rule is used:
v(t+1) = wv(t) + c1r1*(pbest - x) + c2r2(gbest - x) + c3r3(sbest - x)；
wherein sbest is a sub-population optimal solution, w is an adaptive inertial weight, c1, c2, c3 represent acceleration coefficients, r1, r2 and r3 represent random numbers ranging between [0,1], pbest represent historical optimal positions of particles themselves, and gbest represent global optimal positions of the whole particle swarm.
A co-evolution mechanism is introduced to periodically exchange elite individuals among sub-populations, and competition-collaboration strategies are used to assess individual fitness. Constructing a diversity maintaining strategy, maintaining the diversity of the pareto front by using the crowding distance, introducing small probability mutation, and jumping out of local optimum. Dynamically adjusting the quantity and the scale of the sub-populations, combining similar sub-populations, and splitting sub-populations with strong exploratory property. An archive policy is applied, maintaining a global non-dominant solution set. Periodically reconstructing the search space, focusing on a potential area, and outputting a final pareto optimal solution set P.
Inputting the pareto optimal solution set P into a fuzzy analytic hierarchy process network (FHAN) to obtain an optimal action A opt , wherein the optimal action A opt is specifically as follows:
And constructing a decision hierarchy structure comprising a target layer, a criterion layer and a scheme layer. In each level, a fuzzy comparison matrix a= (a ij )n×n：a ij = (l ij ,m ij ,u ij ) is established, representing the fuzzy number, where l ij ,m ij ,u ij represents the lower, median and upper bounds, respectively, of the fuzzy number in the fuzzy comparison matrix. Calculating weights by using an improved eigenvector method, constructing a fuzzy consistency matrix R, and solving a fuzzy eigenvalue: and (3) reducing the dimension of the fuzzy weight, wherein Θ represents a multiplication operator of the fuzzy matrix, W represents a weight vector, λ represents a characteristic value in a fuzzy characteristic equation, max represents a maximum value operation, and Wc represents a normalized weight vector. Introducing a neural network to process the interlayer relation, learning the interlayer mapping relation by using a BP network, and applying dropout to prevent overfitting. Constructing an adaptive membership function:
μ(x) = 1 / (1 + ((x-c)/a) 2 b)；
Wherein a, b, c are dynamic parameters, which are adjusted according to historical data.
Multiple criteria evaluation using Choquet fuzzy integral aggregation: e (f) =Σ (f (x (i)) -f (x (i-1))) μ (a (i)), where f (x (i) represents an evaluation function value corresponding to criterion i;
And (3) applying sensitivity analysis to evaluate the robustness of the result, and outputting the action with the highest comprehensive score as an optimal action A opt .
In another particular embodiment, the optimal action is selected from the ranked candidate actions under a plurality of optimization objectives. Based on the optimization target set O, an evaluation function is built for each optimization target by adopting a weighted sum method, and the evaluation functions are combined into a multi-target optimization problem to form a multi-target evaluation function M. Based on the power grid operation constraint condition E and the multi-objective evaluation function M, applying the power grid operation constraint condition to the optimization problem by adopting a penalty function method to obtain the multi-objective evaluation function M c with constraint. Based on the constrained multi-objective evaluation function M c and the ordered candidate action list R C , an improved multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) is adopted to solve the optimal action, and the pareto optimal solution set P is obtained. And selecting a final optimal action A opt from the pareto optimal solution set P by adopting a TOPSIS decision method. By using the graph annotation force network and the time sequence graph neural network, the topological structure and the time dynamic characteristic of the power grid are comprehensively considered; a multi-objective optimization method is adopted, so that a plurality of optimization objectives which are possibly in conflict with each other are balanced; the concept of pareto optimization is introduced, and a series of non-dominant solutions are provided for a decision maker; the final decision is made using the TOPSIS approach, taking into account the comprehensive performance of multiple targets.
Not only the complexity and the dynamics of the power grid are considered, but also a flexible decision framework is provided, and the weight of the optimization target can be adjusted according to different operation requirements. The final output optimal action a opt will be a comprehensive optimal selection under multiple objectives and constraints.
According to the embodiment, the overall effect of power grid topology optimization is improved through a self-adaptive multi-objective optimization and fuzzy comprehensive decision method. The application of the dynamic weight self-adaptive fusion algorithm realizes the dynamic balance of a plurality of optimization targets by defining the target importance index and constructing the self-adaptive weight updating rule. The relative importance of different targets is considered, the self-adaptive adjustment can be carried out according to the historical performance and the current system state, and the flexibility and the adaptability of the optimization process are ensured. The dynamic constraint processing and the self-adaptive penalty algorithm are introduced, and complex power grid operation constraint conditions are effectively processed by distinguishing hard constraint from soft constraint and constructing self-adaptive penalty factors. Not only ensures that the optimization result meets the key operation requirement, but also improves the feasibility and practicality of the optimization through flexible processing of soft constraint. The use of the co-evolution multi-population particle swarm optimization algorithm improves the searching efficiency and diversity by initializing a plurality of sub-populations which are focused on different targets or searching areas and introducing a co-evolution mechanism. The improved speed update rules and adaptive parameter adjustment further enhance the convergence and exploration capabilities of the algorithm. The application of diversity maintenance strategies and archiving mechanisms ensures the quality and distribution of the obtained pareto optimal solution set. By the application of the fuzzy analytic hierarchy process, the complex decision problem is effectively processed by constructing a decision hierarchy structure and using a fuzzy comparison matrix. The improved feature vector method and the neural network are introduced, so that the accuracy of weight calculation and the modeling capability of interlayer relation are improved. The use of the adaptive membership function and Choquet fuzzy integrations further enhances the flexibility and comprehensiveness of the decision.
The embodiment realizes the efficient solution of the power grid topology optimization. Not only can a plurality of optimization targets and complex constraint conditions be considered at the same time, but also uncertainty and complexity in the optimization process are effectively processed through a co-evolution and fuzzy comprehensive decision method. The method improves the quality and reliability of the optimization result, simultaneously realizes the rapid optimization of a large-scale power grid system through parallel computing and a self-adaptive mechanism, and provides powerful support for practical application. In addition, the flexibility and the adaptability of the scheme enable the system to effectively cope with various complicated conditions in the operation of the power grid, and the overall performance and the reliability of the system are improved.
According to the application, through the innovative data preprocessing, feature fusion, action evaluation and multi-objective optimization method, the overall effect of power grid topology optimization is remarkably improved. The data preprocessing and the action space construction lay a solid foundation for subsequent optimization, and the data quality and the retrieval efficiency are improved through multi-level action space optimization and structured storage. The dynamic double-tower feature fusion recall model realizes accurate perception and efficient action recall of the power grid state, and the accuracy of feature representation and recall efficiency are improved through multi-scale time sequence feature extraction and the self-adaptive double-tower model. The method for evaluating the action of the neural network of the graph attention and the time sequence graph realizes the comprehensive evaluation of candidate actions through the construction of a space-time self-adaptive graph and a multi-criterion decision network. The self-adaptive multi-objective optimization and fuzzy comprehensive decision method effectively solves the problem of multi-objective optimization through dynamic weight adjustment and a co-evolution algorithm. Through the organic combination of the steps, the quality and the reliability of an optimization result are improved, and the rapid optimization of a large-scale power grid system is realized through a parallel computing and self-adaptive mechanism, so that strong support is provided for practical application.

A search ordering based power grid topology optimization system comprising:
At least one processor; and

The memory stores instructions executable by the processor for execution by the processor to implement the search ranking based grid topology optimization method of any one of the embodiments described above.
The application provides a new thought and method for solving the problems through innovative technologies such as data preprocessing, dynamic feature fusion, multi-scale graph neural network, self-adaptive multi-objective optimization and the like, and is expected to make breakthrough progress in the aspects of improving the optimization efficiency, enhancing the adaptability, improving the decision quality and the like. The multi-scale temporal feature extraction algorithm decomposes the input time series into multiple time scales and captures features of different scales using an adaptive window sliding algorithm. Thus, dynamic changes of the state of the power grid can be effectively captured. The time-space self-adaptive graph construction algorithm realizes accurate modeling of the change of the power grid topological structure along with time by dynamically adjusting a time window and edge weights. The combination of the two algorithms enables the system to adapt to the change of the power grid state in real time, and the adaptability and accuracy of the optimization result are improved.
And the target weighing quantification in the multi-target optimization problem is realized through a dynamic weight self-adaptive fusion algorithm. By defining the target importance index and constructing the self-adaptive weight updating rule, the dynamic balance of a plurality of optimization targets is realized. The system can automatically adjust the weight of each target according to the historical performance and the current system state, and ensures the flexibility and adaptability of the optimization process. In addition, the application of the fuzzy analytic hierarchy process further improves the accuracy and reliability of multi-objective decisions by constructing a decision hierarchy structure and using a fuzzy comparison matrix.
The high-efficiency screening and evaluation of mass possible actions in a large-scale power grid system are realized through the self-adaptive double-tower model and the multi-scale dynamic diagram attention network. The self-adaptive double-tower model realizes the efficient indexing and retrieval of a large-scale action space through a dynamic structure multi-layer perceptron and a layered local sensitive hash. The multi-scale dynamic graph attention network can rapidly capture complex space-time dependency relations in the power grid through a plurality of attention heads and time attenuation factors, and efficiency and accuracy of action evaluation are improved. The combination of the methods improves the capacity of the system for processing mass actions and improves the optimization efficiency.
And complex and changeable constraint condition processing is realized through dynamic constraint processing and an adaptive penalty algorithm. By distinguishing the hard constraint from the soft constraint and constructing the self-adaptive penalty factor, flexible processing of complex constraint conditions is realized. For hard constraint, the algorithm uses feasibility rules to rapidly screen solutions meeting the conditions; for soft constraint, by dynamically adjusting penalty weights, various operation constraints are satisfied while optimizing efficiency is ensured. The method not only ensures the feasibility of the optimization result, but also improves the efficiency of the optimization process.
The coordination of topology optimization decisions under different time scales is realized through a multi-scale time sequence feature extraction algorithm and a self-adaptive space-time diagram convolution network. The multi-scale time sequence feature extraction algorithm can capture short-term and long-term time features at the same time, and the self-adaptive space-time diagram convolution network realizes effective fusion of different time scale features through a multi-layer network structure comprising a space convolution layer, a time convolution layer and a combination layer. The method enables the system to consider both short-term and long-term objectives, and achieves coordination and consistency of decisions at different time scales.
The application effectively solves the key technical problems existing in the power grid topology optimization through the organic combination of innovative algorithm construction and a plurality of methods. Not only improves the optimization efficiency, but also enhances the adaptability and decision quality of the system, and provides powerful support for the practical application and popularization of the power grid topology optimization technology.
The preferred embodiments of the present invention have been described in detail above, but the present invention is not limited to the specific details of the above embodiments, and various equivalent changes can be made to the technical solution of the present invention within the scope of the technical concept of the present invention, and all the equivalent changes belong to the protection scope of the present invention.

Title
Method for integrating individual load forecasts into a composite load forecast to present a comprehensive, synchronized and harmonized load forecast

Abstract
A method is provided for merging different load forecasts for power grid centers. Area load forecasts are accepted from load forecast engines. A relational database saves load forecast engine data. A comprehensive operating plan integrates individual load forecasts into a composite load forecast to present a comprehensive, synchronized and harmonized load forecast.

Description
RELATED APPLICATION
This patent application is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 14/012,853, filed Aug. 28, 2013, and entitled “METHOD FOR INTEGRATING INDIVIDUAL LOAD FORECASTS INTO A COMPOSITE LOAD FORECAST TO PRESENT A COMPREHENSIVE, SYNCHRONIZED AND HARMONIZED LOAD FORECAST”, and now issued as U.S. U.S. Pat. No. 9,851,700, which is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser.
